recipes.title: Why Just Devil the Eggs When You Can Possess Them
ingredients: Deviled eggs and Alabama white sauce (from the video; amounts only where spoken):
Sugar, salt, garlic and black pepper
Cajun seasoning, plus extra to finish
A squeeze of lemon (or lime) juice
Vinegar slaw (from the video; amounts not stated):
White cabbage and a little red cabbage, thinly sliced
Apple cider vinegar, sugar, a touch of salt and black pepper
Cornbread to serve (from the description; baked off camera):
8 in (20 cm) square or round baking dish
steps: Cornbread (optional side): The cornbread was baked before filming. Per the description: mix the ingredients, pour into an 8 in dish and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 20–25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Slaw veg: Grate about half a carrot and thinly slice the radishes (leave the red skin on if you like), white cabbage and a little red cabbage. Toss together in a bowl.

Slaw dressing: Warm the apple cider vinegar over a low flame with sugar, stirring just until it dissolves (don't boil). Add a touch of salt, black pepper and any seeds, then stir in a little oil. Pour over the cabbage and mix well so it starts to soften.

Alabama white sauce: Mix the mayonnaise with about a tablespoon each of apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard and horseradish, plus a splash of Worcestershire sauce, sugar, salt, garlic, pepper, Cajun seasoning and a little lemon juice. Keep it fairly thick. Let it stand so the flavours come together.
Boil the eggs: Boil the eggs about 7 minutes, turn off the heat and leave 2–3 minutes, then cool them in cold water and peel. (Or bring to the boil, turn off and leave about 12 minutes.)
Make the filling: Halve the eggs, pop out the yolks and mash them finely with a fork (or press through a sieve). Mix in the Alabama white sauce, keeping a little back for the top.
Fill: Pipe or spoon the filling back into the whites, add a little white sauce on top and dust with Cajun seasoning (jalapeños optional).
Serve: Serve with the vinegar slaw and cornbread.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w_vz_-X5hdQ

Time and temperature tips from the video description: 190°C / 375–380°F; Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.

recipes.title: POP TARTS Flaky Jam Filled Shelf Stable!
ingredients: Vegetable shortening or unsalted butter — 170 g (¾ cup / 12 tbsp); shortening is more shelf-stable
Cold water — 3–4 tbsp (45–60 ml), mixed with ½ tsp vinegar or lemon juice
Jam, any flavour — ½ cup (160 g)
Optional icing (this makes them no longer shelf-stable):
Lemon juice or vanilla extract — ½ tsp (optional)
steps: Make the pastry: Rub vegetable shortening (or butter; the host uses shortening because it is more shelf-stable) into the flour with the sugar and salt. Add cold water with a little splash of apple cider vinegar (or lemon juice, from the description) and bring the dough together. If it is too wet, add a little flour; if too dry, a little more water.
Thicken the jam: Warm the jam gently with a little splash of water until it is a thick goo. The description also lists 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tsp water to thicken it.

Roll and fill: On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough to cut eight rectangles about 6½ by 3¼ inches, store-packet size. Spoon jam on, keeping back from the edge so they will seal. Top with another piece of pastry, trim, crimp with a fork and cut a vent.
Bake: Bake at 175°C / 350°F for about 22–25 minutes until golden and firm.

Cool, and ice if you want: Rest a minute, then move to a rack to cool. Un-iced, the host says they are shelf-stable for weeks if wrapped or kept in an airtight box. Icing (powdered sugar with 1–2 tbsp water, and optional lemon juice or vanilla) means they are no longer shelf-stable. Ice only after they have cooled.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3d_7GpXkTWw
Uploaded 2025-05-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake: 175°C / 350°F for 22–25 minutes, until golden and firm.

recipes.title: Processed PARMESAN Cheese Creamy, sliceable,  MELTS beautifully TOO!
ingredients: 200g (2 cups) Parmesan powder (or finely grated Parmesan)
30g (6 tsp) soy lecithin powder (or 12 tsp liquid lecithin)
2g baking soda (½ teaspoon) — optional, helps smooth but can be left out
30g (6 tsp) cornstarch or sodium citrate (for smooth emulsification)
2½ tbsp powdered gelatin (or agar-agar for a vegetarian option) (helps firm up)
a pinch of turmeric or paprika (optional, for colour)
Put in the fridge to set up for about 6 hours - leave overnight for best results.
Shelf life: 7–10 days safely in the fridge. Vacuum-sealed? You might get up to 2–3 weeks.
Cut into usable blocks or slices, wrap tightly, and freeze.
Shelf life in the freezer: Up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge overnight. Texture may soften slightly but still melts well.
steps: Grate the Parmesan: Finely grate the Parmesan, rind and all, by hand or in a food processor (or use Parmesan powder).
Warm the base: On a fairly low flame, warm the milk with the butter (melted) and whisk in the soy lecithin powder to help it emulsify. A few lumps are fine because it gets blended later.

Add the cheese and the rest: Stir in the Parmesan, then the salt, gelatin, cornflour (or sodium citrate) and baking soda (optional). Add turmeric a little at a time until you get the colour you want, or leave it out to keep the cheese white.
Thicken: Keep stirring over low heat until it thickens and turns smooth. It firms up a lot in the fridge.
Blend: Blitz it with a stick blender until completely smooth, with no flecks of powder.

Mould and set: Pour it into a mould (the host uses a clean, cut-down milk carton), tap it to level the top and release air bubbles, let it cool, cover, and refrigerate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight.

Slice and use: Turn it out and slice. It melts well on burgers (the host melts it under a lid on Italian sausage patties) and in pasta. It keeps 7–10 days in an airtight container in the fridge, or up to 3 months frozen.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WzaaICJools

recipes.title: KETCHUP Before  KETCHUP  - BRITISH UMAMI in a Bottle
ingredients: Chestnut, button or flat-cap mushrooms, finely chopped — 500 g (1.1 lb)
Allspice berries or ground allspice — ½ tsp
Malt vinegar — 300 ml (1¼ UK cups / 1¼ US cups + 1 tbsp)
steps: Chop the mushrooms (the day before): Wipe the mushrooms and chop them quite finely. Put them in a non-reactive bowl (ceramic, glass or plastic, not metal).
Salt and leave overnight: Mix in the salt so it is all the way through — it will draw out a lot of moisture. Cover and leave on the side, not in the fridge, for 24 hours.

Into the pan: The next day there will be plenty of fluid. Put the mushrooms and all that salty mushroom water into a pan with the onion, garlic, pepper, allspice (the host uses ground; berries are traditional), cloves if using, a bay leaf, and the malt vinegar from the description.
Simmer: Mix, bring it up, and simmer about 40 minutes, partially covered, stirring now and then so nothing sticks. There will be a vinegary aroma and some evaporation.

Cool and strain: Turn it off, take out the bay leaf, and let it cool. Traditionally you would wring it in a cloth once cold. The host tried blending with a stick blender after about 10 minutes, then straining in a cloth, but then recommends not blending — it makes a paste that is harder to squeeze. Squeeze out the juice and bottle it.

Store: The host says this is a vegan, Worcestershire-style seasoning, mushroom-forward, salty and sour. Kept in the fridge it will last 3 months; it has a higher mushroom content and a shorter shelf life than commercial versions.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3eJd-pfNtRc

recipes.title: Oldest BRITISH CURRY Recipe Ever Written (1751 Revival)
ingredients: 5 chicken thighs, boneless and skinless cut into chunks
1 litre (1000ml / 4 US cups / 3½ UK cups) water
3 large onions, finely chopped (approx. 400g / 14 oz / 2 cups packed)
½ tsp ground black pepper (1g / ½ tsp)
Salt, to taste (optional) not in the recipe
steps: A 1751 curry: This follows Hannah Glasse's 1751 recipe in The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy — the earliest known curry recipe written in English. It will not taste like a modern curry: there is no chilli, tomato or garam masala, just turmeric, ginger and pepper. The original uses two small chickens, skinned and cut as for a fricassee, stewed in a quart of water; the host uses five boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into chunks, and 1 litre of water.
Stew the chicken: Bring the water to the boil first, then add the chicken and stew about 5 minutes. Strain off the liquor and set the chicken aside in a clean dish, as the original says.

Fry the onions and bloom the spices: Chop three large onions small and fry them in the butter until soft and golden. Mix the ground turmeric, ground ginger and black pepper, stir them into the onions and let them bloom a little.

Add the liquor and cook: Pour the reserved chicken cooking water back in. Return the chicken to the pan as well — the captions are clearer about the liquor than about the exact moment the meat goes back; watch that in the video rather than inventing it. Cook uncovered 30 minutes, stirring gently now and then so nothing catches, as some of the liquid evaporates.

Cream and lemon: Stir in the cream (double or heavy; the original says a quarter of a pint) and let it cook only a very short moment. Turn the flame completely off before you add any lemon juice, so it doesn't curdle. The recipe says the juice of two lemons; the host tasted after one because the lemons were large and stopped there. Salt is optional and is not in the original recipe.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K7m9e4U1Y6s

recipes.title: The ULTIMATE Grilled Chicken Combo: Cajun Heat + Alabama White Sauce
ingredients: Optional: a dash of hot sauce or cayenne pepper
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
A little oil for the pan
steps: Mix the spice blend: Combine a good couple of tablespoons of Cajun seasoning with the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and black pepper.

Make the white sauce: Whisk the mayonnaise (about ¾ cup was spoken in the video), horseradish, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, about ¼ tsp garlic powder, black pepper, sugar (optional), a little hot sauce and the lemon juice until smooth. The description says to chill it at least 30 minutes so the flavours meld.
Season the chicken: Pat the chicken dry. Stir the oil into the spice blend to make a sticky paste and rub it all over the chicken. Marinate 30 minutes (or overnight if you can).

Cook low and slow: Heat a little oil in a griddle pan over the lowest flame and lay in the chicken. Cook about 7–8 minutes until it turns opaque around the edges, then turn it, cook the other side, and stand the pieces on their sides to cook the edges; a little blackening adds flavour.
Check and rest: Cook until a thermometer reads 75°C in the thickest part, then move to a plate, cover with foil and rest about 5 minutes.
Serve: Slice, scatter with parsley and serve with the Alabama white sauce for dipping.

recipes.title: SUNDAY Pie - FRIDGE Pie - NO WASTE  All Flavour CLASSIC!
ingredients: 250–300 g (about 1½–2 cups) chopped leftover roast meat (beef, pork, lamb, chicken, or a mix)
1 cup (150 g) cooked veg (e.g., carrots, peas, cabbage, swede, sprouts)
200 ml (¾ UK cup / ⅞ US cup) thick leftover gravy (plus extra for serving)
Optional: a spoon of horseradish, mustard, or a few drops of Worcestershire sauce stirred into the gravy
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
Red onion and a stick of celery, diced
Leftover roast potatoes, carrots and cabbage (used as the cooked veg)
steps: Chop the leftovers: Cube or slice the leftover roast beef, dice the leftover carrots, flatten and dice the roast potatoes and chop the cabbage, then mix everything together in a bowl so it is evenly spread.
Sauté the aromatics: Dice the red onion and celery and sauté gently just to soften and release their flavour, then tip them into the bowl.
Make the filling: Stir in about a teaspoon of English mustard (optional), a splash of Worcestershire sauce, the leftover gravy, a pinch of dried thyme and pepper to taste.
Line the tin: Heat the oven to about 190°C. Roll out the shortcrust pastry on a little flour and line a lined 8½–9 in springform tin, leaving a lip at the top; patch any tears.
Fill and lid: Pack in all of the filling. Roll out a lid, egg-wash the rim, lay the lid on, trim the excess overhang and fold the edges together to seal.
Vent and bake: Cut a couple of air vents, egg-wash the top and bake about 35–45 minutes until golden brown and the pastry is cooked.
Rest and serve: Cool about 8 minutes, release from the tin and serve with veg, mash or chips and extra gravy or mustard.

recipes.title: Devon SPLITS   Brings the KID out in ME!
ingredients: 250 ml (8.5 fl oz / 1 UK cup / 1 US cup) double cream (or heavy whipping cream)
8 tsp (40 g) strawberry jam (or any preferred jam)
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the yeast into the warm milk and leave it about 5 minutes until it bubbles and froths. If it doesn't, add more yeast.

Make the dough: Mix 250 g bread flour and 250 g plain flour with the sugar and salt (all bread flour or all plain flour also works). Add the egg, the yeast and milk mixture, and the butter (melted or softened). Knead with a dough hook for about 8 minutes, or about 10 minutes by hand, into a slightly sticky dough.
First rise: With floured hands, tuck the dough into a ball and put it in a buttered bowl. Cover it (a plastic bag works) and leave until doubled in size.

Shape: Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and divide it into about eight, weighing the pieces if you like. Tuck each piece into a roll and put them on a parchment-lined tray. Cover and leave to rise again.
Bake: Bake at 190°C for about 18–22 minutes until golden. You can brush them with milk before baking; the host doesn't.
Butter: About a minute after they come out, brush the tops with melted butter for a soft, darker top (or use a sugar glaze). Leave them to cool.
Whip the cream: Whip the cream with a little icing sugar until thick.
Fill: Cut each bun on a diagonal from the top, without going all the way through. Spread jam generously inside on both sides so it is fully coated, then fill with plenty of cream.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S8AW0RwXrn8
Uploaded 2025-05-15.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Bake buns for 18–22 minutes until golden.

recipes.title: BAKED for 45 Minutes… and the YOLKS Are Still SOFT!
ingredients: Dried chives or onion powder — 1½ tsp
Oil — 1 tsp (5 g / 5 ml), for frying the onion
Fresh or panko breadcrumbs — 100 g (3.5 oz)
Unsalted butter, melted — 30 g (2 tbsp / 1 oz)
steps: Heat the oven and blind-bake the pastry: The host uses an 8½ or nearly 9 inch springform tin. Line it with shortcrust pastry (500 g in the description) and blind-bake at 180°C for about 10 minutes, then let it stand a minute.

Soft-boil the eggs: The host aims for about 4–5 minutes so the yolks will be jammy in the pie, not fully runny. The description says to boil exactly 6 minutes. Transfer them to ice-cold water, then peel carefully — they are delicate.

Cook the onion and make the topping: Cook the finely chopped onion in a little oil (and the host also melts butter in the pan). Mix breadcrumbs with melted butter, dried parsley, and garlic powder, salt and pepper if you are using them — this stands in for the fried coating on a Scotch egg.

Fill: Season the sausage meat (the description has English mustard, dried parsley, dried chives or onion powder, salt and pepper). Put a layer of sausage meat in the pastry, nestle the eggs in, and cover with the rest of the sausage meat. The host puts the cooked onion in this top layer, under the breadcrumbs, for flavour around the eggs. Mark or remember where the eggs sit so you can slice through them later.

Top and bake: Spread on the buttered breadcrumb topping. Bake about 40 minutes (the description says 40–45 minutes) at 180°C. The host mentions an internal temperature of 70°C, or 71°C if you are in America, for the sausage.
Rest and slice: Leave it about 8 minutes, then cut straight through an egg. The host was aiming for jammy, not hard-boiled, yolks after the long bake.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1cXPI4UPyoA
Uploaded 2025-05-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Boil exactly 6 minutes. Transfer to ice water; Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake for 40–45 minutes; 70°C (160°F) — UK/European standard; 71°C (160°F) — USDA recommendation for ground pork or sausage.

recipes.title: Old Fashioned Potato & Bacon Soup
ingredients: Salt, pepper, thyme to taste (approx. 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1/2 tsp dried thyme)
Green onions & shredded cheddar cheese for garnish (about 50g cheddar | 1/2 cup)
steps: Cook the bacon: Chop the streaky bacon (scissors are fine). Start it in a little butter or oil and render the fat until it has some colour — the host wants visible pieces, not only tiny crisp bits. Take it out and keep some for the top; you can cook it in the fat first and add butter afterwards if you prefer.

Onion, garlic and potatoes: In the same pan, cook the diced onion (any colour) and optional minced garlic until the rawness has gone. Add the diced potatoes (about 800 g / 4 large) and start them off, then pour in the stock — chicken or vegetable, from a cube is fine, but go easy on extra salt because stock cubes are salty. Add black pepper and dried thyme if you like.

Simmer: Simmer uncovered about 15–20 minutes so some liquid can evaporate before the cream goes in (or lid on if you prefer). Test a potato with a fork. Mash a few of the potatoes in the pan with a fork or masher to thicken it naturally. You can blend it if you want it completely smooth, but the host doesn't.

Thicken and finish: If you want it thicker, stir in a cornflour slurry (the host uses a tablespoon of cornflour mixed with water — the water amount is not stated) and cook a little longer, about an extra 5 minutes. Stir in the cream or milk (1 cup in the description), then half of the bacon, saving the rest for garnish.
Serve: Ladle it up with more bacon, a little shredded cheddar, chopped green onion and a bit of pepper. The host says it freezes well.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7_evEutaQzE

recipes.title: HAPPY Waitress The BEST Diner Style GRILLED Cheese with BACON and Tomato
ingredients: 4 slices of cheddar cheese (or American cheese)
2 tbsp (28 g) mayonnaise and butter 1 tbsp each
steps: Prep: Grill the bacon until crisp, slice the tomato, and mix the mayonnaise and butter together.
Spread: Spread the mayo-butter all the way to the edges of the outsides of thick-sliced bread.

Build: On the unspread side, layer American cheese, extra cheddar (optional), plenty of bacon (let some hang out the sides), tomato slices and a bit more cheddar, then top with the second slice, mayo-butter side out.

Start in a cold pan: Put the sandwiches in a completely cold pan, cover with a lid set slightly ajar to let steam out, and turn the flame on very low. Cook slowly so the bread toasts while the cheese starts to melt.
Flip and crisp: When the underside is golden and the cheese is melting, flip it, take the lid off and toast the other side as brown as you like.
Serve: Cut and serve, with a little ketchup if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ps_KMvC3ehE

recipes.title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken  – Family Favourite One Tray Meal!
ingredients: ½ cup | 50 g grated Parmesan cheese
¼ tsp | 0.5 g red pepper flakes (optional)
½ cup | 60 g chopped sun-dried tomatoes, drained
1 red or yellow bell pepper, sliced
Optional: pinch of oregano or smoked paprika
steps: Prep: Season the bone-in chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Strip the spinach leaves, cut the onion, slice the courgette into thick pieces (it turns watery when cooked) and slice or dice the peppers. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).

Sear the chicken: Heat some of the oil from the sun-dried tomato jar in a pan and sear the chicken skin side first, then turn it. It doesn't need to cook through, and crowding the pan is fine. Move it to the baking tray.

Stir fry the veg: In the same pan, quickly fry the garlic, onion and peppers with a little salt and the Italian herbs (or oregano), keeping the courgette back. Turn off the flame and put the veg in the tray alongside the chicken.

Make the sauce: Over a gentle heat, cook a heaped tablespoon of tomato paste with a little butter to take out its sourness. Stir in the smoked paprika and chilli flakes to bloom, then add the stock, at least a cup of cream and the Parmesan.
Add the spinach: As soon as the sauce starts to bubble, stir in the spinach to wilt, then turn off the flame.

Assemble and bake: Pour the sauce into the tray around the chicken, keeping the chicken sitting above it. Add the sun-dried tomatoes, lay the courgette on top and bake for about 35–40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (75°C/165°F).
Serve: Rest about 10 minutes, then serve with potatoes, mash, rice or crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gKsaDK55OAs
Uploaded 2025-05-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: To 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F; uncovered for 35–40 minutes, until chicken is cooked through (75°C / 165°F internal temp) and sauce is bubbling.

recipes.title: NOT Just EGG - SMOOTH Pourable SCRAMBLES like a real egg!
ingredients: Split mung beans, soaked overnight — 300 g
Fresh water — 720 ml | 3 UK cups | 3 US cups
Canola oil (or avocado/neutral) — 90 ml | 6 tbsp | ¼ UK cup + 2 tbsp
Psyllium husk powder — 1.5 g | ½ tsp
steps: Soak the mung beans: Leave the split mung beans in water overnight, then rinse them three or four times until the yellow water runs clear.

Blend everything: Put the fresh water in a blender, then add the drained mung beans, cornstarch, turmeric, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, baking powder, onion powder, canola oil, psyllium husk, the black salt (the only salt used) and about a tablespoon of carrot juice for colour. Blend until completely smooth.
Rest: Leave the mixture for about 20 minutes so the cornstarch and psyllium husk can thicken it.

Scramble: Warm a small pan as you would for eggs, pour in about two ladles of the mix and turn the heat down so it sets. Leave it to set like an omelette at first, then move it about gently, letting it set a little before turning so it doesn't turn stodgy. Cook on low until it comes together like scrambled egg, browning it lightly if you like, and serve on toast.

Omelette: Heat a little butter or oil in the pan and add about one and a half ladles. Cook low and slow like a flatbread until it releases from the pan and the top sets and turns matte (a lid would speed this up). Brown the underside, turn it, colour the other side and fold. Filling it with cheese and tomato before folding while it is still too soft makes it break up, so let it set first.
Store: Keep any leftover mix in the fridge.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Py7LYnhwY5c
Uploaded 2025-05-10.

recipes.title: OLDEST FLATBREAD Yorkshire HAVERCAKE
ingredients: 170 g fine oatmeal (1½ UK cups / 1¾ US cups)
90 g plain flour (¾ UK cup / ¾ US cup)
250 ml milk (1 UK cup / 1 US cup)
250 ml water (1 UK cup / 1 US cup) more as needed
Butter or oil, for greasing the griddle
steps: Mix the batter: The host blends rolled oats, leaving a bit of texture (the description lists 170 g fine oatmeal). Mix with the plain flour, salt, and fast-acting yeast (7 g / 2 tsp in the description). Add the milk and water (250 ml of each, and more water as needed) to a pourable batter — the oats will soak some of the liquid as it stands.
Rest: Cover and leave about an hour so the yeast can bubble (traditionally the batter was left overnight and went a little sour; the host doesn't do that here).

Cook on a griddle: Grease a griddle or pan with butter, lard, dripping or oil. Pour the batter — it should be pourable, not a thick stodge. If it is too thick, thin it with a little more water. A thinner mix, the host says, needs to be cooked low and slow to set; he likes it a little thicker. When it has set on one side, flip it (traditionally with a big knife) and cook the other side until pliable.
Serve: Eat warm, with butter, honey, cheese, or rolled around a filling — whatever you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6rNAao9PRfs
Uploaded 2025-05-09.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: KATSU Chicken BITES with Japanese Curry Sauce
ingredients: Japanese curry roux: 100g (½ a standard 200g box, or 4 cubes)
Oil for frying (about 500ml for shallow fry)
Cooked Japanese rice: 300g uncooked (makes about 3-4 portions) I had Thai rice.
steps: Blanch the chicken: Cube the chicken breast (500 g in the description), and blanch it in boiling water about 5 minutes. Lift the chicken out and keep that cooking water — the host uses it to make the curry.

Start the curry: In a little oil, cook the chopped onion just to take the rawness out. Add the carrot, cut on an angle in a Japanese style, and the cubed potato. The host notes that carrots take a little longer, and that you don't strictly have to pre-fry the veg because everything will boil, but a little cooking helps. Pour in the reserved blanching water (the description lists 750 ml) and bring it up to the boil.

Curry roux: Stir in the Japanese curry blocks or powder — 100 g, about half a standard 200 g box, or 4 cubes. You can also make a curry with powder and flour if you prefer. Cook it uncovered so it thickens into a sauce. With about 5 minutes to go, turn it down and keep it warm while you fry the chicken.

Bread and fry: Season the blanched chicken with salt and pepper, then coat it in plain flour, beaten egg and panko breadcrumbs. Because it is already blanched, you can fairly shallow-fry it (the description allows about 500 ml oil) until the crumbs are crisp and golden.
Serve: Spoon the curry, with the carrots and potatoes, over cooked Japanese rice (the host used Thai rice) and the katsu bites.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KPMGebxLcus
Uploaded 2025-05-08.

recipes.title: TRADITIONAL  Yorkshire Pikelets – Old Fashioned GRIDDLE CRUMPETS
ingredients: 250 g (1½ UK cups / 2 US cups) strong white bread flour – All-purpose/plain flour works
300 ml (10 fl oz / 1¼ UK cups / 1¼ US cups + 1 tbsp) warm water
75 ml (2½ fl oz / 5 tbsp / ¼ UK cup / ¼ US cup + 1 tsp) warm milk
½ tsp (2.5 g) baking powder (optional for extra lift before cooking)
A little butter or oil for greasing the griddle/pan

Drop tablespoons of batter onto the griddle — about 3 to 4 inches (8–10 cm) wide. Cook for about 2–3 minutes, until bubbles form on the surface and the top starts to set. Flip and cook another 1–2 minutes until golden.
steps: Make the batter: Mix the strong white bread flour (plain flour is fine too) with the caster sugar, salt and dried yeast. You can bloom the yeast in the warm milk or water first if you like, or just mix it all together. Add the warm water and warm milk to make a batter thicker than pancake batter but thinner than crumpet batter — add a little more flour or water if you need to.
Rest: Leave it about 45 minutes to an hour, depending on how warm the room is, until it has come up.

Optional baking powder: This is a modern touch to take up slack in the batter. The host cooks one or two pikelets first without it, then stirs in baking powder — about ¼ teaspoon for a test, or about ½ teaspoon for the full mix in the description — for just 5–10 seconds before cooking the rest. You can decide which you prefer.

Cook on a griddle: Grease a griddle or non-stick pan with a little butter or oil and keep the heat nice and slow. Drop tablespoons of batter, about 3 to 4 inches (8–10 cm) wide. Cook about 2–3 minutes until bubbles form and the top starts to set, then flip and cook another 1–2 minutes until golden. Control the heat so they cook through without burning.
Serve: Eat them with butter and jam, honey, golden syrup or, if you're proper Yorkshire, dripping. They can also be cooled and eaten later.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LmE3HjvHJcQ
Uploaded 2025-05-07.

recipes.title: COSORI TwinFry Air Fryer - Chicken and Broccoli ALFREDO Stuffed JACKET Potatoes
ingredients: 2-4 large baking potatoes (about 250g / 9 oz each) I used 2 @ 400g each
1 cup (240 ml / 240 g / 8.5 oz) whole milk (UK: 250 ml / g)
½ cup (120 ml / 120 g / 4.2 oz) double/heavy cream
½ cup (40 g / 1.4 oz) grated Parmesan cheese
1 cup (150 g / 5.3 oz) cooked chicken, shredded or diced
1 cup (90 g / 3.2 oz) cooked broccoli, finely chopped
¼ tsp (1.25 ml / 1.25 g) salt (adjust to taste)
¼ tsp (1.25 ml / 1.25 g) black pepper
¼ tsp (1.25 ml / 1.25 g) garlic powder (optional)
½ cup (50 g / 1.8 oz) grated mozzarella or cheddar cheese
Preheat your Cosori air fryer to 200°C (390°F).
Cook for 40–45 minutes, no foil, until crisp outside and soft inside. (Flip after 25 mins if desired.
Return stuffed potatoes to the air fryer at 190°C (380°F) for 5–8 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
steps: Cook the jackets: Prick 2–4 large baking potatoes all over, rub with olive oil and a pinch of salt, and cook them without foil until the skins are crisp and the insides are soft. In an air fryer, preheat to 200°C (390°F) and cook 40–45 minutes, flipping after 25 minutes if you like. The host notes this is roughly half the oven time; you can bake them in a regular oven instead — watch the video rather than inventing an oven time. For a softer skin, wrap the cooked potatoes in foil for about 5 minutes after they come out.

Alfredo sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook the rawness out, then add the milk, stirring so there are no lumps, and the cream. Season with black pepper and optional garlic powder — the host skips extra salt at this stage because of the Parmesan. Stir in the grated Parmesan until you have a thick sauce.
Filling: Stir the cooked shredded or diced chicken and the cooked, finely chopped broccoli into the sauce and let the chicken warm through.
Stuff: Cut the potatoes, scoop some of the flesh out and stir it into the Alfredo, then pack the filling back into the shells. Top with grated mozzarella or cheddar if you like.

Finish: Return the stuffed potatoes to the air fryer at 190°C (380°F) for 5–8 minutes (or the oven) until the cheese is bubbly and golden. Use a tray if you don't want cheese dripping into the basket.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O0kSQ-ig8e0
Uploaded 2025-05-06.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your Cosori air fryer to 200°C (390°F); Cook for 40–45 minutes, no foil, until crisp outside and soft inside. (Flip after 25 mins if desired; Return stuffed potatoes to the air fryer at 190°C (380°F) for 5–8 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.

recipes.title: Yorkshire Teacakes – Soft, Fruity & Made for Butter
ingredients: 250 g bread flour 250 g All-purpose/plain flour (3¼ UK cups / 4 US cups)
1 tsp (2.5 g) ground mixed spice (or use ½ tsp cinnamon + ½ tsp allspice)
100 g mixed dried fruit (raisins, currants, sultanas)
Optional: extra flour for shaping and 1 tbsp milk for brushing
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the yeast into the warm milk and leave it a couple of minutes until it starts to froth.

Mix the dough: In a stand mixer bowl (or by hand), combine 250 g plain flour and 250 g bread flour with the salt, sugar, dried fruit and mixed spice, and stir the dry ingredients together. Add the yeasted milk, egg and melted butter and knead with the dough hook into a dough that is slightly sticky but not wet.
First rise: With lightly floured hands, fold the dough over, put it in a lightly buttered bowl and cover it (a plastic bag works) until doubled in size, about 1 hour to 1 hour 10 minutes.
Shape: Knock the dough back and divide it into about eight pieces, weighing them if you like. Shape each into a ball and put them on a lined tray. It doesn't matter if they end up touching.
Second rise: Cover again and leave for about 40 minutes. You can brush them with milk at this point; the host doesn't.
Bake: Bake at 190°C for up to about 15 minutes, until golden. The description gives 18–22 minutes, until golden on top and hollow-sounding underneath.

Butter and cool: Straight from the oven, brush the tops with melted butter for a soft sheen (or use a sugar glaze if you prefer). Leave them 5 minutes, then cool on a rack. Serve split and toasted with butter or raspberry jam.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RZaEbzECmo8
Uploaded 2025-05-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 190°C (375°F); bake for 18–22 minutes until golden brown on top and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: GREEK-Style LEMON Chicken Thighs with Roast Potatoes
ingredients: 2 tbsp (30 ml) fresh lemon juice (about ½ lemon)
1 tbsp (15 g) Dijon mustard (optional, adds depth)
½ tsp (0.5 g) dried thyme or rosemary
4–6 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 1.2 kg / 2.5 lb)
Salt & pepper to season the skin
750 g (1.6 lb) potatoes (e.g. Maris Piper or Yukon Gold)
Drizzle of olive oil for roasting
½ tsp dried thyme or a few sprigs fresh
Optional: ½ tsp (2.5 ml) honey or a squeeze of lemon
Optional: 1 tsp (3 g) cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp (15 ml) cold water
Optional: small knob of butter or extra lemon juice to finish
steps: Parboil the potatoes: Peel and cube the potatoes, put them in cold salted water, bring to the boil and boil 8 minutes. Drain, return them to the hot pan for a moment to dry, and shake them to rough up the edges.

Make the marinade: Mix the minced garlic, lemon zest and juice, about a tablespoon of red wine vinegar, the Dijon, olive oil, oregano, thyme, salt and pepper. Add a little sugar if it's too sour for you.

Marinate the chicken: Pat the thighs dry, loosen the skin and rub a little marinade underneath and on the underside, keeping the skin dry so it crisps. Season the skin with salt and pepper and leave about 30 minutes. Keep the rest of the marinade for the sauce.
Season the carrots: Toss the baby carrots with olive oil, a pinch of salt and thyme.

Roast: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Put a little oil in a roasting tray, spread the potatoes over it (with any leftover garlic trimmings), and sit the chicken on top so its juices baste the potatoes. Roast about 20 minutes.
Add the carrots: Tuck the carrots in around the edges and roast about 35 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through.

Make the lemon sauce: Mix the remaining marinade with the chicken stock, bring it to the boil in a pan and simmer about a minute. Thicken lightly with the cornflour slurry (loosen with more stock if it gets too thick), then finish with a knob of butter. Add a little sugar if it's too sour.

Finish the potatoes: Lift out the chicken, stir the potatoes and carrots and roast about 8 minutes more to colour them (adding lemon wedges if you like). Cover the chicken loosely with foil meanwhile.
Serve: Plate the potatoes, carrots and chicken and spoon over the lemon sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_e2GbqbvLx0
Uploaded 2025-05-04.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: TOMATO Soup - ULTIMATE crispy GRILLED Cheese - PERFECT Combo
ingredients: Grilled cheese (per sandwich, from the description):
2–3 slices or grated cheddar, mozzarella, or cheese of choice
Caramelised onions (from the video; amounts not stated):
Boiling water, a little butter and oil
A small pinch each of salt and sugar
Tomato soup (from the video; amounts not stated):
A pinch of Italian herbs (or basil/oregano)
A good heap of tomato purée
Tinned whole tomatoes with their juice
steps: Quick caramelised onions: Put the sliced onions in a pan with some boiling water, a little butter and oil, a pinch of salt and a pinch of sugar. Cover and boil about 12 minutes until soft. Remove the lid and let the water evaporate so the butter and oil take over, then fry, stirring often, until caramelised to your liking. Set aside.
Soup base: Gently cook the diced onion and garlic in oil and butter with salt and pepper until the rawness is gone, then add a pinch of Italian herbs.
Cook the purée: Stir in a good heap of tomato purée and cook it briefly without burning to take off the sourness, then add a little sugar.
Simmer: Add the vegetable stock (or water) and the tinned whole tomatoes with their juice, snipping them up with scissors in the pan. Simmer about 6–7 minutes.

Blend and finish: Turn off the heat and blend to your liking (cook it down longer for a thicker soup). Over a low flame or off the heat, stir in a couple of tablespoons of cream. If you're storing the soup, add the cream when reheating.

Build the sandwiches: Spread the mayonnaise and butter on the outside of the bread right to the edges. Mix the cheddar and mozzarella, and layer cheese, caramelised onions and more cheese between the slices.
Toast from cold: Put the sandwiches in a completely cold pan, cover with a lid and cook on the lowest flame so the bottom toasts as the cheese melts. Flip, cover again and toast the other side.
Serve: Serve the grilled cheese with the tomato soup and a little parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wNHXU6q0S_w
Uploaded 2025-05-03.

recipes.title: Easy Bacon Floodies – Old School Northern British Comfort Food
ingredients: Mashed potato (plain, not buttery) — 250 g | 9 oz
Salt — ½ tsp (less if your mash is salted)
Milk — 60 ml | 2 fl oz | ¼ UK/US cup | 4 tbsp (add more if needed)
Cooked streaky bacon, chopped — 120 g | 4 oz
Butter, lard, or oil — for frying
steps: Two versions: The host makes bacon floodies two ways: with plain mashed potato (no butter or milk in the mash — leftovers are fine) and with raw grated potato. For the grated version, salt the potato, leave it about 5 minutes, then wring it out well. The description lists 250 g mashed potato for 8–10 floodies.

Make a stodgy batter: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt (less if the mash is already salted) and black pepper with the egg and the milk (60 ml in the description, plus more if you want it thinner). Some people throw everything in together; the host makes the batter first and then folds in the potato and the chopped cooked streaky bacon (120 g in the description).

Fry the bacon fat if you need it: The host cooks the bacon first, chops it with scissors, and likes to fry the floodies in a little of that fat. Butter, lard or oil also work. You don't really need extra oil if you have bacon fat.

Cook low and slow: Spoon the mix into the pan — you can use a ring if you want a tidy shape. Fry on a low heat about 3–5 minutes, then turn (and turn again if you need to) so the flour and potato cook all the way through. Don't rush them.
Serve: They're good with brown sauce or ketchup, or topped with a fried egg, or with cheese melted under the grill. You can also reheat them in the microwave.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JYnyCuJV9UQ
Uploaded 2025-05-02.

recipes.title: CARROT Cake Cookies - The ONLY WAY to Eat Carrot Cake Without a Fork!
ingredients: 4 tbsp (60ml) melted coconut oil or neutral oil
Optional: 2 tbsp (16g) extra almond flour if dough feels sticky
225g (8 oz) full-fat cream cheese (cold but soft enough to beat)
Optional: 1 tbsp milk powder or 1 tsp cornstarch for added firmness
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: In a bowl, stir together the rolled oats, raisins, walnuts, the raising agent (the host says baking powder; the description lists baking soda), salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, almond flour and grated carrot until evenly mixed, so the carrot doesn't clump.

Add the wet ingredients: Add a couple of teaspoons of vanilla, the coconut oil and the weighed maple syrup, and stir well. There's no egg; the carrots release moisture as they bake. If you can't get maple syrup, use honey with 1 tsp of molasses or black treacle stirred in.

Rest: Leave the mix about 15 minutes so the oats absorb the moisture. Only then, if it is still too wet, add a couple of tablespoons of almond flour; if it is too dry, add a tablespoon or two of milk or water.

Make the filling: Squash the cold cream cheese and butter together with a spatula, then beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth. A tablespoon of milk powder or about a teaspoon of cornflour will firm it up. Cover and chill so it stays firm.
Shape: Preheat the oven to about 175°C and line a tray with parchment. Roll the dough into balls of about 30–32 g, space them out on the tray and flatten them slightly.
Bake: Bake about 12–15 minutes, until the tops are a little crisp but the middles are still soft. Leave them on the tray a minute, then cool completely on a rack.
Sandwich and set: Spread or pipe the cream cheese filling onto half the cookies and top with the rest. Chill in a box for about an hour so the filling sets.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T76K7cm04a8
Uploaded 2025-05-01.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 350°F (175°C); Bake: 13–15 minutes until golden at the edges.

recipes.title: Cauliflower Steak Bake with Spinach Ricotta and Marinara Sauce — This really Stacks up!
ingredients: 1 large head cauliflower, cut into 5–6 thick steaks (¾–1 inch)
1 cup cooked spinach, drained and finely chopped
1½ cups | 360 ml 1½ US cups | 1⅓ UK cups passata
1 tsp | 5 ml dried oregano or basil if no Italain herbs
Pinch of sugar to balance the acidity
½ tsp dried oregano or Italian seasoning
steps: Heat the oven: Put it on about 220°C to start; it will be turned down to 180°C later.

Roast the cauliflower: Cut a large head into thick steaks (the description says 5–6 steaks, ¾–1 inch) and keep the leftover bits for the layers. Rub with a little olive oil, salt and pepper, and bake about 25 minutes (the description says 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway). It only needs to take some colour; it will go into the bake.

Blanch the spinach: Wash and roughly chop the spinach. In a pan with a lid, blanch it in a little boiling water from the kettle for about a minute, no longer (or steam it if you prefer). Drain and let it cool, then chop again if you want.
Make a quick marinara: Cook a couple of cloves of garlic in a little olive oil, then add the passata with Italian herbs (or oregano or basil), salt, pepper and a little sugar to taste.

Spinach-ricotta and crumb: Stir the cooled spinach through the ricotta and add a little nutmeg. For the topping, mix breadcrumbs (panko in the description) with Parmesan (from the description), oregano or Italian seasoning, and garlic powder if you are using it. The host also mentions maybe a little mozzarella over the top, which is not listed in the description — use it only if you want, and don't invent an amount.

Layer in an 8 × 8 × 2 inch dish: Turn the oven down to 180°C. Sauce in the bottom, then cauliflower, then spinach-ricotta (the host aims for about two layers of that), more marinara, more cauliflower. Finish with the Parmesan breadcrumb topping and a little mozzarella if using. The dish may bubble over, so stand it on a tray.

Bake: Cover with foil (oiled if you wish) for about 15 minutes, then take the foil off and bake about another 20 minutes until bubbling and golden on top. Let it cool about 10 minutes before slicing, like a lasagna.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1DqVIAL9ET0
Uploaded 2025-04-30.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 220°C (425°F); Roast for 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway; Bake: Preheat the oven to 180°c (350°f); Bake covered for 15 minutes, then uncover and continue baking for an additional 20 minutes until bubbling and golden on top.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Strawberry Banana BREAD – A Fruity Twist on a Classic Favourite
ingredients: 115g (½ cup) unsalted butter, melted (or vegetable oil)
150g (¾ cup) granulated sugar or brown sugar
1 tbsp all-purpose flour (for coating strawberries, prevents sinking)
Extra sliced strawberries for the top
1 tbsp coarse sugar for a crunchy topping
steps: Mash the bananas: Mash the ripe bananas with a fork or beater and leave them a while. Left an hour or more they darken, which gives a darker loaf; the host leaves them about 10 minutes.
Prepare: Preheat the oven to about 175–180°C and line a 2 lb (9×5-inch) loaf tin.
Beat the eggs and sugar: Beat the eggs with the sugar until creamy and frothy. Mix in the vanilla, yogurt (or buttermilk), melted butter and mashed banana.
Coat the strawberries: Toss the diced strawberries with a tablespoon of flour so they don't sink.
Combine: Mix the flour with the salt, baking soda, baking powder and cinnamon, then stir it into the wet mixture until combined. Fold in the strawberries.
Fill and decorate: Pour the batter into the middle of the tin (smoothing it is optional) and arrange sliced strawberries on top, with coarse sugar if you like.
Bake: Bake about 50–60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Leave 10 minutes in the tin, then cool completely on a rack before slicing. Serve with butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_V-W9xiNKik
Uploaded 2025-04-29.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 175°C (350°F). Grease and line a 9x5 inch (23x13 cm) loaf tin with parchment paper; Bake for 50–60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

recipes.title: How To Make PERFECT Pulled BEEF every time! Foolproof!
ingredients: Beef chuck or brisket — 1 kg | 2.2 lbs | about 4 UK cups | 4¼ US cups (cut into large chunks)
Black pepper — ½ tsp | 2.5 g | 2.5 ml
Beef stock or broth — 250 ml | 250 g | 1 UK cup | 1.06 US cups
Optional: Worcestershire sauce — 1 tbsp | 15 ml | 15 g for extra depth
Natural release for 10–15 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure.
steps: Season and sear: Season the beef (any cut; chuck or brisket in large chunks) with salt and pepper. Sear it all over in hot oil, just for colour, not to cook it through, then set it aside on a tray.
Onions and garlic: Without cleaning the pan, add a touch more oil and cook the onion and garlic briefly, scraping up the bits from the bottom. Add some pepper.

Build the gravy: Stir in about 2 tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce (or soy sauce) and about 2 tablespoons of tomato paste, and cook briefly to remove the tomato's sourness. Stir in the beef stock or gravy (gravy powder, granules or stock cubes all work) to deglaze the pan.

Pressure cook: Pour the onion gravy into the Instant Pot liner, add the beef and its juices (it doesn't need to be submerged) and pressure cook on normal/high for 60 minutes. Let it release naturally for about 10–15 minutes, then release the rest. Without an Instant Pot, simmer on the stove for about 3 hours until it falls apart.
Pull: Lift the beef out and shred it with two forks, as fine or chunky as you like. Mix in a little of the cooking liquid to keep it moist.

Gravy and storage: Thicken the leftover liquid in a pan with a little cornflour for gravy. The beef freezes well in some of its gravy; reheat in the microwave for about a minute and serve in crusty bread.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nmhQskYtyDA
Uploaded 2025-04-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: High Pressure for 60 minutes; Natural release for 10–15 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure.

recipes.title: Ultimate Chicken Cordon Bleu Rolls – Crispy, Juicy & Garlic Loaded!
ingredients: 2–4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, depending on size
Salt and black pepper, to taste
½ tsp paprika (optional, for extra colour)
steps: Make the filling: Mix the softened cream cheese and softened unsalted butter with the minced garlic, chopped parsley, optional onion powder, salt and a little pepper. If you use salted butter, skip the added salt.

Prep the chicken: Butterfly 2–4 boneless chicken breasts, depending on size, and pound them out so they will roll. Season with a little salt and pepper — the host seasons one side before pounding, not both sides.

Fill, roll and freeze: Spread some of the garlic filling on the chicken, add a slice of packet ham, and roll it up. No toothpicks — wrap it tightly in cling film, twisting both ends, and freeze until solid so it holds its shape for breading.

Bread: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Set up flour, beaten eggs mixed with a couple of tablespoons of cornflour (the mixture needs to be sticky because the frozen rolls will start to give off moisture), and breadcrumbs seasoned with a little salt and paprika (the host doesn't usually season breadcrumbs, but does here because the chicken is already frozen). Coat flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.

Fry and bake: Heat the oil and shallow-fry the rolls just until you have a golden coating — the host talks about about a minute, turning them around — then transfer to a tray and bake about 25 minutes, or until the middle reaches 75°C (165°F).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ie3wyU-0JZo
Uploaded 2025-04-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 180°c (350°f); Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked (internal temperature reaches 75°c/165°f).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Paneer Takeaway Style
ingredients: Self-raising flour — 100g / ¾ cup (UK & US) / 7 tbsp
Water — 100 ml / 7 tbsp / just under ½ UK cup / ⅓ US cup (adjust for thick, coating batter)
For the Sweet and Sour Sauce:
White vinegar — 2 tbsp / 30 ml / 1 UK tbsp + 1 US tbsp
Pineapple juice — 2 tbsp / 30 ml (optional but great)
Water — 4 tbsp / 60 ml / ¼ UK cup / ¼ US cup
Cornflour (cornstarch) — 1 tbsp / 8g mixed with 2 tbsp / 30 ml water (for thickening)
Bell peppers — ½ red, ½ green, cut into chunks
steps: Make the sauce: Stir together the ketchup, light soy sauce, a couple of tablespoons of sugar, about 2 tablespoons of white vinegar, optional pineapple juice from the tin, and the water (4 tbsp in the description). Mix a cornflour slurry (1 tbsp cornflour with 2 tbsp water) and keep it ready to thicken the sauce later.
Batter the paneer: Mix the self-raising flour, cornflour, salt and white pepper, then add water (about 100 ml, adjusted) until you have a thick coating batter. Cube the paneer (250 g) and coat it.
Fry: Deep-fry the paneer until golden. You can take it out and fry it a second time if you want it extra crisp.

Vegetables and finish: In a pan, cook the chunked onion and red and green peppers just enough to take the rawness off — keep some crunch. Add optional pineapple chunks. Pour in the sauce, thicken with the slurry (the longer it cooks, the thicker it gets), and toss the fried paneer through so there is enough sauce to coat. Serve with fried rice or noodles.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OkNfkL0Vfvo
Uploaded 2025-04-25.

recipes.title: Cabbage STEAK  Lasagna – A CHEESY, Hearty Twist!  None of the Rolling!
ingredients: 1 large green cabbage (1.2 kg / 2.6 lbs), sliced into 1 cm (½ inch) thick rounds
1 tsp (5 ml / 5g) dried oregano (optional if no Italian herbs)
1 tsp (5 ml / 5g) dried basil (optional if no Italian herbs)
500 ml (17 fl oz) passata (2 US cups / ~2 UK cups)
1 tsp (5 ml / 5g) Dijon or English mustard
Optional: 100g (3.5 oz) ricotta or cottage cheese
steps: Bake the cabbage first: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Slice a large green cabbage into 1 cm (½ inch) rounds, like steaks, toss or brush with olive oil, salt and pepper, and bake 10–15 minutes (the host also says 15–20), turning once, so they start to soften.

Meat sauce: In olive oil, cook the chopped onion and minced garlic, then the minced beef (chicken or pork also work) until browned. Season with Italian herbs (or oregano and basil), optional smoked paprika, about a teaspoon of lightly crushed caraway seeds, Worcestershire sauce, tomato purée, the passata, mustard (Dijon or English — it's on the list; if the captions don't name it as it goes in, follow the video), optional sugar, and salt and pepper. Cook about 10 minutes uncovered on a lower flame so it thickens a little, stirring so it doesn't catch.

Layer: In a tray (it can bubble over, so use a tray), layer cabbage, meat sauce, and cheese — mozzarella, Parmesan, and optional ricotta or cottage cheese — like a lasagna, using up all the cabbage. Don't worry if some slices break.

Bake: Cover loosely with foil (oil the underside if you worry about sticking) and bake 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 15–20 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest at least 10 minutes before you cut it.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OI_29vHqfMw
Uploaded 2025-04-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 200°C (400°F).

recipes.title: DATE & Walnut OATMEAL Bars   - Hold the cake!! - No flour, no sugar!
ingredients: Soft pitted dates (e.g. Medjool), packed — 1 cup (160 g)
Milk, dairy or non-dairy — 1 cup (240 ml)
Melted coconut oil or butter — 2 tbsp (30 ml)
Unsweetened applesauce or mashed banana — 2 tbsp (30 g) (optional, for moisture)
Maple syrup or honey — 2 tbsp (30 ml)
Butter or coconut oil — 1 tsp (5 g) (optional, for shine)
steps: Soak the dates: Put the packed soft pitted dates (1 cup / 160 g) in hot or boiling water (¾ cup / 180 ml in the description) and leave about 10 minutes, then mash with a fork — lumps are fine.

Mix: Stir in the wet ingredients: the eggs, milk, vanilla, a couple of tablespoons of melted coconut oil or butter, and mashed banana or unsweetened applesauce if you are using them for moisture. Add the dry: rolled oats, cinnamon, baking powder, salt and chopped walnuts. Leave about 10 minutes so the oats can soak up the moisture.
Bake: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 8×8 inch (20×20 cm) dish (the host also used a 10×7). Spread in the mix and bake 30–35 minutes until golden and set in the centre.

Glaze: While it bakes, mix maple syrup or honey with a little coconut oil or butter, vanilla and a pinch of cinnamon if you like. Brush the glaze over the hot bars, then cool about 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B14W8qdJUBs
Uploaded 2025-04-23.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 8x8-inch (20x20cm) baking dish with parchment paper; bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and set in the centre.

recipes.title: Chunky, Cheesy, and 100% Real – The Ultimate Ham & Veggie Chowder / Soup – No Cans, Just Comfort!
ingredients: 30g plain flour (¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup)
120g grated cheddar cheese (1 UK cup | 1 US cup)
steps: Prep: Cube the ham (Canadian bacon was used here), potatoes, carrots and onion as big or small as you like.

Soften the veg: Heat the butter (with a little oil if you like) over a low flame. Cook the carrots first because they take longer, then add the onion and cook out its rawness. Season with black pepper but no salt, because the stock is salty.
Make the roux: Stir in the flour with the garlic powder and cook it in the butter to remove the raw flour taste, without letting it go lumpy.
Simmer: Add the chicken stock, potatoes, ham and frozen peas. Bring to the boil, cover and simmer for about 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Make it creamy: Pour in the milk and warm it through, then add the cream. Simmer for another 6–7 minutes to thicken slightly.
Add the cheese: Stir in the grated cheddar until melted and thick.
Serve: Top with a little cheddar, parsley and black pepper, and serve with soft dinner rolls, crusty bread or even rice.
recipes.notes:

recipes.title: I’ll Never Buy Passata Again After This…
ingredients: Optional: small splash of olive oil and seasoning
Optional: small splash of olive oil or seasoning = negligible cost
Homemade passata is cheaper, especially if you buy tomatoes and purée in bulk or on offer. Plus, you control the texture, flavour, salt, and add-ins — and you can make just what you need.
steps: Blend: Tip the tinned tomatoes with their juice into a blender. Add tomato purée, about 1 scant tablespoon per 400 g tin, to boost the flavour, and blend until liquid.
Sieve: Push the blended tomatoes through a sieve into a bowl to remove the seeds and leftover pulp. What passes through is pure passata.
Store uncooked: Bottle it and keep it in the fridge for 4–5 days.

Optional cooked version: Warm the passata over a low flame with a pinch of sugar (if you want it sweeter), a little salt, dried Italian herbs (not fresh) and a splash of olive oil. Cook low and slow for about 10 minutes, no more, so it stays a sauce rather than thickening.
Bottle: Cool and bottle in sterilised jars. Water bathed to seal, it keeps a good 6 months.

recipes.title: WARNING! This Chocolate Cake Should Be ILLEGAL… It’s THAT Good!
ingredients: All-purpose flour — 230 g | 16 tbsp | 1¾ UK cups | 1¾ US cups
Add 1 tsp of espresso powder to the dry mix to intensify the chocolate flavour.
Mascarpone (or cream cheese) — 115 g | 8 tbsp | 4 oz
Heavy cream (35%) — 60 ml | 60 g | 4 tbsp | ¼ UK/US cup
Powdered sugar (icing sugar) — 40 g | 5 tbsp | ⅓ UK/US cup
Dark or semi-sweet chocolate — 100 g | 3.5 oz (roughly ⅔ UK/US cup chopped)
Heavy cream (35%) — 160 ml | 160 g | 11 tbsp | ⅔ UK/US cup
steps: Prep: Heat the oven to 155°C (310°F). Line the base and sides of a deep 8 in loose-bottomed cake tin.

One-bowl batter: Put the flour, salt, baking powder, sugar, instant coffee/espresso powder and cocoa in a bowl. Briefly beat the eggs with the vanilla, then add them with the butter, milk and oil and mix everything together in one go (a stand mixer or by hand) until no dry powder remains.
Bake: Pour into the tin, swirl a skewer through the batter, and bake 60–70 minutes, checking from 60 minutes; it is done when a skewer comes out clean (about 65 minutes here).
Cool: Leave in the tin about 10 minutes, turn out onto a rack, peel off the paper and let it cool completely.
Make the cream filling: Whip the heavy cream, then fold it into the mascarpone mixed with the powdered sugar.

Split and fill: Slice the cake in half horizontally (a cake-slicing guide helps). Spread the cream over the bottom layer, stopping short of the edge, and gently set the top layer on without squashing it.
Ganache: Melt the chocolate in a bowl over boiling water, then stir in the cream until smooth; return it to the heat if it starts to firm up.
Finish: Pour the ganache over the top and let it run down the sides, then smooth it roughly. Slice and serve.

recipes.title: You Won’t Believe What a Banana Does to Brownies!
ingredients: 115g melted butter or coconut oil (½ cup / 8 tbsp / 120ml)
steps: Mash the bananas: Mash the ripe bananas, leaving some chunks for bursts of banana, or mash smooth for an all-over banana-bread flavour. The host also slices in an extra banana.
Prepare the tin: Line an 8×6×2-inch tin with parchment. Parchment is fine in an air fryer.
Dry mix: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and cocoa (per the description), then stir in the brown sugar.
Combine: Add the banana, melted butter (or coconut oil), vanilla, walnuts and chocolate chips and mix until no dry flour shows. The batter is gooey.

Bake in the air fryer: Preheat the air fryer on bake for about 5 minutes (160°C in the description). Spread the batter into the corners of the tin (a craggy top is fine) and bake. The host checks at 17 minutes, then adds 4 minutes and 1 more, about 22 in total, until a skewer comes out with just a few moist crumbs. The description gives 24–25 minutes at 160°C.
Oven alternative: Bake at 175°C for 22–28 minutes, checking from 22: about 22 for gooey, or 25–26 for firmer edges.
Cool: Cool in the tin at least 15 minutes before slicing, so they firm up.

recipes.title: Cosori TwinFry Air Fryer - My GO TO method for PERFECT chips Every time!
ingredients: Potatoes (Maris Piper or Russet) 500g | 1.1 lb | 3 medium. (the host says any potatoes work)
Optional seasoning: garlic powder, smoked paprika, vinegar salt, etc.
steps: Cut the chips: Wash the potatoes. Peel them for regular chips, or leave the skin on for steak-fry style, and cut into chips.
Soak: Put the chips in a bowl of water with a little salt and soak at least 30 minutes (or overnight) to draw out starch.
Dry: Drain and rinse, dry them in a tea towel, then go over them with kitchen towel until fully dry so they crisp.

Season and oil: Toss with salt and a little oil of your choice. If you use cornflour (best for thinner chips), coat the dry chips evenly with about a tablespoon first, then add the oil so there are no powdery patches.

Air-fry: Pile them into the air fryer basket (the host fills the whole large basket) and cook at 200°C for about 20 minutes, taking the basket out to shake halfway. Add about 5 minutes more if a crowded basket needs it. The description suggests preheating 3 minutes, then 15–20 minutes for thinner fries or 20–25 for chunky chips.
Serve: Season to taste, with garlic powder, smoked paprika or vinegar salt if you like.

recipes.title: CRISPY Coconut CHICKEN with Bang Bang Sauce
steps: Make the bang bang sauce: Mix the mayonnaise with the sriracha and the sweet chilli sauce, plus a little lime juice if you like (or other hot sauce), and set aside so the flavours come together.
Season the chicken: Pat the chicken tenders dry with kitchen towel and toss with about a teaspoon of smoked paprika, about a teaspoon of garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Flour: Toss the seasoned chicken in the bowl with the flour to coat. This saves setting up a separate station.
Egg and coconut crumb: Mix the panko and coconut on a tray. Dip each tender in beaten egg, then press it into the coconut crumb, using one wet hand and one dry. Chilling them helps the coating stick.

Shallow fry: Heat oil in a pan until a skewer bubbles. Fry the tenders slowly without crowding, turning often, so they crisp without browning too fast before the chicken cooks through. Air frying with an oil spray, or part-frying and finishing in the oven, also works.
Rest and serve: Rest them briefly on a rack (they keep cooking), then serve with the bang bang sauce for dipping or drizzling.

recipes.title: Strawberry PEACH Pie – A CLASSIC Made Simple
ingredients: For the Pie Crust (Homemade or Store-Bought):
(Or use a pre-made 9-inch pie crust for convenience.)
1 can (400g/14 oz) peach slices in juice, well-drained and chopped
250g (2 cups) fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
1 tbsp unsalted butter, cubed (for dotting on top)
1 egg yolk + 1 tbsp milk (for egg wash)
steps: Mix the filling: In a bowl combine the well-drained, chopped tinned peaches, the hulled sliced strawberries, granulated and brown sugar, 2 tablespoons of cornstarch, 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, a little vanilla, and optional cinnamon. The host also adds a pinch of salt to cut the sweetness (salt is not listed in the description). Leave it about 10 minutes.
Line the dish: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Roll homemade or store-bought pastry to fit a 9-inch pie dish and come up the sides with a little overhang.

Fill and finish the top: Tip in the fruit. You can add a lid or a lattice; the host starts to talk about a lattice and then decides on an open pie. Dot the filling with small cubes of unsalted butter — don't go crazy. If you do add a lid or lattice, an egg-yolk-and-milk wash and a little coarse sugar are listed as optional.
Bake: Sit the dish on a tray and bake 45–55 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OaMTeRTCw8E

recipes.title: EASY Paneer CHEESE from Scratch
ingredients: Full-fat whole milk — 5 litres (21¼ cups UK | 21¼ cups US)
Apple cider vinegar — 7½ tbsp (110 ml | 110 g | 11 UK tsp | 15 US tsp)
(or use half vinegar, half lemon juice for a milder taste)
steps: Set up: You need a large pan, cheesecloth (cotton cloth) and, optionally, two square baskets so the paneer comes out square. The host uses 10×8×3-inch baskets; use smaller ones for less milk.

Heat the milk: Pour the milk into the pan and add the salt now if you're using it (a couple of teaspoons). Heat it, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch, and more often once it steams. Watch closely, because it goes from steaming to boiling over quickly. The description says to bring it slowly to 85–90°C.

Split the milk: When it is steaming and just starting to bubble, add the vinegar (or half vinegar, half lemon juice) and keep heating about 25 seconds so it mixes in. Turn the heat off and leave it 10 minutes to split fully into curds and whey.
Drain: Line a basket with cheesecloth and set it on a rack over a tray or in the sink. Carefully ladle in the hot curds and let the whey drain away. The host uses the whey on his plants.
Press: Level the curds, fold the cloth over, set the second basket inside, then a board and a heavy weight on top (the host uses about 6 kg). More weight and longer pressing give firmer paneer.
Turn out: After about an hour, remove the weight, turn the paneer out and cube it, trimming the edges square if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VnuvS4Z_fuM

recipes.title: Ultimate SHREDDED BEEF Pie
ingredients: Beef chuck, shin, or brisket — 500g | 1 lb
Refrigerated pie crusts — about 400g total | UK/US: 2 crusts, shortcrust and puff pastry
steps: Season and brown the beef: Season cheap stewing beef (chuck, shin or brisket, about 500 g) with salt and pepper — better on the meat than in flour — and cut it quite large. Brown it in a little olive oil.

Aromatics and pressure-cook: Cook the chopped onion (and minced garlic from the list) just to take the rawness out, then add the beef broth or water (250 ml), about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, and about a teaspoon of dried thyme. Pressure-cook on high 45 minutes, then natural release at least 10 minutes (longer is fine).

Shred and thicken: The meat should be tender enough to shred. In a pan, cook a couple of tablespoons of flour over a moderate flame to take the rawness out, then stir in the cooking liquid and let it thicken into gravy. Season to taste. Mix enough gravy through the shredded beef to keep it moist, and keep some back — you can add an extra teaspoon in the pie if it looks dry. The captions are clearer about moistening the meat than about the exact shredding moment; watch the video if you want to see how he pulls it.

Line and fill: Heat the oven — the host says about 180°C; the description says 190°C / 375°F. Roll shortcrust (ready-rolled is fine) to fit your tins with a little overhang, then trim. Fill with the beef.

Lid and bake: Roll puff pastry for the lids (or use shortcrust throughout). Brush a little beaten egg around the rim to glue them, add the lids, and bake 30–35 minutes until golden. Rest about 6 or 7 minutes before serving. It's a fairly solid meat pie.

recipes.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole  -  No Tinned Soup
ingredients: 3 cups cooked chicken, shredded or diced — 450g
2 cups shredded Swiss cheese (or mix Swiss & mozzarella) — 200g
1½ cups milk — 360ml — 360g — 1½ UK cups — 1½ US cups
1 cup chicken stock (low salt) — 240ml — 240g — 1 UK cup — 1 US cup
½ cup sour cream — 120ml — 120g — ½ UK cup — ½ US cup
1 tsp Dijon mustard — 5g (optional, adds that classic cordon bleu zing)
steps: Prep the chicken and ham: Cube (or shred) the cooked chicken, removing the skin, and cube or tear the ham, keeping the pieces big enough to see. Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and grease a 9×13 inch dish set on a tray in case it bubbles over.
Make the topping: Mix the breadcrumbs with about a teaspoon of garlic powder, pepper and a little salt (go easy if topping with Parmesan), then stir in the melted butter.

Make the sauce: Melt the butter in a pan, stir in a couple of tablespoons of flour and cook briefly. Add the milk all in one go and stir until smooth. Season with pepper (no salt) and garlic powder, and stir in the remaining sauce ingredients from the list (chicken stock, sour cream and Dijon). If it gets too thick, loosen with a little more milk or water.
Combine: Stir the chicken and ham into the sauce, then the cheese: Swiss, mozzarella (used here for stringiness), or a mix.

Top and bake: Tip into the dish and cover with the breadcrumbs, leaving little peaks. Add a little more cheese and some Parmesan and pepper, then bake for about 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Rest 5–10 minutes, sprinkle with parsley and serve with broccoli, carrots or salad.

recipes.title: APPLE PIE meets PORRIDGE   Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal Bars – Easy Breakfast Meal Prep
ingredients: ½ cup (60g) chopped pecans or walnuts (optional)
¼ cup (40g) raisins or chopped dates (optional)
2 tbsp (14g) ground flaxseeds (adds structure and fiber, optional)
1 cup (110g) grated apple (about 2 medium apples, skin on or off). Skin on for colour specs
¼ cup (60ml) maple syrup or honey
2 tablespoons (2 tbsp / 30ml) melted coconut oil or butter
2 tablespoons (2 tbsp / 30g) unsweetened applesauce (for added apple flavour and moisture)
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
Glaze: maple syrup — about 2 tbsp, and coconut oil — about 1 tsp (spoken)
steps: Mix the dry: Combine the oats, cinnamon, nutmeg, baking powder, salt, walnuts and raisins. Line a 9½ × 7½ in tin (or an 8 × 8 in dish).
Mix the wet: Beat the eggs with the maple syrup (or honey), vanilla, milk and about 2 tablespoons of coconut oil, then pour into the dry ingredients.
Add the apple: Grate the apples (skin on adds colour) and squeeze lightly to remove some juice, but don't wring them dry. Stir them in with the applesauce if using (the host had none).
Soak: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Leave the mix about 10 minutes for the oats to absorb the liquid, stir in the ground flaxseed, and rest about 5 minutes more.
Fill the tin: Spread into the tin and press down just enough to settle it; don't compact it.
Bake: Bake until the centre feels set but still has a little give (the time isn't stated in the video); it firms up as it cools.
Glaze: Mix about 2 tablespoons of maple syrup with about a teaspoon of coconut oil and brush over the warm top.
Cool and cut: Cool about 10 minutes, turn out onto a rack and let it cool completely, then cut into bars.

recipes.title: Easy CHICKEN Meatball Boats with Garlic Butter Hoagie Rolls
ingredients: Hoagie rolls or sub buns, about 6 in / 15 cm — 4
Cooked meatballs — 12–16 (about 360 g total, roughly 30 g each)
Marinara sauce — 360 ml (1½ cups / about 350 g)
Garlic powder — ½ tsp (or 1 clove fresh garlic, finely minced)
Dried Italian herbs or oregano — ½ tsp
steps: Heat the oven: Put it on about 190°C / 380°F — you'll cook the meatballs and later melt the cheese in the same oven. You could pan-fry the balls instead, but the oven is already on.

Mix the meatballs: Soak the breadcrumbs in a little milk or water, then mix them with the chicken mince, egg, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, Italian herbs and optional grated Parmesan. It will still be a bit sticky, but the crumbs help you roll 12–16 balls (about 30 g each in the description). Oil the tin and your hands if it helps.

Bake the balls and crisp the rolls: Bake the meatballs 15–18 minutes, turning them after about 4 or 5 minutes. Meanwhile, mix melted butter with garlic (fresh minced, or garlic powder) and Italian herbs or oregano. Split the hoagie rolls and hollow them into boats without going right through to the bottom — or squash the insides down. Brush with the garlic butter and bake 4–5 minutes until lightly crisp. Leftover bread can go in as croutons.
Sauce and assemble: Warm the marinara. Put a little mozzarella in each boat, add the cooked meatballs (12–16, or about 360 g total), more sauce, more mozzarella and a little Parmesan.
Finish: Bake the filled boats 10–12 minutes until the cheese is bubbling. Garnish with fresh basil if you like.

recipes.title: Britain’s OLDEST seasonal bake  Simnel Cake EASTER and Mothering Sunday Cake
ingredients: Light brown sugar — 225g | 1 cup (UK & US) | 16 tbsp
Plain flour (all-purpose) — 225g | 1 ¾ cups (US) | 1 ½ cups (UK)
Milk — 2 tbsp | 30ml | 2 US tbsp | 2 UK tbsp
(Divided: ⅓ for middle layer, ⅓ for top, ⅓ for decoration)
steps: Prepare: Preheat the oven to about 150°C and line an 8-inch springform tin.

Make the batter: Cream the butter and brown sugar together (melted butter makes it easier). Beat in the four eggs; the host adds them all at once. Add part of the flour (with the baking powder and a pinch of salt), the ground almonds and spices, then the milk and the rest of the flour, and beat until smooth. Scrape down the sides.
Add the fruit: Stir in the halved cherries, lemon and orange zest, mixed peel, sultanas and currants until evenly mixed. You can mix and match the dried fruit.

Marzipan layer: Spoon about half the batter into the tin. Roll out a third of the marzipan on icing sugar or flour, cut it to the size of the tin, lay it on the batter, then cover with the rest of the batter and smooth it roughly.

Bake: Bake about 90 minutes, then test with a skewer. If it is still a little damp, cover the top with foil and give it about 20 minutes more. Cool in the tin about 10 minutes, then on a rack until completely cold. Cracks don't matter, because the top is covered.

Marzipan top: Brush the top of the cake with warmed apricot jam (optional). Roll out another third of the marzipan a little larger than the cake (a pie tin makes a handy guide), lay it over and trim it or press the edges against the sides.
Decorate and finish: Roll the remaining marzipan into 11 balls and arrange them on top. Brush everything with beaten egg yolk, then lightly toast it with a kitchen blowtorch.

recipes.title: Creamy Red Lentil Moussaka
ingredients: 2 large eggplants (approx. 600g total), sliced into 0.5 cm / ¼ inch rounds
2 tbsp (30 ml) olive oil = 30 ml = 2 US tbsp = 2 UK tbsp
1 cup (200g) red lentils, rinsed 1 US cup = 0.83 UK cup
2 cups (480 ml) vegetable broth 2 US cups = 1.66 UK cups
Salt and pepper, to taste (start with ½ tsp each)
½ cup (50g) grated cheese (cheddar, kefalotyri, or parmesan) ½ US cup = 0.41 UK cup
Salt to taste (start with ¼ tsp)
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
Extra olive oil for the onions, and extra grated cheese for a layer inside
steps: Roast the eggplant: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Slice the eggplants about ¼ inch thick, lay them on a parchment-lined tray, brush both sides with olive oil and roast about 20 minutes, turning them after about 15. They should be soft but still hold their shape. (No salting needed.)

Start the lentil sauce: Rinse the lentils and leave them in water so they don't clump. Sauté the onion (red or white) in olive oil with a tiny pinch of salt, add the garlic, then the oregano and a pinch of cinnamon.

Simmer: Add the tomatoes and the tomato paste, then the drained lentils and the stock. Simmer uncovered about 20 minutes, stirring often so the lentils don't stick, and top up with water if it dries out. Stop when the lentils are swollen and soft but there's still a little juice.

Cheese sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then add all the milk at once with a little nutmeg and black pepper (salt optional). Stir until it thickens, then stir in the cheese off the heat, loosening with more milk if too thick.

Layer: In a dish about 11×9 in (or 9×9 in), lay the less attractive eggplant slices on the bottom, spread over all the lentil mixture, add a light layer of cheese, top with the best eggplant slices and pour over the cheese sauce.
Bake: Set on a tray (it may bubble over) and bake 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Cool about 10 minutes, then serve with a little parsley.

recipes.title: EASY Soft CRUST FRENCH Bread
ingredients: 500g / 3¼ UK cups / 4 US cups strong white bread flour. I used 250g All-purpose/plain flour and 250g bread flour
300ml lukewarm water (about 35°C) 1¼ UK cups / 1¼ US cups
steps: Mix the dough: In a stand-mixer bowl, combine 250 g plain flour and 250 g bread flour with the yeast, sugar, salt, about a tablespoon of olive oil and the lukewarm water. Blooming the yeast in the water for 5 minutes first is optional.
Knead: Mix on low until combined, then up a notch, letting the machine knead until the dough comes away from the sides: slightly tacky but not sticky. Add a little flour or water if needed.
First rise: Shape into a ball, put it in an oiled bowl, cover and leave for an hour or more until doubled.
Shape: Dust with flour, divide the dough, and roll each piece up tightly, sealing the seam and rolling the edges, into loaves of any size.
Second rise: Place in a baguette tray, cover and leave for about 20–40 minutes until puffed up.

Score and bake: Score the tops with a knife or lame. Put a tray of boiling water in the bottom of the oven (220°C/430°F in the description) for steam, then bake for about 20–25 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding.
Cool: Leave a minute, then cool on a rack.

recipes.title: Mini Burger Steaks with Mushroom Gravy
ingredients: All-purpose/ plain flour: 2 tbsp / 16g, depending how the beef broth is made
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs: Stir the milk into the breadcrumbs and set them aside to absorb it. This keeps the burgers juicy instead of dense.
Prep the veg: Slice the mushrooms (any shape), finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.
Mix the beef: Season the mince with salt and pepper (mixed herbs are optional), add the soaked breadcrumbs and mix well by hand.
Shape: Divide the mix into about eight balls (or up to 12 for smaller ones), then flatten them into patties and press a thumb dent into the middle of each so they don't swell up as they cook.
Brown the patties: Fry in a little oil in batches, about 3–4 minutes a side, turning as often as you like, until well coloured. Transfer to a tray and cover with foil.

Make the gravy: In the same pan, melt a good couple of tablespoons of butter and cook the onion and garlic until translucent (a little colour is fine). Add the mushrooms and cook until coloured. Pour in the beef broth (the host makes it from gravy powder) and simmer gently. If your broth is thin, make a roux with the flour first.
Simmer together: Return the patties, spoon the gravy over them and simmer about 6–7 minutes, until thickened and heated through.
Mash and serve: Boil peeled, cubed potatoes in salted water until they break up, drain, and mash with salt, pepper, warm milk and butter. Serve the burger steaks and mushroom gravy over the mash.
