recipes.title: Apple Pie – Buttery, Tender, and Absolutely Irresistible!
ingredients: 4 apples (500g), peeled and grated I used Granny Smiths
1 egg yolk + 1 tablespoon milk (for egg wash)
steps: Make the dough: Mix the eggs, oil, softened butter, sugar and vanilla (vanilla sugar is in the description) with all-purpose flour and baking powder. Bring it together with your hands — it should be a fairly wet, slightly sticky dough. The host's looked a little dry but still came together. The description lists 2 small eggs, 3 tbsp (50 g) sugar, 8 g vanilla sugar, 2 tbsp (40 g) butter, 4 tbsp (40 ml) oil, 4 g / 1 tsp baking powder and 3 large cups flour (300 g).

Divide it: Use about a 9–10 inch baking dish (the host says the measurement is in the description). Divide the dough roughly in half: one piece for a base that comes a little way up the sides, and one for the lid. The host traces around the dish on parchment as a size guide for the top.

Prep the apples: Peel the apples (the description is 4 apples / 500 g; the host uses Granny Smiths). Use lemon juice so they don't brown (juice of ½ lemon in the description). Grate about half and dice the rest so you keep some texture instead of a mush.

Cook the filling: Stir in the sugar and a little pinch of salt. Melt the butter in a pan over a flame that is not too high, add the apples and cook about 8 minutes so the grated apple breaks down, the diced pieces soften and some juice cooks out. If there isn't enough fluid and you worry about burning, add a splash of liquid (the amount isn't stated). Take it off and let it cool.
Line the dish: Have the oven on about 180°C / 350°F. Roll or stretch the slightly buttery, oily pastry into the dish and up the sides. The host says you could use ordinary shortcrust if you prefer.

Assemble: Spread apricot jam on the base (cheaper jam is fine), then add the cooled apple mix. Roll the lid to the parchment mark, cut vents or a pattern if you like, lay it on, and tuck the edges in. Fork the edge. Brush with an egg-and-milk wash (1 egg yolk + 1 tablespoon milk in the description) and scatter chopped almonds (or peanuts, from the description) on top — some may fall off.

Bake: Put the pie on a tray, because the pastry is quite oily and may leak. Bake until golden, about 30–35 minutes according to the description. The captions don't rest on an exact minute count at the end; watch for a golden bake in the video.
Cool and serve: Let it cool about 5 minutes, then turn it out and dust lightly with icing sugar.

recipes.title: Creamy Garlic Chicken Pasta – Easy & Delicious 30 Minute Meal
ingredients: 225g pasta of choice (penne or rotini) cooked as packet instructions
½ tsp black pepper (or to taste)
steps: Cook the pasta: Put a pan of boiling water on and cook 225 g pasta (penne or rotini, or your choice) as the packet says. The host lifts it straight from the water into the sauce at the end.

Cook the chicken: This is a butter dish (you can use oil, but the host is making a butter pasta). Melt butter in a pan, add the cubed chicken, and season with salt and pepper as it cooks. When the chicken is done, take it out. The whole meal is meant to be on the table within 30 minutes.

Garlic-Parmesan sauce: Add a little more butter if you want — it is a butter sauce. Put in the minced garlic with the flame not high, 30 seconds maximum, and try not to brown it. Pour in the cream (as much as you like; the description lists 1 cup / 240 ml). Don't lean on extra salt at this stage — the chicken already has some — and add a little pepper. Chilli flakes or other seasonings are optional; the host doesn't want the creamy butter Parmesan overpowered.

Finish: Stir in the grated Parmesan so the sauce thickens, but not too thick. Return the chicken and any juices, then add the pasta, turning it in the sauce. Garnish with fresh basil if you like. The host says you can use less butter or less cream if you want.

recipes.title: EASY Restaurant-QUALITY BUTTER Chicken Hack Using Jarred Sauce
ingredients: 500g (1.1 lbs) boneless chicken thighs or breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
½ tsp (1g) Kashmiri red chilli powder (or smoked paprika for colour)
¼ tsp (1g) smoked paprika (optional, for depth)
1/8 tsp (a pinch) baking soda (to balance acidity)
1 tbsp (5g) dried fenugreek leaves (Kasuri methi), crushed
Serve with naan, roti, or steamed basmati rice
steps: Marinate the chicken: Mix the chicken with the salt, tandoori masala, garam masala, smoked paprika or Kashmiri chilli, cumin, coriander, turmeric, about a tablespoon of lemon juice, a little food colouring (optional) and the yogurt. Marinate at least 30 minutes (ideally 4 hours or overnight) in the fridge.

Sear the chicken: Heat a little oil and butter over a moderate flame. Add the chicken, leaving most of the excess marinade behind, and cook, turning, until the liquid cooks off and the pieces take on colour. Lift out and set aside, and scoop any burnt bits out of the pan.
Build the base: Add butter and the chopped onion over a medium-low flame, then the garlic and ginger, and cook about 30 seconds just to take out the rawness without colouring.
Bloom the spices: Stir in the garam masala and smoked paprika, then the sugar and pinch of baking soda to tame the jar sauce's sourness. Don't add salt yet, as the jar sauce is already salted.
Simmer: Pour in the jarred butter chicken sauce with a little water, return the chicken and simmer about 5 minutes until the oil starts to separate.
Finish: Stir in a little butter and the cream, add the crushed kasuri methi in the last few minutes (adding it late keeps it from turning bitter), and cook about 4 minutes more.
Serve: Top with a knob of butter to melt into the sauce, garnish with coriander if you like, and serve with naan, roti or rice.

recipes.title: NOT just for the IRISH EASY Corned BEEF & Potato Slice with Buttered Cabbage & Parsley Sauce
ingredients: 1 can (340g) corned beef, diced or mashed
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
Extra butter for the onions and mash
Milk, beaten into the egg wash
Extra cheddar, stirred into the parsley sauce to make a parsley cheese sauce
steps: Boil the potatoes: Boil the cubed potatoes in salted water, then drain and return them to the pan to steam dry.
Prep the veg: Shred the cabbage, discarding the outer leaves and core. Finely chop the green onions and about 2 tablespoons of parsley, and dice the onion.
Soften the onions: Sauté the onion in butter until the rawness is gone, then add the green onions for about 20 seconds and turn off the heat.

Make the filling: Mash the potatoes fairly dry and chunky with a little butter and seasoning, stir in the onions, and let cool a little. Fold in the corned beef in chunks without over-mashing, then stir through about a teaspoon of Worcestershire sauce and about ½ teaspoon of mustard powder.
Line the tray: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a 9×13 in tray with parchment and lay in the bottom pastry sheet with an overhang to crimp.

Fill and top: Spread the filling over the pastry and rough it up with a fork, then scatter over the cheddar (50 g or more for a cheesier pie). Lay the top sheet on, fold the overhangs over and press to seal, tucking any loose edges under.

Decorate and bake: Score a pattern with the back of a knife, cut a few vents, brush with egg beaten with a little milk and bake about 25–30 minutes until golden and puffed. (It can be frozen before egg-washing.) Rest about 10 minutes.
Boil the cabbage: Boil the cabbage about 4 minutes, then leave it in the water while you make the sauce.

Parsley cheese sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook briefly, then whisk in all the milk at once. Season with salt, black pepper and the Dijon mustard, add the parsley, then stir in some cheese until melted.

Butter the cabbage and serve: Drain the cabbage and toss with a chunk of butter, pepper and a little salt. Lift the slice out using the parchment, cut into portions and serve with the cabbage and parsley cheese sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m0ZOROU6eVU

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and puffed up.

recipes.title: COLONIAL Currant Bun Mashed Potato – A Taste of SIMPLICITY and TRADITION
ingredients: 125g (½ cup) mashed cooked potato(about 1 large potato, peeled, boiled, and mashed)
150g (1 cup) currants (or sultanas, but currants are best)
60ml (¼ cup) milk (plus extra for glazing – about 1 tbsp)
steps: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a baking tray with parchment.

Mix the potato and flour: Rub the mashed potato (leftover mash is fine) into the self-raising flour with a pinch of salt until combined. To make your own self-raising flour, mix 1 kg plain flour with 1 tablespoon of double-acting baking powder and a pinch of salt.
Add the sugar and fruit: Stir in the sugar and the currants (or sultanas or raisins).

Make the dough: Add the milk and bring it together into a shaggy dough, adding only a tiny bit more milk if needed. There's no butter in the original recipe. Knead it briefly on the worktop without overworking it.
Shape: Divide it into four buns (or six smaller ones), shape them to roughly the same size and put them on the tray.
Glaze and bake: Brush with milk and bake about 20–25 minutes (the description says 30–35) until lightly browned. A single large loaf would need about 40–45 minutes.
Serve: Cool a little, then split and spread with butter while still warm. They are good with a pot of tea.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VPdBL9YaXGw
Uploaded 2025-02-18.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a baking tray with parchment paper; Bake 30-35 mins.

recipes.title: Crispy Arabic Spinach Rolls – Easy & Delicious Middle Eastern Fatayer Sabanekh
ingredients: 60-80g Spreadable white cheese: 3-4 tablespoons cream cheese would work well as a substitute. You could also use Labneh or ricotta for a more traditional touch.
120-150g Crumbled white cheese (feta, Akkawi, or similar)
Mix feta with a bit of cream cheese or ricotta to make it creamier.
steps: Make the dough: Dissolve the salt in the warm water, then add the flour and knead about 8 minutes in a stand mixer, or by hand for 8–10 minutes, adding the flour a bit at a time. You want a slightly sticky dough.
First rest: Shape it into a ball, put it in a lightly floured bowl (no oil), cover and rest 30 minutes.
Divide: On a floured surface, divide the dough into about eight equal pieces, shape them into balls, and cover them in a box for about 15 minutes.
Salt the spinach: Chop the washed spinach and mix it with about a teaspoon of salt. Leave about 5 minutes, stirring once, to draw out the liquid.
Grease the dough: Mix the melted butter with the vegetable oil. Roll out each ball a little, coat it with the butter-oil mix and stack them on a plate.
Make the filling: Wearing gloves, squeeze as much liquid as you can from the spinach. Mix in the chilli flakes, chopped onion, feta and the creamy cheese (ricotta, cream cheese or labneh).

Stretch: Oil the work surface, lay a piece of dough on it and stretch it out with your fingers until paper-thin, the way rotis are made; small tears don't matter. Trim the edge straight with a pizza wheel and fold it over on itself to make layers.
Fill and roll: Spoon filling along one edge, fold the dough over and roll it up like a sausage roll, tucking in the sides as you go. Put it on a parchment-lined tray and repeat.
Bake: Brush the tops lightly with more butter-oil mix and bake at 190–200°C until golden and crisp (35–40 minutes in the description). Cool 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_J0B8HDBd1c

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F); Bake for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown and crisp.

recipes.title: Easy Chicken Broccoli Rice Casserole with Cheesy Crunchy Topping
ingredients: 1.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breast, cut, bite-sized pieces
4 cups broccoli florets, cut into bite-sized pieces
½ cup panko breadcrumbs (for extra crunch)
steps: Steam the broccoli: Bring a little water to the boil in a pan, set a small colander or sieve of broccoli florets on top, cover with a lid and steam 5–6 minutes until a fork goes in but they are still firm. Tip them into a large bowl. (If you are cooking rice from scratch instead of using cooked rice, you can add the broccoli for the last 5 minutes.)

Cook the chicken: In the same pan, melt a little butter and cook the onion and garlic just to take the rawness out. Add the diced chicken and cook about 5 minutes, a little longer if any pink remains, until it puffs up and is just cooked; it finishes in the oven. Turn the heat off and add the chicken, onion and juices to the broccoli.

Make the cheese sauce: Melt about 4 tablespoons of butter, stir in about 4 tablespoons of flour and cook out the rawness. Add the herbs and seasonings, then pour in all the milk followed by the cream, with the Dijon, a little pepper and a little salt. Cook until it thickens, which doesn't take long. Turn the heat off and stir in most of the cheddar, keeping some for the top. It doesn't need to be completely smooth.
Loosen the sauce: If the sauce is thick, stir in the chicken stock. Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Make the topping: Crush the Ritz crackers and mix them with the panko breadcrumbs.
Assemble: Add the cooked rice to the chicken and broccoli, pour over the cheese sauce and mix. Spread it in a baking dish, cover with the cracker crumbs and top with the reserved cheddar.
Bake: Bake about 25 minutes until bubbling and golden. If you like, push a few pieces of broccoli into the top for show at the end, so they don't burn in the oven.
Serve: The top sets into a crust, so cut a portion, lift the crust off, spoon out the filling, then put the crust back on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6L9BWrw1aQ

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). 9x13-inch baking dish; Bake for 20-25 minutes, until bubbly and golden brown.

recipes.title: Ultimate ENGLISH MUFFINS – Big, Soft & Griddle-Cooked to PERFECTION!
ingredients: 400g (3 ¼ cups) bread flour. I used 300g Bread flour and 100g All purpose/plain flour
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
A little oil (or butter) for the bowl
steps: Activate the yeast: Stir the yeast into the warm milk and leave it until it starts to bubble; if it doesn't bloom, use fresh yeast. Lightly beat the egg.

Mix the dough: In a stand mixer bowl, briefly mix the flour (300 g bread flour + 100 g plain was used), sugar and salt. Add the milk-yeast mixture, the egg and the melted butter, mix on low until combined, then knead 8–10 minutes to a soft, sticky dough.
First rise: Shape into a ball, put it in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and leave about 1–1½ hours until doubled.

Roll and cut: Knock back on a lightly floured surface and roll to about 1 inch thick. Dip a cutter in flour so it doesn't stick and cut out muffins, re-rolling the scraps; the last scraps can be shaped into a ball by hand.
Second rise: Set the muffins on a tray dusted with semolina (or cornmeal), sprinkle more on top and leave to rise about 40 minutes.

Griddle low and slow: Heat a pan gently over a low flame and cook a few at a time, uncovered (or lidded to steam if you prefer), turning a couple of times until golden on both sides and cooked through. Cool on a rack.
Serve: Split with a fork for the craggy texture, toast, and serve with butter and jam, or use for breakfast sandwiches.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lv1QwZ9bQq8

recipes.title: EASY Chicken MARSALA – CLASSIC Italian American COMFORT Food
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts — can be butterflied or cut in half
1 small onion, finely diced or thinly sliced
¾ cup Sweet Marsala wine (Dolce) Dry works just fine
1 teaspoon red wine vinegar or ½ teaspoon lemon juice (to balance sweetness)
½ cup heavy cream (optional for a creamy version)
1 teaspoon fresh thyme (or ½ teaspoon dried)
steps: Prep: Thickly slice the mushrooms, finely dice the onion (or shallot) and dice the garlic. Keep the chicken breasts whole (three skinless, boneless breasts were used).
Season and dust: Season the chicken itself, not the flour, with white pepper, salt and garlic powder, then dust lightly in flour and shake off the excess.

Fry low and slow: Heat about 3 tablespoons of oil with some butter and fry the chicken gently about 7 minutes, then flip; turn it onto its sides and back again until golden all over and cooked through. Transfer to a tray and cover with foil.
Clean the pan: Spoon out any burnt bits, keeping the good fond.
Onions and mushrooms: Soften the onion to take the rawness out, add a little more butter and the mushrooms and cook until lightly coloured but still with texture, then add the garlic briefly.

Marsala sauce: Pour in the Marsala (sweet was used here) and add about a teaspoon of red wine vinegar or lemon juice to balance the sweetness. Let it bubble briefly to cook off some alcohol, then add the chicken stock and the thyme (or oregano).
Finish the chicken: For a creamy version, stir in the cream now. Return the chicken and any juices to the sauce and simmer until the chicken is cooked through.
Serve: Serve the chicken on mashed potato, opened up a little, with the mushroom sauce spooned over, a side of carrots and a scattering of parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oHbP2HrT4-4
Uploaded 2025-02-14.

recipes.title: STEAK and Onion Pie with FORGOTTEN Suet Crust
ingredients: For the Pie Filling (Instant Pot Version):
Salt and black pepper, to taste
400ml beef stock (more liquid for stove top 600ml)
1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water (slurry, if needed)
1 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp oil for frying
Pressure cook on HIGH for 35 minutes.
Let it naturally release for 10 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure.
steps: Brown the steak: Season 1 kg cubed stewing steak (topside or chuck) and fry it in about a tablespoon of oil and a tablespoon of butter until it has some colour. The host prefers a pan to the Instant Pot's sauté mode because he finds that too hot, but use sauté if you like. Tip the beef into the Instant Pot (or a casserole if you're cooking on the stove) and leave the browned bits in the pan.

Onions and gravy: Add a little more butter and cook the sliced onions and optional minced garlic just to take the rawness out — keep some texture. Add them to the beef with dried thyme, about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, 1½ tbsp tomato purée, a little salt and pepper, and the beef stock (400 ml for the Instant Pot; the description suggests 600 ml on the stove).

Cook the filling: Pressure-cook on high 35 minutes, then natural release 10 minutes before you vent. On the stove, simmer about 2 hours until the beef is tender. If the gravy needs thickening, mix a little of it with a cornstarch slurry (1 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water in the description) and stir it back in. An 8 × 8 inch dish works well.

Suet crust: While the pot releases, mix the self-raising flour, cornflour, shredded suet, optional dried thyme and salt with the milk to a lump-free batter — this is a poured, forgotten-style suet crust, not a rolled pastry. Spoon or pour it over the filling in the dish.

Bake: Heat the oven to 170°C fan / 190°C conventional. The host talks about 20–25 minutes; the description says 25–30. Bake until the top is risen and golden — it can bubble over a little, and the underside of the crust should be a bit soft where it has absorbed the gravy. Serve with peas if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PVhwAUz-b7g
Uploaded 2025-02-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Let it naturally release for 10 minutes, then quick release any remaining pressure; Preheat oven to 170°C (fan) / 190°C (conventional); Bake 25 - 30 mins.

recipes.title: EASY ONE Pan BBQ Chicken Chilli
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can cannellini beans, not drained
1 (15 oz) can of kidney beans, not drained
1 (15 oz) can pinto beans, not drained
1 tsp chipotle powder (or 1 chopped chipotle in adobo) (optional for heat)
1 tbsp butter (optional, for a silky finish)
steps: Sear the chicken: Cut the chicken breasts in half through the middle (it doesn't need to be neat). Without seasoning, sear them in a little oil until there's a good crust on both sides, then take them out and cover with foil. They will keep cooking in their own steam.
Soften the aromatics: Add a little more oil and cook the garlic and onion on a low-moderate flame, scraping up the browned bits from the chicken, just until the rawness is gone.

Add the sauce: Turn the flame right down and stir in the BBQ sauce, ketchup, about 1½ tablespoons of brown sugar, about 2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar, about 2 tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce, the liquid smoke and about 2 teaspoons of yellow mustard (Dijon also works). Stir in the spices. There's no need to bloom them, since it all stews together.

Add the beans: Add the cannellini, pinto (or chilli) and kidney beans with their liquid, undrained (drain and rinse them if you prefer), plus the chopped jalapeño. Add just a little chicken stock so the sauce stays thick.
Simmer: Bring it to the boil, then turn it down and simmer uncovered for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the chicken: Shred the chicken with two forks (leftover or rotisserie chicken also works), stir it in and simmer about 20 minutes more, stirring gently, until thick. A lid is optional.
Serve: Top with cheddar, sour cream and fresh coriander, with rice, crusty bread or cornbread. You can cut the sugar by a tablespoon, but don't leave it out completely.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UUISw_CAL2Y

recipes.title: EASY CHICKEN Sausage Rolls – PERFECT Party Snack
ingredients: 1 clove garlic, minced (or ½ tsp garlic powder)
2 tbsp milk powder (binder) or an egg
1 sheet ready-rolled puff pastry cut 4 inch x 4.5 inch
1 egg (for egg wash) OR milk for a non-egg wash
Sesame seeds or poppy seeds (optional for topping)
Milk or cream — Gives a lighter golden finish.
Oil spray — Crispier finish without colour depth.
steps: Mix the filling: Put the chicken mince in a bowl with all the spices and the milk powder (the binder). Add a little Worcestershire sauce, about a teaspoon of Dijon (or American yellow) mustard and the breadcrumbs, and mix well by hand until sticky.

Rest: Leave the mix for about 10–15 minutes so the breadcrumbs absorb the moisture. Meanwhile heat the oven to about 200°C (400°F), beat an egg and cut the ready-rolled puff pastry into 4 × 4½ inch pieces.
Roll: With damp hands, shape some filling into a sausage on each piece of pastry, brush the edge with egg, roll it over to seal underneath and place seam side down on a lined tray.
Glaze and vent: Brush with egg wash (or milk, or milk and water), cut a couple of vents in the top and sprinkle with white and black sesame seeds if you like.
Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes until golden (the description says 25–30). Rest a minute, then cool on a rack. Serve with yellow mustard, or with veg and gravy.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mOi5nFu0DR4

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a baking tray with parchment paper; Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and crispy.

recipes.title: MAC and CHEESE MEATLOAF  - The ULTIMATE Comfort Food Mash Up!
ingredients: For the Mac and Cheese Layer:
8 ounces (225g) elbow macaroni (or pasta of choice)
2 cups (200g) shredded cheddar cheese or more
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
steps: Cook the macaroni: Boil the macaroni in salted water according to the packet, then drain.

Season the meat: Mix the beef with the garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, up to a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, the ketchup and the egg (the video adds no breadcrumbs here).
Part-cook the meat: Fry the onion and garlic in a little oil until the rawness is gone, then add the meat mixture, breaking it up, and cook to about 80% done with some browning. Let it cool.

Cheese sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook a minute, then add the milk and stir as it thickens. Season with black pepper and about a teaspoon of English mustard, lower the heat and stir in cheddar until smooth.
Mac and cheese: Stir the cheese sauce through the drained macaroni and let it cool a little.
Glaze: Mix the ketchup, brown sugar, black pepper and a splash of Worcestershire sauce.

Layer: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Butter a 2 lb loaf tin and set it on a tray. Press in a layer of meat, then macaroni, a layer of cheddar, more meat, more macaroni and more cheese, keeping a loaf shape. Add breadcrumbs on top if you want crunch, then spread over the glaze.
Bake: Bake 15–20 minutes to set it and cook on the glaze.
Rest and serve: Rest at least 10 minutes, then loosen with a knife, slice and garnish with parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tn4SOfSixgA
Uploaded 2025-02-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a baking dish (8x8 or similar); Bake for 15-20 minutes.

recipes.title: EASY Hearty Sausage and Bean Stew – ONE POT Comfort Food
ingredients: ½ tsp dried thyme and oregano
300ml vegetable stock (or chicken stock for more depth)
Salt, to taste (optional, depending on baked beans’ saltiness)
steps: Prep: Chop the onion, mince the garlic and dice the carrot. Strip the kale leaves from the stalks and shred them.
Boil the sausages: Put the sausages (any kind) in a pan of water and boil them until the water evaporates.
Brown: Add a little oil and fry the sausages to colour them slightly, then add the onion and garlic and cook together.
Bloom the spices: Stir in the smoked paprika and herbs to bloom in the oil, then add the carrot and a splash of Worcestershire sauce. Cut large sausages into pieces with scissors.

Simmer: Add the stock (veg, chicken, beef or pork) and bring it back up to temperature. Stir in about a teaspoon of Dijon mustard and the tinned tomatoes, adding salt only if needed. Cover and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Beans and greens: Stir in the baked beans and white beans, then the kale, and cook for about 5 minutes more, lid on or off, until it thickens into a stew. Spinach can replace the kale.
Serve: Serve as it is, or with mashed potatoes or rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mY3TZ3d2K0c

recipes.title: CHEESY Garlic CHICKEN Wraps
ingredients: For the wraps (the description gives no amounts for these; spoken amounts are noted):
Cooked chicken (leftover or rotisserie), cubed small
Fajita seasoning (makes a jar; mix together and store):
80g chili powder — gochugaru Korean red chilli powder -
steps: Make the filling: Cube the cooked chicken small and mix it with the cheddar, mozzarella, Parmesan and black pepper. The host skips salt because of the Parmesan. Stir in about a teaspoon of fajita seasoning.
Make the garlic butter: Mix the melted butter with the minced garlic, a little garlic powder and a little oregano.

Wrap: Preheat the oven to 190°C and line a tray with parchment. Spoon some filling onto a warmed tortilla about a third of the way up, fold in the sides, roll it up and put it seam-side down on the tray. Repeat with the rest.
Brush and bake: Brush the wraps with the garlic butter, spooning the garlic over the top, then bake until golden and crisp (12–15 minutes in the description).
Serve: Rest a minute, garnish with parsley and serve with sour cream, salsa or salad.

recipes.title: Easy Pepper and Chorizo Crustless Quiche Low-Carb No Crust, All Flavour!
ingredients: 1 cup roasted red peppers, sliced (you can use jarred or roast your own)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup shredded Manchego, Mozzarella or Cheddar cheese
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
A little Parmesan, for the top
steps: Roast the peppers: Slice red (and yellow) peppers and roast them with a little olive oil at about 180°C, or use drained jarred roasted peppers.

Seal the tin: Lay parchment over the base of a loose-bottomed or springform tin, clip it back into the ring and fold the excess paper under the base so it forms a seal against leaks. Set it on a tray and heat the oven to 190°C (375°F).

Make the custard: Beat the cornflour into the milk first (it firms the quiche and gives a better texture), then beat in the cream and eggs and season with black pepper. Skip the salt, as the chorizo is salty.
Add the peppers: Spread the roasted peppers evenly over the base of the tin.

Fry the chorizo: Fry the sliced chorizo and onion in a little olive oil until coloured and the onion loses its rawness, adding the smoked paprika. Lift them out, leaving the oil behind, and scatter over the peppers.
Fill: Scatter over the cheese (a mix of cheeses works), pour in the custard carefully and finish with a little Parmesan.
Bake: Bake 30–35 minutes until set in the centre and golden.
Cool and serve: Cool about 10 minutes, release from the tin, slide off the paper onto a plate, slice and garnish with parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BExJznZ_lDc
Uploaded 2025-02-07.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). 9-inch pie dish; Bake for 30-35 minutes until the quiche is set in the centre and the top is golden brown.

recipes.title: Ultimate IRISH Comfort Food Cabbage BACON MASHED potato CRISPY Pancake Rolls with Guinness Gravy
ingredients: 150g cooked bacon (diced) (slightly increased for more flavour)
½ tsp brown sugar (optional, to balance bitterness)
steps: Make the batter: Whisk the flour, salt and sugar, then whisk in the eggs, milk, oil and melted butter to a smooth pancake batter. Let it rest while you prepare the filling so the flour hydrates.
Boil the potatoes: Boil the potatoes in lightly salted water until tender.
Infuse the milk: Warm the milk with the chopped scallions and some of the butter for a minute or two to soften them and flavour the milk.

Cook the cabbage: Melt butter in a pan and sauté the finely diced onion to take off the rawness, then add the cabbage with a little salt and black pepper. Stir through the diced cooked bacon and let it cool.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with the infused milk and scallions, then let them cool.
Cook the pancakes: In a 10 in pan over a lowish flame, swirl in a thin layer of batter, cook until set, flip and cook the other side, adding a little butter if you like. Repeat with the rest.

Mix and roll: Combine the mash with the cabbage and bacon, then mix in the grated cheddar. Spoon some filling onto each pancake, fold in the sides and roll up like a burrito. (They can be frozen at this stage.)

Guinness gravy: Put the chopped onion in a pan with a little water, butter, salt and brown sugar, cover and boil until the water evaporates and the onions soften. Fry in butter until they colour, stir in about a tablespoon of flour and cook it out, add the Worcestershire sauce, then pour in the Guinness and let the alcohol cook off. Add about a teaspoon of Dijon and the stock, and simmer gently until thickened as you like.
Bread the rolls: Dip each roll in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs, and set seam-side down.
Fry: Heat oil to about 160–170°C and fry the rolls seam-side down first, a few at a time, until crisp and golden all over. Serve with the Guinness gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m2ty90UgV-o
Uploaded 2025-02-06.

recipes.title: CLASSIC Gobi Manchurian  Indo Chinese – The ULTIMATE Fusion Dish
ingredients: For the Cauliflower Batter (Frying the Gobi):
1/2 tsp red chili powder or flakes
1 tbsp red chili sauce or use sweet chilli sauce
1 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water (for thickening)
Also used in the video (amounts not stated):
Chinese black vinegar was used as the vinegar
steps: Blanch the cauliflower: Blanch the florets in salted boiling water about 3 minutes (up to 4 for large florets) so they're cooked but still firm, then drain and let cool.

Make the batter: Mix the tempura flour with pepper, salt, chilli flakes and the ginger-garlic paste, then add water and the egg (optional) to a smooth batter thick enough to coat the cauliflower without being heavy. (The description also lists cornflour.)
Fry: Heat oil to about 170°C. Coat the florets in the batter and fry until crisp and lightly coloured. Drain on a rack over kitchen towel so they stay crisp.

Start the sauce: In a small pan with a little of the frying oil, cook the garlic, ginger, slit green chillies, onion and capsicum until softened without burning. Add about ½ teaspoon of sugar and some black pepper.
Season the sauce: Add about a teaspoon of vinegar, a tablespoon of soy sauce, and the ketchup and chilli sauce.

Make it a gravy: For the gravy version, add water, then stir in a cornflour slurry (about a tablespoon of cornflour with a tablespoon of water was used) until it thickens to a glossy, pourable sauce; it thickens further the longer it cooks.

Finish and serve: Turn off the heat, stir in most of the spring onion greens and spoon the sauce over the crispy cauliflower. Garnish with the rest of the spring onions and serve with rice or noodles.

recipes.title: EASY Creamy BEEF and Bowtie Pasta with Alfredo Sauce Delicious
ingredients: 480 ml — 2 cups heavy cream (or half-and-half for a lighter version)
1/4 tsp red pepper flakes (optional, for a slight kick)
steps: Cook the pasta: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil and cook the bowtie pasta until al dente. Drain, keeping back about a cup of the pasta water.

Brown the beef: Meanwhile, heat a little olive oil in a pan (add a splash more if your beef is lean) and add the beef, breaking it up. Season with a little salt and pepper and the Italian seasoning, and cook until the moisture has cooked off and the beef takes on some colour. Remove the beef and set it aside; wipe out the pan if there is oil left in it.
Start the sauce: Melt the butter in the pan and cook the garlic for no more than 30 seconds, without colouring it, just to take out the raw aroma.
Warm the cream: Pour in the cream and warm it over a lowish heat without boiling. No extra salt is needed at this point, as the cheese is salty.

Add cheese and seasoning: When a few small bubbles appear, stir in the mozzarella and Parmesan, then the optional chilli (red pepper) flakes and some freshly ground nutmeg. Let it thicken a little; if it gets too thick, loosen with some pasta water.
Combine and serve: Return the beef and the pasta to the sauce and stir to coat, adding a little pasta water if the sauce is too thick. Serve topped with a little Parmesan and parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KSQkP7RNSfM
Uploaded 2025-02-04.

recipes.title: Ultimate IRISH Comfort Food, Cabbage, BACON, and MASHED Potato Casserole
ingredients: 2 pounds (900g) potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
2 cups (200g) shredded cheddar cheese (or any strong, mature cheese of your choice)
½ cup panko breadcrumbs (for extra crunch)
steps: Crisp the peels: Toss the potato peelings with a little oil and a sprinkle of salt and roast them in the oven until crisp, keeping an eye on them. Serve them as a side.
Boil the potatoes: Boil the peeled potatoes until tender for mashing.
Infuse the milk: Chop the green onions into chunky pieces and add them to the milk with some black pepper. Warm the milk and stir in a little butter.
Cook the bacon: Melt a chunk of butter in a pan and cook the chopped bacon until cooked through (crisp if you like). Remove it, leaving the fat and juices in the pan.

Cook the cabbage: Soften the onion and garlic in the bacon fat to take out the rawness, then add the roughly chopped cabbage (core removed) and black pepper. Salt is optional, as the bacon is salty. Cook it down for about 7 minutes. Stir the bacon back in, or keep it aside for layering.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with the infused milk, green onions and a little butter.
Make the topping: Crush the Ritz crackers, mix with the panko breadcrumbs and stir in the melted butter.

Layer: In a baking dish, layer the mash, cabbage and bacon, distributing the bacon evenly, then add cheddar and more cabbage and bacon. Spread a thin final layer of mashed potato on top. It doesn't need to be neat.

Top and bake: Scatter over the cracker and crumb topping, then more cheddar, keeping the cheese towards the inside. Bake at about 170–180°C (360°F) for 15–20 minutes, until golden on top and bubbling.

Quick onion gravy (optional): Boil sliced onions in a little water with a tiny bit of salt and sugar under a lid until soft. Once the water is gone, add butter and let them caramelise. Pour in your gravy and thicken it to your liking. The gravy itself isn't in the ingredient list.
Serve: Let the casserole cool for a minute, then cut out portions and serve with the onion gravy and crispy peels.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kwuD2_UI9Do
Uploaded 2025-02-03.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven: Bake at 360°F (180°C) for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown and bubbling.

recipes.title: BOSTON Cream Pie CHEESECAKE
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups (150g) graham cracker crumbs (use gluten-free crumbs for a GF option)
1 1/2 cups (180g) digestive biscuit crumbs (about 12-14 biscuits, finely crushed)
1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar (optional, since digestives are already slightly sweet)
steps: Make the base: Line a 9 in springform tin and preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Crush the digestive biscuits or graham crackers to crumbs. For a firmer base, mix in 1–2 tablespoons of plain flour (gluten-free works too), then the sugar and melted butter until fully combined.
Bake the base: Press the crumb mixture evenly into the tin and bake for 10–15 minutes. Let it cool a little.
Make the filling: Beat the softened cream cheese with the sugar, then beat in the sour cream and vanilla. Add the eggs one at a time along with the cornflour (cornstarch), mixing until smooth.

Bake the cheesecake: Pour the filling over the cooled base and give the tin a little jiggle to level it. Bake for 40–45 minutes, until set around the edge but still slightly jiggly in the centre (not runny).
Cool slowly, then chill: Turn off the oven, wedge the door open and leave the cheesecake to cool inside for about an hour. Any cracks will be covered. Then refrigerate for up to about 4 hours.

Make the pastry cream: In a pan, whisk the sugar, egg yolks, cornflour and a little of the milk, then whisk in the rest of the milk (the video also mentions a pinch of salt). Heat gently, stirring, until it thickens into custard. Take it off the heat, stir in the butter and vanilla, and let it cool a little.
Layer the custard: Spread the cooled pastry cream over the cheesecake, smooth it and return it to the fridge to set for about 1–1½ hours.

Make the ganache: Warm the cream until steaming but not boiling, and pour it over the chopped chocolate (the video gives the chocolate a head start over a pan of boiling water). Stir until smooth with the vanilla, then let it cool so it doesn't melt the custard.

Finish and set: Pour the ganache over the top and let it run down the sides; the safer option is to keep it on top and chill longer. Refrigerate for about 45 minutes to an hour until the top sets, then remove the paper and slice. Chilling the cheesecake for 4 hours or overnight before topping is recommended.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HT38G7Ius-Y
Uploaded 2025-02-02.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 325°F (163°C); Bake base 10 -15 mins; Bake cheesecake 40 - 45 mins.

recipes.title: EASY One-Pot CHICKEN STEW – COMFORT Food at Its BEST!
ingredients: 900g — 2 lbs bone-in chicken thighs or drumsticks (or chicken breast)
1 tablespoon olive oil — Oil of choice – I used coconut
¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional, for heat)
Potatoes, peeled and diced I used new potatoes
2 ears fresh corn, cut into thirds. I used baby corn
½ cup spinach leaves (optional, for freshness)
¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped (plus extra for garnish)
½ cup 120ml heavy cream (or ¼ cup heavy cream + ¼ cup coconut milk for balance)
Juice of 1 lime (plus extra wedges for serving)
Salt and black pepper to taste
Chopped celery (used in the video; not in the description list)
steps: Season the chicken: Mix the smoked paprika, cumin and cayenne (or red pepper flakes) together. Season the chicken pieces lightly with salt, then rub some of the spice mix over them. You don't need to smother them.
Prep the veg: Halve the new potatoes (skins on), and chop the celery, onion, garlic and carrots. Cut the baby corn into pieces.

Sear the chicken: Heat the oil in a large pan and sear the chicken, skin-side down, until it has some colour and is about 60–65% cooked. There's no need to crisp the skin, as it will soften in the stew. Remove and set aside, leaving the flavour in the pan.
Soften the aromatics: Add the onion and garlic to the pan and soften them to take away the rawness.

Add veg and stock: Add the potatoes, carrots, celery and corn. Season with pepper; skip extra salt, since the chicken is salted and the stock carries salt. Pour in the chicken stock (and water) to at least the level of the vegetables, then add the thyme and bay leaf.

Simmer: Bring to the boil, then turn down to a simmer, cover and cook for about 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally so nothing sticks, until the potatoes and vegetables are tender. Add the frozen peas towards the end, as they only need a short cook.

Finish: Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the chopped coriander (cilantro), the lime juice to taste and the cream. Return the chicken and any pan juices to the stew and heat the chicken back through. Serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9rVH2Few75I
Uploaded 2025-02-01.

recipes.title: CLASSIC Old Fashioned GOULASH – EASY One Pot COMFORT Food
ingredients: ½ cup beef broth (or use all broth for richer flavour)
½ teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional, for a mild kick)
1 cup 120g shredded cheddar cheese (optional, for topping)
steps: Sauté the aromatics: Heat the olive oil in a large pan and add the garlic and onion. Sauté for about a minute to take the rawness out of the onions.

Brown the beef: Add the minced beef and season with salt and black pepper. Add the oregano, basil and the optional chilli flakes, and stir them through so the spices bloom in the oil and fat. Keep stir-frying until no red or pink remains.

Build the sauce: Stir in about 3 tablespoons of tomato purée (paste), then the chopped tomatoes and beef broth until fully incorporated. Add about 2½ cups of water and about a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce, and bring back up to a boil.

Cook the macaroni: Once boiling, stir in the elbow macaroni, turn the heat down and simmer uncovered for 15–20 minutes. Stir now and then so nothing sticks to the bottom; the pasta absorbs much of the liquid and leaves a good sauce.
Serve: When the pasta is cooked, serve topped with a spoonful of sour cream, a little grated cheddar and some chopped parsley. Crusty bread and butter goes well alongside.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=puWF4-3ehdU
Uploaded 2025-01-31.

recipes.title: ICONIC AUSSIE Bunnings SNAG 3 Ways! and the DEBATE
ingredients: Aussie beef sausages (beef is traditional, but pork works too)
Brown onions, sliced into thin rings
A pinch of sugar (used in the video for the onions)
The video description lists no quantities; use as many sausages, slices and onions as you are serving.
steps: Caramelise the onions quickly: Put the sliced onions in a pan with a little oil and some water, a tiny pinch of salt and a little sugar. Boil until the water cooks off and the oil takes over, then cover with a lid and let them brown, stirring now and then, until caramelised. Remove from the pan.
Cook the snags: Cook the sausages in the pan (traditionally on a grill) until they are as brown as you like. Don't worry if they plump up and burst.

Classic build: Lay a slice of white sandwich bread flat, put onions down the middle, then lay the sausage diagonally across the bread. Add tomato sauce, plus yellow mustard or barbecue sauce if you like.
Elevated build: Butter the bread first, then add the onions, the sausage and tomato sauce, layered over or under the sausage, or both.
Onions-on-top build: Put the sausage on the bread first and pile the onions over the top, finishing with tomato sauce.
Serve: Wrap each snag in a folded napkin or kitchen towel and serve straight away.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hl1ZGQvj4kI
Uploaded 2025-01-30.

recipes.title: Homemade BEEF SAUSAGES – JUICY Flavourful and EASY to Make
ingredients: 2 kg ground beef (80/20 mix for a good balance of fat and meat)
18 g kosher salt or 14 g table salt
5 g garlic powder (or 4 cloves fresh minced garlic)
50 g bread crumbs or rusk (optional for binding)
3 meters of sausage collagen casings (natural hog casings, soaked and rinsed)
steps: Mix the spices: Combine the salt, paprika, black pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, nutmeg, oregano, thyme and coriander in a bowl first so they don't go into the meat in lumps.
Season the beef: Put the cold beef mince in a large bowl and, wearing gloves, work the spice mix in a bit at a time.
Add water and binders: Work in some of the cold water, then the breadcrumbs, then the rest of the water. Mix in the optional milk powder to help bind, and keep mixing until the meat gets sticky.

Stuff the casings: Load the mixture into a sausage stuffer (ideally bolted down), packing it to avoid air bubbles, and wind the handle to push the meat into the casings. You can also stuff them by hand.
Link the sausages: Pinch the filled casing at your chosen length and twist, alternating the twist direction for each sausage, to get roughly even links.
Rest: Refrigerate the sausages for a few hours (the description suggests overnight) so the flavours develop.
Cook: Fry the sausages in a little oil over a moderate, not too hot, heat, cooking them slowly until browned and cooked through. Serve with brown sauce if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27gFuuBVX5o
Uploaded 2025-01-29.

recipes.title: QUICK and EASY Chickpea CURRY Recipe – IN 20 Minutes
ingredients: 2 cans chickpeas (400g each), drained and rinsed
Cooked rice or naan for serving
steps: Prep the chickpeas: Drain and rinse the two cans of chickpeas.

Cook the aromatics: Heat a small amount of oil (coconut oil in the video) and cook the onion, then the freshly grated garlic and ginger, to take out the rawness. It doesn't matter if the onions colour. Turn the heat down a little.
Split the coconut milk: Add some of the coconut milk and cook it down until the water evaporates and the oil separates, giving an intensely flavoured oily base.

Fry the spices: Add a little more coconut milk, and when it starts to bubble, stir in the curry powder, garam masala, chilli powder and paprika, cooking them in the way you would a curry paste. Keep the heat steady and not too high.

Add tomato: Stir in the tomato purée and about a teaspoon of sugar to balance the acidity, then add the tomatoes (snip whole tinned tomatoes in the can, or use chopped). Add the optional curry leaves, a little salt and black pepper.

Add the rest of the coconut milk: Pour in more of the coconut milk and bring it back up to temperature, then add the remaining coconut milk and the chickpeas, and stir through some chopped coriander (cilantro).
Simmer: Cook for about 10–15 minutes, no more, stirring now and then. It thickens a little but should stay a soupy curry.
Serve: Garnish with more coriander and serve with basmati rice (the video uses 1½ cups water to 1 cup rice in a rice cooker) or mashed-potato flatbreads.

recipes.title: MASHED Potato CRUMPETS The Perfect Way to Use Leftovers
ingredients: 1 tsp dried yeast plus 50 ml lukewarm water
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: Combine the plain flour, baking powder, salt and sugar in a bowl.
Activate the yeast: Stir about a teaspoon of dried yeast into the 50 ml of lukewarm water and leave it to see whether it bubbles. If it doesn't, you need fresh yeast.
Rub in the potato: Add the mashed potato to the flour and rub it between your fingers and thumbs, as you would for pastry, to break it down. A couple of small lumps will dissolve in the batter.
Make the batter: Add the yeast mixture and the lukewarm water and mix to a thick batter, adjusting the water slightly if needed.
Prove: Cover and leave for 15–40 minutes (about an hour in the video) until the batter is covered in bubbles.
Prepare the rings: Brush crumpet rings with butter to stop sticking, heat a buttered pan, then set the rings in the pan.

Cook slowly: Ladle batter into each ring (about half a ladle, not full) and cook slowly over a gentle heat so the heat rises through and opens up the holes. When the shiny wet surface turns dull and set, flip and briefly cook the other side.
Repeat and serve: Re-butter the rings and repeat with the remaining batter. Let the crumpets cool a little, then toast and serve with butter, honey or a fried egg.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8XHn6taWReQ

recipes.title: If there is MASHED POTATO, FLOUR, WATER, at home, EVERYONE CAN EASILY MAKE THIS FLATBREAD
ingredients: 300g (2 cups) Mashed potato (smooth, no lumps, can be lightly salted)
660–720ml (2 3/4–3 cups) Water (mix of warm and cold, adjust for consistency)
40g (3 tbsp) Coconut oil (or other cooking oil)
½ tsp baking powder (optional; baking powder isn't necessary—it’s an optional enhancement and can give a slightly bitter taste).
steps: Combine flour and potato: Mix the mashed potato into the flour to loosen any lumps. This is optional, but it gives the blending a head start.

Make the batter: Add the coconut oil (or other oil), up to a teaspoon of salt, about a teaspoon of sugar and the water, give it a mix, then blend with a stick blender (or a stand mixer or food processor) until smooth with no bits of potato. No resting is needed.
Oil the pan once: Heat a small pan with a splash of oil or butter and rub it around to leave a thin film. That is all the oil used for the whole batch.

Add the batter off the heat: Once the pan is hot, lower the flame and, holding the pan off the heat, add a ladleful of batter (a 60–80 ml ladle) and swirl it around gently. If the pan is too hot, the batter seals, slides and breaks up.

Cook the first side: Return the pan to a low heat and leave the flatbread alone. It sticks at first, then turns transparent and releases naturally. When the white of the batter has cooked out, flip it.

Press and puff: Keep flipping as needed. Protecting your hand with kitchen towel (escaping steam is hot), press down lightly on the flatbread so it cooks through and puffs up like a pitta. If a small hole appears before the first flip, dab a little batter over it to seal it.
Repeat and serve: Repeat with the remaining batter (about 10 flatbreads). Serve with curries or use as wraps. They reheat well without drying out and freeze well.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tCYtWBuP4Pw
Uploaded 2025-01-26.

recipes.title: Juicy Pork Hoisin Burgers & Asian Slaw
ingredients: 1 clove garlic, minced 1/2 tsp if powder
1 teaspoon grated ginger 1/2 tsp if powder
2 teaspoons honey or brown sugar (optional, for sweetness)
1 teaspoon sriracha or chilli paste (optional, for heat)
steps: Make the slaw dressing first: Mix about 2 tablespoons of mayo with about 3 tablespoons of vinegar (rice vinegar, or apple cider vinegar as in the video), about a tablespoon of soy sauce and a tablespoon of sesame oil, 2 teaspoons of brown sugar (or honey), about ½ teaspoon of ginger and a teaspoon of sriracha. Season with a little white pepper, plus lime juice if you like. Making the slaw first lets the flavours blend.

Make the slaw: Finely slice the green cabbage (no core) and about a cup of red cabbage, then add the julienned carrot, thinly sliced spring onions and bell pepper, and the coriander. Toss everything with the dressing in a large bowl.

Mix the burgers: To the pork mince, add 2 tablespoons of hoisin sauce, about a tablespoon of light soy sauce, about a teaspoon of sesame oil, ½ teaspoon each of garlic powder and ginger powder (or fresh), a couple of tablespoons of finely crushed panko and the chopped spring onion. Mix well by hand until sticky.
Shape: Divide into evenly sized patties (weigh them if you like).
Cook low and slow: Fry the patties in a little oil over a low heat (or grill or oven-bake them). Let them sear, then flip two or three times until caramelised on both sides and cooked through.
Build the burgers: Toast the bottom buns and spread on hoisin sauce straight from the jar. Add lettuce, the burger, red onion and cucumber, then top with slaw and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=05rUCFw5ivM
Uploaded 2025-01-25.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: SWEET and SOUR BEEF Meatballs Tangy, Crispy, Delicious Chinese Style
ingredients: Onion: 1 small, finely grated (about 50g or 1/4 cup)
For the Sweet and Sour Sauce:
Rice Vinegar or White Vinegar: 1/3 cup (80 ml)
Plum Sauce or Hoisin Sauce (optional): 1 tbsp (20 g)
Additional Water or Chicken Broth: 1/4 cup (60 ml)
Red Bell Pepper (optional): 1 small, diced (about 70 g or 1/2 cup)
steps: Mix the meatballs: Combine the beef mince with the beaten egg, grated onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, a little pepper (white or black), ground ginger, salt and soy sauce, and mix well.
Roll: Roll the mixture into balls about 1 inch across, keeping them roughly the same size.
Pre-fry: Fry the meatballs in oil (shallow-frying works too) until coloured all over. They don't need to be cooked through yet, as they're fried again in batter. Set them aside to cool a little.

Make the sauce: In a pan, combine the ketchup, vinegar (apple cider or white), sugar, a little plum sauce, the pineapple juice and about 2 tablespoons of light soy sauce. Mix the cornflour with the water to a slurry, stir it in and start heating.
Add the veg: Add the diced pepper and pineapple chunks straight into the sauce and simmer for a couple of minutes, until thickened and the pepper softens but keeps some crunch.
Batter: Mix the self-raising flour with about 180 ml of water to a batter. Drop the meatballs in and turn to coat, lifting each one out with a skewer.

Fry until crisp: Reheat the strained frying oil and fry the battered meatballs, turning, until golden and crispy all over. Fish out the loose batter scraps as you go. You can re-dip and fry again to fill any gaps.
Serve: Drain briefly on a rack, then serve with the sweet and sour sauce and a little greenery.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P8vCOKvWxCw
Uploaded 2025-01-24.

recipes.title: BEEF Mushroom BLACK BEAN sauce and NOODLES
ingredients: 350g beef, thinly sliced — I used Chuck Roll, topside is good
300g wide rice noodles (ho fun or similar)
1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
¼ cup water or chicken broth
1 tablespoon cornstarch or potato starch mixed with 2 tablespoons water (optional, for thickening)
steps: Coat the beef: Mix the thinly sliced beef with a little oil and a splash of Shaoxing wine and set it aside while you prep. A good cut doesn't need baking soda or a long marinade.
Prep the veg: Dice about half a green pepper and some onion. Slice the red chillies on the diagonal; they are for colour.

Mix the sauce: Combine about a tablespoon of Shaoxing wine, about half a tablespoon of dark soy, about a teaspoon of oyster sauce (or soy sauce mixed with a little sugar), the sugar and a splash of sesame oil.
Stir-fry the mushrooms and beef: Heat oil in a wok and stir-fry the mushrooms until coloured, then remove them. Stir-fry the beef quickly and add it to the mushrooms.
Cook the aromatics: In the juices left in the wok, stir-fry the garlic, onion and green pepper, letting any water evaporate.

Add noodles and sauce: Add a splash of water (or chicken stock) and the noodles (fresh in the video, but any noodle works), toss, then add the sauce and the prepared fermented black beans, plus the beef and mushrooms. The order doesn't matter.
Thicken and finish: Optionally stir in a little cornflour slurry to thicken. Turn off the heat, add a shake of white pepper and the sliced chillies, stir through and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-N2M5HVU0hU
Uploaded 2025-01-23.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: MEDITERRANEAN Eggplant Rolls A BEEFY CHEESY Herb Infused Delight
ingredients: 350g minced meat (beef, pork, or a mix)
1 tsp Tomato paste mixed with a little water for brushing
2 tbsp olive oil/butter (to mix with breadcrumbs)
steps: Salt the aubergines: Top and tail the aubergines (eggplants), slice them lengthwise and soak the slices in a bowl of salted water to draw out moisture.
Start the filling: Heat olive oil in a pan and cook the finely chopped onion and garlic (plus bell pepper if using) for about a minute.
Cook the mince: Add the mince, break it up and cook it through, seasoning with salt and pepper. Stir in about a teaspoon of cumin and about a tablespoon of Italian herbs.

Add tomato and stock: Stir in a couple of tablespoons of tomato paste and cook for a minute to take off the sourness, then add the stock. You want a moist but not wet, fairly tight filling with no runny liquid. Turn off the heat and let it cool.

Pre-bake the slices: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Drain and pat the aubergine slices dry, lay them overlapping on a parchment-lined tray, brush with olive oil and season lightly with Italian herbs and a little garlic powder. Bake for about 20–25 minutes.
Fill: Spread the meat mixture over the aubergine, stopping short of one end. Scatter over grated mozzarella and a little Parmesan.

Roll: Starting at the filled end, use the parchment to roll it up towards the empty end, squashing it down and tucking small chunks of mozzarella in as you roll. Push back any filling that falls out. It's hot, so take care.

Top and bake: Mix a little tomato paste with water and brush it over the roll. Top with breadcrumbs (mixed with olive oil or butter), oregano, more mozzarella and the remaining Parmesan. Bake for about 15–25 minutes, until golden and bubbling.
Rest and slice: Let it rest (the video waits about 20 minutes so it holds together), garnish with parsley and slice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oBx9dlD9qJs
Uploaded 2025-01-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Slices on a parchment-lined baking tray and bake at 180°C (356°F) for 20-25 minutes; Bake the assembled dish at 180°C (356°F) for 15 minutes, or until the cheese is melted, golden, and bubbly.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Crispy BBQ Chicken Thigh Roll Ups with Cheesy Herb Filling
ingredients: 1/2 cup shredded cheddar or mozzarella cheese (or a mix of both)
1/2 cup BBQ sauce (your favourite variety, or the sauce below)
1 tbsp olive oil (for greasing the dish)
Diced tomato, diced onion and garlic (used in the filling in the video; no amounts given)
1/8 tsp salt (a pinch, or to taste)
A pinch of garlic powder or onion powder
steps: Make the BBQ sauce: In a pan, combine about ½ cup ketchup, a tablespoon of honey, the sriracha, ½ teaspoon smoked paprika, about a tablespoon of brown sugar, the white vinegar, ½ teaspoon yellow mustard, a little salt and black pepper, and the optional Worcestershire sauce and garlic powder. Heat gently until it just starts to thicken, keeping it brushable, then let it cool.
Flatten and marinate: Lay the chicken thighs skin-side down and pound them lightly to an even thickness. Brush a little BBQ sauce over the flesh side and leave to marinate for at least an hour.
Make the filling: Finely dice the tomato and onion and mince some garlic, then mix with the shredded cheese and chopped parsley.

Roll: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and oil a baking tray. Spoon filling onto each thigh, add a slice of burger cheese if using, and roll up with the skin on the outside. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until the skin starts to crisp.
Glaze: Brush the tops with more BBQ sauce and return to the oven for about 5 minutes to caramelise. The chicken should reach 74°C (165°F).
Serve: Rest for a couple of minutes, garnish with parsley and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAa8T1sC5z0
Uploaded 2025-01-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C); Bake in the oven for 25-30 minutes or until the chicken is fully cooked and reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Cheese and Onion Pasties – Mash Potato Pastry - A Perfect Savoury Treat
ingredients: 200g mashed potatoes (cold, no added milk or butter)
steps: Make the pastry: Mix the cold mashed potato with the flour, cornflour (cornstarch) and salt, then rub in the cold cubed butter to fine crumbs. If your mash already has lots of butter or milk, you may need to reduce the butter. Mix in the egg yolk for richness and add cold water only as needed to bring it into a dough; it is already quite sticky. A food processor works too.
Rest: Wrap the dough in cling film and flatten it slightly so it holds its shape for rolling.

Caramelise the onions: Put the thinly sliced onions in a lidded pan with the sugar, a little salt, the butter and oil, and the water. Cover and boil so they steam and soften, stirring occasionally. Once the water evaporates, uncover and let them caramelise properly in the butter. Turn off the heat and cool.
Make the filling: Mix the cream cheese with the cooled onions, grated cheddar, thyme, salt, black pepper and about ½–1 teaspoon of Dijon mustard until fully combined.
Roll and cut: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and line a tray. Roll the pastry out on a floured surface to about 3 mm and cut rounds about 15 cm across (the video gets five).
Fill and shape: Spoon filling onto each round, fold over into a half-moon (or bring the edges up over the top), make sure the seam is joined, and crimp with a floured fork.
Bake: Brush with beaten egg and bake for about 12–15 minutes (the description says 20–25) until golden. Let them cool a little before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tFSqBeeeySk
Uploaded 2025-01-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F); Bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown.

recipes.title: The Ultimate FLOURLESS CHOCOLATE Cake – A Gluten Free Dessert Dream
steps: Melt the chocolate: Heat the oven to 170°C (340°F) and line a 38 x 26 cm (15 x 10 in) tray with parchment. Melt the 120 g chocolate with the butter (in short microwave bursts or over boiling water), then stir in the milk.
Whip the whites: Beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt, adding the sugar gradually in a few additions, until stiff peaks form.
Combine: Beat the egg yolks with the vanilla, then mix in the melted chocolate. Fold in the whipped egg whites in two additions. There's no flour.
Bake: Spread the batter into the corners of the tray, level it and tap out the air, then bake for about 20 minutes until set, springy and coming away from the sides.
Turn out: Immediately flip the cake onto a parchment-lined rack and peel off the baking paper. If it won't come off, leave it, since the syrup still soaks through.

Make the syrup and cream: Dissolve the cocoa powder and sugar in the hot water for the syrup. Melt the 150 g chocolate with the 90 g cream until smooth. Whip the cold cream with the sugar, then fold the chocolate mixture and whipped cream together.

Layer: Trim the ragged edges and cut the cake into three equal pieces. Brush a layer with syrup, pipe or spread chocolate cream over it, and repeat to build the layers. Chill in the fridge for a couple of hours.

Make the glaze: Bloom the gelatin in the cold water for about 5 minutes. Heat the water, sugar, cocoa and cream in a pan until the sugar dissolves and it no longer feels gritty. Let it cool slightly, stir in the gelatin, then cover the surface with cling film and cool to a pourable temperature.

Glaze and set: Pour the glaze over the chilled cake and refrigerate for about an hour, until shiny and set. Top with chocolate flake if you like. Slice with a knife warmed in hot water, wiping it between cuts.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KRtmv_lDt5c

recipes.title: Have MASH potatoes MAKE PIZZA
ingredients: All-purpose/plain flour: 2 ½ cups (315g; adjust as needed)
For the Topping: suggested, but make your own:
Tomato sauce or passata: ¾ cup (180ml)
Fresh mozzarella: 1 ½ cups (225g), sliced or torn
Fresh basil leaves: A generous handful (15-20 leaves)
Optional: Grated Parmesan cheese for extra flavour (30g)
Pepperoni slices (for the second pizza in the video; no amount given)
steps: Make the dough: Mix the cold mashed potato with the flour, baking powder and salt. Allow for any salt already in leftover mash. Add the beaten egg and work it together into a dough.
Divide: Split the dough roughly in half to make two 10 in pizzas.

Shape in the tray: Line pizza trays with parchment and press each piece of dough out directly in the tray, keeping it no thinner than about ½ inch, since it won't rise like a yeast dough. Push up the edges to form a crust.
Pre-bake the base: Brush lightly with olive oil and bake at 220°C (425°F) for about 10–12 minutes, until it takes some colour and is firm.

Top: Spread the tomato sauce over the base. For a margherita-style pizza, add mozzarella (or any melting cheese), torn basil leaves and a little Parmesan. For the second, use sauce, cheese and overlapping pepperoni, plus oregano if you like.
Bake again: Return to the oven for about 8–15 minutes, checking at 10, until the cheese has melted. Finish the margherita with more basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
For a crisper base: Baking on parchment keeps the base soft. For a crunchy bottom, bake straight in the tin or cook it a little longer.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WtJdfCfF1Ek

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake until lightly golden and firm (about 10-12 minutes at 220°C/425°F); Add your desired toppings and bake at 220°C/425°F for 8-10 minutes, or until the toppings are heated and the cheese is melted.

recipes.title: EASY MEXICAN Potato Rolls with Spiced CHEESY Chicken Filling
ingredients: 2 fresh jalapeños (approx. 40g), finely chopped, seeds removed for less heat
1 spring onion or red onion (50g), finely chopped
2 tablespoons masa harina or all-purpose flour (20g)
1 tbsp Fajita seasoning mix – see seasoning mix below
or instead of the fajita seasoning:
2 tablespoons vegetable oil or avocado oil (30ml)
200g (7 oz) ground chicken or shredded cooked chicken
1 red bell pepper and 1 poblano pepper (combined 150g), finely diced. (Optional)
1 teaspoon chili powder or chipotle powder (2g)
30g (1 oz) shredded Monterey Jack or queso Oaxaca
1 tbsp fajita seasoning – see seasoning mix below
or instead of the fajita seasoning:
1/4 teaspoon chili powder or chipotle powder (0.5g)
Homemade Fajita Seasoning Mix (300 g; mix all in a bowl):
80g chili powder — gochugaru Korean red chilli powder -
steps: Grate and drain the potatoes: Grate the potatoes, then squeeze out as much liquid as possible through a sieve and leave them to drip while you prep the veg.

Mix the potato layer: In a bowl, combine the diced red pepper, red onion, deseeded jalapeños and chopped coriander (cilantro). Add the potato and mix well so it doesn't clump. Stir in the beaten eggs, a couple of tablespoons of flour and about a tablespoon of fajita seasoning (or the cumin and smoked paprika).
Bake the potato sheet: Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread the mixture evenly on a parchment-lined tray and bake for about 20–25 minutes until firm. Let it cool.

Make the red sauce: Mix the tomato paste into the chicken stock with a little black pepper, about a tablespoon of fajita seasoning, about a teaspoon of garlic powder and up to a teaspoon of lime juice. Go easy on salt if your stock is salty.

Cook the filling: Heat oil in a pan and cook the chicken (cubed breast in the video; mince works too) until it starts to colour, then add the diced red onion and garlic and cook off the rawness. Season with fajita seasoning, then add the red sauce, keeping the filling thick. Turn the heat down, stir in grated cheese to make a sticky filling, then take it off the heat.
Roll: Cut the potato sheet into strips (about six), spoon filling onto each and roll them up. They don't need to be neat.
Bake and serve: Bake for about 15 minutes until the cheese melts and they brown a little. Serve with a spoonful of sour cream and jalapeños.

recipes.title: Raspberry Roll Cake - Swiss Roll
ingredients: 55g oil (neutral, like vegetable or sunflower oil)
A small amount of pink food colour
20g powdered sugar (or 40g sugar if skipping condensed milk)
Fresh raspberries (to decorate, as in the video; optional)
steps: Prepare: Line a tray with parchment and preheat the oven to about 170°C (340°F).
Make the yolk batter: Mix the egg yolks with the oil, milk and vanilla, then mix in the flour and as much pink food colouring as you like.
Whip the whites: Whisk the egg whites, adding the sugar gradually, to soft-to-firm peaks. Don't overbeat, or the cake tends to crack when rolled.

Fold and bake: Fold the whites into the yolk batter, pour it down the middle of the tray, spread it to the sides and tap the tray. Bake for about 18–25 minutes, until the sponge springs back when pressed and a toothpick comes out clean.
Roll while warm: Slide the cake out on its parchment onto a rack, let it cool for about a minute, then gently roll it up with the parchment and leave it to cool completely.
Whip the filling: Whip the chilled cream with the powdered sugar and condensed milk (or double the sugar instead of using condensed milk).
Fill and roll: Gently unroll the cake, spread on raspberry jam (not quite to the end), then a layer of cream. Roll it back up, peeling off the paper as you go, and wrap it in clean parchment.
Chill and serve: Refrigerate for about 30 minutes to an hour. Trim the ends, then pipe on extra cream and add raspberries if you like before slicing.

recipes.title: Swedish Dill CHICKEN - Forget IKEA Meatballs!
ingredients: 4–6 bone-in chicken thighs or drumsticks (or a whole chicken, cut into pieces)
1 cup 240 ml whole milk (or cream for a richer sauce) I used a little more milk to thin
1 tsp white vinegar or lemon juice
2 tbsp fresh dill, chopped (or 1 tbsp dried dill)
Optional: 1-2 tbsp sour cream for extra creaminess
steps: Brown the chicken: Melt a couple of tablespoons of butter in a pan and add the bone-in, skin-on chicken skin-side down, seasoning with salt and pepper. Brown both sides for about 5–7 minutes, turning as needed. It only needs to be partly cooked, as it finishes in the sauce. Remove and set aside, keeping the buttery juices in the pan.
Soften the onion: Sauté the chopped onion in the pan juices, low and slow, for up to 5 minutes.
Make the roux: Stir in a couple of tablespoons of flour and cook for about a minute to take away the raw taste.

Build the sauce: Stir in the chicken stock over a moderate heat, then the milk (or cream), and let it thicken slightly. Add the Dijon mustard and about ½–1 teaspoon of lemon juice (or vinegar), then the bay leaf.
Simmer the chicken: Return the chicken and any juices to the pan, cover and cook gently for about 20 minutes, until cooked through.
Finish the sauce: Take out the chicken and remove the bay leaf. Turn off the heat, stir in the chopped dill (about 2 tablespoons) and a couple of tablespoons of sour cream.
Serve: Serve the chicken with the dill sauce, creamy mashed potato and a few gherkins.

recipes.title: BEEF CHOW FUN – Cantonese Stir Fried Rice Noodles - Quick & Easy
ingredients: 300g wide rice noodles (ho fun or similar)
½ tsp Baking soda (bicarbonate of soda)
Bean sprouts (used in the video; no amount given)
Salt and white pepper to taste
steps: Marinate the beef: Toss the sliced sirloin with a tiny amount of baking soda (to tenderise), a little light soy sauce, a splash of sesame oil and about a teaspoon of cornflour. Add a little water if you like (the beef absorbs it and stays moist). Scrunch it together and leave for about 20 minutes.
Prep the veg: Have the garlic ready, slice the half onion into long pieces to match the noodles and break them apart, and chop the green onion. Have the bean sprouts and wide fresh noodles ready.
Stir-fry: Heat oil in a wok until hot. Add the garlic and onion, then the noodles, about a tablespoon of oyster sauce and about a tablespoon of soy sauce.
Add the beef and finish: Add the beef and stir-fry until cooked through, then toss in the bean sprouts and green onions. Finish with a shake of pepper and serve.

recipes.title: Double CHEESY NEW Potato and CHORIZO Hash
ingredients: Fresh parsley or spring onions, chopped (for garnish)
steps: Par-boil the potatoes: Put about 500g of new potatoes in a pan of salted water, slicing any big ones in half so they are roughly the same size. Boil for 5–7 minutes, just until they start to go tender, then drain.

Prep the rest: While they boil, cube the onion and put it in a bowl with the garlic. Cube the chorizo (take the skin off some or leave it on; the skin gives a little crunch). Pull the spinach leaves off their woody stems.

Crisp the chorizo: In a pan with a lid, heat a little olive oil over a moderate heat and cook the chorizo for about 5 minutes to crisp it and release its oil. Lift it out with a slotted spoon, leaving the oil in the pan.

Cook the onion, garlic and potatoes: Cook the onion and garlic in the chorizo oil for a minute to take off the rawness, then add the drained potatoes. Season with pepper and smoked paprika, but hold off on salt until you have tasted it, because the chorizo is salty. Fry until the potatoes take on some colour.
Make it a hash: Lightly crush some of the potatoes with the back of a spoon (or a masher) for texture, return the chorizo, and stir through some of the cheese so it is double cheesy.

Form and crisp the bottom: Set a cooking ring in the pan, pack the mixture into it and turn the heat down so a crust forms on the bottom. Top with the rest of the cheese. Add the spinach to the pan around the ring to wilt.

Melt the cheese: Put the lid on and cook low and slow until the cheese melts (or finish under the grill to crisp the top). Let it settle for a couple of minutes, mark it with a knife and lift off the ring.
Serve: Plate the hash with the wilted spinach, top with a fried egg and finish with a sprinkle of pepper.

recipes.title: ROASTED Garlic BUTTER Cauliflower STEAK, PARMESAN Sauce and  Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: For the Garlic Butter Cauliflower Steaks:
For the Creamy Garlic Parmesan Sauce:
1 tbsp all-purpose flour (or cornstarch for gluten-free)
½ cup heavy cream (or plant-based milk)
½ cup extra virgin olive oil
Optional: Lemon zest or red chilli flakes
steps: Start the mash: Put the peeled, cubed potatoes in salted water and boil until soft for mashing.
Make the garlic butter: Melt the butter and mix in the minced garlic, olive oil, a little pepper and salt (not much, as Parmesan goes on later) and about ½ teaspoon of paprika.
Cut the steaks: Leaving the core in, cut the cauliflower into steaks about an inch thick. If it breaks into florets, just cook them alongside.
Roast: Lay the steaks on a parchment-lined tray and brush the garlic butter generously over both sides. Roast for about 25–30 minutes, turning them halfway (the description gives 220°C / 430°F).

Infuse the herb oil: Warm about ½ cup of oil on a very low flame with garlic, fresh thyme (and rosemary) and pepper for about 5 minutes without burning. Turn off the flame and strain, keeping only the oil.

Make the Parmesan sauce: Melt about 2 tablespoons of butter, stir in the flour and cook out the raw taste, then add the cream. Add a little garlic powder (or fresh garlic), then the Parmesan, and stir as it thickens quickly. Finish with a pinch of nutmeg and a squeeze of lemon, then turn off the heat.
Mash the potatoes: Drain, then add a little butter, a little of the cream, black pepper and salt. Mash, leaving some texture if you like.

Plate up: Put the cauliflower steak on a bed of mash, squeeze over some lemon, spoon over the Parmesan sauce and drizzle with the herb oil. Add parsley if you like; the video serves it with peas and a slice of lemon.

recipes.title: Bang Bang Chicken Crispy, Spicy, and Irresistibly Delicious
ingredients: 2 chicken breasts (as used in the video)
Water, sugar, salt and garlic powder for the brine (amounts not given)
2 tsp paprika (for colour and a mild smokey flavour)
1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (adjust for spice level)
1 tsp white pepper (for a peppery kick)
1/2 tsp salt (use less if your sauce is salty)
1 tsp sugar (adds a touch of sweetness to balance the heat)
1/2 tsp ground coriander (for a citrusy, herbal note)
1/4 tsp ground ginger (adds a warm, aromatic kick)
1 tsp dried parsley or chives (for a fresh herbal element)
1/2 tsp Chinese five spice powder (optional, for depth of flavour)
Water, enough to form a batter
steps: Brine the chicken: Mix water with sugar, salt and garlic powder in a bowl. Skin the chicken breasts, check for bones and cut into bite-sized pieces, then put them in the brine for 1 hour (4 hours or overnight is even better; 30 minutes adds little).

Blanch: Drop the chicken into boiling water for about 2–3 minutes, just until the outside is cooked and opaque but the inside is still pink. Drain, spread on kitchen towel and let it air dry while the oil heats.
Make the batter: Gradually whisk water into the self-raising flour until you have a smooth, bubbly batter that is not too thick. Do not season the batter.
Season and batter: Sprinkle some of the bang bang seasoning over the chicken, then coat it in the batter. Keep some seasoning back for after frying.
Deep fry: Heat the oil to about 180°C (360°F). Fry the chicken in two batches, stirring, until puffed up and golden. Drain on a rack over kitchen towel.

Finish: Dust the hot chicken with more bang bang seasoning, drizzle over a little bang bang sauce (combine the listed sauce ingredients; mixing it isn't shown in the video) and serve the rest as a dip, scattered with green onion.

How to use — shake over chicken or shrimp before frying - shake after frying

Use it: Shake it over chicken, shrimp, Brussels sprouts or potatoes before frying, and again after frying.
