steps: Combine: In a bowl, add 3 tablespoons of mayo, 2 tablespoons of sweet chilli sauce, 1–2 teaspoons of sriracha to taste, and 1 teaspoon of honey or sugar (sugar is better if you make it in bulk).

recipes.title: 3 Foolproof Caramel Dulce de Leche Recipes No Fail Methods for Any Dessert
ingredients: 14 oz (397g) sweetened condensed milk (do not skip or substitute)
1/4 cup (60ml) golden syrup (instead of granulated sugar)
1 oven-safe glass jar or metal dish with a lid or foil to cover
Water (enough to fill the Instant Pot to the required level)
steps: Method 1, melt the sugar: Put the sugar in a pan over a low heat, give it a swirl and leave it to melt to an amber colour. Lift the pan off the heat if needed so it doesn't burn (the darker the caramel, the darker the sauce).
Add the butter: Stir in the cubed butter a little at a time, controlling the heat, until it melts in.

Add the milks: Carefully stir in the hot milk a little at a time (it will bubble), then the condensed milk. Stir gently over the lowest flame until it thickens, about 15 minutes in total. Stop a little before your ideal thickness, since it thickens more as it cools, and stop earlier for a pourable sauce.

Method 2, golden syrup: Gently warm the golden syrup until it bubbles, then melt in the butter. Add the hot milk, then the condensed milk, and cook, stirring every now and then, for up to about 15 minutes as the colour deepens. The video stops at about 14 minutes for a thicker caramel.

Method 3, Instant Pot dulce de leche: Pour the condensed milk into a metal jug or other suitable container (about 2 cans fit a 1 litre jug; check that the lid still closes freely with the jug inside). Cover with parchment tied on with string, trim the loose ends, then seal it with foil.

Pressure cook: Stand the jug on a trivet in the Instant Pot, add water to halfway up, and pressure cook for 60 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for at least 10 minutes (up to 20), then release the rest manually.
Finish: Remove the foil and parchment and stir. It thickens as it cools. To thin a thick caramel, warm it with a little milk or water in the microwave or a pan.

recipes.title: EASY Oven-Baked BACON-WRAPPED Chicken with Garlic Mustard Sauce
ingredients: 2 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (butterflied or pounded thin)
8 slices of streaky bacon or as much as you like
2 cups fresh spinach (or frozen, thawed, and squeezed dry)
1 cup grated mozzarella cheese (or cheddar for more flavour)
Optional: Fresh thyme or tarragon for added flavour
1 tbsp fresh tarragon or 1 tsp dried tarragon
steps: Prep the spinach and chicken: Get a pan of water on to boil. If the chicken breasts have skin, remove it (the video salts the skin and crisps it alongside later). Butterfly the large breasts in half from the thick end, then pound them thin under cling film or in a bag.
Blanch the spinach: Blanch the fresh spinach briefly in unseasoned water, drain and let it cool. Then squeeze out as much water as you can (if using frozen spinach, just thaw and squeeze it).

Make the stuffing: Tear up the spinach and mix it with the garlic, cream cheese, about a teaspoon of oregano, smoked (or plain) paprika, pepper, some of the mozzarella and cheddar (save some for later) and a little grated Parmesan.

Stuff and roll: Spread the filling over each flattened breast and press it on, leaving a gap at the far edge. Season with just a little salt (the Parmesan is salty), roll it up, and wrap it in as much bacon as you like.

Bake: Put the rolls seam-side down in a tray with a drizzle of olive oil and bake at about 200°C for 25–30 minutes, until the centre reaches 74°C (165°F) on a thermometer. Crisp the salted chicken skin in the oven alongside if you have it.

Make the mustard sauce: Melt about 1½ tablespoons of butter over a gentle heat, cook the garlic and season with pepper. When it starts to go golden, add the stock, about a tablespoon of Dijon mustard, the cream and tarragon (about a teaspoon if dried). Simmer to a pourable sauce, or keep stirring to thicken it more.
Optional cheese: Top the chicken with a little cheese and return it to the oven just to melt, without browning.
Serve: Slice the chicken thickly and serve it on mashed potatoes with the mustard sauce poured over.

recipes.title: Sweetened Condensed Milk in UNDER 5 Minutes NO FAIL Method
ingredients: 3/4 cup granulated sugar (150g) however, you are in control if you want less
2 cups powdered milk (250g) I used whole - you can use semi
4 tbsp unsalted butter (optional for extra creaminess)
The method stays the same — blend it for 2-3 minutes.
If the mixture feels thick, add 1-2 extra tablespoons of boiling water while blending for perfect consistency.
Using regular milk involves simmering and reducing for 20-30 minutes, so while it works well, it's more effort and time-consuming. Ingredients: 2 cups whole milk (480ml)

2/3 cup granulated sugar (135g) 2 tbsp unsalted butter (optional for extra creaminess) Let it cool to room temperature — it will thicken further as it cools. Store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
steps: Quick way: Put the boiling water, milk powder and sugar in a blender jug and blend. It works perfectly well but can be slightly grainy, which doesn't matter for baking.
Smooth way, dissolve the sugar: Gently heat the water in a pan until it starts to bubble, then add the sugar and stir until it dissolves, without letting it brown. Turn off the flame.
Optional butter: If the condensed milk is only for baking (not coffee), add 1–2 tablespoons of butter for creaminess.
Blend: Pour the sugar solution over the milk powder in the blender and blend for about 2–3 minutes. If it is too thick, blend in about 2 tablespoons of boiling water.
Cool: Pour it into a container. It thickens slightly as it cools (the description says to store it in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks).

recipes.title: IS this the BEST IN the WORLD CLASSIC Boulangère Potatoes
ingredients: 1 kg (2.2 lbs) potatoes (Yukon Gold or Maris Piper), thinly sliced
500 ml (2 cups) beef, vegetable or chicken stock
3-4 sprigs fresh thyme (or 1 tsp dried thyme)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Slice the onions and potatoes: Thinly slice the onions. Thinly and evenly slice the potatoes with a mandoline or knife (perfectly even slices aren't critical).

Caramelise the onions: In an oiled ovenproof pan (the video uses a paella pan), cook the onions over a moderate heat with a little salt, a pinch of sugar if you like, and pepper. Cook slowly without blackening for about 25–35 minutes. Use only a little salt overall, because the stock (beef stock cubes in the video) is salty.
Clarify the butter: Put the butter in a bowl set over a bowl of boiling water and cover it so it melts and the milk solids sink. Spoon off the clear butter.
Start the base: Lift some of the onions out to use between the layers. Spread the rest evenly in the pan with some clarified butter so they don't catch, and add a little stock.

Layer: Overlap the potato slices in layers, like a hotpot. Drizzle each layer with butter and stock, scatter on some of the reserved onions and a few fresh (or dried) thyme leaves, season with pepper, and repeat. Tuck in a couple of bay leaves.
Bake covered: Pour over more stock, cover with foil without letting it stick to the potatoes, and bake for about 55 minutes to 1 hour at about 160°C (or 180°C to cook quicker).
Crisp the top: Uncover, dot the top with a little butter and bake for about another half hour until golden and crisp. Remove the bay leaves, add thyme for colour and serve with a roast or salad.

recipes.title: Classic CHICKEN NOODLE Soup – QUICK Hearty Delicious
ingredients: 1.5 lbs (700g) chicken thighs or breasts (bone-in or boneless). I cooked mine in the oven
1 tsp dried parsley (or fresh parsley, chopped)
2 cups egg noodles (or any pasta of choice) I used tagliatelle
Stores in the fridge 3 days — freeze 3 months
steps: Roast the chicken: Roast the chicken thighs, unseasoned, at about 180–190°C for about 35 minutes (or simply boil the chicken in the soup instead). Let them cool, then pull the meat off the bones.
Prep the veg: Dice the onion and garlic, trim and slice the celery, and cube the carrots (plus a couple of peeled potatoes, or any veg you like) to whatever size you prefer.

Sauté: Put a good wedge of butter and a splash of olive oil in a cold pan, add the onion, garlic and celery and cook until they start to colour and lose their rawness. Season with black pepper (and chilli flakes if you like).
Add veg and stock: Stir in the potatoes and carrots for a couple of minutes, adding a little chicken stock so nothing burns. Add the herbs (dried if you have no fresh) and the rest of the stock.
Simmer: Bring to the boil, then cover and simmer for about 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks.

Add the noodles and chicken: Add the noodles or pasta (tagliatelle in the video) and simmer with the lid on for about 7–8 minutes, or as the packet says. After about 5 minutes, stir in the chicken to warm through.
Finish: Add a squeeze of lemon juice and serve topped with parsley.

recipes.title: EASIEST BOSTON cream PIE
ingredients: 1 tsp vanilla extract (or vanilla bean paste for more flavour)
1 tsp butter (optional for a glossy finish)
steps: Prepare the tin: Line a 7-inch springform cake tin.
Make the cake batter: Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar and a splash of vanilla, then whisk in the oil, the milk and the cake flour (with the baking powder and salt) until smooth.
Make the meringue: Whisk the egg whites with the caster sugar and a splash of vinegar to a meringue, then gently fold it into the batter.

Bake: Pour into the tin, tap it to knock out large air bubbles and swirl a skewer from the centre outwards. Bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for about 25–30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Turn it upside down onto a rack to cool.

Make the cream: In a cold saucepan, combine the egg yolks, sugar, sweetened condensed milk, a pinch of salt, vanilla, the milk and the cornflour, and whisk. Stir over the heat until it thickens into a lump-free custard. If it goes too thick, thin it with a little milk or water. Cover the surface with cling film and leave to cool.
Cut the layers: Slice the cake into layers with a cake leveller or knife, keeping the domed top piece for the chocolate.
Assemble: Spread custard over the bottom layer almost to the edge, add the middle layer and more custard, then the top. Chill for about 5 minutes to set.
Make the ganache: Melt the chocolate with the warm cream over boiling water, add a pinch of salt and mix until smooth. Let it cool and thicken slightly.
Glaze and chill: Pour the ganache over the domed top and let it run naturally down the sides. Chill for about 10 minutes to set before slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sl_0-RxhTfY
Uploaded 2025-01-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 170°C (340°F).

recipes.title: The Aussie Pizza
ingredients: Optional herbs: Oregano or parsley for garnish
steps: Part-cook the bacon: Put the bacon in the hot oven (the one you'll bake the pizza in) and cook it about 80% of the way, turning it once for some colour.

Soften the onions: Scatter the sliced onions over the bacon and return it to the oven for a couple of minutes, so they soften in the bacon fat. The pizza only bakes for a few minutes, so raw toppings wouldn't cook through.

Build the pizza: On ready-cooked or part-cooked pizza bases, spread the bottled pizza sauce right up to the edges (barbecue sauce works too). Add a decent amount of mozzarella, a little cheddar for contrast, dried oregano, the bacon and onion mix, and any extras (the video adds cubed cooked ham).
Add the egg: Make a well in the centre and crack an egg into it (two on a big base).
Bake and serve: Bake until the egg is cooked to your liking, taking it out sooner for a runny yolk (the description says 220°C / 430°F for 8–12 minutes). Drizzle with HP sauce to serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nTSvManoZxc
Uploaded 2025-01-04.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 220°C (430°F); Bake for 8-12 minutes or until the cheese is bubbly, the crust is golden, and the eggs are cooked to your preference.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: CHEESY Baked Whole Cauliflower Pie A Comfort Food Classic with a Twist
ingredients: 1 medium whole cauliflower, leaves removed, base trimmed (approx. 800g)
1/2 cup grated cheddar cheese (50g for the mash)
1 tbsp unsalted butter or oil (for sautéing the onion)
2 tbsp unsalted butter (for the cheese sauce)
1 cup grated cheddar cheese (100g for the sauce)
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese (50g for the sauce)
steps: Blind bake the base: Line a tin that fits your cauliflower (about 7 inches in the video) with the rolled shortcrust pastry, leaving an overhang. Prick the base, line it with paper and fill it with baking beads, rice or sugar. Blind bake at 180°C for about 15 minutes, remove the beads and bake for another 5 minutes. Let it go completely cold.
Blanch the cauliflower: Trim the cauliflower and remove the leaves, then blanch it whole in boiling water for about 8 minutes, weighing it down if it floats. It should still be quite firm.

Make the cheese sauce: Melt about 2 tablespoons of butter, stir in 2 tablespoons of flour and cook it out for a minute. Add the warm milk and cream all at once, then pepper and about a teaspoon of Dijon mustard. Once it thickens, melt in a good handful of cheddar and some Parmesan. Keep it a little thicker than usual, as it goes inside a pie.

Make the cheesy mash: Sauté the onions in a little butter with pepper and a tiny bit of salt until soft and translucent, without colour. Stir them into plain mashed potato (no butter or milk) with a little of the cheese sauce, more cheese and some Parmesan.

Assemble: Trim the pastry neatly if you like. Spread the mash over the base and up the sides as a barrier, then sit the cauliflower in it, pushing the mash up around it. Pour the cheese sauce over so it runs down around the cauliflower, and top with a little more cheese.
Add the lid: Wet the pastry rim with water, lay on puff pastry cut slightly larger than the pie, seal it, and cut a couple of vents. Brush with egg wash.
Bake: Raise the oven to 200°C and bake until the puff pastry is golden (the description says 30–35 minutes). Cool for about 10 minutes before turning out and slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M0qCyK6yNlY
Uploaded 2025-01-03.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove weights and bake for 5 mins; Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Bake the pie for 30-35 minutes or until the puff pastry is golden and crisp.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: MOIST & FUDGEY Chocolate Cake
ingredients: 3 g (1 tsp) instant coffee granules (dissolved in boiling water)
200 g (7 oz) semi-sweet or dark chocolate, chopped
30 g (2 tbsp) unsalted butter (optional, for extra richness)
steps: Prepare the tin and coffee: Line an 8-inch springform tin. Dissolve the cocoa powder and instant coffee in about a cup of boiling water and set aside.
Mix the dry ingredients: In a bowl, mix the plain flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, cocoa powder and sugar.
Add the wet ingredients: Add the oil, milk, eggs, vanilla and the hot coffee mixture and whisk into a runny batter.

Bake: Pour into the tin and bake at 175°C (350°F) for about 45–55 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. The video needed about 10 extra minutes. Turn it out upside down onto a rack to cool, which also flattens the top.
Make the frosting: Mix the melted chocolate with the warmed cream and a little butter, then let it cool until thick enough to spread.
Layer: Cut the cake into two layers with a leveller or knife. Spread the frosting over the bottom layer and put the top back on.
Ganache: Melt the chocolate over a pan of water, stir in the warm cream, and let it cool slightly so it still runs. Pour it over the top and let it run down the sides. Leave it to set, then chill.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EX0p7tKshPU
Uploaded 2025-01-02.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).

recipes.title: CLASSIC  Italian -American CHICKEN Piccata in 30 Minutes
ingredients: 1/4 cup white wine (optional, or substitute with chicken broth)
2 tbsp lemon juice (freshly squeezed); the video also uses a little lemon zest
steps: Prep the capers and chicken: Rinse and drain the capers, since jarred capers are very salty. Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make four fillets, pat them dry and season with salt and pepper (or any seasoning you like).
Dredge: Dust the chicken in plain flour, shake off the excess and leave it while you prep the rest.
Prep the lemon and parsley: Zest a little of the lemon, squeeze its juice and chop the parsley.
Brown the chicken: Heat olive oil and butter in a pan and cook the chicken, flipping a couple of times, until it is golden with a good crust. Rest it on a tray.

Start the sauce: Pour off the burnt flour bits from the pan if you like. Add the white wine (or stock) and give it a minute, then add the lemon juice, a little of the zest (save some for the end), the capers and a little butter. Add the stock and pepper, and cook it down to a thin, runny sauce.
Finish: Add more butter, return the chicken with any resting juices, spoon the sauce over and stir in some parsley. If it tastes too salty or sour, add a small pinch of sugar.
Serve: Top with the rest of the lemon zest and parsley, and serve with rice, vegetables or pasta.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_M6nACEDMgo
Uploaded 2025-01-01.

recipes.title: BAILEYS Rice Krispie Treats – A Boozy Twist on a Classic Snack
ingredients: (1 teaspoon of vanilla extract weighs about 4 grams.)
steps: Melt the marshmallows: Put the butter and marshmallows in a large microwaveable bowl. Microwave on high for 1 minute, stir, then heat in 10–20 second bursts, stirring, until fully melted and gooey.
Flavour: Stir in a splash of vanilla and the Baileys. The description lists Baileys, but the captions don't say exactly when it goes in.
Coat the cereal: Quickly stir the Rice Krispies through the mixture until coated, before it sets.

Press and chill: Butter and line a tray of about 9 by 13 inches with parchment, press the mixture in (firmer if you want it less crumbly) and chill until it starts to set. You can simply cut it into squares at this point.
Optional balls: For the version in the video, rub your hands with butter (or keep wetting them with water) and roll the mixture into balls. Chill them until firm.

Coat in chocolate and nuts: Lightly crush toasted macadamia nuts. Dip each ball halfway into melted dark chocolate by hand (a skewer made them fall off), then sprinkle with the nuts so they stick. Chill to set, then add more chocolate on top if you like and chill again.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZP0tVhJoO0w
Uploaded 2024-12-31.

recipes.title: CORN RIBS Perfectly crispy with a Tangy Dip
ingredients: Fresh corn on the cob (used in the video; amount not given)
Seasoning of your choice (for example Cajun or Old Bay)
1 teaspoon of the seasoning of your choice
Optional: 1 teaspoon chilli powder or cayenne pepper (adjust to taste), if not using a seasoning
Optional: 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika, if not using a seasoning
steps: Make the dip: Mix about ½ cup of mayonnaise with the garlic, a little salt, a little chopped coriander (cilantro), lime juice to taste and up to a teaspoon of the same seasoning you'll use on the corn. Set aside.
Cut the corn: Strip off the husks and trim the ends. Using a heavy knife (not a thin blade), cut each cob in half crossways, then cut each piece lengthways into quarters (the "ribs").
Deep fry: Heat enough oil in a wide pan to cover the corn without bubbling over, to about 175°C (350°F). Fry the ribs gently until golden and puffed up, with a little charring.
Season: Drain on kitchen towel, remove the towel, then toss the hot ribs in the seasoning. Add a light squeeze of lime, or a little butter if you prefer.
Serve: Serve with the tangy dip and small lime wedges.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7B5bBBbDnZQ
Uploaded 2024-12-30.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Fry in oil 175°C (around 350°F) until golden.

recipes.title: BUDGET Friendly BEEF Stroganoff  A Comfort Food Classic
ingredients: 500g (1 lb) top round beef (thinly sliced across the grain)
Soy sauce, for marinating (no exact amount; the video uses a generous splash)
1 cup sour cream (or Greek yoghurt for a lighter option)
Egg noodles or rice for serving (tortellini in the video)
steps: Marinate the beef: Toss the thinly sliced lean top round (silverside) in a generous splash of soy sauce until it is absorbed, then marinate for about 30 minutes to tenderise it. With a tender cut like sirloin, you can skip this.
Cook the pasta: Cook your pasta, noodles or rice as the packet says (tortellini in the video).

Flash-fry the beef: Heat butter (or oil) and quickly fry the beef in batches without overcrowding the pan, seasoning with salt and pepper. It doesn't need colour, because lean meat cooked for long goes tough. Set it aside.

Cook the onions and mushrooms: Add a little more butter, then the onion and garlic with pepper, plus any meat juices. Add the thickly sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their moisture. Cut any long beef slices shorter with scissors.

Make the sauce: Stir in the flour and cook off its rawness, then add Worcestershire sauce and the beef broth. Add boiling water if you want more sauce. Stir in the Dijon mustard, then about a cup of sour cream.
Finish: Return the beef and its juices just to warm through (don't cook a lean cut any longer), turn off the flame, and serve over the pasta with parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=svNFZvKhKlY
Uploaded 2024-12-29.

recipes.title: BAILEYS COFFEE Cake for Any Occasion
ingredients: 2 tbsp Baileys Irish Cream (or more to taste)
steps: Dissolve the coffee: Dissolve the cocoa powder and instant coffee in a little warm water.

Make the yolk batter: By hand, whisk the 4 egg yolks with the sugar until it no longer feels gritty. Whisk in the oil, milk and coffee mixture, then the cake flour and baking powder (and salt). Line a 7-inch springform tin and heat the oven to about 160°C.

Fold in the meringue: Whisk the egg whites with a little vinegar, adding the sugar gradually, to a meringue. Fold it into the batter and pour into the tin, then run a skewer through to remove air bubbles.
Bake and cool: Bake until a skewer comes out clean (the description says 40–50 minutes). Turn it upside down onto a rack to cool completely.
Make the Baileys cream: Dissolve more instant coffee and cocoa in a little water. Whip the cream with the sweetened condensed milk, about 2 tablespoons of Baileys and the coffee mixture until thick.
Layer: Keep the flat former base as the top. Cut the cake into three layers, spread Baileys cream between them, and cover the top and sides with a thin layer of cream. Chill for about an hour.
Ganache: Gently heat the cream until it just steams, pour it over the softened chocolate and stir until melted. Cool to room temperature, pour over the cake, and chill again before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CDjnZBoqpYk

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 160°C - 320°F and line a 7-inch round cake pan; Bake for 40–50 minutes until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.

recipes.title: EASIEST and Quick 4 Minute POACHED EGGS No Gimmicks!
ingredients: Mini pie tins (about 3½ inches across the top, 3 inches at the base and 1½ inches high) or ramekins
A pan with a lid (and a trivet for the second method)
steps: Grease the tins: Rub small pie tins or ramekins with butter (or oil). If you use thicker ramekins, adjust the cooking time.

Method 1, direct contact: Bring some warm water to the boil in a pan, then turn it down to a simmer. Crack an egg into each tin, stand the tins directly in the water, cover with the lid and cook for 4 minutes (3 minutes for runny, 5 minutes for a firm yolk).
Method 2, on a trivet (preferred): Put a trivet in the pan with water below it and bring to the boil. Set the egg-filled tins on the trivet above the water, cover and cook for 4 minutes.
Serve: Run a knife around each egg, spoon it out onto buttered toast and season with salt and pepper to taste.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PUHKYboxuI4

recipes.title: Creamy Blue Cheese and Herb Meatballs
ingredients: 500g (1 lb) ground beef or a mix of beef and pork, chicken
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped if no Italian herbs
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried) if no Italian herbs
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs: Stir the breadcrumbs into the milk and leave for a couple of minutes to soak.

Mix the meatballs: In a bowl, combine the mince (beef, pork, chicken or turkey), salt, black pepper, garlic, about a teaspoon of Italian herbs, the crumbled blue cheese, the egg and the soaked breadcrumbs. Mix with gloved, wet or oiled hands so the blue cheese is spread through.
Shape: Roll into meatballs about 1–2 inches across. You can freeze them at this stage (semi-freeze them on a tray, then bag them).

Brown: Heat oil over a moderate heat and fry the meatballs in batches, turning, until golden all over (or oven-cook them in a shallow dish with oil). Lift them out. They finish reheating in the sauce.
Make the roux: Wipe out the excess oil and bits with kitchen towel. Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook until the rawness goes and it just starts to brown.

Make the sauce: Whisk in the stock (chicken, beef or veg), then melt in the blue cheese over a low flame. Season with black pepper only, as the cheese and stock are salty. Stir in the cream and bring it back to a gentle simmer without boiling.
Finish: Return the meatballs and simmer for about 5–6 minutes, spooning the sauce over. Serve over mashed potatoes with a little greenery, such as chives.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9_RILQsTi0c
Uploaded 2024-12-26.

recipes.title: Basil Pesto Spread
ingredients: Pinch of salt and pepper (optional, to taste)
Fresh basil leaves or a drizzle of olive oil for garnish (optional)
steps: Mix: Soften the cream cheese, then mix in about 3 tablespoons of basil pesto (homemade or from a jar), a couple of tablespoons of Parmesan and a shake of black pepper. Taste before adding any salt, as the pesto and Parmesan are already salty.
Serve: Spoon it into a bowl, swirl lines into it with a spoon, drizzle with olive oil and top with a little basil. Serve with crackers, carrots or celery.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r9eoHXWsjxk
Uploaded 2024-12-25.
Short video, brief method.

recipes.title: Chive and Garlic Spread
ingredients: Pinch of salt and black pepper (optional, to taste)
A drizzle of olive oil for garnish (optional)
steps: Season the cream cheese: Whip up the cream cheese, then blend in the garlic powder and a little pepper. It benefits from standing for about half an hour so the garlic flavour develops.
Add the chives: Stir the chives through.
Serve: Spoon it into a bowl, swirl it with a spoon and drizzle olive oil into the crevices. Serve with crackers or veg.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8xDERJaSkqA

recipes.title: Mustard and Bacon Spread
ingredients: 1/2 cup crispy bacon bits (about 4-5 slices of cooked bacon, crumbled)
Optional garnish: Chopped parsley or chives
steps: Prep the bacon: Break or cube cooked bacon into bits, using as much as you like and saving some for garnish.
Mix: Beat the cream cheese (softened is easier) with 2 tablespoons of Dijon mustard, then fold in the bacon bits.
Serve: Spoon it into a bowl, garnish with the reserved bacon and some chopped onion (chives or parsley in the description), and serve with crackers or toast.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gKvOR23i9tY
Uploaded 2024-12-25.

recipes.title: OAT and CORNFLAKE Ginger Slice
ingredients: 70g brown sugar — worried about sugar drop to 50g easily
1 tsp ground ginger (or more, to taste)
50g crystallized ginger, chopped (optional, for extra ginger flavour)
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: Line an 8 by 8 inch tin. In a bowl, mix the rolled oats and cornflakes, then add the chopped crystallised ginger.

Melt the binder: Melt the butter slowly with the golden syrup (or honey), a couple of tablespoons of brown sugar and about a teaspoon of ground ginger, stirring until the sugar dissolves without cooking it hard. Turn off the flame.

Combine and press: Pour the melted mixture over the oats and cornflakes and stir until everything is coated. Spread it evenly in the tin, then press it down (harder for a firmer slice, lighter for a crumblier one).
Bake and cut: Bake for about 15–20 minutes until golden (the description gives 180°C / 350°F). Let it cool completely in the tin, then cut into squares.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Df_9kzjqBGw
Uploaded 2024-12-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake for 15-20 minutes or until the slice is golden brown.

recipes.title: SIMPLE RED Wine JUS   Sauce and Bonus
ingredients: About 1 kg beef trimmings (spoken amount; any bones or trimmings work)
2 sprigs of fresh rosemary or thyme
4 cups (1 litre) beef or chicken stock
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
2 tablespoons unsalted butter (optional, for a glossy finish)
Prepared jus: 1-2 cups (depending on the desired quantity and richness)
Shallots: 1 finely chopped (optional for added flavour)
Fresh or dried herbs: thyme, rosemary, or bay leaf (optional)
Sugar or honey: 1 teaspoon (optional, to balance acidity)
steps: Prep the veg and beef: Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and dice the celery and carrots, all into one bowl (size doesn't matter, since it's pressure cooked). Cut about 1 kg of fatty beef trimmings into large cubes and season with pepper (the stock is salty).

Sear: Brown the beef all over in a hot pan on the stove (the Instant Pot sauté setting is too hot) just for colour, then move it to the Instant Pot liner. Briefly cook the veg in the same pan to pick up the meat goodness and add it to the liner.

Deglaze and build the flavour: In the pan, add a little red wine, a little beef stock, about a tablespoon of balsamic (or soy sauce), a couple of tablespoons of tomato purée and about a tablespoon of sugar (optional). Cook it out for about a minute, then add it to the pot.
Pressure cook: Add the rest of the beef stock and red wine and some fresh rosemary. Pressure cook on high for about 36–40 minutes, let it release naturally for 10 minutes, then release manually.
Bonus beef: Lift out the tender beef and shred it for sandwiches.

Blend and strain: Blend the pot with a stick blender, then strain it through cheesecloth, or press it through a fine mesh sieve for a thicker-bodied jus. Make about a litre and freeze what you don't use.

Make the red wine sauce: Soften chopped onion (or shallot) in a little olive oil without colouring, then add about a cup of red wine and about a cup of jus, a tiny pinch of dried thyme and a splash of balsamic. Simmer until reduced to the thickness you want, then stir in a little butter to make it glossy.
Serve: Pour it over steaks or roasts, or over the shredded beef as the bonus dish.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8ZX2pHuXQ8
Uploaded 2024-12-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Pressure cook for 40 mins - pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then do a quick-release blend and sieve; Slow cooker 8-10 hours.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: BLACK Forest TRIFLE LUSCIOUS dessert ALL the classic flavours of Black Forest Cake
ingredients: Vegetable oil or melted butter: 3 tbsp (~45ml or 40g)
Optional: chopped chocolate or chocolate chips: 3 tbsp (~30g)
1 can (400g) cherry pie filling or pitted black cherries in syrup
2 tbsp kirsch (cherry brandy) or cherry juice (optional)
Optional: crushed amaretti biscuits or chocolate sprinkles for extra texture
steps: Make the microwave sponge: Oil a microwaveable bowl and put a circle of parchment in the bottom. Mix the flour, baking powder and cocoa, then add the oil (or melted butter), milk and about a teaspoon of vanilla. Add a little more milk if it's too dry, then mix in the sugar.
Microwave: Spoon it into the bowl (about halfway up) and lay parchment loosely on top. Microwave for 2–3 minutes, then in 15-second bursts until a skewer comes out clean. Turn it out.

Make the chocolate custard: In a pan, mix the cocoa powder, cornflour and sugar, then add about a teaspoon of vanilla and about 500ml of milk. Heat, stirring, until it thickens (add more milk if it goes too far), then turn off the flame.
Whip the cream: Whisk the whipping cream with a little icing sugar and vanilla until softly whipped.

Layer: Crumble some sponge into the bottom of a trifle bowl (any firmer microwaved crust is good here) and soak it with about a tablespoon or more of cherry brandy. Add cherry pie filling with some of its sauce, then a layer of chocolate custard, then cream.
Repeat and top: Repeat the sponge, cherry filling, custard and cream layers, finishing with cream and grated chocolate. Chill to set.
Decorate: Arrange about 12 cherries on top and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MfhYSsYuHm8
Uploaded 2024-12-23.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: CHEESY ITALIAN Sausage Pastry WREATH with TOMATO Dipping Sauce
ingredients: 2 sheets of ready-made puff pastry (thawed, if frozen)
200 g mozzarella (cut into sticks or shredded)
1/2 tsp red chilli flakes (optional, for heat)
Salt and black pepper to taste
steps: Prep the tin and oven: Heat the oven to 200°C. Grease a bundt pan with butter and line it with parchment that has a hole cut for the centre.
Fill the pastry: Cut a sheet of puff pastry in half lengthways. Lay a line of Italian sausage meat (from skinned sausages) down each strip, make a well along the middle and fill it with mozzarella.
Roll and seal: Wet the pastry edge with a little water, fold it over and seal it into long sausage rolls. Lay them in the bundt pan, joining the ends into a ring.
Bake: Snip slits along the top with scissors, egg wash, and bake until golden and puffed (the description says 35–40 minutes).

Make the tomato sauce: Gently cook garlic in a little olive oil, add the tomato paste and cook it briefly, then stir in about ½ teaspoon of dried oregano. Add the tomatoes, snipping any whole ones with scissors, and simmer with about a teaspoon of sugar. Blend it smooth or leave it chunky, and let it cool.
Serve: Turn out the wreath and tear and share (scissors make it easy), with the tomato sauce for dipping.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q6y7j273JWc
Uploaded 2024-12-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake for 35-40 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed.

recipes.title: BAILEYS CHOCOlate 5 minuet FIX
ingredients: 2 tablespoons granulated sugar (or brown sugar for a richer flavour)
1 tablespoon Baileys Irish Cream (plus extra for drizzling)
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: In a bowl, mix the plain flour, baking powder, cocoa powder, sugar (brown or white) and a pinch of salt.
Prepare the bowl: Butter a microwaveable pudding bowl and put a circle of parchment in the bottom. A half-litre bowl gives a taller pudding.
Add the wet ingredients: Mix in the melted butter, milk and Baileys until combined. Spoon it into the bowl and lay a piece of parchment loosely on top.
Microwave: Cook on high for 1 to 1½ minutes, then in 30-second bursts until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Serve: Turn it out onto a plate, peel off the parchment and drizzle with extra Baileys.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qBMuTQoKuuE
Uploaded 2024-12-22.

recipes.title: EASY CRISPY Chicken Thighs with Caramelised ONION and MUSHROOM Sauce
ingredients: 1 tsp dried thyme (or 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves)
1 tsp smoked paprika (optional, for extra flavour)
For the Caramelized Onion and Mushroom Sauce:
1/2 cup chicken broth (or white wine for added depth)
steps: Prep the onions, garlic and mushrooms: Slice the onions as thinly as you can so they caramelise quickly, mince a couple of garlic cloves, and slice the mushrooms (not too thin).

Season the chicken: Pat the chicken skin dry and season with paprika and salt. Set the thighs on a trivet or rack in a roasting tin so the air can circulate and crisp the skin. Heat the oven to 200°C.
Butter and herbs: Brush the chicken with melted butter, then sprinkle with a pinch of thyme and freshly ground black pepper.

Start the onions: Melt a little butter (or oil) over a moderate heat, add the onions with a little salt and a little sugar to help them caramelise, and cook for at least 15 minutes, stirring, without burning.
Roast the chicken: Put the chicken in the oven for about 35 minutes, until crisp and cooked through (the description gives 30–45 minutes, to 75°C / 165°F inside).
Add the garlic and mushrooms: Stir the garlic into the caramelised onions for a couple of minutes, then add more butter and the mushrooms. Cook just until they take on a little colour.

Build the sauce: Add the chicken stock (careful with salt if using a cube), pepper, up to a tablespoon of balsamic vinegar, about a teaspoon of Dijon mustard and a little nutmeg. Turn the heat down and stir in about ½–1 cup of cream, then simmer to the thickness you like.
Serve: Serve the crispy chicken over mashed potatoes with the onion and mushroom sauce, topped with parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XktzliOs820
Uploaded 2024-12-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C); Bake for 30–45 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (75°C).

recipes.title: Leftovers CHRISTMAS  Pudding MOUSSE
ingredients: 1 tbsp brandy or rum (optional, for flavour)
1/2 tsp mixed spice (or cinnamon and nutmeg)
Extra crumbled Christmas pudding (to sprinkle on top)
Fresh red currants or holly leaves (optional, for decoration)
Dark chocolate shavings or a dusting of cocoa powder
steps: Crumble the pudding: Break the leftover Christmas pudding into crumbs and set aside, keeping some for garnish.
Whip the cream: Whip the cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks, without overwhipping.
Flavour the mascarpone: Beat the mascarpone with about a tablespoon of brandy and the mixed spice (or pumpkin spice, or nutmeg and cinnamon) until creamy.
Fold: Gently fold the mascarpone mixture into the whipped cream, then fold in the crumbled pudding.
Chill and serve: Spoon into serving dishes, cover with cling film and chill for a couple of hours. Crumble the reserved pudding over the top to serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QLzpxR7Mr-0
Uploaded 2024-12-20.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: TRADITIONAL Brandy Sauce
ingredients: A pinch of nutmeg or cinnamon (optional)
steps: Warm the milk: Gently warm the milk and cream without boiling, then set aside.
Make the roux: Melt about 50g of butter in a pan and stir in about a tablespoon of flour.
Add the milk: Gradually stir in the warm milk and cream until it starts to thicken, then stir in the sugar until it dissolves (sugar is in the description), along with the nutmeg (or mixed spice).
Add the brandy: Stir in about 4 tablespoons of brandy (or rum). Cook low and slow to a pourable thickness, since it thickens as it cools. Thin it with a little milk if it goes too far.
Finish: Stir in a tiny pinch of salt at the end and serve warm over Christmas pudding. It can be chilled and reheated the next day.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s5FoW-BqxQE
Uploaded 2024-12-20.

recipes.title: Baked Camembert with Garlic and Rosemary
ingredients: 1 wheel of camembert (in its wooden box or wrapped in foil)
steps: Score the cheese: Unwrap the camembert and put it back in its box. Score the top in one direction, then across, to make a crosshatch.
Stud with garlic and rosemary: Thinly slice the garlic and push the slices into the cuts, then tuck in small sprigs of rosemary.
Bake: Put it on a tray, drizzle with olive oil and add a little cracked pepper. Bake until soft and gooey in the centre (the description gives 180°C / 350°F for 12–15 minutes). Serve with toast.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-MYcfMFYud4
Uploaded 2024-12-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake in the oven for 12-15 minutes or until the cheese is soft and gooey in the centre.

recipes.title: Honey and Mustard Glazed Brussels Sprouts – Sweet, Tangy, and Irresistible
ingredients: Brussels sprouts, trimmed, halved and cooked (steamed) — 500 g
Parmesan and parsley — optional, to finish
steps: Start with cooked sprouts: Use sprouts that are already steamed and still a little warm (the host links his steaming method on the channel); this is what makes the dish quick. Preheat the oven to 200°C / 400°F.
Make the glaze: In a bowl, mix the honey with about a tablespoon of Dijon mustard, about a teaspoon of wholegrain mustard and the garlic.
Coat the sprouts: Add the sprouts to the glaze, season with a little salt and pepper, and mix so they are all coated. Tip them into an ovenproof tray or dish.
Roast: Bake in the hot oven (15 minutes per the description) until glazed and caramelised.
Finish: Spoon any honey glaze left in the dish over the top and grate on a little Parmesan for a salty kick; parsley is just garnish. Serve hot.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v8t7m-6NrBA
Uploaded 2024-12-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Heat your oven to 200°C (400°F); Roast the sprouts for 15 minutes (pre-cooked as above).

recipes.title: Baked Camembert with Maple Syrup and Pecans
ingredients: Camembert — 1 wheel (in its wooden box or wrapped in foil)
Maple syrup — 2–3 tbsp, depending on the size of the cheese
Sea salt or cinnamon — optional pinch
Crusty bread — sliced, for toasting and dipping
steps: Toast the pecans: Toast the pecans lightly in a dry pan — not much. Then roughly chop them with a knife, keeping some texture.
Prepare the cheese: Unwrap the Camembert, put it back in its box base (or on foil), and use a knife to score or slice into the top rind, turning it as you go.
Top it: Drizzle on some maple syrup (not too much this first time), scatter over the pecans and press them down lightly, then drizzle on a little more syrup and finish with a pinch of sea salt.
Bake with the bread: Cut the crusty bread into any shape you like and put it on the tray around the cheese so it toasts at the same time. Bake in a preheated oven for 12–15 minutes.
Serve: Serve straight away, dipping the warm toasted bread (or crackers) into the soft, gooey cheese.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=26EJhN9M14g
Uploaded 2024-12-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake for 12-15 minutes or until the cheese is gooey and soft in the centre.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Christmas LEFTOVER  Quiche with MASH Pastry
ingredients: Mashed potatoes, firm, not too wet — 250 g
Plain flour, plus extra for dusting — 150 g
Butter, cold and diced (optional, for a richer pastry) — 50 g
Cooked ham, turkey or bacon (optional) — 100 g
steps: Make the mash pastry: Put the flour in a bowl with a pinch of salt (the host uses rosemary salt), add the mashed potato and butter, and rub together into a dough. The mash should be fairly dry; if it is damp from the fridge, work in a little more flour (about a tablespoon at a time) until it comes together without being floury. It won't be a true shortcrust, but it works. Chilling is optional.

Line the tin: Roll it out gently on a floured surface — it is looser than normal pastry. Line a parchment-lined, loose-bottomed square tin (or quiche tin), pressing any breaks back together with your fingers, and leave a little overhang because it shrinks. Trim with scissors.

Blind bake and seal: Fill with baking beads, pushing some up the sides, and bake about 15 minutes until the sides take colour. Remove the beads, brush the inside with beaten egg, and bake about 5 minutes more to seal it so the bottom doesn't go soggy.
Make the custard: Whisk the milk with the beaten eggs (the same ones used for the egg wash), black pepper, nutmeg, a pinch of salt and the English mustard.

Fill: Cube the leftover potatoes, roughly chop the sprouts, and mix them with the stuffing, ham (or bacon or turkey) and broken-up roasted chestnuts — any leftover veg works. Spread evenly in the case, pour over the custard and top with cheddar.
Bake: Bake until a skewer comes out clean. The deep-dish version took about 38 minutes; a thin quiche would need about 25.
Rest and serve: Leave about 5 minutes or a little longer so it is warm, not hot, before lifting it out of the tin. Serve warm (cranberry sauce suits it) or cold.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y-hzNQ8CSA8
Uploaded 2024-12-18.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Blind bake the pastry for 15 minutes, then remove the weights, egg wash and bake for another 5 minutes; Bake in the preheated oven for 35-45 minutes or until the filling is set and golden.

recipes.title: How to Make BAILEYS IRISH Cream FOR LONGER LIFE Without Heavy Cream
ingredients: Irish whiskey (Jameson, or any whiskey you like) — 340 ml
Chocolate syrup — 2 tbsp (or 1.5 tbsp cocoa powder dissolved in water)
steps: Make a coffee paste: Froth or whisk the instant coffee with the water (the host uses a milk frother; on camera he calls it 1 tablespoon coffee to 1½ tablespoons water) until creamy and lump-free.

Combine the milks and whiskey: Pour the evaporated milk into a jug, then the sweetened condensed milk, then the whiskey. (Evaporated milk has most of its water removed; condensed milk is the sweet, sticky one — they are not interchangeable.)
Flavour it: Add the coffee paste, a couple of tablespoons of chocolate syrup and the vanilla, and stir well.
Bottle and chill: Pour into a clean, sterile bottle (a little froth is fine; it settles) and keep it in the fridge. Serve cold, like Baileys.
Adjust to taste: In the tasting the host found shop-bought Baileys a little stronger and suggests adding about another 50 ml whiskey if you want it the same.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YPGwiunSzVg
Uploaded 2024-12-17.

recipes.title: EASY Creamy Potato Soup Using LEFTOVERS Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: Chicken or vegetable stock — 3 cups (adjust for thickness)
Heavy cream or milk (optional) — ½ cup
Salt and pepper — to taste (depends on how the mash was seasoned)
Optional toppings: shredded cheese, cooked bacon bits, chopped chives, sour cream
steps: Prep: Dice the onion and roughly chop the garlic; neither needs to be fine since the soup is blended.

Sauté: Melt the butter (or any oil) in a pan and cook the onion and garlic over moderate heat — no need to wait for the pan to heat. Season with salt (the host uses rosemary salt) and black pepper, and add a pinch of herbes de Provence or any herbs you like.
Add stock and mash: Pour in some of the stock first, then add the cold mash a bit at a time, breaking it up and stirring it in with more stock until it is all in.
Simmer: Bring to the boil, then simmer about 5–8 minutes (no more than 10).
Blend and finish: Blend until smooth, stir in the cream (or milk) and warm it through. Let it cool slightly.
Serve: Top with a little parsley and black pepper, or cheese, and serve with buttered crusty bread. The host notes it freezes well in portions.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5zbdrLdmSGw
Uploaded 2024-12-17.

recipes.title: EASY Individual GINGER and RUM Cakes
ingredients: Mixed spice (pumpkin spice works) — 1 heaped tsp
Ground cinnamon (if no mixed spice) — 1 tsp
Ground nutmeg (if no mixed spice) — ¼ tsp
Unsalted butter, softened — ½ cup (115 g)
Dark brown sugar — ½ cup (100 g)
Black treacle (or molasses) — ¼ cup (85 g)
Crystallised ginger, finely chopped — ½ cup (75 g)
steps: Dry mix: Mix the flour, baking powder, ground ginger, mixed spice and salt in a bowl.
Wet mix: Beat the butter and sugar together (creamy is good, but don't worry if it isn't). Beat in the black treacle.

Buttermilk: No buttermilk? Stir about ½ tablespoon apple cider vinegar into the milk and leave about 5 minutes until it splits. Add the vanilla and rum to the wet mix, then the eggs one at a time, then the buttermilk, and fold in the dry mix gently.
Add the ginger: Stir in the chopped crystallised ginger, breaking up any sticky clumps as you mix.

Fill the tins: Line small loaf tins (about 5 × 2½ inches) with strips of parchment running both ways so the cakes lift out. Spoon the batter in — the host planned five but filled four so each rises into a proper little loaf.
Bake: Bake on a tray (the host's oven at 170°C) for about 20–25 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. They may crack a little on top.

Make the rum glaze: In a small pan gently heat a couple of generous tablespoons of butter, the sugar, about a tablespoon of black treacle and a splash of rum until the sugar dissolves — don't let it get too hot. Chop a little extra crystallised ginger for the tops.

Glaze and finish: Rest the cakes about 5 minutes, drizzle over some glaze to soak in, lift them out onto a rack, and add more glaze. After about 5 minutes peel off the paper and dot the tops with crystallised ginger. Let them cool before slicing — they are crumbly when warm.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iZnwJ9Ji8qg
Uploaded 2024-12-16.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C); Bake for 20–25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: EASY No-Bake BAILEYS Cheesecake Creamy & IRRESISTABLE
ingredients: Chocolate cookies (such as Oreos, cream filling removed) — 240 g
Heavy cream, whipped to soft peaks — 320 ml
Chocolate flake (the host used a bought one) and/or chocolate shavings
steps: Line the tin and make the crumbs: Line a square (or round) tin with paper so the cheesecake lifts out. Twist apart the Oreos and scrape out all the cream filling, then crush the biscuits — the finer, the firmer the crust.
Press the base: Mix the crumbs with the melted butter, spread evenly in the tin, then compress firmly with a spoon. Chill while you make the filling.
Whip the cream: Whip the cream to soft peaks and set aside.

Bloom and dissolve the gelatine: Stir the 3 teaspoons gelatine into about 3 tablespoons water and let it bloom (agar can be used instead). Dissolve it by sitting the cup in a little just-boiled water and stirring (or in short microwave bursts). It must not be hot when it goes in.
Make the filling: Beat the softened cream cheese with the powdered sugar and Baileys (taste and add more if you like), then add the gelatine and fold in the whipped cream.
Set: Spread the filling over the chilled base and level it roughly. Refrigerate about 6 hours to set.
Finish: Lift it out on the paper, dust lightly with cocoa powder, and top with a chocolate flake (or grated chocolate) in the middle. Slice and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CAOJtp7TsRQ
Uploaded 2024-12-15.

recipes.title: Lemon Crunch Pie
ingredients: Lemon zest — from 3 lemons (reserve some for garnish)
Lemon juice — from 4 large lemons (about 120 ml)
Extra crushed biscuits, lemon zest curls, whipped cream
steps: Zest and juice the lemons: Zest over the top of the lemons so you get no white pith, then juice them. (The recipe calls for 3 lemons' zest and 4 lemons' juice; the host simply zests all 4.)

Make the base: Crush the biscuits in a bag or food processor and mix with the melted butter. Sugar is only worth adding with graham crackers. Press into a lined 9-inch tin, smooth and flat (not up the sides), and chill while you make the filling (about 30 minutes is suggested, but not essential).

Bloom the gelatine: Stir about 2 teaspoons gelatine into about 2 tablespoons water and leave a minute or two. Dissolve it by standing the container in just-boiled water (or a few seconds in the microwave), then let it cool slightly.
Blend the filling: Put the cream, lemon juice, condensed milk, zest and a splash of vanilla together and blend until thickened. Fold in the dissolved gelatine.
Fill and chill: Spread the filling over the base, smooth roughly and refrigerate until set.
Finish: Pull out the lining to release the pie onto a serving plate, then press a ring of crushed biscuit around the edge (optional) and garnish with the reserved zest.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dn--VdxlK8g
Uploaded 2024-12-15.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Spiced ROAST Red Cabbage and Apples PERFECT Holiday Side Dish
ingredients: Apples (such as Granny Smith or Fuji), cored and sliced — 2 medium
Mixed nuts (optional; walnuts or pecans in the video) — a handful
steps: Slice the cabbage: Cut out the hard core, then slice the cabbage thinly any way you like. Put it in a bowl, loosening the shreds.

Add the apples: Peel and core the apples (the host uses an eating apple and a couple of Granny Smiths) and slice them thin, but not too thin. Add to the cabbage. Preheat the oven to about 200°C / 400°F.

Season: Add about a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar, pepper, the sugar (white is fine) and about a teaspoon of mixed spice (or pumpkin spice, or cinnamon and nutmeg). Mix well, by hand with gloves if easier.

Roast: Spread on a parchment-lined tray (it contains sugar). It looks like a lot but reduces as it cooks. Roast, then turn it all over and return it; with a full tray the host gave it about another 15 minutes. Turn it as often as you like to get it as cooked as you want — browned, not blackened.
Add the nuts: For the last 5–6 minutes, give it a stir and scatter over walnuts (or pecans) crushed in your hands to warm through.
Serve: Serve hot; it goes with pork, chicken or turkey.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ZsmQYHEwp8
Uploaded 2024-12-15.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F); Roast for 20–25 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the cabbage is tender and slightly caramelised and the apples are soft.

recipes.title: Loaded Smashed Potatoes with Cheddar, Bacon, and Creamy Dip
ingredients: Chives or green onions, chopped — 2 tbsp
Garlic, minced — 1 clove (or ¼ tsp garlic powder)
Fresh lemon juice or white vinegar — 1 tbsp
Dried dill — 1 tsp (or 1 tbsp fresh, chopped)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Boil the new potatoes in salted water (about 12 minutes or more) until a fork goes in easily. Drain and let them cool a few minutes.
Smash: Put them on a tray and press each one down with the bottom of a cup or a burger smasher — squashed, but with some height left, not flattened.
Season and roast: Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper — this is the only seasoning they get. Smoked paprika or chilli flakes are optional. Roast at about 200°C.

Make the ranch dip: Mix about ½ cup each of mayonnaise and sour cream with about ¼ teaspoon garlic powder, about 1 teaspoon each dried dill and dried parsley, about ½ teaspoon onion powder, a little salt and pepper and about a teaspoon of Dijon mustard. Leave about 15 minutes so the dried herbs rehydrate. For a spicy version add 1–2 teaspoons hot sauce.
Load them up: Top each potato with cheddar, then Parmesan, then bacon — any cheese you like works (mozzarella, Jack and so on).
Bake again: Return to the oven about 10–15 minutes until the cheese melts and crusts. Rest about 2 minutes.
Serve: Scatter with chopped onion or chives and serve with the ranch dip.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PHrMctaGnxk
Uploaded 2024-12-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F); Boil the new potatoes and cook for 15-20 minutes; Bake for 20 minutes; Bake for another 5-10 minutes until cheese melted.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Creamy Fennel Soup
ingredients: Fennel bulbs, trimmed and chopped (reserve fronds for garnish) — 2 large
Leek, white and light green parts, sliced — 1 medium
Olive oil or unsalted butter — 1 tbsp
Vegetable or chicken stock — 3 cups (720 ml)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — to taste
Olive oil or crème fraîche — to finish
Parmesan (optional, spoken in the video) — to finish
steps: Prep the fennel: Cut off the stalks and the root end, keeping the bulb. Pick off a few fronds and set aside for garnish. Chop the bulb roughly — it gets blended, so shape doesn't matter.
Prep the leek and potatoes: Trim the leek, keeping a little of the green, and slice it fairly thin. Dice the potatoes any size.

Sauté without colour: Melt butter with a little oil, turn the heat down, and add all the veg. Stir gently for about 5–7 minutes until slightly soft, without browning. Season with pepper and a little salt (the host uses rosemary salt) — go easy, since stock cubes carry salt. Herbs are optional; the aim is a mild soup.
Simmer: Transfer to a soup pan with the stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer about 25 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sinks and sticks.
Blend and add cream: Blend with a stick blender, return to the heat and stir in the cream — warm it through, don't boil.
Serve: Optionally add grated Parmesan to the bowl so it melts into the soup, top with fennel fronds, and drizzle with a little olive oil if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nHcttxpUj1Y
Uploaded 2024-12-14.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Easy Mushroom and Herb Pâté Recipe – Perfect for Any Party!
ingredients: Button mushrooms, cleaned and roughly chopped — 500 g
Fresh thyme — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Crusty bread or crackers — to serve
steps: Toast the nuts: Toast the walnuts and almonds lightly in a dry pan, keeping them moving so they don't burn, then set aside.
Soften the aromatics: Add olive oil (and butter) to the pan and sauté the onion and garlic until soft with little colour. Don't salt yet. If using dried herbs, add them now to rehydrate.

Cook the mushrooms: Add the mushrooms (wiped clean and chopped), then salt and pepper — the salt draws out their moisture. Cook, turning, until the liquid has cooked off; add fresh thyme. Keep going until the mushrooms take on a little golden colour.
Cool: Turn off the heat and let them cool about 5 minutes before blending.

Blend chunky: In a chopper or processor, pulse the mushrooms with the cream cheese, a little extra butter if you want it richer, about a tablespoon of lemon juice for freshness, the parsley and the toasted nuts. The host keeps it chunky; blend longer for smooth.

Chill and store: Pack into a container and chill, then serve with crackers or crusty bread. It keeps about 7 days in the fridge wrapped tightly in cling film (or sealed with melted butter), or about 3 months frozen.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mnyn-5ItnTE
Uploaded 2024-12-13.

recipes.title: Roasted Parsnip and Sprout Medley - Perfect side dish
ingredients: Parsnips, peeled and cut into sticks — 3 medium
Wholegrain mustard — 1 tbsp (heaped in the video)
Pecans, butter, parsley and sea salt — to finish (used in the video)
steps: Prep the veg: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Trim the sprout ends, remove the tough outer leaves and halve them. Peel the parsnips down to the white flesh, top and tail them and cut into sticks (batons), leaving the core in.

Make the coating: In a bowl mix a heaped tablespoon of wholegrain mustard, about ½ teaspoon salt (the host uses rosemary salt), smoked paprika if using, about a tablespoon of maple syrup and some black pepper.
Coat: Toss the veg in the mustard mix, then add a couple of tablespoons of olive oil (any oil works) and mix again so it all coats.
Roast: Spread in as single a layer as possible on a lined tray and roast about 25–35 minutes, turning them over partway (more than once is fine) until tinged and charred but not burnt.
Add pecans: Scatter pecans over for crunch and return to the oven for about 5–6 minutes.
Finish: Top with a little butter to melt through, some parsley and a pinch of sea salt. Serve as a side for a roast dinner.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YfpWKmi2hXE
Uploaded 2024-12-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper; Roast for 25–30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the parsnips are tender and caramelized and the Brussels sprouts are crispy on the edges.

recipes.title: Roasted Cauliflower with Parmesan Crust - Perfect Side dish
ingredients: Cauliflower, cut into bite-sized florets — 1 medium
Grated Parmesan — ½ cup, plus extra to finish
Salt (the host used garlic salt) — ¼ tsp, to taste
Breadcrumbs (optional, for extra crunch) — a handful, mixed with a little melted butter
Lemon juice (optional) — a squeeze, to serve
steps: Trim the cauliflower: Even a reduced, slightly marked cauliflower works — just trim off any bad bits, rinse and dry. Cut into fairly large florets of similar size.

Season: Preheat the oven to about 190–200°C / 400°F and line a tray with parchment. Toss the florets with about 3 tablespoons olive oil, about ½ teaspoon each garlic powder, smoked paprika and black pepper, and about ½ teaspoon garlic salt, then about ½ cup Parmesan. Leave a couple of minutes so the cheese sticks.
Butter the crumbs: Melt a little butter (the host sets a bowl of butter over boiling water) and mix in the breadcrumbs.
Roast, first stage: Lay the florets out fairly close together on the tray, scatter over half the buttered crumbs and a little more Parmesan, and roast; turn them over after about 15 minutes.
Roast, second stage: Scatter on the rest of the crumbs and more Parmesan (saving a little for the end) and roast about another 10 minutes, until golden.
Serve: Finish with the reserved Parmesan and some parsley, plus a squeeze of lemon if you like, and serve with the crumbs from the tray.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iKqX9FC8-CM
Uploaded 2024-12-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F) and line a baking sheet; Roast for 20–25 minutes, turning halfway through, until the florets are tender and golden brown with crispy edges.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: NO PASTRY Christmas Mince Pies
ingredients: White or wholemeal bread, crusts removed — 12 slices (for a 6-hole tin: one base and one lid per pie)
Unsalted butter, melted — 100 g (7 tbsp), or more if needed
steps: Roll the bread: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Cut the crusts off the bread, then roll each slice flat with a rolling pin — this is your "pastry". You need 2 slices per pie (12 for a 6-hole tin, 24 for a 12-hole tin).
Cut bases and lids: Cut out 6 discs for the bases with a cutter, as you would with pastry, and 6 smaller lids with a fluted cutter (cutting first saves butter).
Butter generously: Brush the bases and lids with melted butter on both sides — don't scrimp; the butter is what makes them crisp like tart cases. Works with white or wholemeal bread.

Fill: Press a base into each hole of the tin, squashing it down to the bottom. Fill with mincemeat straight from the jar (it puffs up a little), then set a lid on top and flatten gently. Sealing the edges is optional.
Bake: Bake until the bread is golden and crisp, then cool on a rack. They firm up like pastry; dust with powdered sugar if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tYQ9lBdoIrA
Uploaded 2024-12-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); Place the tin in the oven and bake for 15–20 minutes or until the bread edges are golden and crisp.

recipes.title: QUICK and Easy INDIVIDUAL CHRISTMAS PUDDINGS: A Festive Instant Pot Recipe
ingredients: Shredded suet, vegetable or beef (or butter) — 100 g (½ cup)
Rum, brandy or sherry (optional; or more orange juice) — 50 ml (3 tbsp)
Butter — for greasing; parchment and foil for covering
steps: Rub in the suet: Rub the suet into the self-raising flour with your fingertips — it doesn't need to be fine (you could just mix everything, but the host prefers this).

Mix: Add the dried fruit, cranberries, zests, mixed peel, cinnamon, mixed spice, sugar, orange juice and brandy (or extra orange juice), a little milk and the beaten egg. Mix well with a wooden spoon. Molasses, treacle, golden syrup or nuts can be added if you like.
Prepare the moulds: Grease six dariole moulds well with butter (even non-stick ones) and put a parchment disc in the bottom of each. Cut six parchment tops and butter them lightly too.
Fill and cover: Fill each mould about ¾ full (around two heaped tablespoons). Put a buttered parchment top on each, then squash a square of foil over the top and around the sides to keep water out.

Pressure-steam: Put a trivet and 2 cups of water in the Instant Pot. Stand the puddings on the trivet (five fit, the sixth can sit slightly raised). Cook on high pressure for 33 minutes, natural release for 10 minutes, then release the rest manually.
Turn out: Lift the puddings out carefully (they are hot) and rest about 10 minutes. Remove the foil and top, run a knife around the edge and shake the pudding out. Serve with cream or custard.

Make ahead (optional): To store, remove the top, prick the pudding with a skewer, spoon over brandy to soak in, re-cover with parchment and foil, cool completely, wrap in cling film and refrigerate for a couple of months (or freeze). Reheat in the Instant Pot, steam in a shallow pan of water on a trivet, or microwave. Without an Instant Pot, steam traditionally in a pan for a couple of hours.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Su42rdF_5PQ
Uploaded 2024-12-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: High pressure 30 -35 mins; These puddings can be made a few days in advance and reheated in an instant pot (5–10 minutes at high pressure). Microwave in 30 sec bursts.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Mince Pie Slice
ingredients: Ready-made shortcrust pastry — enough for a base and lid for a 13 × 9 inch tray (no weight given)
Sweet mincemeat — 1 jar (about 400 g), or two for more filling
steps: Line the tray: Preheat the oven to 180°C. On a floured surface, roll out about two-thirds of the pastry to fit the base and sides of the tray, and line it.
Fill: Spread the whole jar of mincemeat evenly over the pastry.
Add the lid: Roll the remaining third into a thinner lid (it may be very thin in places — that's fine), lay it over the filling, patch any gaps and prick the top.
Bake: Bake about 20–25 minutes until golden.
Rest and serve: Leave about 10 minutes in the tray, then lift out and cut into squares. Eat by hand like a mince pie, or serve with cream, ice cream or custard (the host likes cold custard).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UVLxxVkvX78
Uploaded 2024-12-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake in the oven for 20-25 minutes or until the top is golden brown.

recipes.title: EASY CHRISTMAS Bread PUDDING
ingredients: Day-old bread, cubed or torn — 6 cups (about 500 g)
Brandy or tipple of choice (optional) — 1 tbsp
Granulated sugar (brown is fine) — ½ cup (about 100 g)
Whipped cream, custard or ice cream, to serve (optional)
steps: Tear the bread: Rip the bread into pieces of any size, crusts and all — any bread works (baguette, soda bread, wholewheat).

Make the custard: Beat the eggs with the sugar, then mix in the milk, about a cup of cream and the mixed spice (the host uses about ½ teaspoon; more makes it spicier). Pumpkin spice works too. Preheat the oven to about 170–180°C.
Soak: Pour the custard over the bread, add the whole jar of mincemeat and a drop of brandy (optional), mix, and leave about 10 minutes for the bread to soak it up.
Fill the dish: Brush a dish of about 9 × 13 inches with melted butter, tip in the pudding mixture without pressing it down, and drizzle more melted butter over the top.
Bake: Bake about 40–45 minutes until the top is crusty and golden.
Serve: Cool about 10 minutes, then serve with custard, cream or ice cream, or dusted with powdered sugar.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2-3vk8mZLQ
Uploaded 2024-12-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Green Beans and Mushrooms
ingredients: Fresh green beans, trimmed — 300 g (10 oz)
Mushrooms (button or cremini), sliced — 250 g (8 oz)
Salt (the host used garlic salt) — ½ tsp, to taste
Lemon — zest and juice of ½
steps: Melt the butter: Melt a couple of tablespoons (maybe three) of butter — the host stands the bowl in just-boiled water with a lid over it.
Prep: Mince the garlic finely. Top and tail the beans and halve them. Wipe the mushrooms and cut into thick slices or quarters (a mix is fine). Zest half the lemon, keeping the juice for later.
Make the garlic butter: Stir pepper and about ½ teaspoon garlic salt into the melted butter, then the fresh garlic (and the olive oil).
Roast: Toss the beans and mushrooms in the garlic butter, spread on a tray and roast about 20–25 minutes, turning them over halfway, until the mushrooms have colour and the beans are cooked.
Finish: Squeeze over the lemon juice and top with the lemon zest, a little Parmesan and parsley. Serve as a side.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YRxeODUzwlU
Uploaded 2024-12-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F); Roast in the preheated oven for 20–25 minutes, tossing halfway through, until the green beans are tender and the mushrooms are golden.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Layered Sausage Meat and Apple Pie
ingredients: Large cooking apples, peeled, cored and thinly sliced — 1–2
Red eating apple, thinly sliced (optional, for sweetness and colour) — 1 medium
Herbes de Provence — 1 tsp (or 1 tsp fresh thyme / ½ tsp dried)
Mixed spice (or pumpkin spice) — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp each cinnamon and nutmeg)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Shortcrust pastry, ready-made — enough for a base and lid
Olive oil — for browning (spoken in the video)
Breadcrumbs (panko style) — 50 g (1.7 oz), for a crispy middle layer
steps: Line the tin: For a 9-inch springform tin, fold a square of parchment into a narrow wedge, guess the centre of the tin, and trim the end to make a circle for the base. Butter the tin lightly and lay the paper in.
Prep the fruit and veg: Dice the onion and thinly slice the leek. Peel, core and thinly slice the apples (a red apple can keep its skin for colour), and cover them so they don't brown too quickly.
Brown the sausage meat: Heat a little oil and brown the sausage meat (or meat squeezed from sausage skins), breaking it up. Lift it out.
Soften the onion and leek: Add a little butter to the pan and sauté the onion and leek with pepper and a little salt (to draw out the liquid), then stir in the herbes de Provence.

Layer the pie: Line the tin with pastry, leaving an overhang. Layer a little sausage meat on the bottom, then the onion and leek mix, the apple slices with a sprinkle of mixed spice, grated cheddar and a layer of panko breadcrumbs (the middle cheese and crumb layer is the important one), then the rest of the sausage meat. A top layer of cheese is optional.
Lid and seal: Wet the pastry edge with water, lay on the lid, fold the overhang over and crimp with a fork or two fingers. Cut a couple of steam vents and brush with egg wash.
Bake and rest: Bake 35–40 minutes until golden. Rest a good 10 minutes before releasing it from the tin and slicing — the filling is fairly loose. Good hot or cold with chips or mash.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fkf62KxoOeo
Uploaded 2024-12-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F) and lightly grease a 9-inch pie dish; Bake in the oven for 35-40 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown and crisp.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Mini Potato Stacks The Perfect Cheesy Side Dish
ingredients: Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tsp (or ¾ tsp dried)
Gruyère (or other melting cheese; the host used mozzarella), cut into 12 squares — 75 g (2.5 oz)
steps: Slice the potatoes: Peel any potatoes and slice them thinly (a mandoline helps) so the slices fit inside the muffin-tin holes; trim odd shapes to fit.
Butter the tin: Melt the butter in a pan, turn off the heat and brush the muffin tin generously with it.

Make the garlic cream: Return the pan to a gentle heat and infuse the garlic in the remaining butter without burning it. Add pepper (salt optional) and a pinch of dried thyme, turn the heat right down and stir in about ½ cup cream and some Parmesan (save a little for the top). Let it thicken slightly, then turn off the heat.

Stack: Stack potato slices about halfway up each hole, spoon in some sauce, add a square of cheese, then keep stacking to about a centimetre above the rim, finishing with the thinner end slices. Spoon over a little more of the buttery sauce.
Bake covered: Cover with foil and bake 40 minutes.
Top and bake again: Remove the foil and use two spoons to push any collapsed stacks back into shape. Top with shredded cheese and Parmesan and bake about another 10 minutes until browned.
Rest and serve: Let them settle a few minutes so the juices soak back in, then lift them out with two spoons. Garnish with fresh thyme. They are also good cold as a snack.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9NR93cOFpkk
Uploaded 2024-12-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 350°F/180°C; Bake uncovered for an additional 10 minutes or until golden and bubbly.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Crispy Parmesan Duchess Potatoes
ingredients: Heavy cream, warm — ¼ cup (60 ml)
Unsalted butter, softened — ¼ cup (60 g)
Grated Parmesan — 50 g (½ cup), plus extra for sprinkling
steps: Boil: Peel and cube any potatoes, cover with water, salt and boil until very fork-tender and starting to break up.
Dry: Drain, then return to the pan over the heat and shake briefly to steam off the moisture.

Mash with warm dairy: Add some of the warm cream, warm milk and warm butter (cold dairy makes mash firm, not creamy), season with salt and pepper and mash, adding more warm milk and butter as needed. The host keeps a little texture.
Add Parmesan, cool, add yolks: Stir in the Parmesan, then let the mash cool. Once cold, stir in the egg yolks.
Pipe: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Pipe the mash into rosettes on a lined tray.
Glaze and bake: Brush gently with beaten egg (butter also works) and sprinkle with Parmesan. Bake until golden and crisp at the edges, then rest a moment before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rklt3AKiZ0w
Uploaded 2024-12-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake in the oven for 15-20 minutes or until the edges are golden brown and crisp.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: How to make Mashed Potatoes others DO NOT KNOW
ingredients: Heavy cream, warm — ¼ cup (60 ml)
Unsalted butter, softened — ¼ cup (60 g)
Optional: black pepper, garlic, chives or cheese for flavouring
steps: Boil: Peel and cube any potatoes, cover with salted water and boil until very fork-tender and starting to break up.
Dry: Drain, return to the pan over the heat and shake briefly so the surface moisture steams off.
Warm the dairy: Use warm milk, warm cream and warm (melted) butter — cold dairy makes the mash firm, not creamy. Add some of each with salt and pepper.

Mash: Mash by hand, adding more warm milk and butter until it is as creamy as you like (the host keeps a little texture). For extra-smooth mash, push the plain potatoes through a ricer or sieve first, then add the butter and milk.
Serve: Spoon onto the plate, swirl the top with a spoon, add a little butter and scatter with chives or green onions.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cqoHotZ-jdU
Uploaded 2024-12-09.

recipes.title: How to Make the PERFECT Roast Potatoes Fluffy Inside, CRISPY Outside
ingredients: Starchy potatoes (any potato works, per the host) — 1.5 kg (3.3 lb)
Vegetable oil (or goose/duck fat for flavour) — 3–4 tbsp
Salt (the host uses rosemary salt) — to taste
Freshly ground black pepper — to taste
steps: Peel and cut: Peel the potatoes and cut into roughly even pieces — big roasties in the video.

Parboil with baking soda: Add about ½ teaspoon baking soda to a pan of boiling water, carefully add the potatoes, return to the boil and boil 7 minutes. You are not cooking them tender, just breaking down the outside starch (ignore the foam).
Heat the oil: Meanwhile pour the oil into a roasting tray and heat it in the oven (about 200–220°C) — hot, not scorching.
Dry and fluff: Drain the potatoes in a colander and let them steam-dry a minute, then shake them in a bowl so the edges rough up.
