Roast: Tip the potatoes into the hot oil so they sear underneath, coat them, and season with rosemary salt. Roast about 25 minutes, then turn them gently, coat in the oil, add rosemary or garlic if using, and roast until crisp.
Drain and serve: Tilt the tray so the potatoes aren't sitting in oil and let them settle a minute. Serve with a few rosemary sprigs and a pinch of sea salt.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zu-22dV02Q0
Uploaded 2024-12-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F); Roast for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Its just a CHUNKY Vegetable SOUP with Barley
ingredients: Italian seasoning — 1 heaped tsp (or 1 tsp each dried thyme and dried oregano)
steps: Chop everything chunky: Peel and cube the swede, and cut the potatoes, carrots, celery and onion into big chunks; slice the mushrooms. Size isn't critical over a long simmer. Meat (beef, chicken) is optional.

Soften the base: Heat the oil with a knob of butter and cook the onion, celery and garlic, then add the carrot and cook about 5 minutes, turning. Add pepper and only a little salt (stock cubes are salty).
Add mushrooms and herbs: Stir in the mushrooms (optional) and let them release their moisture, then add the Italian seasoning (or thyme and oregano) and the bay leaf.
Add tomatoes, stock and barley: Add the tomatoes with their juice (snip whole tomatoes with scissors in the pan), the vegetable stock and the rinsed barley, along with the potatoes and swede.
Simmer: Bring to the boil, reduce to a simmer, cover and cook about 40–50 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks. When the veg is done, the soup is done (cook longer for softer veg).
Serve: Remove the bay leaf and serve scattered with parsley. (The host notes an Instant Pot does it in about 20 minutes.)
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ca5s_pdeH0Q
Uploaded 2024-12-08.

recipes.title: How to Make Chimichurri Sauce A Zesty Argentinian Classic
ingredients: Fresh parsley leaves, packed (flat-leaf, curly, or half and half) — 1 cup
Fresh cilantro leaves (optional; traditional uses parsley only) — ½ cup
Red chilli flakes — ½ tsp, to taste
Olive oil (or sunflower or rapeseed oil) — ⅓ cup
Lemon juice (optional) — juice of ½ lemon
steps: Chop the parsley: Pulse the parsley in a chopper so it keeps some texture rather than turning to purée. Curly parsley works as well as flat-leaf; the taste is nearly identical.

Blend in two halves: Put about half the parsley back in the chopper with half the lemon juice, red wine vinegar, garlic, pepper, oregano and chilli flakes and half the olive oil, and pulse. Tip into a bowl and repeat with the other half.
Combine and season: Mix both batches together and adjust the salt. Add cilantro only if you want the Mexican-style take.
Rest: Refrigerate a couple of hours so the flavours meld.
Store: Keep in a jar in the fridge up to 5 days, or freeze in portions. Serve over steak, grilled chicken or vegetables.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mMgxtP70zWU
Uploaded 2024-12-08.

recipes.title: One Pan Creamy Tuscan Chicken Perfect for Weeknight Dinners
ingredients: Unsalted butter — 2 tbsp, plus a little extra for the garlic
Tomato paste — 1 tbsp (1–2 tbsp in the video)
Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and chopped — ½ cup
steps: Prep: Strip the spinach leaves from their stems (optional, but it removes the stringy bit). Roughly chop the sun-dried tomatoes and the garlic — it needn't be fine.

Season and sear the chicken: Season the chicken on both sides with salt and pepper only. Heat the olive oil and butter and sear the chicken a couple of minutes per side, turning as needed, until about 85% cooked. Cover with foil to rest (it keeps cooking). Discard any burnt bits from the pan.
Start the sauce: Add a little fresh butter and fry the garlic over moderate heat, then stir in the tomato paste, chilli flakes and paprika and cook briefly.

Build it: Add the chicken stock, the sun-dried tomatoes and the Italian seasoning, then the cream, and bring together. Stir in the Parmesan. Season with black pepper only — the stock cube is salty enough.
Spinach and chicken: Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then return the chicken and warm it through until fully cooked.
Serve: Serve over mashed potatoes or pasta, garnished with basil if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1EchYgO78R0
Uploaded 2024-12-07.

recipes.title: Beef and Mushroom Black Bean Sauce
ingredients: Beef, thinly sliced (the host used chuck roll; topside is good) — 350 g
Mushrooms, cut into thirds or quarters — amount not given
Vegetable oil — 2 tbsp (3–4 tbsp in the video)
Shaoxing wine or dry sherry — 1 tbsp
Water or chicken broth — ¼ cup
Cornstarch or potato starch mixed with 2 tbsp water (optional, to thicken) — 1 tbsp
Also used in the video: about 1 tsp oyster sauce, a splash of sesame oil, a little MSG (optional)
steps: Slice the beef: Partly freeze the beef and slice it very thinly. Thin slices don't need marinating.

Mix the sauce: Combine about a tablespoon of Shaoxing wine, about half a tablespoon of dark soy, about a teaspoon of oyster sauce, a splash of sesame oil, a little sugar and MSG if you use it. Set aside.
Prep the veg: Mash and roughly mince the garlic (leave some bits), cut the onion into pieces, slice the red chilli diagonally (for colour, not heat) and cut the green pepper into pieces.
Fry the mushrooms: Heat 3–4 tablespoons of oil in a wok and fry the mushrooms until they take some colour.
Cook the beef: Add a little more oil and quickly stir-fry the beef, then add the veg and garlic.

Sauce it: Add the black beans, the sauce mix with a little water, and return everything to the wok. Thicken with the starch slurry, turn off the heat, add a shake of white pepper and stir through. Serve with rice or noodles.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Mn2OPJ4h30
Uploaded 2024-12-06.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Wholesome Banana Oat Cake – Perfect for Any Time of Day
ingredients: Rolled oats (ground in a blender in the video) — 200 g
steps: Mash the bananas: Mash the bananas. (The host's tip: left a couple of hours, they oxidise and give a browner cake.) Soak the raisins in a little boiling water for about 10 minutes to plump them.
Dry mix: Grind the oats in a blender, then mix with the brown sugar, salt, baking powder and baking soda.
Wet mix: Blend the bananas with the oil and eggs (a few banana chunks are fine).
Combine: Fold the oat mix into the banana mix to make the batter, then stir in the nuts, chocolate chips and drained raisins.
Bake: Pour into a lined 9 × 4 inch loaf tin, tap it level and set it on a tray in case it overflows. Bake about 25 minutes, then test with a skewer; return to the oven if it doesn't come out clean.
Cool: Cool a few minutes in the tin, then turn out onto a rack for about 10 minutes before slicing. Good warm with butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EAs47vClLBA
Uploaded 2024-12-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F) and grease or line a loaf tin or baking pan with parchment paper; Bake for 25–30 minutes or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes clean.

recipes.title: Cheesy BACON Stuffed Potatoes The Ultimate Comfort Food
ingredients: Sour cream or heavy cream (optional) — 2 tbsp
Parmesan and chopped green herbs — to finish (used in the video)
steps: Start the potatoes: Prick the potatoes all over with a fork and microwave for 10 minutes. Rub with a little oil and salt.

Bake with the bacon: Put the potatoes and the lardons in the oven. Turn the bacon after about 20 minutes and take it out after a further while, still a little soft (it finishes later); the potatoes take about 40 minutes.
Hollow out: Brush off the excess salt, slice the top off each potato and scoop the flesh into a bowl, taking care not to break through the skins. Keep the tops too.
Make the filling: Mash the potato with sour cream (or butter), then mix in cheddar and the bacon. (The host made one veggie potato with cheese only.) Green onion or other cheeses can go in too.
Fill and bake: Pile the filling back into the skins, top with more cheese and bake until golden and bubbling.
Serve: Finish with a little Parmesan and some chopped green herbs.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wd8CyjR8RtU
Uploaded 2024-12-04.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake 45-50 minutes or until they are 60% cooked; Return the stuffed potatoes to the oven and bake for 15-20 minutes or until the cheese is melted and bubbling with golden edges.

recipes.title: ETON MESS
ingredients: Large egg whites, at room temperature — 4
Lemon juice or white vinegar — 1 tsp
Meringue nests, shop-bought or homemade — 100 g
steps: Whip the meringue: Whisk the egg whites with a pinch of salt until frothy, then add the sugar and keep whisking to soft peaks.

Pipe and bake: Pipe small rounds onto baking paper (hold the bag just above, squeeze, lift). The host baked them in an air fryer, starting at 160°C and dropping to 120°C (about 240°F), for about 40 minutes, then turned it off and left the meringues to air dry.

Macerate the strawberries: Chop most of the strawberries (keep a few for the top), add about 2 tablespoons of sugar and a pinch of salt, stir and leave about 15 minutes to draw out the juices, then mash or blitz them a little.
Whip the cream: Whip the cream to soft, spoonable peaks; no extra sugar is needed because the meringue is sweet. The host gave it a quick pulse with a stick blender.
Crush the meringue: Break the meringues into rough clumps.
Layer: In glasses, layer meringue, strawberry mixture and cream, repeating and leaving it rough rather than smooth.
Finish and serve: Top with a whole strawberry and a few cut strawberries and serve immediately, while the meringue is still crisp.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3DQK3zWMpVo
Uploaded 2024-12-03.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 180°C (360°F)  for about 40-45 minutes; Airfryer 120°C (240°F)  for about 40-45 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese Spread
ingredients: Fresh dill or parsley, finely chopped — 1 tbsp
Horseradish (optional) — ½ tsp (the host used about 1 tsp)
steps: Blend the salmon: Put the cream cheese and smoked salmon together and pulse with a stick blender, keeping some texture (or go as smooth as you like). Mash in a little extra flaked salmon for visible pieces.
Add the flavourings: Stir in the chopped parsley or dill, a little lemon zest and a drizzle of lemon juice.
Add onion and capers: Add a small amount of finely chopped shallot or onion (too much overpowers the spread) and the chopped capers.
Season: Season with black pepper, and salt only if you want it, then stir through about a teaspoon of horseradish.
Chill: Transfer to a bowl, cover and refrigerate for 1 to 2 hours so the flavours come together. Serve on toast or crackers.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V5_XXLQ5RmY
Uploaded 2024-12-02.

recipes.title: How to Make Clarified Butter in the Microwave
steps: Melt in bursts: Put the butter in a microwave-safe bowl or container and microwave on medium power for 20 to 30 seconds at a time, watching it, until fully melted and separated into a foamy top, clear butter and milk solids at the bottom. Don't overheat it, or the solids can pop and spatter (a cover helps).
Skim: Spoon off the foam from the top.
Strain: Pour the clear butter gently through a sieve lined with cheesecloth into a container, leaving the milk solids behind.
Store and use: Keep it in a container for baking, frying and sautéing. (In a pan the method is the same; cook the solids on until brown and nutty and you have ghee instead.)
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EfpnzS_WFwM
Uploaded 2024-12-02.

recipes.title: EASY Salt and Pepper CHICKEN  A Flavourful Chinese-Inspired Dish
ingredients: Green bell pepper, finely sliced — ½ (the host used small red, yellow and green peppers)
Chinese salt and pepper chilli seasoning — 1–2 tsp, or to taste
Onion — a little (used in the video)
Chinese salt and pepper chilli seasoning (mix together):
Sea salt — 2 tbsp (or 1½ tbsp table salt)
steps: Bake the chicken: Toss the drumsticks with sesame oil, tip into a tray and bake for about 25 to 35 minutes until fully cooked. (Any cut, or rotisserie chicken, works.)
Prep the veg: Chop the garlic; cube or slice the peppers evenly; slice the chilli on the diagonal; chop the onion; cut the spring onion into short pieces, keeping the green tops to add at the end.
Fry the aromatics: Heat a little oil in a pan over moderate heat and gently cook the garlic until fragrant and just tinged brown.
Stir-fry the veg: Add the peppers and onion, stir-fry briefly with a little of the seasoning until just softened.
Toss the chicken: Add the chicken with a little more seasoning, toss, then add the chilli and spring onion and stir briefly.
Serve: Sprinkle with a tiny bit more seasoning and serve with rice or fries.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aLBekPj7MZE
Uploaded 2024-12-01.

recipes.title: QUICK & Easy Last Minute CHRISTMAS Pudding
ingredients: Whisky or brandy — 3 tbsp (plus extra to drizzle, optional)
Unsalted butter, melted — 75 g (plus extra for greasing)
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: In a bowl, combine the self-raising flour, orange zest, chopped (or briefly blitzed) mixed nuts, brown sugar and mixed spice.

Add the wet ingredients: Stir the mincemeat first to loosen it, then add it with the marmalade, glacé cherries, about 3 tablespoons of brandy or whisky, the melted butter, the beaten eggs and about 2 tablespoons of black treacle. Mix well.
Prepare the basin: Butter a pudding basin (about 1 litre) thoroughly. Put a small disc of parchment in the bottom, and butter a second disc for the top.
Fill: Tip in the mixture and press the buttered parchment disc, butter side down, gently onto the surface.
Microwave: Cook on medium (about 500–600 W) for about 20 minutes, keeping an eye on it so it doesn't rise out of the bowl.
Test: Insert a skewer; if it doesn't come out clean, continue in 10 to 30 second bursts until it does.
Turn out: Let it settle a minute (it is extremely hot), run a knife around the edge, and turn it out onto a plate. Peel off the paper.
Serve: Drizzle with a little brandy if you like, and serve with brandy sauce, cream or custard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O1_DoVaz_Ns
Uploaded 2024-11-30.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake in a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F) for 2.5 to 3 hours.

recipes.title: Black Pepper Chicken bold and flavourful
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, bite-sized pieces — 500 g
Cornstarch — 2 tbsp in total (includes the marinade; the rest for a slurry)
Ground black pepper — 2 tsp in total (adjust to taste)
Green and red bell peppers, sliced — 1 cup
Sugar (optional) — under ½ tsp (used in the video)
steps: Marinate: Toss the chicken with about 1 teaspoon black pepper, 1 tablespoon light soy sauce and 1 tablespoon cornflour. Leave 20 to 30 minutes.

Mix the sauce: Combine 2 tablespoons oyster sauce, about 1 teaspoon dark soy, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, the chicken stock, about 1 teaspoon black pepper and, if you like, under half a teaspoon of sugar to balance the saltiness.
Prep the veg: Crush and chop the garlic and ginger; slice the peppers and onion; cut the spring onions into roughly 1 cm pieces.
Fry the chicken: Heat oil over moderate heat and fry the chicken, turning, until golden and nearly cooked through; don't rush it on a fierce flame. Remove to a bowl.
Cook the aromatics: Add a little more oil and cook the garlic and ginger gently just to take the rawness off, without browning them bitter.
Stir-fry the veg: Add the onion and peppers and stir-fry until slightly softened.
Combine: Return the chicken and its juices, pour in the sauce and bring back up to temperature.
Thicken and finish: Stir in a little cornflour-and-water slurry until the sauce clings. Turn off the heat, stir in most of the spring onion, and scatter the rest on top to serve with rice or chips.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NZoZ_1T1i5E
Uploaded 2024-11-29.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken Mushroom Stroganoff Recipe - A Comfort Food Classic
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thighs, bite-sized — 500 g (1 lb)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Sour cream or Greek yogurt — 1 cup (250 ml)
Plain flour or cornflour (optional, for thickening) — 1 tbsp
Cooked egg noodles, tagliatelle, rice or mashed potatoes — to serve
steps: Cook the pasta: Cook tagliatelle (or your chosen pasta) to the packet instructions; rice or mash also work.
Brown the chicken: Heat oil and butter in a pan, add the chicken, season with salt and pepper and cook until coloured and nearly cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Soften the aromatics: Add a little more butter, then the garlic and onion, and cook briefly to take off the rawness.
Cook the mushrooms: Add the mushrooms and paprika and cook until their moisture has cooked off and they take on some colour.
Add stock and mustard: Pour in the stock, stir in about 1 tablespoon of Dijon mustard and let it cook for a minute.
Add the sour cream: Lower the heat and stir in about a cup of sour cream (or yogurt).
Thicken: Return the chicken, add a little cornflour slurry and heat through until the sauce is nicely thick.
Serve: Spoon over the pasta and finish with chopped parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fnePVSdhGjc
Uploaded 2024-11-28.

recipes.title: EASY Lemon Curd and Mascarpone Danish
ingredients: Lemon curd (shop-bought or homemade) — about 1 tsp per pastry
steps: Make the filling: Mix the mascarpone, powdered sugar and a splash of vanilla with a mixer (or by hand) until smooth.
Heat the oven: Preheat to about 200°C (400°F).
Cut the pastry: Cut the ready-rolled pastry into squares (about 4 × 4 in or 4½ × 4 in).
Fill: Put a dollop of the mascarpone mixture in the middle of half the squares, leaving a border, make a small dip in it and add about a teaspoon of lemon curd.
Seal: Lay another square over the top, press the corners down first, then the sides, and crimp the edges with a fork.
Bake: Brush with egg wash and bake for about 15 to 20 minutes until golden.
Cool and serve: Cool on a wire rack and dust with powdered sugar if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nTEsEaaYk60
Uploaded 2024-11-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake for 15-20 minutes or until the pastry is puffed up and golden brown.

recipes.title: EASY OAT Stuffing with Sausage and CIDER
ingredients: Sausage meat (or sausages out of their casings) — 300 g
Butter — 50 g (¼ cup), plus extra for the dish
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried)
Fresh sage, finely chopped — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried)
Salt — ¼ tsp (adjust to the sausage seasoning)
Cider or chicken stock — 75 ml (⅓ cup), or more
Chopped nuts or dried cranberries (optional) — a handful
steps: Brown the sausage: Fry the sausage meat in a little oil, breaking it up (into small bits or chunks as you like), until coloured, about 5 minutes. Remove and set aside.

Soften the onion and apple: Lower the heat, melt the butter and cook the onion for a minute or so until soft. Season with salt and pepper, add the apple and let it soften, then stir in the dried cranberries (or nuts).
Toast the oats: Add the oats and stir so they soak up the butter and turn golden. Add the dried thyme (and the sage now too if it is dried).

Add sausage and cider: Return the sausage meat, then add cider a little at a time until the mixture is damp but not soggy. Cook a couple of minutes. (Apple juice, water or chicken stock can replace the cider.)
Add the sage: Turn off the heat and stir in the fresh sage.

Bake: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Butter a deep dish, pack in the stuffing, pat it down, then fluff up the top so it crisps, and bake until crunchy and golden on top (about 20 to 25 minutes per the description).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YlSRD7C9EN4
Uploaded 2024-11-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 20–25 minutes.

recipes.title: EASIEST No-Bake No-Gelatin  Cheesecake Recipe EVERYONE Should Master
ingredients: Digestive biscuits, crushed — 1 cup (about 8–10 biscuits, 100 g)
Sugar (optional; digestives are already sweet) — 1 tbsp (12 g)
Unsalted butter, melted — ¼ cup (60 ml)
Sugar (the video uses powdered sugar) — ¼ cup (50 g)
All-purpose or heavy cream, chilled — 1 cup (250 ml)
Topping of choice (fresh fruit, canned pie filling, etc.; the video uses canned blueberry filling)
steps: Line the tin: Take the base out of a 7-inch springform tin, flip it so the ridge is underneath, lay parchment over it and clip the ring back on so the paper is held taut. Fold the excess paper underneath.
Make the crust: Crush the biscuits (add sugar only if using graham crackers or you have a sweet tooth), then mix thoroughly with the melted butter.
Press and chill: Spread the crumbs in the tin, pat down evenly and compress. Refrigerate about 1 hour to set.
Whip the cream: Whip the cream until thick and set aside.
Beat the cheese: Beat the cream cheese with a splash of vanilla and the sugar, gently at first, scraping down the sides.
Combine: Fold or stir the whipped cream into the cream cheese just until combined; don't overbeat.
Fill and set: Spread the filling over the chilled base, pressing up to the sides and smoothing it towards the edge. Refrigerate a couple of hours to set.

Unmould and top: Release the ring, slide the cheesecake off the paper using the folded edge, and spread your topping over it, stopping just short of the edge (or let it run down the sides). Slice and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=omtF46jh68c
Uploaded 2024-11-26.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Old Fashioned Buttery Date Slice – A Sweet Treat Everyone Loves
ingredients: Ready-made shortcrust pastry — enough for a base and a lid in a 13 × 9 in tray
Caster sugar — 50 g (¼ cup), plus a little to sprinkle
Water — ¼ cup or more, as needed
steps: Chop the dates: Remove any stones and chop the dates so they break down easily.

Cook the filling: Put the dates in a pan with a couple of tablespoons of water (about ¼ cup in all, adding more as needed), the sugar and the butter. Cook over a low-to-medium flame for about 5 to 8 minutes, stirring and mashing any firm pieces, until you have a smooth buttery paste. Don't let it burn; add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Flavour and cool: Turn off the heat, stir in about a teaspoon of vanilla and a pinch of salt, then let it cool.
Line the base: Line a roughly 13 × 9 in baking tray with parchment. Roll out pastry on a floured surface into an oblong to fit the bottom with a little overhang.
Fill: Spread the date filling evenly over the pastry.
Add the lid: Roll out the top, brush the edges with a little water as glue, lay it on, trim the excess and crimp the edges.
Prick and sugar: Loosely mark the slices, prick all over with a fork so steam can escape, and sprinkle with caster or granulated sugar.
Bake: Bake at 180°C for about 25 minutes until golden. Leave in the tray about 15 minutes, then move to a wire rack and cut into slices.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SI7B6A3ty9k
Uploaded 2024-11-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake in the oven for 20-25 minutes or until the top is golden brown.

recipes.title: HAPPY THANKSGIVING  Bacon Wrapped Green Bean and Potato Stacks
ingredients: Small new potatoes — 12 (or large potatoes cut into thick rounds)
Green beans, trimmed — a good handful per bundle
Streaky bacon — 6 strips (the host used about 3 per bundle)
Salt and pepper (the host used rosemary salt) — to taste
Gravy — to serve (used in the video)
Fresh rosemary or parsley, to garnish (optional)
steps: Prep: Top and tail the green beans. Cut the potatoes into rounds about 1 cm thick, trimming any bad ends.
Blanch the beans: Boil the beans 4 to 5 minutes, no more, then plunge into iced water to stop the cooking.
Par-boil the potatoes (optional): Boil the potato rounds about 5 minutes for a head start, then drain well.
Season the potatoes: Toss with olive oil, rosemary salt (or salt), pepper and garlic powder. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Roast the potatoes: Spread them in a single layer on one side of a lined tray, drizzle over any oil left in the bowl, and roast about 20 minutes.
Wrap the beans: Pat the beans dry, gather them into portion-sized bundles and wrap each tightly in bacon (around three rashers), tucking the ends underneath.

Roast together: Turn the potatoes and add the bean bundles to the tray. Roast about 12 to 15 minutes, flipping the bundles and the potatoes partway, then give them up to about 8 more minutes until the bacon is crisp.
Stack and serve: Lay a base of potato rounds, top with a bacon-bean bundle, spoon over a little gravy and finish with cranberry sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJ4GBYZZ_88
Uploaded 2024-11-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: How to Make Cranberry Sauce in 15 Minutes
ingredients: Water or orange juice (or cordial) — 1 cup, plus extra as needed
steps: Plump the cranberries: Put the dried cranberries in a pan with the orange juice, topped up with water so there is enough liquid. Bring to the boil, lower the heat and simmer about 5 minutes until they plump up.
Add the sugar: Stir in the sugar and cook low and slow for about 10 minutes, stirring so it doesn't burn, until the cranberries soften and the sauce thickens.
Mash: Press some of the cranberries with the spoon for a jammier consistency (optional), and cook a little longer.
Finish off the heat: Remove from the heat and stir in the orange zest, a pinch of cinnamon and about ¼ teaspoon of vanilla. Serve with turkey, chicken or pork.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wodU1iLFdjc
Uploaded 2024-11-24.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: ONE PAN ITALIAN Meatballs with Spaghetti in Marinara Sauce
ingredients: Ready-made raw meatballs (or homemade Italian sausage meatballs) — 500 g
Onion, finely chopped (red or white) — 1 medium
Water or chicken broth — 2 cups (500 ml), plus more if needed
steps: Brown the meatballs: Heat the oil over a moderate flame and brown the meatballs all over, turning; they don't need to cook through. Remove and set aside.
Soften the aromatics: In the same pan, sauté the onion and garlic until softened. Season with black pepper (go easy on salt if your broth is salty).
Cook the paste and herbs: Stir in a good tablespoon of tomato paste and cook gently without burning, then add the sugar, oregano, basil, chilli flakes and Italian herbs if using.
Add the tomatoes: Pour in the canned tomatoes, breaking them up, then add a couple of cups of broth.
Simmer: Simmer, covered if you can, for about 10 to 15 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks.

Cook the spaghetti: Lay the spaghetti in the sauce and push it under as it softens, then stir it through. Cook for the packet time (about 7 to 8 minutes or more) until al dente, adding water or stock if it gets too thick.
Return the meatballs: Add the meatballs, stir and cook about 5 more minutes to heat through.
Serve: Serve topped with fresh basil and grated Parmesan.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HQlteo7QZ-U
Uploaded 2024-11-23.

recipes.title: ITALIAN Sausage Mix All About the Seasoning and Taste
ingredients: Fennel seeds — 6 g (1 tablespoon, lightly crushed)
Crushed red pepper flakes — 1 g (1 teaspoon, optional for mild heat)
Cayenne pepper — 1 g (1 teaspoon, optional for extra heat)
steps: Toast and crush the fennel: Quickly toast the fennel seeds, then whizz them briefly in a blender so they are broken up — fennel is a must in Italian sausage.
Combine: Put the pork mince in a bowl with the salt, pepper, powders, herbs and fennel; add chilli flakes (and cayenne) if you want a little kick. Adjust the herbs to your taste.
Mix until sticky: Mix by hand (or in a mixer) for about 5–6 minutes until the mixture turns sticky and clings to the bowl. No extra water is needed.
Rest and use: Cover and chill for 1–2 hours to let the flavours meld, then stuff into casings for sausages or roll into balls and cook in your pasta sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t6glr10IH8c
Uploaded 2024-11-23.

recipes.title: CLASSIC Sausage STUFFING
ingredients: Sausage meat (or uncased sausages) — 500 g (1 lb)
Apples — 1–2, peeled, cored and diced (optional, for sweetness)
Fresh sage — 1 tbsp, finely chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tbsp (or 1 tsp dried)
Poultry seasoning — 1 tbsp, if no fresh herbs
Chicken or vegetable stock — 250 ml (1 cup), as required
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Fresh parsley — finely chopped, for garnish
steps: Prep the bread and veg: Cube or tear the day-old bread into a large bowl — it doesn't need to be neat. Finely chop the celery, garlic, onion and sage, and peel, core and dice the apple (no need for lemon, it cooks in the stuffing).

Brown the sausage: Heat a little oil and a couple of tablespoons of butter in a pan, add the sausage meat and break it up, cooking it through with some colour. Tip it, juices and all, over the bread so it soaks in.

Soften the aromatics: Add more butter to the pan and sauté the onion, garlic, celery and apple for about 5 minutes until softened, then add them to the bowl with the herbs (or poultry seasoning) and mix.
Bind: Stir in stock a little at a time so the bread soaks it up without getting soggy, then mix in the beaten egg. Remember it will dry out a little as it bakes.
Fill the dish: Spoon into a baking dish, pressing the bottom down lightly but roughing up the top into peaks. Dot with a few small pieces of butter.
Bake covered: Cover with foil, set on a tray, and bake at about 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes.
Crisp the top: Remove the foil (turning it away from you to let the steam out) and bake for another 15–20 minutes until the top is golden and crunchy. Spoon onto plates and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2IWwqGp25g0
Uploaded 2024-11-23.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).

recipes.title: PUMPKIN CHEESECAKE Gingersnap Crust – Creamy, Spiced, and Perfect for Holidays
ingredients: Gingersnap (gingernut) biscuit crumbs — 2 cups (about 250 g, 1 packet)
Unsalted butter, melted — ¼ cup (56 g), plus more if needed
Pumpkin purée (not pie filling) — 1 cup (about 245 g)
Mixed spice or pumpkin spice — 1 tsp
Spice mix if you have no mixed or pumpkin spice:
steps: Make the crust: Crush the gingersnaps (in a bag, by hand or in a blender), then mix with the melted butter until it holds together, adding a little more butter if it seems dry. The host skipped the sugar.

Press into the tin: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Line an 8-inch springform tin, press the crumbs firmly over the base, pushing them outward so they rise a little up the sides, and tap to compact.
Pre-bake: Bake the crust 8 to 10 minutes, then let it cool a little.
Dry the purée: For a firmer filling the host stirred his pumpkin purée over a low flame until most of the moisture cooked off.

Make the filling: Beat the cream cheese until creamy, then add the sour cream, pumpkin purée, vanilla, brown and white sugar and spice and mix. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing in and scraping down the bowl.
Fill: Pour the filling over the crust and smooth it as best you can.
Bake: Bake for 55 to 65 minutes. If it rises or cracks, turn off the oven and leave it inside with the door open for about an hour to settle.
Chill and serve: Refrigerate at least 4 hours before slicing. Serve with a little cream.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u2vf_dqOq8g
Uploaded 2024-11-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C); Bake the crust for 8-10 minutes; Bake for 55-65 minutes.

recipes.title: Easy Pumpkin Puree
ingredients: Pumpkin — 1 small to medium (the video uses a quarter of one)
Water — a little, only if needed to blend
steps: Seed the pumpkin: Cut the pumpkin into pieces and scoop out the seeds and stringy flesh (the seeds can be roasted separately).
Roast: Lay the pieces on a lined tray and roast in a preheated 190°C (375°F) oven for about 40 to 60 minutes, until a fork slides easily into the flesh.
Scoop: Let it cool a little, then scoop the flesh off the skin, leaving behind any blackened caramelised bits.
Blend: Blend until smooth, adding a splash of water only if it won't blend.
Strain: Tip into a sieve (or cheesecloth) and leave about 30 minutes to drain off the excess liquid; keep the thick purée.
Store: Pack into an airtight container or zip-lock bag. Refrigerate up to a week or freeze up to 3 months.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e7JLmQg5AOo
Uploaded 2024-11-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat Oven to 375°F (190°C); Roast in the oven for 45-60 minutes or until the pumpkin flesh is tender and easily pierced with a fork.

recipes.title: EASY JAMAICAN GINGER Cake Moist, Sticky, and Richly Spiced Loaf
ingredients: Mixed spice — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp cinnamon plus ¼ tsp nutmeg)
Vegetable oil or melted butter — 125 ml (½ cup)
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, mixed spice, ground ginger and a good pinch of salt. Set aside.
Line the tin: Line a 2 lb loaf tin with a liner or parchment paper and preheat the oven to about 170°C.
Melt the sugars: In a pan over a low flame, dissolve the brown sugar, golden syrup and black treacle together.
Add the butter and milk: Turn off the heat, stir in the butter until melted, then the vanilla and the milk. Beat the egg and whisk it in.
Make the batter: Add the dry mix to the wet and whisk to a smooth, runny batter.
Bake: Pour into the tin and bake about 50 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Glaze: Warm the golden syrup (the host stood the jar in boiling water) until runny, brush it over the warm cake, and leave about 10 minutes to soak in. Lovely with a cup of tea, plain or buttered.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mPFbvCS2xIg
Uploaded 2024-11-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 170°C (340°F) or 150°C (300°F) fan-assisted; Bake for 50–60 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes clean.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Cheesy Parmesan Brussels Sprouts – The Perfect Side Dish
ingredients: Olive oil or melted butter — 2 tbsp
Italian seasoning — a little (used in the video)
Breadcrumbs (optional, for crunch) — 2 tbsp, mixed with a little melted butter
steps: Heat the oven: Set the oven or grill to 200°C (400°F).
Season the sprouts: Toss the steamed sprouts with the olive oil, salt, black pepper, Italian seasoning, some of the Parmesan and the garlic.
First bake: Spread in an ovenproof dish and bake about 5 to 7 minutes, just until the cheese starts to melt.
Prepare the crumbs: Meanwhile stir the breadcrumbs with a little melted butter.
Top and crisp: Scatter over the breadcrumbs and the remaining Parmesan, add a little black pepper and return to the oven until crisp and browned to your liking.
Serve: Finish with a little more Parmesan and chopped parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0niCNNaUA8Y
Uploaded 2024-11-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Set your oven to 200°C (400°F) or preheat the grill/broiler; oven or grill for 5–7 minutes until the cheese begins to melt.

recipes.title: EASY Mince BEEF and mushroom HAND pies
ingredients: Shortcrust pastry, shop-bought or homemade — enough for 8 rounds (about 6 in)
Egg, beaten, for egg wash (used in the video)
steps: Brown the beef: Heat a little oil, add the mince and break it up as it browns, seasoning with salt, pepper and a pinch of dried thyme.
Add the onion: Stir in the onion and soften it, cooking off the water released by the meat.
Garlic and mushrooms: Add a little butter, then the garlic, then the mushrooms; cook until the mushrooms release and lose their moisture.
Flavour: Stir in about ½ teaspoon paprika, a splash of Worcestershire sauce and a tablespoon of tomato paste, and cook the paste in.
Cook it thick: Add the beef stock and cook until the mixture is moist but not saucy, so the pastry can hold it. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
Cut the pastry: Roll out the pastry on a floured surface and cut 6-inch rounds.
Fill and shape: Put a spoonful of filling on each round, bring the pastry up over it and pinch together along the top, then pinch in the ends. Crimp with a fork.
Bake: Brush with egg wash, poke a couple of small vent holes in the top and bake in a preheated 200°C (400°F) oven for about 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cS1eIaP0t-4
Uploaded 2024-11-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and crisp.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Pan Fried Brussels Sprouts, Chestnuts with Pancetta or Bacon lardons
ingredients: Pancetta or bacon lardons, diced — 100 g
Salt (the host used sea salt) and pepper — to taste
steps: Crisp the pancetta: Fry the pancetta or lardons in a little olive oil until coloured and crisp. Remove, leaving the flavoured fat in the pan.
Cook the garlic: Add the garlic and cook just until it takes a tinge of colour, without burning.
Fry the sprouts: Add the steamed sprouts and let them pick up a little colour.
Add the chestnuts: Add the chestnuts, leaving some whole and breaking some up, and warm through. Season with salt and pepper.
Return the pancetta and add lemon: Put the pancetta back, squeeze in the lemon juice and toss for no more than half a minute, then stir in most of the lemon zest.
Serve: Turn off the heat and serve with a little sea salt, pepper and the remaining zest on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=80H_KRhg-u0
Uploaded 2024-11-19.

recipes.title: Classic Buttered Brussel Sprouts  Easy and Flavourful Side Dish Recipe
ingredients: Unsalted butter — 2 tbsp (or more to taste)
steps: Trim the sprouts: Cut across the bottom of each sprout to trim the end and peel off the first couple of outer leaves.
Cross or halve: Cut a cross into the hard stalk at the base so it steams evenly; halve any very large sprouts instead.
Set up a steamer: Bring a pan of water to the boil and set a colander or sieve (or a steamer) over it, with a lid to cover.
Steam: Add the sprouts, cover, and steam for 6–8 minutes, turning them over after about 4 minutes so the bigger ones cook evenly.
Test: They're done when fork tender — the fork goes in but you still feel some resistance.
Dress and serve: Tip into a bowl, toss with butter, salt to taste and black pepper, and serve, with a little extra melted butter drizzled over if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w3AmIUSWk2I
Uploaded 2024-11-19.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Colman’s-Style Traditional ENGLISH Mustard at Home with Simple Ingredients
ingredients: Water — 95–102 g (start with 95 g, just over 1/3 cup; add more only if needed)
Xanthan gum — 0.2 g (1/8 tsp, or a tiny pinch)
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: Whisk the mustard flour, sugar, salt, turmeric and wheat flour together in a bowl.
Add water gradually: Tip in the water a little at a time, whisking, and stir in the citric acid. Go carefully — too much water gives a runny mustard that is only good for sauces.
Thicken: Whisk in about 1/8 tsp xanthan gum to give the thick, smooth texture.
Rest: Cover (so it doesn't discolour) and leave to stand for about an hour so it thickens and the flavours mellow. If it's still loose, make the next one with less water.
Jar and store: Spoon into a jar and keep in the fridge.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gj_W6dcTjqE
Uploaded 2024-11-18.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: BEEF Medallions in Red WINE CREAM Sauce Parsnip and Potato Mash
ingredients: For the red wine cream sauce:
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tsp (optional), or herbs of choice
For the parsnip and potato mash:
steps: Boil the mash veg: Peel and cube the parsnips and potatoes, put them in a pan of salted water and boil until fork tender.
Season the beef: Season the medallions generously with salt and pepper — this is the only chance to season the meat.

Sear: Heat the olive oil and butter in a pan over a moderate (not super high) heat and sear the beef for 3–4 minutes, turning it regularly so it sears on all sides, including the edges. Transfer to a tray and cover.
Soften the aromatics: In the same pan, sauté the shallots and garlic for a minute or so to take away the raw onion taste.

Build the sauce: Pour in the red wine to lift the debris off the bottom of the pan, add the broth and let it cook, then add the cream and reduce a little to thicken — not too much unless you want a very thick sauce. Stir in the butter for a sheen and the thyme for aroma.
Mash: Drain the parsnips and potatoes and mash with the butter, pepper and a touch of cream, keeping some texture if you like.
Serve: Spoon a generous amount of mash onto the plate, top with the beef, pour over the sauce and finish with a little parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eQr2613rihQ
Uploaded 2024-11-17.

recipes.title: EASY Brisket CHEESESTEAK with Caramelised Veggies
ingredients: Fresh beef brisket — 500 g, thinly sliced
Bell pepper (any colour) — 1 large, thinly sliced
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Provolone cheese — 6 slices (or 1/2 cup cheese sauce)
Crusty loaf — 1, cut into sandwich-sized portions and sliced open
steps: Make the horseradish mayo: Mix the mayonnaise, a good dollop of horseradish and the Dijon mustard with a pinch of salt; taste and set aside.
Prepare the bread: Spread the cut sides of the crusty bread and toast them cut side down until nicely browned.
Slice the veg: Thinly slice the onion and the pepper (any veg you like works).

Cook the brisket: Heat oil in a pan, add the brisket with salt, pepper, Worcestershire sauce and smoked paprika, and cook briefly, getting a little colour if you can. Remove to a bowl and wipe out the pan.
Caramelise the veg: Add a little more oil, fry the onion and pepper, then add the garlic, cooking until they take on colour.
Combine: Return the brisket and its juices to the pan and stir just to bring it back up to temperature. Divide into portions in the pan.
Melt the cheese: Lay the provolone (or mozzarella) over each pile, turn off the heat and let it melt.
Assemble: Spread the horseradish mayo on the toasted bread and pile in the cheesy brisket and veg.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TFj-rgBpgnE
Uploaded 2024-11-16.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: STEAK-Stuffed BAKED Potatoes with Creamy Parmesan Sauce
ingredients: Russet potatoes — 4 large, scrubbed clean and dried
Steak (NY strip, ribeye, sirloin or tenderloin) — trimmed and cut into 1–2 inch cubes
Black pepper — freshly cracked, to taste
steps: Prep the potatoes: Prick the washed potatoes all over with a fork and cut a cross in the top of each (it makes them easy to open and stuff later). Set on scrunched parchment on a tray, rub with oil and sprinkle with salt.
Bake: Bake for about 50 minutes, possibly longer, until a fork pierces straight through.
Season the steak: Cut the steak into reasonable cubes and toss with Cajun seasoning.

Sear the steak bites: Heat the oil in a pan, add the steak bites in a layer and sear over a high heat, then add a couple of tablespoons of butter. Remove from the pan and cover with foil to keep warm.
Start the sauce: Lower the heat, add more butter to the flavourful pan and cook the garlic briefly. No flour — pour in the cream and stir as it thickens slightly.
Finish the sauce: Add chilli flakes if using, then the Parmesan, cooking until it's as thick as you like. Stir in fresh parsley and a squeeze of lemon.
Stuff and serve: Open up each baked potato, add a little butter if you like, pile in the garlicky steak bites, pour over plenty of sauce and finish with a little parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iTU8DWKFN50
Uploaded 2024-11-15.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper; Bake for 50-60 minutes until tender when pierced with a fork.

recipes.title: Creamy CHICKEN or TURKEY  spinach and mushrooms  lasagna
ingredients: Cooked chicken or turkey, shredded — 2 cups
Milk (or a mix of milk and cream) — 3 cups
steps: Cook the base: Heat olive oil and a little butter, add the onion with pepper (no salt — the stock and Parmesan bring enough) and cook briefly, then add the garlic and Italian herbs.
Add the veg: Add the mushrooms and cook, getting a little colour if you can, then add the spinach and let it wilt down, keeping the juices in the pan.
Add the meat: Stir in the shredded brown and white meat until fully incorporated, then turn off the heat.

Make the sauce: Melt a couple of tablespoons of butter, add the flour and the chicken stock (made from a stock cube), then whisk in the milk until lump-free. Add nutmeg and Italian herbs and keep stirring as it naturally thickens.
Add the cheese: Stir in Parmesan (and a little mature cheddar, as in the video) and cook until the sauce is as thick as you like — add more milk or cream if it gets too thick.

Layer: In an 8x8 tin, spread a little sauce, then lasagna sheets, filling, sauce, ricotta or cottage cheese and mozzarella. Repeat, adding a sneaky sprinkle of Parmesan between layers, and finish with sheets and pepper on top.
Bake covered: Cover with foil (use a deep tin for a deep fill) and bake for about 30 minutes.
Brown the top: Uncover, top with mozzarella, cheddar and more Parmesan, and return to the oven until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let it settle for 5–7 minutes before cutting into thick slices.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nDHJ_O5suiI
Uploaded 2024-11-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Zesty Cranberry Orange Loaf Cake
ingredients: Orange zest — of 1 orange, approx. 1 tbsp (6 g)
Sour cream (or Greek yoghurt) — 1/2 cup (120 g)
steps: Plump the cranberries: Soak the dried cranberries in the orange juice for about 15 minutes, then drain for 6–7 minutes, keeping the juice. (Skip this if using fresh cranberries.)
Prep: Heat the oven to about 175°C (350°F) and grease and line a 9x5 loaf tin. Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt together.
Cream: Beat the butter and sugar together until creamy.
Add eggs and yoghurt: Beat in the eggs and the yoghurt (or sour cream), then add the flour mix and beat it all in — adding flour now stops the eggs curdling.
Add the orange: Mix in the reserved orange juice and about a tablespoon of orange zest.
Add the cranberries: Toss the cranberries in a little flour and fold them into the batter, then pour into the tin. (In the video some still sank — the flour trick doesn't always work.)
Bake: Bake until a skewer comes out clean. Leave in the tin for about 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.
Glaze: Mix the powdered sugar with a couple of tablespoons of orange juice and some zest, drizzle over the cake and let it set before slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h2TT9S7iah0
Uploaded 2024-11-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan and line it; Bake for 50-60 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes clean.

recipes.title: Easy Cranberry Bread Pudding A Cosy Dessert for Any Occasion
ingredients: Day-old bread — 6 cups (about 500 g), cubed or ripped up
Granulated sugar — 1/2 cup (about 100 g), plus extra for the top
Mixed spice — 1 tsp (or 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon and 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg)
Whipped cream, custard or ice cream — for serving (optional)
steps: Tear the bread: Rip the 2–3 day old bread, crusts and all, into a large bowl — size doesn't matter, it will soak up the custard.
Make the custard mix: Add the cranberries, eggs, sugar, a little salt, vanilla, milk, cream and mixed spice, and beat it all together. Add more milk if there doesn't look to be enough liquid.
Soak: Stir so all the bread absorbs the mix and leave for about 10 minutes. Heat the oven to about 175°C (350°F).
Fill the dish: Butter a dish (about 13x9) and layer the mixture in without squashing it down, so the custard cooks through without burning on top. Dot with butter.
Bake: Bake for about 40–45 minutes.
Sugar top: With 10 minutes to go, take it out, sprinkle over sugar (granulated or demerara) for a crunchy top, and return to the oven.
Serve: Let it cool a minute, run a knife around the edge and serve warm.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WRCZd44lUJo
Uploaded 2024-11-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).

recipes.title: TRADITIONAL Sage and Onion STUFFING
ingredients: White or brown breadcrumbs — 200 g (7 oz)
Fresh sage — 2 tbsp, finely chopped (or 2 tsp dried sage)
Unsalted butter, melted, mixed with the breadcrumbs — 75 g (1/3 cup) (optional)
Hot chicken or vegetable stock — 100 ml (1/2 cup)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — to taste (rosemary salt was used in the video)
steps: Prep: Dice the onion as small as you like and mince the fresh sage leaves.

Soften the onions: Melt a chunk of butter in a pan, add the onions with about 1/2 tsp (rosemary) salt and sauté gently for about 5 minutes to soften without much browning. Add dried sage now, if using, so it rehydrates.
Butter the crumbs: Optionally stir the melted butter through the dried breadcrumbs.
Combine: Mix the onions into the breadcrumbs with the fresh sage, add a little hot stock if it's too dry, then stir in the beaten egg to enrich and bind.
Shape: Butter a baking dish and press the stuffing in (compress it, then fluff up the top if you like), or roll it into stuffing balls. It can be prepped up to 2 days ahead and kept chilled.
Bake: Bake at 190°C (375°F): about 35 minutes for a dish, or 25 minutes for stuffing balls.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j5nQ3fM1bRE
Uploaded 2024-11-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F).

recipes.title: Best Sausage and Cranberry Stuffing for Thanksgiving Christmas or any Sunday Roast
ingredients: Sausage meat or sausages (casings removed) — 500 g (1 lb)
Apples — 2 medium, peeled and finely diced
Chicken or vegetable stock — 120 ml (1/2 cup)
Salt and pepper — to taste (celery salt was used in the video)
steps: Prep: Remove the sausage skins and crumble the meat. Dice the onion, mince the garlic, chop the parsley, and peel, core and cube the apples small (no lemon needed). Dice the celery.
Brown the sausage: Cook the sausage meat in a little oil and butter (or bacon grease) with pepper and celery salt until coloured and about 80% cooked through. Set aside in a bowl.

Cook the aromatics: Add butter to the pan and cook the onions, then the poultry seasoning (or a tablespoon of sage and a teaspoon of thyme) and garlic. Toss in the apples just to take on the flavour, then turn off the heat and let cool.
Mix: Combine the breadcrumbs with the sausage meat and its juices, the cranberries, celery, the onion and apple mixture, and the parsley.
Bind: Once the mix has cooled (so the egg doesn't cook), stir in the stock and beaten egg.
Bake: Spoon into a dish, cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover for 15 minutes until golden. Garnish with parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=czBtS3x8fDA
Uploaded 2024-11-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).

recipes.title: Easy Roast Parsnips Crispy, Golden, and Delicious
ingredients: Parsnips — 1 kg, peeled and cut into evenly sized batons (or halved if small)
Olive oil, vegetable oil or goose fat — 2 tbsp
Fresh thyme and rosemary — 1 tsp (or 1/2 tsp each dried)
Semolina or polenta — 1 tbsp (optional, for extra crispiness)
steps: Prep the parsnips: Peel, top and tail the parsnips. Cut off the thick top end and quarter it, and cut the rest so all the pieces are roughly the same size. No need to remove the sweet core or parboil.
Make the glaze: In a bowl, whisk the olive oil with pepper, a little celery salt, a little honey (or maple syrup) and the bruised rosemary and thyme.
Coat: Toss the parsnips in the glaze until well coated, then sprinkle over a tablespoon (or more) of semolina or polenta and stir to give them a crusty coating.

Roast: Spread in a single layer on a tray and roast at 190°C for 35–40 minutes, flipping them over halfway. (If you parboil them for 4 minutes first, roast hotter, around 200°C, for about 30 minutes.)
Honey glaze: Drizzle honey over the roasted parsnips and return to the oven for 5 minutes only to caramelise.
Finish: Transfer to a dish, sprinkle with a pinch of rosemary salt and add a little butter to melt through.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eAXT2RFp60w
Uploaded 2024-11-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 190°C (380°F); Gas Mark 5 (190 °C / 380 °F); Roast in the preheated oven for 35–40 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and crispy on the edges. In the last 5 minutes, drizzle with honey.

recipes.title: EASY Tuna CHEESE Leek Pie  A Creamy DELICIOUS Dinner Idea
ingredients: Chicken or vegetable broth — 1 cup (optional, if not using milk)
Dijon mustard — 1 tsp (English mustard used in the video; optional)
steps: Sauté the leeks: Thinly slice the cleaned leeks into a pan with the butter (add a little more if needed), season with salt and pepper and cook gently for 5–7 minutes until softened — no need to brown them. Add the mixed herbs.
Add the flour: Stir in the flour and cook for a couple of minutes, turning, to cook out the raw flour without burning.
Make the sauce: Stir in about a cup of milk (a little more if needed) and let it come back up to temperature and thicken until creamy.
Flavour: Stir in the mustard, then a good cupful of cheddar, saving a little, and cook until melted and gooey. Leave the mixture to cool.
Line the tin: Line the base of an 8.5-inch springform tin with parchment and fit one sheet of pastry inside. Roll out a lid to fit. Heat the oven to 190°C.
Fill: Stir the drained tuna through the cooled mixture. Spread half into the pastry, sprinkle with the reserved cheese, then add the rest, spreading it to the sides.
Lid and vent: Lay the lid on, roll the edges over to seal, cut vent holes with a knife and brush with egg wash.
Bake: Bake on a tray for about 35 minutes until golden brown.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ycoswYl6saY
Uploaded 2024-11-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F).

recipes.title: EASY Creamy Basil Pesto Parmesan CHICKEN with Mashed turnips & Wilted Cress
ingredients: For the chicken in creamy basil pesto sauce:
Turnips or swede/rutabaga — 2 medium, peeled and cubed
steps: Boil the turnips: Peel the turnips, cut into cubes and boil in salted water until soft.
Prep the cress: Pull the watercress leaves off the woody stems into a bowl.
Season the chicken: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and Italian herbs on both sides.

Cook the chicken: Heat the olive oil and butter in a pan and cook the chicken gently, turning as often as you like, until about 80–85% cooked (a thermometer is the best check). Transfer to a tray and cover with foil — it will keep cooking.

Make the sauce: Pour off the fat and any burnt herbs. Add about 3/4 cup cream over a moderate heat, stir in a good couple of tablespoons of basil pesto, then the Parmesan, and cook gently until thickened to your liking.
Finish the chicken: Return the chicken to the sauce for a couple of minutes to warm through and finish cooking, then cover to keep warm.
Mash: Drain the turnips and mash with butter and black pepper, then stir through a little cream.
Wilt the cress: Warm a little olive oil, sauté the garlic briefly without burning, then add the watercress with a little pepper and cook just until wilted.
Serve: Plate the chicken and pesto sauce with the mashed turnips and wilted cress.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ge-Y7WFFg4w
Uploaded 2024-11-08.

recipes.title: GARLIC SALT simple seasoning blend of savoury saltiness
ingredients: Salt (sea salt or table salt) — 3 tablespoons
steps: Grind the salt: If using sea salt, grind it finer (table salt can be used as it is). Generous, heaped spoonfuls are fine.
Mix and store: Mix the salt with the garlic powder until evenly combined and keep in a jar.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HzhKEjFge7A
Uploaded 2024-11-07.
Short video, brief method.

recipes.title: Perfectly Roasted Carrots Easy and Flavourful Side Dish Recipe
ingredients: Carrots — 500 g, peeled and cut into 2-inch sticks (or baby carrots)
Honey or maple syrup — 1 tbsp (optional, for sweetness)
Salt — 1/2 tsp (rosemary salt used in the video)
Fresh thyme or rosemary, chopped — 1/2 tsp (optional)
steps: Top and tail: Wash and dry the carrots and trim off the leafy tops (they blacken in the oven); trim the tails a little too if you like. Peel larger carrots and core them if you prefer.
Cut evenly: Halve the carrots lengthways so the thick and thin ends cook more evenly, and put them in a bowl.
Glaze: Add the olive oil, about a tablespoon of honey or maple syrup (choose one), the garlic powder, pepper, salt (or season after roasting) and the fresh thyme and rosemary, and toss to coat.
Roast: Spread in a single layer on a lined tray, scraping over any leftover glaze, and roast in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for about 25–30 minutes.
Turn: About halfway through, turn the carrots over so they caramelise, then return to the oven until tender. Garnish with parsley to serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gljPdTzALds
Uploaded 2024-11-07.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F); Roast for 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway through until the carrots are tender and slightly caramelised.

recipes.title: SIMPLE Side Dish Fennel with Lemon and Parmesan
ingredients: Fennel bulbs — 2 large, trimmed and cut into wedges
Salt and black pepper — to taste (about 1/2 tsp rosemary salt in the video)
Fresh herbs such as thyme or rosemary — 1 tsp (optional)
Lemon zest — of 1 lemon, for garnish (optional)
steps: Trim the fennel: Cut off the stalks, keeping some of the feathery fronds for garnish. Trim a thin slice off the cut base without cutting too far in, so the layers stay together.
Cut wedges: Halve each bulb, then cut into wedges through the core (leave the core in for roasting — it holds the segments together).
Season: Mix the olive oil, pepper and rosemary salt in a bowl, add the fennel and turn it gently to coat without breaking it up.
Roast: Lay on a lined tray, drizzle over any oil left in the bowl, and roast in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for about 30 minutes.
Turn and add herbs: Halfway through, turn the wedges over and sprinkle with bruised fresh thyme and rosemary.
Add Parmesan: For the last 5–6 minutes, sprinkle the Parmesan over the top and return to the oven.
Serve: Transfer to a serving dish, add a little lemon juice (not too much) and garnish with the fronds.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AcTwyuk6WoU
Uploaded 2024-11-07.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C); Roast in the preheated oven for 25–30 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Easy Buttermilk Biscuits and Gravy Recipe for a Hearty Breakfast
ingredients: For the buttermilk biscuits (amounts as stated in the video):
Apple cider vinegar — 1 tbsp (to make buttermilk)
Breakfast sausage meat (mild or spicy; Cumberland used) — 1 lb (500 g)
Milk (whole works best) — 2 cups, plus extra to thin
Salt and black pepper — to taste
steps: Make buttermilk: Stir 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar into 1 cup milk and leave for 5 minutes. Heat the oven.

Make the dough: Mix the self-raising flour with salt and 1/4 tsp baking soda, then rub in the butter with your fingertips. Pour in most of the buttermilk and bring it together into a fairly loose dough, adding more if needed.
Shape: Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and pat (or roll) to about 1 inch thick — the cracks make for flaky biscuits. Cut with a cutter (about 3 inches for large breakfast biscuits).
Bake: Place on a parchment-lined tray and bake for about 12–15 minutes (up to 20) until risen and browned on top.
Brown the sausage: Meanwhile, heat bacon grease in a pan and brown the sausage meat in lumps, getting a good crusty colour for flavour.
Add flour: Stir in the flour and cook briefly to take out the rawness, letting it absorb the fat.
Add milk: Pour in a couple of cups of milk and stir as it thickens; keep extra milk handy to loosen it.
Season: Add a pinch of cayenne, a heaped teaspoon of wholegrain mustard, salt and pepper, and cook to the thickness you like.
Serve: Split the warm biscuits and spoon over the sausage gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dGxFCls1a0Y
Uploaded 2024-11-06.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper; Bake for 10–12 minutes or until the biscuits are golden brown.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: VICTORIA Sponge Cake A TIMELESS BRITISH Treat for Afternoon TEA
steps: Cream: Beat the butter and sugar together until creamy and light, scraping down the sides.

Add eggs and flour: Mix the flour with the baking powder (if using) and salt. Beat the eggs in, adding about half the flour to stop the mixture curdling, then add the milk, vanilla and the rest of the flour and mix.
Fill the tins: Divide the batter between the two buttered and lined 8-inch tins (weigh it if you like; otherwise use the fuller one as the base).
Bake: Bake for 20–25 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Leave in the tins for about 5 minutes, then turn out onto a rack, peel off the paper and cool.
Whip the cream: Whip the cream with just a little icing sugar — the cake and jam are sweet enough.
Assemble: Choose the best sponge for the top. Spread a deep layer of raspberry jam on the bottom sponge, then the whipped cream, and set the top sponge on.
Finish: Dust with just enough icing sugar to cover the top and a little down the sides, then slice and serve with afternoon tea.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aQIpfpG30Yg
Uploaded 2024-11-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and line two 20cm (8-inch) round cake tins with baking parchment; Bake in the preheated oven for 20–25 minutes or until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.

recipes.title: How to Make ROSEMARY SALT Perfect for Seasoning Meats & Vegetables
ingredients: Coarse sea salt or kosher salt — 1/2 cup (8 tablespoons)
Fresh rosemary leaves — 2 tablespoons (or 1 heaped tablespoon dried rosemary)
steps: Grind the rosemary: Put the rosemary in a grinder with a couple of tablespoons of the sea salt and grind it up (use more rosemary for a stronger flavour).
Add the rest and store: Add the remaining salt, grind or mix together until blended, and store in a container or bag ready to use.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HbdwlUBM6Pk
Uploaded 2024-11-05.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.
Short video, brief method.

recipes.title: Cumberland Sausage Breakfast Hash A Hearty Start to Your Day
ingredients: Oil, butter or bacon grease — for frying
steps: Prep: Dice the onion and pepper, halve the small tomatoes (or leave whole — they may pop), quarter the mushrooms, and peel the potatoes and cut them into small cubes.

Crisp the potatoes: Heat a good amount of bacon grease (or oil/butter) and fry the potatoes, letting them brown before flipping, until coloured and cooked. Season with a little garlic salt, then remove to a bowl lined with kitchen towel.
Fry the sausage: Add the Cumberland sausage meat to the pan, breaking it into clumps, and fry until browned and a little crispy.
Add the veg: Add the onion, pepper and tomatoes and cook, then add a little butter and the mushrooms and let them absorb the fat. Season with pepper.
Combine: Return the potatoes to the pan and toss together (or serve them alongside).
Serve: Pack the hash into a ring on the plate, top with a fried egg and serve with baked beans.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pp_BxJwwYq8
Uploaded 2024-11-04.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: CUMBERLAND SAUSAGE Mix TRADITIONAL BRITISH sausage blend
ingredients: Pork shoulder, coarsely ground (20–30% fat) — 1 kg
Sausage casings — soaked and rinsed, if making links
steps: Combine: Put the pork mince in a large bowl with the breadcrumbs, milk powder (the binder, which also adds a subtle creaminess), salt, both peppers, nutmeg, mace and the herbs. Add other spices such as chilli flakes if you like.

Mix until sticky: Mix by hand (or with the beater paddle on a mixer) until it turns into a sticky mix. Add up to 1/4 cup ice-cold water if needed — the video skipped it because the just-defrosted mince was already cold and wet.
Use or freeze: Stuff into sausage skins for Cumberland sausages, use as loose sausage meat, or freeze in portions.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VMDBLgeQGag
Uploaded 2024-11-04.

recipes.title: EASY Creamy Mushroom Chicken with Mashed Potatoes & Spinach
ingredients: Mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake or portobello), sliced — 1 cup
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tsp (or 1/2 tsp dried)
Whole milk or cream, warmed — 1/4 cup
steps: Boil the potatoes: Put the diced potatoes on to boil in salted water.
Season the chicken: Season the chicken with salt, black pepper and a little poultry seasoning.
Cook the chicken: Heat a little butter and olive oil, add the chicken and cook, turning a few times, until it firms up and is about 80% cooked. Wrap in foil — it will finish cooking inside.

Cook the aromatics and mushrooms: Add a little more butter to the pan, cook the onion (shallot) and garlic gently, then add the mushrooms and cook for several minutes, turning, until they take on a little colour.
Deglaze and flavour: Add a splash of chicken stock to deglaze the pan, then stir in a teaspoon each of Dijon and wholegrain mustard and a pinch of dried thyme.
Add cream: Pour in about a cup of cream, bring back to the boil and simmer for a minute or so until thick enough.
Mash: Drain the potatoes and mash with a little milk, butter, pepper and salt, keeping some texture if you like.
Finish the chicken: Slice the chicken, return it to the sauce to finish cooking, then cover with a lid to keep warm.
Wilt the spinach: In another pan, heat a little oil and butter, add the spinach with a little salt (and a pinch of nutmeg) and stir until wilted.
Serve: Plate the mash, chicken and creamy mushroom sauce with the spinach.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sfaGXVrvkvw
Uploaded 2024-11-03.

recipes.title: Easy Corned Beef Dirty Rice Recipe:  A Cajun Twist on Classic Comfort Food
ingredients: Corned beef, chopped — 340 g can or about 1 cup cooked
Green onions or parsley, chopped — for garnish (optional)
steps: Prep the veg: Dice the onion small, mince the garlic and finely dice the green pepper (plus a little red and yellow pepper for colour, as in the video). Other veg like celery or carrot work too.
Fry the aromatics: Heat a little bacon grease and butter in a wok or pan and quickly fry the onions, garlic and peppers.
Crisp the rice: Add the cooked rice, breaking up any clumps, and leave it to get a little crusty and crispy on the bottom before stirring.
Season: Stir in 1–2 tablespoons of Cajun seasoning, then let the rice blacken a little on the bottom without burning.
Add the corned beef: Stir through the corned beef (canned or a cooked joint) — no need to break it up much — then turn off the heat, taste and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RHYVapP7tqc
Uploaded 2024-11-02.

recipes.title: Easy Key Lime Pie Trifle: No-Bake Dessert Recipe
ingredients: Sponge fingers (ladyfingers) — 2 packs, or as many as you need
Key lime juice (fresh or bottled) — 1 cup (240 ml)
Whipped cream (homemade or store-bought) — 1 cup (240 ml)
Milk or lime juice — 1 cup (240 ml) (optional, for soaking the sponge fingers)
Lime slices or extra lime zest — for garnish (optional)
steps: Zest and juice: Zest some of the limes and set the zest aside, then juice them.
Lime base: Whisk the lime juice with the sweetened condensed milk in a bowl.
Make the mousse: Whip about a cup of cream with about half a cup of powdered sugar to peaks, then fold it together with the lime mixture.
Whip the topping: Whip more cream with a little sugar to stiff peaks for the top.
Dip the sponge fingers: Dip the sponge fingers briefly in lime juice (don't let them soak too much) and lay them in the base of the trifle dish, squashing them down.
Layer: Spoon over the lime mousse, add a little cream and stir it gently for a creamy layer, then build up more mousse to the edges.
Chill: Refrigerate to let it set.
Decorate: Spread the whipped cream smooth over the top or pipe it on, then finish with lime zest and lime halves. Chill for a couple of hours more if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tR5neOvcfxU
Uploaded 2024-11-01.

recipes.title: Hawaiian style MEATLOAF tropical twist on a CLASSIC
ingredients: Ground beef (or a beef and pork mix) — 500 g (1 lb)
Crushed pineapple, drained — 1/2 cup (reserve the juice for the glaze)
SPAM, diced — 1/2 cup (for folding into the mixture)
SPAM, thin slices — 1–2 (for the bottom and/or top of the loaf tin)
Salt and pepper — to taste (go light on salt — SPAM is salty)
Pineapple juice (from the crushed pineapple) — 1–2 tbsp
steps: Start the mix: In one bowl, combine the beef mince (the video also adds a little chopped smoky ham), finely diced onion and green pepper, breadcrumbs, a splash of milk, smoked paprika, garlic powder, pepper and a little salt.
Prepare the tin: Grease a 2 lb loaf tin. Cut thin slices of SPAM and lay them over the bottom, keeping some slices for the top; cube the rest and add it to the bowl.
Finish the mix: Add about a tablespoon of soy sauce, the drained crushed pineapple (squeezed so it's not too wet) and the egg, and mix well by hand.
Fill: Press the mixture into the tin, flatten the top and lay the remaining SPAM slices over it.
Bake covered: Cover with foil and cook at 180°C for about 35–40 minutes.
Turn out: Carefully turn the meatloaf out of the hot tin onto a tray (it's a little fragile at this stage).
Glaze: Mix the ketchup and brown sugar (and a little pineapple juice), spread over the meatloaf and return it to the oven for 15–20 minutes, uncovered.
Serve: Slice while warm (it's a crumbly loaf) and serve with pineapple, over rice with gravy or with mash.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9H7sjNthlPI
Uploaded 2024-10-31.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Cover the loaf tin with foil and bake for 35-40 minutes.

recipes.title: Easy Dairy and Gluten-Free Cheese Sauce Recipe: Perfect for Every Dish
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: In a pan, mix the cornflour, nutritional yeast, garlic powder, mustard powder, salt and black pepper.
Add the milk: Stir in the almond milk and a tiny pinch of turmeric.

Thicken: Heat, stirring, until the cornflour thickens the sauce, then turn the heat down. It keeps thickening as it cooks — loosen with more almond milk or water if needed, and add more salt to taste.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rtcihVi0S1o
Uploaded 2024-10-31.

recipes.title: SCOTTISH Chicken Liver Pâté with WHISKY and OATS – A Rustic Twist!
ingredients: Pinhead oats (steel-cut), toasted — 40 g (rolled oats used in the video)
Unsalted butter — 150 g (divided into 100 g and 50 g)
Fresh thyme — 2–3 sprigs (or 1/2 tsp dried), stirred through
steps: Trim the livers: Use scissors to snip out the connective tissue between the two lobes of each liver.
Toast the oats: Toast the oats in a dry pan until they have some colour and a toasty flavour, without burning, then tip into a bowl.
Soften the aromatics: Melt a little butter and gently sauté the onion and garlic with pepper for 4–5 minutes to cook out the rawness.
Cook the livers: Add the livers, turn up the heat and get a little colour on them if you can.
Add whisky: Add a good couple of tablespoons of whisky and let it cook off gently (or flambé it) until the moisture has cooked down to the buttery juices and the livers are still slightly pink.

Blend: Transfer to a chopper or blender with butter, a drizzle of cream, about a teaspoon more whisky, the toasted oats, salt and more pepper, and blend, leaving a little texture. Blend in fresh thyme leaves at the end.
Seal and chill: Spoon into a container and smooth the top, then pour over melted butter to seal. Refrigerate for about 4 hours until set, and serve on toast.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EoYN14h2xQ4

recipes.title: Comforting Chicken and Barley Soup – Ready in 30 Minutes!
ingredients: Chicken breast or thighs, cubed — 1 lb (450 g)
Chicken broth or stock — 6 cups (1.5 L)
steps: Prep: Rinse the barley, cube the chicken, chop the onion, mash the garlic, and cut the celery and carrot as big or small as you like.
Sear the chicken: Heat olive oil in a pan (it won't brown in a pressure cooker) and sear the chicken with salt and pepper just for colour, not to cook it through.

Cook the veg: Add a little more oil, then the onion and garlic briefly, followed by the celery and carrot. Add a splash of stock to help soften the veg, and a good pinch of herbes de Provence (or the thyme and rosemary).
Load the pot: Transfer everything to the Instant Pot with the bay leaf, barley and chicken stock (or veg stock), and stir.
Pressure cook: Cook on high pressure for 15 minutes.
Serve: Stir, remove the bay leaf and serve hot, with croutons or parsley if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JgGS4tNljuw
Uploaded 2024-10-29.

recipes.title: Chinese Black Bean Sauce: Flavourful and Easy to Make
ingredients: Steak — prepared and cooked how you like (sirloin/strip loin in the video)
For the green pepper black bean sauce:
Shaoxing wine or dry sherry — 1 tbsp
Cornstarch or potato starch — 1 tbsp mixed with 2 tbsp water (optional, for thickening)
steps: Prep the veg: Slice the red chilli (for colour, not heat), cut the onion into cubes and separate the layers, chop the green pepper and mince the garlic.
Sear the steak: Pat the cooked steak dry, then sear it all over in a hot oiled pan, including the fat cap. Remove, cover with foil and rest.
Start the stir-fry: Wipe out the pan, add a little fresh oil and stir-fry the garlic, then the onion and green pepper, quickly.
Make the sauce: Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, a tiny bit of sugar and a good tablespoon of prepared black beans, then the water or broth — as much as you want for a saucy finish.
Thicken: Stir in the starch slurry to thicken (add a little water if it goes too thick), then stir through the chillies.
Serve: Slice the rested steak and spoon the black bean sauce over it.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPVSzpzj1VI
Uploaded 2024-10-28.
