recipes.title: HOW to Prepare CHINESE Black Beans: Step-by-Step TAKEAWAY-Style
ingredients: Oil (your choice) — 2 tbsp, plus more for cooking and covering the beans
steps: Soak: Cover the black beans with water and soak for about an hour, stirring now and then to draw some of the salt out into the water.
Prep aromatics: While they soak, mince the garlic and a thumb-sized piece of ginger.
Drain: Drain the beans for about 20 minutes. Pick out any dried ginger pieces or debris if you like.
Fry the aromatics: Heat a couple of tablespoons of oil and cook the garlic and ginger without letting them colour.
Add the beans: Stir in the beans and cook gently with the ginger and garlic.
Simmer and season: Add the water, then the five-spice, sugar and sesame oil, and keep turning the beans until the water evaporates and the beans plump up.

Cook in oil: Once the water has mostly gone, add oil about a ladle at a time, cooking low and slow and stirring between additions, for about 15 minutes until the beans are coated and the oil is infused.

Jar and store: Turn off the heat, let cool, then spoon into clean jars, wipe the rims and top up with the infused oil to seal. Keep in the fridge for months; the beans are still salty, so watch salt levels when cooking with them.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nqq3xKEJF4A
Uploaded 2024-10-28.

recipes.title: EASY Mushy Peas Ham and Cheese Puff Pastry Turnovers - Perfect Savoury Snack
ingredients: Ready-made puff pastry — 1 pack (about 500 g), cut into 4½ × 4 inch squares
Butter — about ½ tbsp (for the peas, per the video)
White pepper — a little (per the video)
steps: Flavour the peas: Heat the mushy peas, stirring, until they thicken a little, then stir in about half a tablespoon of butter and a little white pepper. Take off the heat and let them cool completely.
Fill: On each pastry square, spoon on peas, stack on plenty of ham and press on a good amount of cheese.
Seal: Dab a little egg around the edges as glue (not too much, or it won't stick), fold the pastry over the filling and seal.
Egg wash: Brush the tops with egg.
Bake: Air fry at 170°C (340°F) for 20–25 minutes, or bake in an oven preheated to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F for 20–25 minutes, until golden.
Serve: Let them cool slightly before eating; brown sauce on the side is suggested.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K4HEcE9tEPY
Uploaded 2024-10-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) or 400°F. 20-25 mins; Air fryer 340°F  (170°C) 20-25 mins.

recipes.title: Traditional SCOTTISH Black Treacle Scones
ingredients: Dried fruit of your choice — 100 g (optional)
steps: Dissolve the treacle: Warm the milk (the video sets the jug over a bowl of boiling water) and stir in the black treacle until it dissolves. Set aside.
Dry mix: In a bowl, combine the self-raising flour, a good pinch of salt, the baking powder and the sugar.
Rub in: Add the butter and rub it in with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Bring together: Pour in the treacle milk, add the vanilla if using (and dried fruit, if you want fruit scones), and mix gently just until it comes together.
Shape and cut: Turn onto a floured board, shape and pat out (not too thin), then cut out the scones, gently re-forming the trimmings for the last few.
Egg wash: Brush the tops with beaten egg (or milk).
Bake: Bake in an oven preheated to 180°C (360°F) for about 15 minutes.
Cool and serve: Cool briefly on a rack and serve with butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i9IUP0HJTlk
Uploaded 2024-10-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Pre heat oven to 360°F (180°C)  bake 15 mins.

recipes.title: HALLOWEEN Worms and Dirt Cake PERFECT for Kids' Parties!
ingredients: Unsweetened cocoa powder — ¾ cup (64 g)
Unsweetened cocoa powder — ⅓ cup (28 g)
steps: Make the batter: Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa, salt, baking powder and baking soda, then add the milk, eggs, vanilla and water and mix to a fairly runny batter.

Bake: Pour into a lined 8 × 8 inch tin and bake at 180°C (360°F) oven or 170°C (340°F) air fryer for 25–30 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Rest about 20 minutes, then cool completely; don't trim the top.
Make the dirt: Scrape the cream out of the Oreos and crush the biscuits by hand into crumbs (not powder).
Chocolate custard: Heat the milk with the cocoa, cornflour, salt and sugar, stirring until it thickens into a thick custard. Cool it (cover with cling film if you don't want a skin).
Poke and fill: Poke holes in the cake and push gummy worms into them, keeping some worms back (halved for the top and whole for the sides). Spread over a layer of thick chocolate sauce.
Finish the topping: Stir crushed biscuits and a good amount of whipped cream into the cooled custard, chill about 15 minutes, then spread it roughly over the cake.
Chill: Refrigerate 2½–3 hours to set.
Decorate: Unmould onto a board, peel off the paper, scatter over more crushed biscuit dirt and add worms on top and poking out of the sides.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=86RSqRmEOZI
Uploaded 2024-10-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 360°F (180°C)  25-30 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C).

recipes.title: Easy Garlic Butter Chicken Bites with Rich Parmesan Pasta
ingredients: Chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces — 1 lb
White wine — ¼ cup (optional; add with the butter and cream)
Fresh spinach or steamed broccoli — 1 cup (optional)
steps: Cook the pasta: Boil the pasta (spaghetti in the video) in well-salted water to the packet instructions.
Brown the chicken: Heat a couple of tablespoons of butter with a little olive oil, add the chicken and season with salt, black pepper, paprika and pepper flakes. Cook until browned.
Add garlic and parsley: Turn the heat down, add the garlic and cook it gently, then stir in the parsley. Remove the chicken to a bowl.
Start the sauce: Wipe out the pan, add the butter over a higher heat, then the cream and garlic powder, and the zest of about half a lemon.
Add Parmesan: Stir in the Parmesan and let it melt; the sauce will start to thicken. Season to taste.
Wilt the greens: Stir in the spinach for about a minute until it wilts.
Toss the pasta: Transfer the pasta straight into the sauce (a little pasta water is fine) and toss to coat.
Serve: Plate the pasta, top with the garlic butter chicken bites and finish with extra Parmesan and parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yxfWecXwhPo

recipes.title: Spice Up Your Cooking: Easy Cajun Seasoning Recipe for Home Chefs
steps: Mix: Combine all the spices and herbs in a bowl and mix well.
Store: Transfer to a labelled bag or box. Use for jambalaya, shrimp, blackened fish and other Cajun dishes.

recipes.title: Poultry Seasoning Blend: The Key to Flavorful Chicken & Turkey
steps: Mix: Combine all the herbs and spices. No salt goes in, so you can salt the poultry separately and stay in control.

Store and use: Keep in a labelled bag or box. Rub on poultry before roasting, grilling or frying; add 1–2 tbsp to bread stuffing, 1 tsp to gravy or broth-based soups and stews, or 1–2 tsp to root vegetables tossed in olive oil before roasting (uses from the description).

recipes.title: CORNED BEEF and SAUERKRAUT Cannelloni REUBEN-inspired
ingredients: Corned beef, shredded or finely chopped — 1½ cups
Sauerkraut, drained and squeezed dry — 1 cup
Swiss or cheddar cheese (or cheese of choice), shredded — 1½ cups
Mustard — 2 tbsp (the video uses 1 tbsp Dijon and 1 tbsp wholegrain)
steps: Prep the filling: Shred the corned beef. Squeeze as much moisture as you can out of the sauerkraut (don't rinse it).
Mix: Combine the corned beef, sauerkraut, caraway seeds and dill, then mix in the cheese.
Stuff the tubes: Squash the fairly solid filling between your fingers and push it into each cannelloni tube until well filled. Keep a little filling back for the top.

Mustard béchamel: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook gently, then whisk in the milk, adding nutmeg, about a tablespoon of Dijon and a tablespoon of wholegrain mustard, and cook until thickened. Season.
Assemble: Lay the tubes in a single layer in a dish, pour over the sauce and ease some underneath, then sprinkle with a little cheese and black pepper.
Bake covered: Cover with foil and bake at 190°C (380°F) (air fryer 180°C / 360°F) for about 35 minutes.
Top and brown: Remove the foil, dot the reserved corned beef over the tubes, cover with more cheese and bake uncovered about 15 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Rest 5–6 minutes before serving, garnished with parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3w2VmKS_CwE

recipes.title: Celery Salt Quick and Easy Seasoning with Bold Flavour
ingredients: Salt (preferably sea salt or kosher salt) — 4 tbsp
steps: Grind: Blend the celery seeds, then sieve; re-blend the leftover bits until you have a fine powder if you like.
Mix and store: Mix 4 tablespoons of sea salt with 2 tablespoons of ground celery seed and keep in a sealed, labelled jar so the salt doesn't take on moisture.

recipes.title: SWEET and Sour CHICKEN Burger Takeaway in a bun
ingredients: Chicken breasts, boneless and skinless — 2 large
Water — ¾ cup, or as much as you need for a batter
Salt — ½ tsp; pepper — ½ tsp (optional)
Sweet and sour sauce — ¼ cup (store-bought or homemade)
Rice vinegar — 2 tbsp (the video uses apple cider vinegar)
Cornstarch — 1 tsp, mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Prep the chicken: Skin and trim the breasts, then butterfly them open into burger-sized pieces rather than bashing them.
Brine: Put the chicken in a bag with the water and fish sauce and leave about 4 hours (or overnight). The description notes this is a brine, not a marinade.
Mix the sauce: Combine the ketchup, vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar and pineapple juice.

Cook the sauce: Quickly stir-fry the diced carrot, peppers and onion in a little oil, keeping them crunchy, add a drizzle of sesame oil and the sauce mix, then thicken with the cornflour slurry and turn off the heat.
Make the batter: Whisk the self-raising flour with room-temperature water to a batter thick enough to cling to the chicken.
Blanch: Drain the chicken and simmer it in boiling water for a couple of minutes until just cooked (don't let it go stringy). Pat dry and season with salt, pepper or a little chicken powder.
Batter and fry: Dip the chicken in the batter and fry in hot oil, turning, until puffed, crisp and golden. Drain on a rack. Fry the pineapple rings too if you like.
Build: Fill toasted buns with mayo, the battered chicken, sweet and sour sauce and a pineapple ring.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZctLYwSg5Ik

recipes.title: Classic Mince Beef and Oven Roasted Potato Pie
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and sliced or cubed — 2 medium
Mixed herbs or dried thyme — ¼ tsp
Shortcrust pastry — for base and top
steps: Line the tin: Line an 8 inch springform tin with parchment (or grease it with butter).
Roast the potatoes: Toss the potatoes with a little oil and salt on a tray and roast at about 180°C, turning, until browned and cooked, rather than boiling them.
Start the filling: Melt a little butter, add the onion and garlic with a little salt, then the mixed herbs.
Brown the mince: Add the beef, breaking it up and turning it, and season with salt and Worcestershire (or Henderson's) sauce.
Add veg and gravy: Add the carrot and celery and cook until soft, stir in the tomato paste, then the beef stock (and flour, if using), and simmer to a thick but still loose gravy. Taste and adjust.
Assemble: Roll out the pastry, line the tin, then layer in the filling and roasted potatoes, taking care the potatoes don't push through the pastry.
Lid and vent: Lay on the pastry lid, tuck it in, roll the edges to seal and crimp, cut three steam holes and egg wash the top.

Bake: Bake at 190°C (380°F) in the oven or 180°C (360°F) in the air fryer for about 35 minutes until golden. Cool a little, release from the tin and serve, for example with mushy peas and brown sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v4LEAqaqpBg
Uploaded 2024-10-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 35 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 35 minutes.

recipes.title: The Power of Tallow: A Traditional Fat for Modern Kitchens
ingredients: Beef fat (suet or trimmings) — as much as you have collected (a little meat attached is fine)
steps: Render: Spread the fat in a tray and cook low and slow at 130°C (260°F) in the oven or air fryer for about an hour (up to 1½–3 hours for a lot of fat) until the fat has melted out, without letting it burn. If cooking in a pan, use a low flame and render slowly.

Strain and store: Drain the liquid tallow into a jar, leaving the solid bits behind, let it cool and keep it in the fridge. Use it for frying, roasting, deep-frying at 175–190°C (350–375°F) or in place of butter or shortening in pastry (uses from the description).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Vj6QFbdsTI

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Beef tallow has a high smoke point (~400°F/205°C), making it suitable for frying and roasting without breaking down into harmful compounds; COOK: Low and slow in the oven. 130°C (260°F).

recipes.title: How to Make INSTANT CUSTARD Powder FULLY Instant
ingredients: Milk powder (full cream or skimmed) — 100 g
Vanilla powder — 2 tbsp (or 1–2 tsp vanilla essence)
Yellow food colouring powder — ¼ tsp (optional)
Salt — to taste (¼ tsp in the video)
steps: Mix the powder: Combine the cornflour, powdered sugar, milk powder, vanilla powder, salt and yellow colouring, mixing gently until fully incorporated and evenly yellow.
Store: Bag it or keep it in a tub (with a tablespoon in it), shaking well before use.

Make custard: Put about 3 tablespoons of the powder in a pan, pour in the milk and whisk, then heat, stirring so it doesn't catch, until it thickens. Cook longer for thicker custard, or add more milk to thin it. It can also be cooked in the microwave for 1–2 minutes.

recipes.title: The CLASSIC SCOTTISH Potato, Cabbage, Onion, and Cheese Pie RUMBLEDETHUMPS in Pastry
ingredients: Butter or olive oil — 2 tbsp (for sautéing)
Cheese sauce (regular or gluten-free) — to serve
steps: Boil the potatoes: Put the potatoes on to boil while you dice the onion and shred the cabbage (core removed).

Cook the veg: Melt about 2 tablespoons of butter, soften the onion, then add the cabbage with a little salt and cook until wilted but not soggy. Season with pepper and caraway, take off the heat and stir in some of the cheese.
Mash: Drain the potatoes and mash with a little butter, salt and pepper, keeping it fairly dry and textured, then stir in the cabbage mixture while hot.
Make the pastry: Rub the flour, fats and salt together, then mix in the egg beaten with the water and vinegar to form a dough. Split about two-thirds for the base and one-third for the lid.
Line and fill: Line a 9 inch springform tin with parchment and the pastry base, spoon in the filling and press more cheese over it.
Lid: Cover with the pastry lid, trim and seal the edges, cut a steam vent and egg wash the top.
Bake: Bake at 190°C (380°F) in the oven or 180°C (360°F) in the air fryer for 30–35 minutes until golden.
Rest and serve: Cool 6–7 minutes, release from the tin, slice and serve with cheese sauce.

recipes.title: Easy Gluten-Free Cheese Sauce Recipe: Perfect for Every Dish
ingredients: Milk (whole or 2%) — 500 ml, plus a splash to loosen
Shredded cheese (cheddar, Gruyère or a mix) — 1 cup
Butter — 1 tbsp (optional, for a buttery taste)
Paprika or cayenne pepper — a pinch (optional)
steps: Heat the milk: Warm about 500 ml of milk in a pan.
Thicken: Whisk in the cornflour until there are no lumps and season to taste. Keep whisking as it turns glossy and thickens; it thickens quickly, so watch it.
Adjust: If it gets too thick, whisk in a little more milk to loosen it.
Add the cheese: Stir in the cheese until melted and smooth, then turn off the heat.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CRiuFpoSZao
Uploaded 2024-10-19.

recipes.title: How to Make the Perfect Creamy Cheese Sauce: Step-by-Step Guide
ingredients: Milk (whole or 2%) — 500 ml, plus a splash to loosen
Shredded cheese (cheddar, Gruyère or a mix) — 1 cup
Mustard (Dijon or English) — ½ tsp (optional; the video adds 1 tsp Colman's)
Paprika or cayenne pepper — a pinch (optional)
steps: Melt the butter: Melt the butter gently over a medium-low flame without browning it.
Make the roux: Whisk in the flour and cook briefly to remove the raw flour taste.
Add milk: Whisk in about 500 ml of milk and season with pepper (salt later if needed).
Thicken: Bring it up gently without boiling over, whisking, and add the mustard. It turns glossy as it thickens; don't let it burn.
Adjust: If it goes too thick, whisk in a little more milk.
Add the cheese: Stir in the cheese until melted, then turn off the heat. Use over pasta, potatoes, fish or in lasagne.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3qDV1RsN-lc
Uploaded 2024-10-19.

recipes.title: French ONION SOUP Bread Pudding
ingredients: Unsalted butter — 3 tbsp (plus a little oil)
Sugar — 1 tsp (optional; brown sugar in the video)
Dry white wine — ½ cup (optional; or more beef broth)
Cubed bread (day-old, sturdy, such as baguette) — 6–8 cups
Grated Gruyère cheese — 1½ cups, plus extra for topping
A little beef stock — to serve as a gravy
steps: Slice the onions: Peel and slice the onions as thinly as you can.
Caramelise: Cook the onions in butter with a little oil, a pinch of salt and the sugar for 30–40 minutes, until most of the moisture is gone and they are well browned.
Add broth: Add about a cup of beef broth (and the wine, if using), let it cook in briefly, then take off the heat and spread out to cool.
Make the custard: Whisk the eggs, milk and cream with pepper (the broth may be salty, so salt carefully).
Soak the bread: Break up the dry bread into the custard, mix and leave to stand about 10 minutes, stirring in the Herbes de Provence.
Assemble: Stir in the onions and a good handful of Gruyère, tip into a greased dish without squashing, and sprinkle a little cheese on top.

Bake: Bake at 180°C (360°F) oven or 170°C (340°F) air fryer for about 35 minutes total. With about 10 minutes to go, scatter over more cheese, press croutons into it, and return to the oven to finish.
Rest and serve: Rest about 8 minutes, then serve with a little beef stock as gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mA-2lBvdpag
Uploaded 2024-10-18.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 180°C (360°F).

recipes.title: CLASSIC Chocolate MAYONNAISE Cake: Rich, Moist, and Easy Recipe
ingredients: Unsweetened cocoa powder — ½ cup (60 g)
Heavy cream or milk — ¼ cup (60 ml)
steps: Dry mix: Mix the flour, cocoa, sugar, baking soda, baking powder and salt in a bowl (no need to sift).
Make the batter: Add the mayonnaise, water and vanilla and whisk to a smooth batter.
Prepare the tins: Butter 8 inch tins and line the bases with parchment. Divide the batter between them.
Bake: Bake about 30 minutes at 180°C (380°F) in the oven or 160°C (340°F) in the air fryer (one tin at a time in the video), until a skewer comes out clean. Turn out and cool completely.
Buttercream: Beat the butter, then beat in the powdered sugar and cocoa a little at a time, with the vanilla, a little salt and the cream.
Assemble: Use the flatter layer as the base, spread buttercream to about 1 cm from the edge, top with the second layer and press gently. Slice and serve.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mWD5Trj9iLk

recipes.title: MUSHY Pea and SAUSAGE Pie
ingredients: Flour — a spoonful (for the gravy, per the video)
steps: Cook the sausages: Oven-cook the sausages in a little oil for about 20 minutes, turning, until browned. Cool, then slice.

Make the pastry: Mix the flour and salt. Gently heat the lard, butter and water until melted (no need to boil), pour into a well in the flour and mix with a wooden spoon, then knead carefully by hand while warm.
Divide: Keep about a third for the lid and the rest for the base and sides; rest it briefly so it's manageable but still warm.
Gravy: Fry the onion in oil until coloured, stir in a spoonful of flour and cook it out, then add the gravy and cook to a thick paste. Cool.
Line the tin: Roll the larger piece and line a parchment-lined 8 inch springform tin up the sides, patching any splits.
Fill: Layer in the sausage slices, then the gravy, then the mushy peas.
Lid: Roll the lid about 1½ cm larger than the inside of the tin, set it on top, fold the side pastry over to form a thick rim, cut a vent and egg wash the top.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (360°F) oven or 170°C (340°F) air fryer for about 30 minutes until golden. Let it cool for a good few minutes before releasing and slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYMFMvtzAiU
Uploaded 2024-10-16.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 180°C (360°F).

recipes.title: Ultimate TOAD-in-the-HOLE Pie: A Hearty Twist on a BRITISH Classic
steps: Make the batter: Whisk the flour with a little salt and pepper, the milk, a little water (it turns to steam in the heat for a crispier batter) and the eggs until smooth.
Heat the oil: Put the oil in an ovenproof dish and heat it in the air fryer (180°C / 360°F) or oven (190°C / 380°F).
Brown the sausages: Add the sausages and cook, turning after about 10 minutes, until browned all over and nearly done (about 15 minutes).
Add the batter: Pour the batter around the sausages and cook about 25 minutes until risen and golden.
Make the onion gravy: Meanwhile fry the chopped onion in a little butter, then mix in gravy and make it thick, like a paste, so it sits on top. Make the mashed potato and grate the cheese.
Layer: Spread the thick gravy over the toad in the hole, then spread the mashed potato from the middle out to the edges; the Yorkshire rim holds it in.
Finish: Top with cheddar and bake about 15 minutes more until the cheese melts. Cool a little, cut into portions and serve with peas.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DBrvCIXq26g

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 190°C (380°F).

recipes.title: CLASSIC Tomato SOUP Spice Cake QUIRKY 20th century dessert
steps: Prepare: Line an 8 × 8 inch tin and heat the oven to 175°C (350°F), or the air fryer to 160°C (320°F).
Cream: Beat the softened butter and sugar together with an electric mixer.
Add the eggs: Beat in the eggs one at a time, adding a little of the flour mixture if it starts to curdle.
Dry mix: Combine the flour, salt, spices, baking soda and baking powder.
Make the batter: Mix the flour mixture, tomato soup and water into the butter mixture until smooth. Spread into the tin and level into the corners.

Bake: Bake on a tray, checking with a skewer after 30 minutes; the video needed about 5 minutes more. The description gives 40–45 minutes in the oven or 30–35 in the air fryer. It may sink a little as it cools.
Frosting: Once the cake has cooled, beat the cream cheese with the butter and vanilla, then slowly beat in the powdered sugar.
Finish: Turn out the cake (top or flat bottom up, your choice), spread with the frosting and slice.

recipes.title: TENDER Shin BEEF KEBABS Perfectly Charred and Flavourful
ingredients: Thyme (fresh or dried) or rosemary — 1 tsp
Water for the pressure cooker — about 1½ cups
Sour cream or Greek yoghurt — ½ cup
steps: Trim and cube: Trim most of the fat from the shin and cut it into cubes that will fit on a skewer.

Marinate: Drizzle the beef with the soy sauce, olive oil and lemon juice, add the thyme, garlic and all the spices, then a squeeze of honey. Rub it all over, cover and marinate for 2 hours (2–4 hours or overnight per the description).

Pressure cook: Put a trivet in the Instant Pot with about 1½ cups of water and pile the meat on top, leaving gaps so the steam can get between the pieces. Pressure cook on high; the description suggests 35–40 minutes (the video's 46 minutes made the meat too tender). Natural release 10–15 minutes, then release the rest manually.
Cool: Lift the beef out and let it cool and rest.
Make the dip: Mix the sour cream, mayonnaise, garlic, chipotle sauce, lime juice and seasoning (plus paprika and cilantro if using).
Skewer and char: Thread the beef onto skewers with the diced onion and peppers and cook in a hot pan until charred on the outside. Serve with the dip.

recipes.title: Hearty Shin Beef and Bean Chili: A Comforting One-Pot Meal
ingredients: Beef shin, cut into large chunks — 800 g
Beef stock — 500 ml (the video makes about 900 ml so some can go into the beans)
Kidney beans, drained and rinsed — 1 can (400 g)
Black beans, drained and rinsed — 1 can (400 g)
Cornflour/cornstarch — 1 tbsp, mixed with a little more than 1 tbsp water (optional, to thicken)
Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped — to garnish
steps: Sear the beef: Heat oil in the pan, season the beef with salt and pepper and sear it all over. Transfer it to the Instant Pot liner.
Soften the aromatics: Add a touch more oil, then the garlic and onions, and stir-fry until the rawness goes and they take a little colour.

Bloom the spices: Add the oregano and spices and cook for about a minute over moderate heat, keeping it moving so they don't burn (burnt spices taste bitter). Add the juice from the can of tomatoes to stop them catching.
Add the tomatoes: Stir in the chopped tomatoes and the tomato paste and cook briefly to take off some of the sourness.

Pressure cook: Tip it all into the pot with the beef, stir in 500 ml beef broth, scraping up anything stuck on the bottom. Pressure cook for about 45 minutes, then natural release for 15 minutes and release the rest manually. (Description alternatives: about 2½ hours on the stovetop or 5 hours in a slow cooker.)
Cook the beans: Meanwhile simmer the kidney and black beans gently in the extra beef broth with the bay leaves for 10–12 minutes, without boiling hard.
Combine and thicken: Stir the beans into the chili and remove the bay leaves. For a thicker sauce, stir in the cornflour slurry and cook on sauté until thickened.
Serve: Serve with rice, cheese, sour cream, fresh herbs or cornbread.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MUJFPa5aad0
Uploaded 2024-10-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Pressure cook 45 mins natural release 15 mins; Slow cooker 5 hours.

recipes.title: Spicy Harissa Lamb Shoulder with Roasted Vegetables and Lemon Couscous
ingredients: Lamb shoulder, whole or in large pieces — 1.5 lb (700 g)
Harissa paste — 3 tbsp (plus a little extra for the sauce)
Chicken or vegetable broth — 1 cup (240 ml)
Vegetables of your choice (the video uses potatoes, baby carrots, red cabbage, red onion, tomato and bell pepper)
Salt, pepper, smoked paprika, cumin, coriander and garlic powder — to taste
Fresh cilantro or parsley, chopped — to garnish
steps: Make the rub: Mash the garlic to a paste and mix with the harissa, olive oil, salt, pepper, lemon juice and the spices. Keep a little back for the sauce.
Marinate: Rub the paste all over the netted lamb, top with an extra spoonful of harissa and leave to marinate for about 3 hours or overnight.

Pressure cook: Put a trivet in the Instant Pot with the stock underneath, sit the lamb on top out of the liquid and pressure cook on high for 45 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes, then release the rest manually. Keep the cooking juices. (Description alternatives: slow cooker 3 hours on high or 5 on low; stovetop 2½–3 hours.)
Prepare the vegetables: Cut the vegetables into chunks, toss with the olive oil, salt, pepper and about half the spice mix, and spread on a lightly oiled tray.
Roast: Roast at about 190°C (380°F) for roughly 30 minutes, turning halfway (or a couple of times) so they cook down and char a little.

Crisp the lamb: Remove the netting, put the lamb in a small tin with a little of the cooking juice and set it above the vegetables to brown, turning once to crust it all over; watch it if it is close to the heating element.
Make the sauce: Warm the remaining juices with the leftover harissa paste and about 1 tbsp cornflour, stirring until thickened.
Couscous: Bring the stock to a boil, pour over the couscous with the lemon zest and juice, cover and leave 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and stir through herbs.
Serve: Slice the lamb over the roast vegetables, spoon over the sauce and serve with the lemon couscous.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=35M7Ix8NN9A
Uploaded 2024-10-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 190°C (380°F); Air Fryer  180°C (360°F); Bake 35 - 40 mins until charred a little.

recipes.title: Harissa Paste spicy chili paste that originates from North Africa
ingredients: Dried red chillies (e.g. guajillo, New Mexico, Thai or a mix) — 8–10
Bell peppers/capsicum, roasted and peeled (or ready-jarred) — 3
Olive oil — 2–3 tbsp, plus a little for roasting and to cover
Red wine vinegar — 1 tbsp (optional, for tang)
Sugar or honey — 1 tsp (optional, for balance)
steps: Soak the chillies: Soak the dried chillies in water (about 2 hours in the video).

Roast the peppers: Cut the flesh off the peppers, avoiding the seeds, and lay them skin side up on a tray. Drizzle with olive oil, turn to coat and roast in a preheated oven for about 15 minutes until the skins blister and blacken.
Prep the chillies: Remove the stems and slit the soaked chillies open to scrape out the seeds, then roughly chop them so they blend easily.
Steam and peel: Put the hot peppers in a plastic bag to steam and soften the skins, then peel the skins off, keeping the flesh.
Blend: Put the peppers, garlic, chillies, spices, salt, sugar, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, tomato paste and olive oil in a blender and blend to a paste.
Store: Spoon into a sterilised jar, cover the top with a layer of olive oil and keep in the fridge for up to about 2 weeks, topping up the oil after each use.
recipes.notes:

recipes.title: CLASSIC Tuna Noodle Casserole: A HEARTY and Comforting Family Favourite
ingredients: Canned tuna, drained — 2 cans (5 oz each)
Condensed cream of mushroom soup — 1 can (10.5 oz)
Shredded cheddar cheese — 1 cup (some for the top)
Fresh parsley, chopped — 2 tbsp (optional, to garnish)
steps: Cook the noodles: Boil the noodles in salted water (no oil needed) for a little less than the packet time so they keep some bite. Drain and set aside.
Soften the onion: Simmer the diced onion in the pasta water for a few minutes to take off its raw, harsh taste.
Make the sauce: Whisk the condensed soup, mayonnaise and milk with pepper, the garlic powder and onion powder (no salt needed, as the soup is salty).
Combine: Stir in the onion, some of the cheese, the peas and the tuna, then fold through the noodles. Spread in a baking dish (about 9 × 13 inch).
Top: Mix the breadcrumbs with the melted butter, scatter over the top and finish with a little more cheddar.

Bake: Bake in a preheated oven at about 180–190°C (360–380°F) until the top is golden and crusty. Everything is already cooked, so it only needs about 20 minutes in the video (the description gives 40–45 minutes in the oven or 20–25 in the air fryer).

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 190°C (380°F); Bake 40 - 45 mins until golden; Air Fryer  180°C (360°F); Bake 20 - 25 mins until golden.

recipes.title: Traditional Chocolate Oliver Pudding: A Classic British Dessert from the 19th Century
ingredients: Butter, softened or melted — 75 g, plus extra for the dish
Milk or cream (the video uses half and half) — 120 ml
steps: Dry mix: Whisk the flour, baking powder, cocoa powder and sugar together in a bowl.
Make the batter: Add the egg, milk/cream and butter and beat with an electric whisk until smooth.
Prepare the dish: Preheat the oven to 180–190°C (or the air fryer to 170°C / 340°F). Butter an 8 × 8 inch dish up the sides and spread the batter in it.
Add the topping: Dust the batter with the cocoa powder, then scatter over the sugar. Pour the very hot milk or cream over the top and don't stir.

Bake: Bake about 25–30 minutes, checking at 20, until the sponge has risen and the sauce has sunk underneath. Rest for a minute, dust with icing sugar if you like and scoop out with the sauce from the bottom.

recipes.title: Cheesy BEEF and Potato Bake: The Ultimate Comfort Food
ingredients: Large potatoes, sliced thickly (about ½ inch; skins on in the video) — 4
Chilli flakes or jalapeños — optional, for heat
steps: Roast the potatoes: Toss the sliced potatoes with olive oil (and pepper if you like), spread on lightly oiled trays and roast at about 190°C (380°F) until browned and crusty, swapping the trays over and turning the slices partway through.
Brown the mince: Heat a little olive oil over moderate heat, add the mince, season and cook, turning, until it starts to brown.

Build the sauce: Add the onion and garlic and stir, then the paprika, oregano and cumin. Snip the tomatoes in the can, add them with the tomato paste and simmer to thicken. Crumble in the bouillon cube; you want a moist sauce that isn't runny. Add chilli if you like heat.

Layer: Turn the oven to about 180°C (360°F). Put half the roast potatoes in a baking dish, spoon over half the meat, scatter with mozzarella, then repeat with the remaining meat and a top layer of potatoes.
Top and bake: Cover with more mozzarella (and cheddar if using) and bake until golden and bubbling; the description gives 20–25 minutes.
Rest and serve: Let it stand for 7–8 minutes before serving, with cornbread if you like.

recipes.title: Quick and Easy Cornbread Recipe: Ready in Under 30 Minutes
ingredients: Sugar — ¼ cup (optional, for a slightly sweet cornbread)
Vegetable oil or melted butter — ¼ cup
steps: Prepare: Preheat the oven to about 180–190°C (360–380°F), or the air fryer to 180°C (360°F). Butter an 8-inch square tin and line it with parchment.
Dry mix: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar (if using), salt and cornmeal in a bowl.
Wet mix: Whisk the buttermilk, melted butter and egg together.
Combine: Add the wet mix to the dry and stir just until everything is moistened. Pour into the tin.
Bake: Bake about 20–25 minutes, until a skewer or toothpick comes out clean.
Serve: Rest 5 minutes, turn out and cut into squares. Serve warm with butter. (Rick trims and saves the crusts for another recipe.)

recipes.title: EASY Ham and Cheese Puff Pastry Turnovers  -  Perfect Savoury Snack
ingredients: Dijon mustard — 1 tsp (optional; no more or it gets too sharp)
Mozzarella — optional, extra on top of the filling
steps: Make the filling: Mix the diced onion, ham, Dijon mustard, cheddar and black pepper in a bowl so the mustard coats everything.
Cut the pastry: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan / 400°F) or the air fryer to 170°C (340°F). Cut the pastry into rectangles (about 4 × 4½ inches), half as bases and half as lids.
Fill: Pile a generous amount of filling on each base, adding mozzarella if you like.
Vent the lids: Cut air vents in each lid before putting it on, which also lets it stretch over the filling.
Seal: Brush the base edges lightly with egg wash, stretch the lid over, press it down and crimp the edges with a fork. Brush the tops with egg wash.
Bake: Bake about 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool for a minute before cutting.

recipes.title: TREACLE GEORGE lesser-known traditional BRITISH dessert
ingredients: Butter or margarine, softened — 100 g (3.5 oz)
Mixed spice (or cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice) — 1 tsp
steps: Prepare: Grease and line a 20 cm (8-inch) square tin. Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan / 350°F); the video uses an air fryer at 160°C.
Cream: Beat the butter and sugar together, then beat in the black treacle.
Add eggs and spice: Add the eggs, spices, salt and about half the flour (the flour stops the eggs curdling) and mix.
Finish the batter: Mix in the milk and the rest of the flour, then stir in the dried fruit if using.
Bake: Spoon into the tin, ease it into the corners and bake about 30–35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool and serve: Leave in the tin about 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack. Slice and serve as a cake or warm with custard.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Chicken Tenders  | Chicken Goujons
ingredients: Chicken tenders (or chicken breast, sliced into strips) — quantity not stated
Salt and white pepper — to season the chicken
Plain/all-purpose flour, seasoned with black pepper — for dredging
Garlic powder — 1 tsp (½ tsp in the flour, ½ tsp in the breadcrumbs)
Smoked paprika — 1 tsp (½ tsp in each)
Chicken powder/bouillon powder — 1 tsp (½ tsp in each)
steps: Season the chicken: Season the tenders on both sides with salt and white pepper.

Season the coatings: Season the flour with black pepper, then split the garlic powder, smoked paprika and chicken powder between the flour and the breadcrumbs, mixing each well so the flavour stays even if some coating comes off.
Coat: Dredge each tender in the flour and shake off the excess, dip in the egg, then roll in the breadcrumbs and set on a rack.

Air fry: Spray with olive oil and cook on a rack above the tray so air circulates. The video's first batch at 180°C needed about 20 minutes, turning halfway, and came out pale; Rick switched to 200°C (400°F) for 22 minutes for the second batch, which the description also gives (oven: 210°C / 420°F for 22–25 minutes).
Make the dip: Mix the mayonnaise with the sriracha, a pinch of garlic powder and a little lime juice if you like.
Serve: Serve the tenders hot with the dip and salad.

recipes.title: Chicken Liver Pâté Creamy Silky Smooth EASY Spread
ingredients: Unsalted butter — 150 g (100 g for cooking, 50 g for blending)
Fresh thyme — 2–3 sprigs (or ½ tsp dried)
steps: Trim the livers: Use scissors to snip out the connective tissue joining each liver.
Soften the aromatics: Melt the butter over moderate heat and sauté the onion and garlic with salt and pepper for 4–5 minutes, until the rawness has gone.
Cook the livers: Turn up the heat, add the livers and cook until lightly browned but still slightly pink inside; don't overcook or they go tough.
Add brandy: Add the brandy and let it cook off (or flambé it).
Blend: Transfer to a blender with the remaining butter, the allspice and the cream, and blend until silky smooth.
Add thyme: Stir in a few fresh thyme leaves, using them sparingly, and spoon into a container. Smooth the top.

Seal and chill: Pour melted butter over the top with a few thyme leaves (or cover with cling film) and chill about 4 hours to set. Keeps 3–5 days in the fridge or up to 3 months frozen. Serve on crusty toast or crackers.

recipes.title: Tikka Masala Cooking Sauce Shelf-stable
ingredients: Water — 3.75 litres (including about 400 ml for the slurry)
Evaporated milk — 525 g (or coconut milk powder, 300 g)
Coconut milk powder — 300 g (or evaporated milk, as above)
Whey protein concentrate — 150 g (optional, for creaminess)
Lactic acid or lemon juice — 150–225 ml (add to taste; not too sour)
Cumin seed — 15 g (optional; not used in the video)
Food colouring — optional, for a red colour
Butter and a splash of oil
steps: Fry the aromatics: Heat the oil and fry the garlic and ginger purée for 2–3 minutes to cook out the rawness, then stir in the onion powder.
Bloom the spices: Add the garam masala, cumin and both paprikas and stir them in the oil.

Add tomato and dairy: Stir in the tomato purée with a little water rinsed round the tin, then the milk, yoghurt, coconut milk powder, whey protein, lemon juice and the rest of the water (minus the slurry water), along with the sugar and salt.
Simmer: Bring to a gentle rolling simmer, add the fenugreek leaves and simmer about 30 minutes, stirring so nothing catches.
Thicken: After about 20 minutes, whisk the cornflour into about 400 ml water and stir it in, then cook briefly without boiling hard until thickened.

Jar: In the video the sauce goes into sterilised jars, which are then processed in boiling water for 10 minutes to seal. (Note: tested home-canning guidelines don't cover dairy or starch-thickened sauces, so refrigerating or freezing is the safer way to store it.)

Weeknight tikka masala: Brown the chicken in butter and a splash of oil with a sprinkle of garam masala. Add a jar of sauce, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered about 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens. Stir in a little cream if you like and serve with rice.

recipes.title: Quinoa Wrap EASY! How to make gluten-free quinoa wraps
ingredients: Water, for blending — 1½ cups (plus water for soaking)
Olive or coconut oil — for greasing the pan (optional)
steps: Rinse and soak: Rinse the quinoa, cover with water and soak overnight.
Blend: Rinse and drain the quinoa. Put a little water in the blender first, then add the quinoa and the rest of the water and blend smooth. Stir in a little salt. The batter will be quite runny.

Cook: Heat a pan over a fairly low flame, pour in a ladleful of batter and swirl it round gently. Leave it to cook as the water bubbles off, until it releases from the pan and the edges start to curl up.
Flip: Don't turn it too early. Once the edges lift, flip and cook another 1–2 minutes until puffed with a little colour, flipping back briefly if needed. Stack the wraps on a plate.
Store and use: Fill like any other wrap. They keep 3–4 days in a zip-top bag in the fridge.

recipes.title: AUSSIE Crunch it's a BRITISH treat!
steps: Prepare: Butter an 8 × 8 inch tin and line it with parchment. Preheat the air fryer to 175°C (340°F) or the oven to 180°C (380°F).
Mix: Stir the melted butter with the sugar, cocoa and golden syrup, then mix in the crushed cornflakes, flour and coconut until fully combined.
Press: Tip into the tin and press it down firmly and evenly.
Bake: Bake about 20 minutes (20–25 in the oven), then leave to cool completely; it firms up as it cools.
Top: Melt the chocolate with the oil in the microwave in 30-second bursts, spread over the base as thick as you like and chill until set before cutting.

recipes.title: BRING out the ICONIC Pickle BRANSTON
ingredients: Spirit vinegar (white vinegar in the video) — 400 ml
Date paste — 800 g (or blend 800 g stoned dates with 4 tsp rice flour)
Apple pulp — 800 g (about 3½ cups finely chopped apples)
Roasted barley malt extract — 8 tsp (optional, for colour)
steps: Dice the vegetables: Peel the swede and carrots and cut them, the onion and the cauliflower into very small cubes (about ½ cm) to match the jar.
Make the date purée: Stone the dates and blend them with the rice flour.
Start cooking: Put the vegetables in a large pan with water (the video used about 800–900 ml and suggests less, since the salt draws a lot of liquid from the veg) and bring to a boil. Add the salt.

Add the sauce ingredients: Add the lemon juice, malt vinegar and white vinegar, then the date purée, tomato purée, apple pulp and sugar. Spread pastes across the top and stir so they don't sink and burn.
Colour and spice: Stir in the barley malt extract, then the allspice, onion powder, cloves, black pepper and mustard powder.

Simmer and thicken: Simmer, stirring so nothing sticks, and thicken with the cornflour as it cooks. The video simmered a couple of hours in total; use more cornflour for a pickle as thick as the original.
Jar: Spoon into jars. Rick found his version a little sweeter and warmer from the pepper and mustard, and less sour than the original, which uses stronger trade-only spirit vinegar.

recipes.title: BASTURMA from Pork Loin
ingredients: Pork loin — 1 kg (the video uses a piece of about 2 kg)
Ground mustard powder (instead of fenugreek) — 15 g
Water — 100 ml (enough for a thick paste)
steps: Make the cure: Mix the salt, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, black pepper, cayenne, paprika and sugar, then mix in the minced garlic.
Cure for 7 days: Pat the rub all over the pork, put it in a zip-top bag with any leftover rub, squeeze out the air and double-bag it. Refrigerate 7 days, turning it daily; don't drain the liquid.
Rinse and air-dry: Rinse off all the spices under cold water, pat dry with kitchen towel and stand on a rack for 24–48 hours (2 days in the video) until the surface feels leathery and firm.
Coat with chaman: Mix the coating spices with the water to a thick paste and smother it all over the meat, wearing gloves because of the cayenne.
Wrap and hang: Wrap loosely in cheesecloth so it can breathe, tie with string and hang in a well-ventilated place for about 2 weeks, until very firm but still slightly soft when squeezed.

Slice and store: Unwrap, slice thinly and serve, for example on a cheeseboard. The description says it keeps 2–3 months in the fridge (wrapped in greaseproof paper in an airtight box) or 6 months frozen.

recipes.title: POTATO and BEEF Brisket Gratin
ingredients: Beef brisket, thinly sliced (or any thinly sliced beef) — about 450–500 g
Potatoes, sliced thinly (skins on) — amount not stated
Butter and a little oil — for frying and the dish
Fresh chives or green onion tops, chopped — 1 tbsp
steps: Prep: Thinly slice the onions, crush the garlic and slice the potatoes to roughly even thickness.
Flash-fry the beef: Heat butter and a little oil and quickly stir-fry the beef just to cook it off, without browning. Remove.
Cook the onions: In the same pan add the onions and garlic with a little salt and about 1 tsp dried thyme, and sauté gently until soft.
Layer: Butter a baking dish set on a tray. Layer potatoes, beef and onions, repeating and finishing with beef on top. Pour over the cream and season with pepper.

Bake covered: Cover with foil and bake in a preheated oven at about 180°C (380°F) for about 45 minutes; the video needed another 10 minutes until the top potatoes were tender (the description gives 50 minutes covered).
Add cheese: Uncover, scatter with cheese and bake about 15–20 minutes more until golden and crisp on top.
Make the sauce: Mix the sour cream, horseradish, lemon juice and chopped green onion or chives, and season.
Serve: Rest the gratin about 8 minutes, then serve with the horseradish sauce and pickled red cabbage.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gmRBZvFrvqc
Uploaded 2024-09-28.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (180°C)  50 mins covered 15-20 mins uncovered; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  50 mins covered 15-20 mins uncovered.

recipes.title: BACON and CHEDDAR BREAD Pudding
ingredients: Bacon, cooked and cut up — 8 slices (about 200 g)
Mozzarella — optional, a handful for stringiness
Bread, cubed (stale or toasted) — 4 cups (about 240 g)
Heavy cream or milk — 1 cup (240 ml)
Fresh thyme, chopped — 1 tbsp (or 1 tsp dried)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Unsalted butter — 2 tbsp (for the onions and greasing)
steps: Cook the onion: Melt a little butter, add the onion with a pinch of salt and the thyme and cook gently until translucent. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
Break up the bread: Tear or cube the bread, crusts and all, into a large bowl.
Make the custard: Whisk the eggs with salt, pepper, garlic powder, mustard, the milk/cream and evaporated milk.
Prepare: Preheat the oven to 180°C (380°F) or the air fryer oven to 170°C (340°F). Cut the cooked bacon into pieces and butter a baking dish set on a tray.

Assemble: Mix the onions and custard into the bread with some of the cheddar and bacon. Tip it loosely into the dish without pressing down, dot the rest of the bacon in and around and top with the remaining cheddar and some mozzarella.
Bake: Bake about 20 minutes (14 in the air fryer per the description) until golden and set.
Serve: Let it set for a minute, cut through the crunchy top with a knife and serve with beans or veg.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yca1Hf6Gr8o
Uploaded 2024-09-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (180°C)  20 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  14 mins.

recipes.title: OATMEAL BANANA Bread
ingredients: Unsalted butter, melted (or coconut oil) — ½ cup (115 g)
Plain yoghurt or sour cream — ½ cup (120 g)
Chopped walnuts or chocolate chips — ½ cup (50 g) (optional)
steps: Mash the bananas: Mash the bananas (the riper the better) and leave them about 10 minutes to start browning, which gives the loaf a better colour.
Dry mix: Stir together the flour, baking soda, salt, oats and cinnamon.
Prepare the tin: Line a 9 × 5 inch (or 9 × 4½ inch) loaf tin with a liner or parchment. Preheat the oven to 180°C (360°F) or the air fryer oven to 160°C (320°F).
Wet mix: Add the vanilla, melted butter, brown sugar, eggs and sour cream to the bananas and mix.
Combine: Gently fold the wet mix into the dry ingredients and spoon into the tin. Fold in the walnuts or scatter them over the top.
Bake: Bake about 40–50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool: Cool on a rack before slicing. Serve with butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gLuMliqnLJY
Uploaded 2024-09-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven 360°F (180°C). 45 mins; Air fryer 320°F  (160°C) 40 mins.

recipes.title: CLASSIC Canadian POUTINE: Double-Fried Perfection!
ingredients: Vegetable oil — enough for deep frying
Beef or chicken stock (stock cubes in the video) — 2½ cups
steps: Cut the chips: Peel the potatoes, keeping them in a bowl of water so they don't brown. Slice the end off each potato so it sits flat, cut into chips any size you like and return them to the water, stirring to rinse off some starch.
Dry: Drain the chips well; wet potatoes spit in hot oil.

Make the gravy: Melt the butter, stir in about the same amount of flour and cook briefly without browning much. Add the stock and simmer until thickened, seasoning with pepper (and salt or herbs as you like). Add cornflour if you want it thicker.
Blanch: Heat the oil to a moderate temperature and fry the chips in batches until just barely coloured. Drain on a rack over a tray, not kitchen paper, so they don't steam and go soggy.
Second fry: Turn up the heat and fry all the chips again until golden and crisp. Season with salt.
Assemble: Pile the chips up, scatter over the cheese curds and pour over the hot gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_khNpi0VVHc
Uploaded 2024-09-25.

recipes.title: CORNED BEEF Mozzarella Stuffed POTATO Pancakes
ingredients: Medium potatoes, peeled and quartered (boiled and mashed plain, cooled) — 2.5 lb (about 1.2 kg)
Corned beef (canned or homemade), crumbled — 1 can (340 g / 12 oz)
Plain/all-purpose flour — 250 g, plus extra for dusting
Salt and pepper — ½ tsp each, to taste
Mozzarella — a small square per pancake
steps: Cook the filling: Heat the oil and butter, add the onion with a pinch of thyme and a little salt, and sauté gently until translucent.

Add the corned beef: Break up the corned beef in the pan with the onions, add a splash of Worcestershire sauce, the garlic powder and onion powder, then turn off the heat. Spread out to cool completely.
Make the dough: Beat the egg into the cold mashed potato with a little salt and pepper, then work in the flour to make a soft dough.
Portion: With floured hands, divide the dough into balls (12 in the video) and flatten each slightly.
Fill and shape: Spoon filling and a square of mozzarella onto each round, bring the potato dough up over the top and press it closed so nothing escapes. Flatten into pancakes on a floured tray.
Fry: Shallow-fry in hot oil until golden on both sides, then drain on a rack (not straight on kitchen paper) to keep them crisp. Serve with ketchup, mustard, sour cream, veg or gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vs-CiP3JObY
Uploaded 2024-09-24.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: RICOTTA Cheese GOATS Cheese UNDER 30 minuets
ingredients: Apple cider vinegar (or lemon juice or citric acid) — 4 tsp
steps: Heat the milk: Heat the milk gently, stirring more as it warms so it doesn't catch on the bottom, until it is just under boiling (about 95°C / 203°F): steaming with a few small bubbles at the edge. Watch it so it doesn't boil over.
Curdle: Stir in the apple cider vinegar, heat a little longer, then turn off the heat and leave about 10 minutes.
Strain: Line a strainer over a bowl with damp cheesecloth, pour in the curds and lift the cloth to drain. Keep the whey for baking or the garden.
Season: Drain to the texture you like (Rick keeps it soft), then mix in a little salt. Careful, it is still warm.
Store: Spoon into a tub and chill; it firms up a little. Use as you would any ricotta, on crackers, toast and more.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tb_XOHaDwvo
Uploaded 2024-09-23.

recipes.title: EASY CURDS, Cottage CHEESE, or FARMER’S cheese
ingredients: Apple cider vinegar (or lemon juice) — 3 tbsp
Herbs or other flavourings — optional, added once the curds have formed
steps: Heat the milk: Heat the milk in a large pan, stirring now and then and more often as it warms, especially over the hot spots of the burner, so it doesn't catch.
Watch it: When it steams, shimmers and starts to froth with small bubbles it is close to boiling. Turn the heat down so it doesn't boil over.
Curdle: Stir in the vinegar. The curds separate from the whey straight away. Keep it on a very low flame briefly, stirring, then turn off the heat and leave about 5 minutes.
Drain: Line a colander with damp cheesecloth (so the curds don't stick) set over a sieve or bowl, and scoop in the curds. Let it drain without squeezing for a loose cottage or farmer's cheese.
Finish: Add salt and any flavourings. For paneer, squeeze out the whey and press the curds firm.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ek_k-ExGyCI
Uploaded 2024-09-22.

recipes.title: Flapjack Oats, Butter, and Nostalgia
steps: Prep the tin: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F), or an air fryer to 170°C (340°F), and line an 8-inch square tin with parchment.
Melt: In a large pan or wok over a low flame, melt the butter with the brown sugar and golden syrup, stirring until just combined; don't take it further.
Mix: Off the heat, stir in the instant oats, the salt and the vanilla until everything is coated.
Press: Tip into the tin, starting in the middle, and press it out evenly to the edges; the firmer you press, the firmer the flapjack.
Bake: Bake for about 20 minutes, until brown around the edges. It will still be soft in the centre; don't overbake, as it sets as it cools.
Cool and cut: Let it cool and firm up in the tin, lift it out on the paper, and cut into squares.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ta7lItMR6q8
Uploaded 2024-09-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) and line an 8-inch square baking tin with parchment paper; Air fryer 340°F  (170°C); Bake 20 mins.

recipes.title: Creamy Spinach and Mozzarella Melts
ingredients: Spinach — 300 g (fresh, or frozen, thawed and squeezed dry)
Mozzarella — 120 g, plus extra for topping
steps: Garlic butter: Melt the butter in a pan and sauté the garlic until it just starts to colour.
Roux: Stir in the flour and cook briefly.
Spinach: Add the chopped, squeezed spinach and pepper and cook for a couple of minutes.
Cream: Pour in the cream and simmer, watching the heat, until it thickens a little.
Cheese: Add a pinch of nutmeg, then the Parmesan and mozzarella, and stir until melted and stringy. Take off the heat.
Top: Heat the oven to about 170–180°C (340°F). Spread the mixture right to the edges of the bread slices and add a little more mozzarella on top.
Bake: Set the slices on a raised rack on a tray and bake (or air fry) until the cheese is melted and browned and the bread is crisp underneath.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aA7GVkCA_TM

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 170°C (340°F); Bake the prepared toast for about 10-15 minutes, or until the cheese on top is melted and golden.

recipes.title: OLIVE LOAF Classic Deli Meat with Pimento-Stuffed Olives – Easy Recipe!
ingredients: Pimento-stuffed green olives — 150 g (5.3 oz), drained and sliced
Kosher salt — 10 g (2 tsp), or 7 g (1¼ tsp) table salt
Pink curing salt (Prague powder #1) — 2.5 g (½ tsp)
Sugar — 10 g (1 tbsp), or 10 ml (2 tsp) light corn syrup
Powdered milk — 15 g (2 tbsp) (optional, helps texture)
Oil — for greasing a 2 lb loaf tin
steps: Season the meat: Mix the beef and pork by hand, then add all the spices, salt, sugar, powdered milk and the pink cure (2.5 g per kg of meat).
Mix: Beat with the paddle of a stand mixer (or by hand) until fully incorporated, adding the cold water a little at a time.
Chop finer (optional): For a finer texture, pulse some or all of the mixture in a food processor; the video leaves some coarse texture.
Fill the tin: Grease a 2 lb loaf tin and press a layer of meat firmly into the bottom, then layer in olives and more meat, pressing everything down well.
Cure: Cover with cling film and refrigerate for about 24 hours (optional, but it lets the cure and spices work).
Bake: Bake at 160–170°C (320–340°F) for about 1–1½ hours (up to 2), until the centre reads 72°C on a probe thermometer.
Rest and slice: Let it rest and cool in the tin, then turn out and slice thinly.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mxMzlTk-iNA
Uploaded 2024-09-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven at 340°F (170°C). 60-90 mins; Air fryer 320°F  (160°C) 60-90 mins; Internal temp of 72°C.

recipes.title: Deviled Ham Creamy, Spicy Spread
ingredients: Cooked ham — 1 lb (450 g), finely chopped or ground
Pickles or pickle relish — 2 tbsp, finely chopped
steps: Prep the ham: If using packet ham, dip it in boiling water for about 30 seconds to remove the slime, then roughly chop it.
Chop the veg: Whizz the onion, celery and pickles in a mini chopper.
Chop the ham: Pulse the ham in batches; leave some texture or blend to a fine paste as you prefer.

Season: Combine ham, veg and mayo in a bowl, then add the vinegar, Dijon, Worcestershire, smoked paprika, cayenne, black pepper and a little salt (the mustard is salty). Mix well, adding more mayo if you want it moister.
Chill: Cover and refrigerate for about an hour so the flavours come together, then serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QYB--TAsTB4
Uploaded 2024-09-18.

recipes.title: EASY Corned BEEF ANY Joint of BEEF
ingredients: Beef cube roll / ribeye roll (or any joint) — 1.67 kg (3.7 lb)
Table salt — 28.5 g (or 16 g kosher salt); about 1.7% of the meat's weight
Pink curing salt (Prague powder #1) — 4.2 g (2.5 g per kg of meat)
Water — enough to cover the beef
Red pepper flakes — ½ tsp (optional, or cayenne)
Garlic — 6–8 cloves, crushed (or 1 tsp garlic powder)
steps: Split the spices: Mix the spice blend and divide it roughly in half: one half for the cure, the other kept for cooking.
Rub: Mix the salt and pink curing salt into the curing half and rub it all over the beef. Trimming the fat is optional.
Brine: Put the beef in a vacuum or zip-top bag, add enough water to submerge it, and seal.
Cure: Refrigerate for 5–7 days (5 for this 1.6 kg joint), turning the bag over every day.
Rinse: Drain off the brine and rinse the beef well.

Cook: Dissolve the stock cube in a little water in the Instant Pot liner, add the reserved spices, the beef, and cold water to cover. Pressure cook on high for 75 minutes, then allow a 15-minute natural release before releasing the rest. (Description alternatives: slow cooker 8–10 hours on low or 4–6 on high; stovetop about 2½–3 hours.)
Rest and slice: Lift the beef onto a tray, let it rest and settle, then slice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R3CgJsAgNPA
Uploaded 2024-09-17.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Instant pot 75 mins; Slow cooker:  On Low: 8 to 10 hours - On High: 4 to 6 hours.

recipes.title: Corned BEEF and MOZZERELLA Bites & Zesty Spicy Mustard Aioli
ingredients: Corned beef — 1 tin (about 340 g), or homemade
Potatoes — a couple, boiled (amount to taste; a filler)
Mozzarella — amount not stated, in small pieces
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs — for coating (amounts not stated)
Dijon mustard — 1 tbsp (the video uses about half)
steps: Dry mash: Boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, drain, and dry them back on the heat. Mash with a little salt and pepper but no butter or milk, so the balls don't fall apart. Let it cool completely.
Mix: Break up the corned beef and mix in enough mash to stretch it without overpowering it. Season as you like.
Stuff: Roll a ball, press a piece of mozzarella into it, and fold the mixture back around so the cheese is fully sealed in. Set on a tray.
Coat: Roll each ball in flour, shake off the excess, dip in egg, roll in breadcrumbs, then dip in egg and breadcrumbs again.
Aioli: Mix the garlic, lemon juice, smoked paprika, cayenne, pepper, honey (from the description), Dijon and whole-grain mustard into the mayonnaise, then refrigerate.
Fry: Heat oil to about 180°C and fry six or seven at a time, stirring gently since they sink, until golden all over. A rack in the pan helps stop them splitting on the hot bottom.
Serve: Drain and serve hot with the aioli.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7eroZPkWImI
Uploaded 2024-09-16.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Whiskey Bourbon Cream Sauce – Your New Go-To 'Ketchup' | Shelf-Stable for 12 Months!
ingredients: Scotch whisky, Irish whiskey or bourbon — 70 ml (¼ cup)
Evaporated milk (or non-dairy creamer) — 150 ml (⅔ cup)
Corn syrup or glucose syrup — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Salt — ½–1 tsp (3–6 g), to taste
steps: Weigh carefully: Use micro scales for the preservatives.
Whisk: In a pan, whisk the whisky, evaporated milk, sugar, salt, pepper, garlic and onion powder, Dijon, Worcestershire and corn syrup together.
Dissolve the preservative: Dissolve the sodium benzoate in a little water and set aside.
Warm: Heat low and slow just until the sugar dissolves; don't boil. Take off the heat and stir for a minute to cool slightly.
Thicken: Sprinkle in the xanthan gum while stirring vigorously to avoid clumps. It thickens more as it cools, so don't overdo it.
Preserve: Stir in the dissolved sodium benzoate, then the citric acid.
Bottle: Pour into a sterilised bottle, cap, and let cool. Store unopened in a cool, dark cupboard for 6–12 months; once opened, refrigerate and use within 2–3 weeks.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BHnwRwQSvtI
Uploaded 2024-09-15.

recipes.title: OATMEAL Bread Pudding
ingredients: Stale bread — 500 g (4 cups), cubed or torn
Evaporated milk — 1 can (about 379 ml), plus 150 ml whole milk (or heavy cream)
Raisins or mixed dried fruit soaked in rum — ½ cup (75 g) (optional)
Butter — melted for the custard, plus extra for greasing and dotting (amount not stated)
steps: Bread and oats: Tear the bread into chunks (crusts on or off) into a large bowl and scatter over the oats.
Fruit: Add the rum-soaked raisins, with the rum if you like.
Custard: Beat the eggs with the evaporated milk, milk, vanilla, a pinch of salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, sugar and some melted butter.
Soak: Pour the custard over the bread, mix through, and leave about 10 minutes to absorb, adding more liquid if it seems dry.

Bake: Grease a 9×13-inch dish with butter, tip the mix in without pressing it down, and dot with butter if you like. Bake at 180°C (360°F) for about 45 minutes, or in an air fryer oven at 170°C (340°F) for 25–30 minutes, until bubbling and a skewer comes out clean.

Caramel: Melt the sugar in a pan over a gentle flame, swirling, until golden amber. Gently add the butter and cream (per the description) with a pinch of salt, and take it off the heat before it gets too thick.
Serve: Rest the pudding for 5–6 minutes, then serve with the caramel and a little cream.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gznFe7hr7po
Uploaded 2024-09-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven 360°F (180°C). 45 mins; Air fryer 340°F  (170°C) 30 mins.

recipes.title: Thai SWEET CHILI Sauce POPULAR Favourite REVEALD!
ingredients: Glucose syrup or light corn syrup — ¼ cup (85 g)
Distilled white vinegar — ¼ cup (60 ml)
Hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco) — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Xanthan gum — ¼ tsp (optional, for thickening)
Sodium benzoate — ⅛ tsp, about 0.24 g (optional; about 0.1% of the sauce's weight)
steps: Dissolve: Put the water, vinegar, sugar and glucose in a pan over a moderate flame and stir until the sugars dissolve, then bring to the boil.
Flavour: Add the tomato paste, hot sauce, salt, paprika, cayenne, garlic powder and chilli flakes, and whisk until the garlic powder dissolves.
Simmer: Simmer 3–4 minutes, stirring so nothing catches.
Thicken: Off the heat, sprinkle over the xanthan gum while stirring vigorously to avoid lumps, then leave about 5 minutes to thicken.
Preserve: Once it has cooled slightly, mix in the sodium benzoate thoroughly. It keeps about 3 months in the fridge (about a week without the preservative), and thickens further as it cools.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1hLIGCr2yGk
Uploaded 2024-09-13.

recipes.title: BEEF & Tomatoes Chinese Style
ingredients: Beef (flank, topside or sirloin) — 400–500 g, thinly sliced
Water — about 2 tbsp (for the baking soda)
Spring onions — a few (part with the onion, part for garnish)
Oyster sauce — 1 tbsp (optional; use more soy instead)
Sugar — 1 tsp (the video uses ¼–½ tsp)
Cornstarch — 1 tsp, mixed with 2 tbsp water as a slurry
steps: Prep the veg: Slice the onion lengthways, chop the garlic, julienne or mince the ginger, and cut the spring onions, keeping thin slices back for garnish.
Tenderise: Slice the beef thinly on the diagonal. Toss with white pepper and the baking soda, then mix in about 2 tbsp water until absorbed. Leave 10 minutes.
Peel the tomatoes: Nick a cross in each tomato, cover with boiling water until the skins loosen, peel, remove the stem end, and cut into wedges.
Rinse and marinate: Rinse the beef (optional, removes any baking-soda taste), pat dry, then mix with the soy sauce, pepper, Shaoxing wine and a splash of sesame oil. Leave about 8 minutes.
Sauce: Mix the soy, oyster sauce, hoisin, sugar and sesame oil. Mix the cornstarch slurry separately.
Sear the beef: In a hot pan with a little oil, lay the beef flat and sear until coloured on both sides, then remove it.
Aromatics: Add a little more oil, then the garlic and ginger; when the garlic just tinges, add the onion and spring onion.
Combine: Add the tomatoes and the sauce and cook briefly to soften them, return the beef, and stir through.
Thicken and serve: Stir in a little slurry for a thick, glossy sauce and garnish with the sliced green onions.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qLKFu7rXgTI
Uploaded 2024-09-12.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: CUMBERLAND Sausage and Apple Pie
ingredients: Large apples (Bramley or Granny Smith) — 4, peeled, cored and sliced
Mashed potatoes — 4 cups, prepared with 2 tbsp butter and ½ cup milk
steps: Cook the sausages: Put the sausages in a pan with water and a little oil and boil, turning, so they plump up; when the water evaporates, fry in the oil until lightly coloured. Remove.
Soften the veg: Melt the butter in the same pan and gently sauté the onion and leek without browning.
Apples: Add the sliced apples with salt and pepper and cook about 5 minutes to soften.
Sweeten: Add the brown sugar and cinnamon and cook on a moderate flame until the sugar dissolves and the apples are soft but still hold some firmness. Turn off the heat.
Assemble: Heat the oven to 180–190°C (360–380°F). Slice the sausages thin and long, mix them through the apple filling, and spread in an ovenproof dish.
Crumb: Stir the breadcrumbs into the melted butter and scatter over the filling.
Top: Fork the mashed potato over loosely, leaving peaks to crisp, and sprinkle with cheddar.
Bake: Bake 20–30 minutes (air fryer 180°C for 20–25) until the top is crusty and golden.
Rest: Let it stand 7–8 minutes before cutting through the cheesy top and serving, with gravy if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=syLpctYCJ70
Uploaded 2024-09-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 25-30 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 20-25 minutes.

recipes.title: MINERS Mix TRADITIONAL Northeast of England Sandwich
ingredients: Red onion — 1 large (or 2 small), thinly sliced
White vinegar (or apple cider vinegar) — 1 cup
Optional: 1 smashed garlic clove, ½ tsp black peppercorns, ½ tsp mustard seeds, 1 bay leaf (the video uses black pepper and 2 bay leaves)
Butter, mustard, sliced corned beef, sliced egg, tomato, pickles, cheese — amounts not stated
steps: Pack the onions: Slice the onions and pack them tightly into a sterilised jar.
Brine: Bring the vinegar and water to the boil, add the sugar, salt, pepper and bay leaves (plus any other flavourings), and stir a few seconds until dissolved. Turn off the heat.
Pickle: Pour the hot brine over the onions (a funnel is safest), wiggle a skewer down to release air, lid, cool, then refrigerate at least an hour. They keep about 2–2½ weeks in the fridge.
Butter: Split the stottie and butter both halves generously.
Fill: Spread with mustard, then layer corned beef, egg, pickled red onions, salt and pepper, tomato and any pickle you like. For the second version use cheese with the onions.
Serve: Close, cut through in one go, and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ceK7xSmTPQs
Uploaded 2024-09-10.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: The ULTIMATE Homemade CORNED BEEF: Ditch the Canned Stuff!
ingredients: Beef shoulder trimmings (or other beef trimmings) — 2 kg (4.4 lb)
Table or kosher salt — 34 g (weigh it)
Pink curing salt (Prague powder #1, 6.25% sodium nitrite) — 5 g
Gelatin or agar-agar powder — 1 tsp, with 1 cup water (optional, for texture)
Water — enough to cover the beef for cooking
steps: Cube: Cut the trimmings into good-sized cubes, keeping the fat in (it melts and gives the tinned texture).
Cure: Mix both salts thoroughly through the beef, seal in a double zip-top bag, and refrigerate 48 hours, turning it over whenever you open the fridge.

Cook: Tip the beef and all its juices into the Instant Pot, add a stock cube dissolved in cold water and enough water to cover, and stir so nothing sticks. Pressure cook 75 minutes, natural release 15 minutes, then release manually. (Description alternatives: slow cooker 8–10 hours on low or 4–6 on high; stovetop about 2½–3 hours.) The water is cooking liquid, not part of the cure.
Shred: Lift the beef onto a tray, let it cool a little, then mash and shred it with forks, keeping the fat.
Gelatin: Sprinkle the gelatin over a little water and let it bloom 5 minutes, then dissolve it with hot (not boiling) water.
Blend: Blitz the beef in a mini chopper in small batches until it resembles tinned corned beef.
Bind: Mix the dissolved gelatin thoroughly through the beef.
Set: Line a tub with parchment, press the mixture in firmly to remove air pockets, cover, and refrigerate until set. Slice for sandwiches, or cut into blocks and freeze.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O8l_m-1hORM
Uploaded 2024-09-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Instant Pot: 75 minutes; Slow cooker: 8–10 hours on Low or 4–6 hours on High.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Pork & Cider CLASSIC NORMANDY  Porc au Cidre
ingredients: Pork tenderloin — 1 lb (450 g), silver skin removed, cut into 1-inch medallions
Boskoop apples (or Granny Smith) — 2 large, peeled, cored and sliced
Dry cider — ½ cup (120 ml) (the video uses a whole 330 ml bottle)
Heavy cream — ½ cup (120 ml), up to 1 cup
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Thyme — 1 tsp fresh, chopped (or a pinch dried) (optional)
steps: Prep: Slice the onion and apples. Cut the tenderloin into medallions just over an inch thick and season with salt and pepper.
Sear: Heat butter and oil and cook the pork 2–3 minutes per side until coloured. Remove, cover with foil and rest.
Fresh pan: Pour the buttery juices into a clean pan, leaving any burnt residue behind, and add a little more butter.
Onions: Sauté the onions with a little salt, pepper and the thyme until just tinged.
Apples and cider: Add the apples and cook briefly, then pour in the cider and let the alcohol cook down. Set a few apple slices aside for garnish if you like.
Cream: Add the cream and simmer about 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Finish: Return the pork and its juices, season, and reduce to the thickness you like.
Serve: Serve with the reserved apple and a little black pepper, with mash or green beans.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p3JB4v3YCps
Uploaded 2024-09-08.

recipes.title: Fried CHICKEN Fried & Country GRAVY Two Ways
ingredients: Pan drippings, bacon grease or vegetable oil — 2 tbsp (the video adds a little butter)
Whole milk (or milk and cream) — 1½ cups, plus more to thin
Flour — about 2 tbsp (traditional way), or cornflour — 1 heaped tbsp (quick way)
Kosher salt — ½ tsp (or to taste)
Chicken breasts — amount not stated, butterflied
Buttermilk — amount not stated (or 1 cup milk with 1 tbsp vinegar or lemon juice, left 5 minutes)
Room-temperature water — a bowlful, for dipping
steps: Gravy, traditional way: Heat the bacon fat, butter or oil, stir in the flour and cook briefly, then whisk in the milk. Season with black pepper, salt, onion and garlic powder. Add more milk to thin.
Gravy, quick way: Whisk the cornflour into cold milk with the same seasonings, heat while stirring until it thickens, then stir in the bacon fat and butter. Both give the same result.
Wet mix: Beat the eggs into the buttermilk.
Seasoned flour: Mix the flour with the garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, smoked paprika, salt, black pepper and chicken powder.
Butterfly: Butterfly the chicken breasts so they're an even thickness (or pound them thin between plastic).
Coat: Dip in flour, then buttermilk, then flour, then briefly in water, and back into the flour; shake off the excess and set on a tray.
Fry: Lay the chicken into the hot oil away from you and fry until golden at the edges, then turn and cook the other side, turning again if needed.
Drain and serve: Drain on a rack (not kitchen paper) so it stays crisp. Serve with the country gravy and mashed potatoes.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3xc7TwG1BDA
Uploaded 2024-09-07.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: BEEF and GINGER Spring Onion CLASSIC stir-fry
ingredients: Beef (flank, topside or sirloin) — 400–500 g, thinly sliced
Ginger — a thumb-sized piece (about 15 g), julienned
Red chilli — a little, sliced on the diagonal, for colour (optional)
Chicken powder — a pinch (about ½ tsp)
Sugar — about ½ tsp (from the video)
Cornstarch slurry — 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with water
steps: Prep the veg: Cut the onion into long slices, finely mash the garlic, julienne the ginger, slice the chilli on the diagonal, and cut the spring onions into lengths.
Tenderise: Slice the beef thinly on the diagonal, mix with pepper and the baking soda, then mix in a little water until absorbed. Leave about 8 minutes.
Sauce: Mix the soy, sesame oil, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, chicken powder, sugar and a little water, and let it stand so the powder dissolves.
Rinse and marinate: Rinse the beef (optional, removes any baking-soda taste), then mix with light soy sauce and a little sesame oil to stop it sticking. Leave about 8 minutes.
Sear: In a hot pan with a little oil, spread the beef out and leave it about a minute to colour, then turn and cook until just done. Remove it and wipe out the pan.
Aromatics: Add a little oil and fry the garlic and ginger for a minute, then the onion, then the green onions.
Finish: Return the beef with the sauce and a drizzle of cornstarch slurry, add the remaining spring onion and the chilli, and toss until glossy. Serve straight away.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_-J7ajLvteY
Uploaded 2024-09-06.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Coconut Loaf Cake GREAT GRANDMA's Recipe BOILING the ingredients
steps: Boil: Put the butter, milk, sugar and coconut in a pan and bring to the boil, stirring, until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves.
Cool: Let the mixture go completely cold (about 10 minutes or more) so the eggs won't scramble.
Line: Grease a loaf tin (about 9 × 4½ inches) and line it with a liner or parchment.
Batter: Beat the eggs into the cooled mixture all at once, then add the flour, baking powder and salt and mix to a lumpy batter.

Bake: Pour into the tin, tap it down, and bake at 180°C (360°F), or 170°C (340°F) in an air fryer, for about 40–45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. If the middle is still damp, bake about 7 minutes more, watching the top.
Cool: Leave 5–10 minutes in the tin, then lift out onto a rack. Serve with tea, or spread with raspberry jam.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_FNJ5cdc3i0
Uploaded 2024-09-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 180°C (360°F)  for about 40-45 minutes; Airfryer 170°C (340°F)  for about 40-45 minutes.
