recipes.title: IRISH Guinness Sausage Stout Pie
ingredients: Guinness or other stout — 440 ml (a whole can)
Irish cheddar — amount not stated, grated
steps: Chop: Cut the celery, carrot and onion into chunky pieces and mince the garlic, all into one bowl. Have the mashed potato ready.
Boil-fry the sausages: Put the sausages in a pan with water and a little oil, boil them while turning so they plump up, then let the water evaporate and brown them in the oil. Remove.
Vegetables: Add the butter to the same pan and fry the vegetables and garlic, then add the thyme and Worcestershire sauce.
Thicken: Stir in a heaped tablespoon of tomato paste, then a heaped tablespoon of flour, and cook out the rawness.
Simmer: Add the stock and the whole can of Guinness and simmer about 12 minutes.
Sausages in: Slice the sausages into chunks, add them, and cook about 8 minutes more, stirring so nothing sticks, until the veg is soft but not mushy and the gravy has thickened.

Assemble: Heat the oven to 180–190°C (360–380°F). Spoon the filling and gravy into a dish on a tray, add the mash down the middle, and fork it out to the edges, leaving nooks and peaks. Top with Irish cheddar.
Bake: Bake 25–30 minutes (air fryer 180°C for 20–25) until the top is golden and crusty.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nquhHfqtbA
Uploaded 2024-09-04.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 25-30 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 20-25 minutes.

recipes.title: Salt & Pepper Chili Chips
ingredients: Sea salt — 2 tablespoons (or 1½ tablespoons table salt)
Chilli flakes (dried red; Korean chili powder used in the video) — 1 tablespoon
Chicken bouillon powder — 1 teaspoon (optional; leave out for vegetarian)
Spring onions, sliced on the diagonal (whites and green tops kept separate)
steps: Prep the veg: Mash the garlic. Cut the onion into long slices and break them apart. Slice the peppers to roughly the same size as the onion. Slice the spring onions on the diagonal; keep the green tops aside for garnish.
Make the mix: Combine the salt, Sichuan peppercorns, white pepper, chili, onion powder, garlic powder, five-spice, sugar, MSG and chicken powder. Store it in a shaker or bag.
Fry the aromatics: Heat a little oil in a pan and let the garlic sizzle briefly without burning.
Stir-fry the veg: Add the onion, peppers and spring onion whites and stir-fry steadily.
Add chips and season: Toss in the chips with about ¼ teaspoon of the mix, then sprinkle more to taste.
Finish: Turn off the heat, stir through the spring onion tops and serve. For crispier chips, keep some back and toss them in at the end, since chips cooked with vegetables won't stay fully crisp.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M6MuoWK9jQI

recipes.title: Porridge Oat Loaf CAKE TRADITIONAL Scottish & Irish
ingredients: Raisins or dried fruit — 50 g (optional; soaked in rum or whiskey in the video, amount not stated)
steps: Soak: Stir the oats into the milk and leave about 20–30 minutes to swell. Soak the raisins in a little rum or whiskey at the same time, if using.
Heat the oven: Oven 180°C (360°F), or air fryer oven 160°C (320°F).
Butter and sugar: Mix the melted butter with the brown sugar until well blended.
Batter: Add the self-raising flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon, then the eggs and vanilla, and mix to a batter.
Add the oats: Mix in the soaked oat mixture and the drained raisins.
Fill the tin: Pour into a 2 lb loaf tin lined with a loaf liner or parchment. No need to smooth the top.
Bake: Bake on a tray for about 40 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool: Leave in the tin about 5 minutes, then turn out.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x2pV8oPeU-0
Uploaded 2024-09-02.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 180°C (360°F)  for about 40 minutes; Airfryer 160°C (320°F)  for about 40 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Easiest HOISIN BEEF
ingredients: Sliced beef (sirloin, flank or top round) — 500 g
steps: Prep the veg: Slice the onion and peppers. Mince the garlic and ginger together in one tub. Cut the spring onion into about 1 cm pieces for garnish.
Slice the beef: Cut the beef on a slight angle into large slices.
Tenderise: Mix the beef with white pepper and the baking soda, then the water, and leave about 8 minutes.
Rinse: Rinse off the baking soda (optional), drain and pat dry with kitchen towel.
Marinate: Add a little more pepper, the Shaoxing wine, soy sauce and cornflour and mix until absorbed, then mix in a little oil so the slices don't stick.

Cook the veg: Heat a little oil in a wok or pan, stir-fry the onion until it starts to soften, add the peppers, then cover briefly with the heat off so they steam and keep their crunch. Push them aside.
Sear the beef: Add the beef to the hot pan, leave it a minute to brown, then push it through until caramelised in places.
Aromatics: Clear a space and stir-fry the garlic and ginger with the beef.
Sauce: Add the soy sauce, the hoisin sauce and a splash of water, stir, then toss everything together with the veg.
Serve: Stir through the spring onion and serve over rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RCPigzTOsCQ
Uploaded 2024-09-01.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie with Mashed Potato Twist
ingredients: Chicken breast or thighs, diced — 500 g
Fresh thyme — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried)
Grated cheddar — ½ cup (optional, for topping)
steps: Brown the chicken: Melt about a tablespoon of butter and fry the chicken until lightly coloured and about 75–80% cooked. Remove to a bowl.
Aromatics: Fry the onion and garlic with the thyme for a couple of minutes.
Veg: Add the carrots and celery with a little more butter and cook about 5 minutes, stirring, until softening.
Roux: Stir in the flour and cook it out for a minute.
Sauce: Add the chicken stock, cream, English mustard and bay leaf, then return the chicken.
Simmer: Simmer about 8 minutes, stirring so nothing catches, until thick but still runny. Remove the bay leaf, add the peas and cook a couple of minutes more.
Assemble: Preheat the oven. Spoon the filling into a dish on a tray, scatter over some cheddar, then top with the mashed potato, leaving it rough for crusty bits, and add a little more cheese.
Bake: Bake at 180–190°C (360–380°F) for about 20–30 minutes (air fryer 180°C/360°F for 20–25 minutes) until the top is golden and the cheese has melted. Let it cool a little before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j8EPMPREO-o
Uploaded 2024-08-31.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 25-30 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 20-25 minutes.

recipes.title: Cashew Chicken | Chicken & Cashew
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken thigh (breast used in the video), bite-sized pieces — 400 g
Chicken broth or water — ¼ cup
Big dried chillies, cut into 1 cm pieces — 4
Green, red and yellow bell pepper, bite-sized — ½ small of each
Cornstarch or potato starch slurry — a little, to thicken (amount not stated)
steps: Marinate: Mix the chicken with the white pepper, soy sauce, oil and a couple of drops of sesame oil and massage until absorbed. No starch is added. Set aside.
Prep: Mash the garlic and have the peppers, onion and spring onion chopped.
Fry the cashews: Heat the oil over moderate heat (not too hot) and gently fry the raw cashews until lightly coloured. Lift them back into their bowl.
Chilli oil: Fry the dried chillies briefly in the same oil.
Part-cook the chicken: Add the chicken and cook a couple of minutes until about 80% done and lightly coloured. Remove it, and pour off any water it released.
Veg: Add a touch of fresh oil, sizzle the garlic briefly, then add the onion and peppers for a moment to take a little colour.
Sauce: Add a little stock, then the sugar, Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, MSG, oyster sauce and about a tablespoon of hoisin, and stir.
Combine: Return the chicken and cashews, toss, and thicken with a dribble of cornstarch slurry.
Serve: Turn off the heat, add the spring onions and a shake of white pepper, and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CMX3tKrxfL4
Uploaded 2024-08-30.

recipes.title: EASY STRAWBERRY Buckle STREUSEL Cake
ingredients: Fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced — 2 cups (300 g)
Light brown sugar, packed — ½ cup (110 g)
Unsalted butter, softened — ½ cup (115 g)
Unsalted butter, cold, in small pieces — ¼ cup (57 g)
steps: Prep the strawberries: Hull them by pushing a knife in at an angle and twisting; quarter or halve large ones, or slice them.
Cream: Mix the butter with the white and brown sugars.
Make the batter: Mix in the vanilla, milk and egg, then add the flour, baking powder and salt. Don't over-beat.
Make the streusel: Rub the flour, sugar, butter and cinnamon together until crumbly.
Assemble: Line an 8×8 tray (9×9 is ideal). Spread a layer of batter in the bottom, turn the strawberries in the remaining batter, and spoon that over the base.
Top: Scatter the streusel over the top.

Bake: Oven 190°C (380°F) for about 35 minutes; air fryer 180°C (360°F) for about 30 minutes. In the video the air-fryer version needed extra time (7 more, then 9 more minutes) until a skewer came out clean.
Cool and serve: Let it cool right down before turning out or slicing; serve with cream, ice cream or custard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_h7YxM4_8FE
Uploaded 2024-08-29.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 35 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 30 minutes.

recipes.title: ITALIAN Sausage and Bean Casserole
ingredients: Italian sausage, spicy or mild, casings removed — 500 g
Cannellini beans, drained and rinsed — 1 can (400 g)
Short pasta (penne, rigatoni or fusilli) — 200 g
Shredded mozzarella or Italian cheese blend — 1 cup (optional, for topping)
steps: Cook the pasta: Boil the pasta until just al dente, drain and stir through a little olive oil so it doesn't stick. Set aside.
Skin the sausages: Slit the casings with scissors or a knife and keep the sausage meat.
Brown the sausage: Fry the sausage meat in a little olive oil over medium heat, breaking it up as it cooks, until well browned. Move to a dish.
Soften the veg: Add a little more olive oil, fry the onion and garlic, then add the carrot, celery and bell pepper with salt and black pepper and sauté about 6–7 minutes.
Season: Stir in just under a tablespoon of Italian herbs, a teaspoon of smoked paprika and 2 tablespoons of tomato paste without letting it catch.

Simmer: Add the tomatoes (chop whole ones in the can with scissors), the chicken stock, the beans and the sausage. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes, stirring now and then. If it's too wet, uncover for about 5 minutes. (At this point it can be served as a stew with crusty bread, Parmesan and basil.)
Mix with pasta: Stir the sauce through the pasta in a large bowl with some torn fresh basil.
Layer: Spoon half into a baking dish, scatter over mozzarella, add the rest and top with more cheese and some Parmesan.

Bake: Bake in a preheated oven at 180–190°C (360–380°F) for about 14–20 minutes (air fryer 180°C/360°F about 14 minutes) until bubbling and golden. Let it cool slightly and serve with basil, Parmesan and garlic bread.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1z9M3cpmwcM
Uploaded 2024-08-28.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 20 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 14 minutes.

recipes.title: BEEF and Bell Pepper Stir Fry | PEPPER BEEF  Stir Fry
ingredients: Sliced beef (flank, topside or sirloin; topside used) — 500 g
Red, green and yellow bell peppers, sliced — 1 each
Oyster sauce — 1 tablespoon (marinade), plus about 1 tablespoon (sauce)
Cornstarch slurry — 1 tbsp cornstarch with 1 tbsp water
steps: Prep the veg: Cut the onion into squares and slice the peppers. Peel the ginger with a spoon, then mince it with the garlic.
Slice the beef: Cut on a diagonal into large, even slices.
Stage one marinade: Toss the beef with the baking soda and a little pepper, add a splash of water, mix until absorbed and leave about 8 minutes at most.
Rinse: Rinse off the baking soda, drain and pat dry.

Stage two marinade: Mix the beef with 2 tablespoons soy sauce, about a tablespoon each of oyster sauce and Shaoxing wine, just under a teaspoon of sesame oil, ¼–½ teaspoon sugar (optional) and a teaspoon of cornstarch. Leave about 8 minutes.
Sauce and slurry: Mix the cornstarch slurry. In another tub combine about a tablespoon each of oyster sauce and hoisin sauce.
Cook the veg: Stir-fry the onion in a little hot oil, add the peppers, keep them moving until lightly charred, then take them out and cover so they steam and stay crunchy.
Cook the beef: Add a little more oil, fry the garlic and ginger with the beef, turning it until cooked through, then add a splash of Shaoxing wine.
Sauce: Add the sauce a little at a time and cook it off, then return the veg and toss. Add slurry if you want a stickier sauce.
Serve: Finish with a couple of drizzles of sesame oil and a shake of pepper, and serve with rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tEHdE5yLsXE
Uploaded 2024-08-27.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: BEEF KEEMA PIE & Cucumber mint Raita
ingredients: Curry powder or garam masala — 2 tablespoons
Frozen peas — 1 cup (optional; not used in the video)
Beef stock (Oxo cube) or water — about ¼ cup in the video (½ cup in the description)
Ready-rolled shortcrust pastry — 1 sheet (base and sides)
Cucumber, peeled, seeded and finely diced — ½ (skin left on in the video)
Salt — ½ teaspoon, or to taste
Black pepper — ¼ teaspoon, or to taste
Lemon juice — 1 tablespoon (up to; plus the juice of ½ lemon in the description)
steps: Prep: Dissolve a stock cube in about ¼ cup boiling water. Chop the onion, garlic, ginger, tomatoes and chillies.
Start the filling: Warm a couple of tablespoons of oil, add the whole spices briefly (don't burn), then the turmeric, garam masala and chilli powder.
Cook the mince: Add the mince, onion, tomatoes and the rest of the aromatics, breaking the mince up and pressing it down. Season with salt and pepper.

Add tomato and stock: Stir in the tomato purée and cook out its rawness (a teaspoon of sugar is optional), add coriander, then the stock so the mix stays moist but not wet. Peas are optional. Let it cool.
Line the tin: Line the tin, roll out the shortcrust and fit it in the base and sides, leaving a little overhang if you can.
Fill: Spoon in the cooled mix and gently press it down.
Top: Cut the puff pastry into roughly equal squares, overlap them over the filling dabbing water between them, trim, fold the edges in and press down to seal.
Glaze and bake: Egg-wash the top, put the pie on a tray and bake at about 180–190°C for 20–25 minutes (air fryer 180°C for about 25 minutes).
Make the raita: Deseed and dice the cucumber, then mix with the yoghurt, mint, coriander, lemon juice, cumin, chaat masala, coriander and pepper.
Serve: Let the pie cool until warm, then serve with the raita and chips.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lvtoyR-dhUI
Uploaded 2024-08-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 25 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Corned Beef Hash Pie
ingredients: Corned beef, canned or homemade, diced — 340 g
Large potatoes, peeled and diced (about 1 cm cubes) — 3
Vegetable oil or butter — 2 tbsp (about 4 tbsp oil used to fry in the video)
steps: Par-boil: Boil the diced potatoes in lightly salted water for about 6–7 minutes, until a fork just goes in. Drain.
Make the mash: Boil more potatoes and mash with the milk, butter, salt and pepper, leaving some lumps if you like.
Fry the potatoes: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the potato cubes, turning now and then, until coloured and crisp in places.
Onion and garlic: Add a little more oil at the side, fry the onion and garlic, then mix through the potatoes and season lightly.
Corned beef: Mash the corned beef slightly and stir it in with a little thyme and the Worcestershire sauce.
Gravy: Add the beef stock or gravy and cook briefly until thickened, without letting the potatoes break down.
Assemble: Spoon the filling into a dish, top with mash roughed up with a fork into peaks, then scatter over the cheddar and the breadcrumbs mixed with melted butter.

Bake: Bake at 180–190°C (360–380°F) for about 20–25 minutes (air fryer 180°C/360°F for 15–20 minutes) until golden and crusty. Rest about 5 minutes and serve, traditionally with a fried egg and beans.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9HTPx433zj8
Uploaded 2024-08-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 15-20 minutes.

recipes.title: Queen Of Tarts Nostalgic BRITISH RARE Treat
ingredients: Unsalted butter, softened — 150 g (⅔ cup), plus extra for the tin
Raspberry or strawberry jam — 100 g (⅓ cup)
steps: Cream: Beat the butter and sugar with a pinch of salt, as light and fluffy as you like.
Batter: Beat in the vanilla, the eggs and the milk, then the flour, scraping down the bowl. A whisk works if you have no electric beater.
Prepare the tin: Butter a 6-hole muffin tin well and set it on a baking tray. Heat the oven to 180°C (360°F), or an air fryer to 165°C (330°F).
Fill: Spoon batter into each hole about halfway, add a blob of jam in the centre, then cover with more batter, aiming for the middle so it encases the jam.
Top: Pile a thick layer of desiccated coconut over each one.

Bake: Bake about 12–15 minutes (the description gives 20–25 minutes in the oven). Test with a toothpick at the side, not the middle where the jam is, and return any that aren't clean for a few more minutes.
Cool: Leave about 5 minutes, then lift out and shake off any over-browned coconut.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gABOQu9W344
Uploaded 2024-08-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 180°C (360°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 165°C (330°F)  for about 20 minutes. I cooked at higher and turned it down.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
ingredients: Sliced beef (flank or sirloin; topside used) — 400 g
Dark soy sauce — 1 tablespoon (optional, for colour)
Beef broth or water — ¼ cup
Starch slurry — 1 tsp potato starch/cornstarch with 2 tbsp water (optional)
Mild red chilli, sliced diagonally — for colour (amount not stated)
steps: Prep the broccoli: Cut the florets off and halve or trim them to a similar thickness. Peel and slice the stalk too.
Aromatics: Mince the garlic and ginger together. Slice the red chilli on the diagonal for colour.
Slice and tenderise the beef: Slice on a diagonal, then mix with a shake of white pepper, the baking soda and about 3 tablespoons of water. Leave 7–8 minutes at most.
Mix the sauce: Combine the soy sauce, oyster sauce, Shaoxing wine, a heaped teaspoon of dark soy, a heaped teaspoon of potato starch, the sugar and about ¼ cup beef broth.
Rinse and marinate: Rinse the baking soda off the beef, then mix in about a tablespoon of soy sauce, a little potato starch and a little oil so the slices don't stick.
Blanch the broccoli: Boil in lightly salted water, covered, for 1–2 minutes, then drain and cool in ice-cold water to keep it bright green.
Sear the beef: In a little oil over medium-high heat, sear the beef until browned and about 80% cooked. Set aside and wipe the pan.
Stir-fry: Sizzle the garlic and ginger in a little oil until just tinged, add the broccoli to warm through, then return the beef.
Sauce: Stir in the sauce, loosening with a splash of water if it's too thick, and cook briefly.
Finish: Turn off the heat, stir in the chilli, drizzle with sesame oil and serve over white rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xjFqNbP9_j8
Uploaded 2024-08-23.

recipes.title: Maids of Honour OLDEST TART with ROYAL approval
ingredients: Icing sugar or sugar — 1 tablespoon (for sweet shortcrust)
Curd cheese, cottage cheese or ricotta — 125 g (4 oz)
Lemon zest — grated zest of 1 lemon
Cream or milk — about 1 tablespoon if needed (video)
Apricot jam (raspberry is more traditional) — as needed
steps: Rub in: At room temperature, rub the flour, shortening, butter, sugar and salt between your fingers to a breadcrumb texture (or use a food processor).
Bring together: Add the egg, water and cider vinegar, mix with a fork then your hand into a crumbly pastry. Wrap and set aside while you make the filling.

Make the filling: Mix the curd cheese with the lemon zest and juice, beaten egg, sugar, ground almonds and a pinch of salt (and rosewater if using) until smooth; loosen with a tablespoon of cream or milk if too dry.
Prep the tins: Butter the tart or muffin tin holes.
Cut and line: Roll out the pastry, cut rounds with a plain cutter and press them into the tins.
Jam and fill: Add a little apricot jam to each case, then fill about two-thirds full with the filling.
Bake: Bake at 190°C (170°C fan), or about 165–170°C in the air fryer, for 15–20 minutes until coloured.
Finish: Cool a little, then dust lightly with icing sugar.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oO2FcgzKtik
Uploaded 2024-08-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F) or 170°C (fan) and lightly grease a 12-hole tart tin.

recipes.title: CARBONARA Casserole ULTIMATE COMFORT food
ingredients: Rigatoni or penne pasta — 12 oz (340 g)
Thick-cut bacon, diced (or cooked ham) — 6 slices (about 300–350 g)
Condensed cream of mushroom soup — 1 can (10.5 oz)
Parmesan, freshly grated — ½ cup (50 g)
Black pepper and salt — to taste (the soup is salty)
Olive oil and a little butter — for the pan
steps: Part-cook the pasta: Boil the pasta in salted water to about 80% done, then drain and let it cool a little.
Cook the meat: Fry the diced bacon (or use cooked ham) until cooked through.
Soften the aromatics: In oil and a little butter over a moderate flame, cook the onion and garlic with a pinch of Italian herbs until the rawness is gone, then set aside to cool.
Make the sauce: Whisk the mushroom soup, cream, eggs and pepper in a bowl.
Combine: Stir the slightly warm pasta, onion mix, meat and frozen peas (not defrosted) into the sauce, with some Parmesan. Taste and season.
Layer and top: Spoon into a baking dish, mixing mozzarella through the pasta and scattering more mozzarella and Parmesan over the top.
Bake: Bake in a preheated oven (180°C suggested; about 170°C in his air-fryer oven) for around 20 minutes until the top browns.
Rest and serve: Cool for 6–7 minutes, then serve with parsley and extra pepper.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FJloxNbkKao
Uploaded 2024-08-21.

recipes.title: Cumberland Pie Traditional BRITISH Dish
ingredients: Beef stock or gravy (made from gravy powder) — 400 ml
Tomato paste — 1 tablespoon (heaped in the video)
Potatoes, peeled and chopped — 1.2 kg (2.6 lb)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Put the peeled, cubed potatoes on to boil in salted water.
Brown the mince: Heat oil, add the beef with salt and pepper, break it up and cook off its raw colour.
Add aromatics and herbs: Add the garlic and onion, then the thyme (and rosemary), Worcestershire sauce, carrots and peas.
Gravy: Stir in the tomato paste and the gravy, then simmer gently about 12–15 minutes, stirring, until the carrots soften and the gravy is thick. Set aside to cool.
Mash: Drain the potatoes, steam them dry briefly, then mash with the butter, milk, pepper and a little salt, leaving some texture.
Make the crumb topping: Mix the breadcrumbs with melted butter and grated cheddar.
Assemble: Spoon the filling into a dish on a tray, cover with mash right to the edges and scatter the cheese and breadcrumb mix on top.
Bake: Bake at 190°C (about 180°C in the air fryer) for 20–25 minutes; it browned in about 15 minutes in the video.
Serve: Rest a few minutes, cut through the crisp top first, then portion.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v_9tUwzCBGU
Uploaded 2024-08-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 190°C (380°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 180°C (360°F)  for about 15-20 minutes.

recipes.title: Chinese BEEF CURRY Easy recipe
ingredients: Oil — about 1 tablespoon (to coat the beef)
Chinese curry paste (homemade, see the Backyard Chef curry paste recipe) — 2½ tablespoons
Chicken stock, made with a cube — 350 ml
steps: Prep the veg: Cube the onion and prepare a little garlic if using.
Slice the beef: Slice the beef on a diagonal to get larger, nicer-looking pieces.
Tenderise: Mix the beef with a little white pepper, the baking soda and 2 tablespoons of water, and leave for about 5 minutes.
Rinse: Rinse the baking soda off with water and drain well.
Season: Add a little more pepper and a little soy sauce, then mix in about a tablespoon of oil so the slices don't stick together.
Flash-fry the beef: Heat oil in a pan until hot, add the beef and stir-fry just until the redness is gone. Tip it into a bowl and set aside, and wipe the pan clean of the liquid the beef released.
Cook the veg: Add fresh oil, then the onion and garlic, and stir-fry for a little colour. Add the peas.
Make the sauce: Add the curry paste and the chicken stock and stir until the paste dissolves. Bring it to a bubble and drizzle in a little sesame oil.

Finish: As soon as the sauce starts to thicken, return the beef and its juices and stir through. Cook a little longer for a thicker curry, or stop sooner for a runnier sauce to pour over rice or chips.
Serve: Serve with rice or chips.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5dp2vzs1os4

recipes.title: CHINESE CURRY Paste Ready 15 Mins MODERN Version
ingredients: Oil (any oil except olive oil) — 150 ml
steps: Blend the fruit base: Blend the banana with the coconut milk until smooth, like a milkshake.

Start the roux cold: Stir the flour into the oil in the pan before turning on the heat (adding flour to hot oil can make it fizz up), then cook on a gentle flame for about 2 minutes, stirring, until a few bubbles appear. Don't let it burn.
Add the spices: Stir in the curry powder, then the soy sauce, MSG, chili powder, onion powder, five-spice and sugar, keeping the flame low.
Tomato and zest: Stir in a heaped tablespoon of tomato purée and about a teaspoon of orange zest.
Cook to a paste: Add the banana and coconut milk and keep stirring on a very low flame so it doesn't stick or burn, until it comes together into a thick paste.
Portion and store: Keep it in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, or freeze it in portions for about 6 months.

To use: Use about 2 to 2½ tablespoons of paste per 300–350 ml of chicken stock: stir-fry your ingredients in a little oil, add the paste and stock and stir until it dissolves and thickens. Watch the salt, depending on your soy sauce and stock.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7nW8OFImovw
Uploaded 2024-08-18.

recipes.title: Mexican Chicken Fajita Spring Roll and Guacamole
ingredients: Bell peppers (capsicum), thinly sliced — a selection
Cornflour and water — a little, mixed as glue if the wrappers won't stick
Jalapeño, seeded and chopped — 1 (optional; chilli flakes used in the video)
Lime juice — about 2 tablespoons (juice of 1 lime)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Chili powder (gochugaru Korean red chilli powder) — 80 g
steps: Slice: Thinly slice the onion and peppers, and cut the chicken into very thin strips (halve thick breasts).
Season: Mix about 2 tablespoons of fajita seasoning through the veg and a heaped tablespoon through the chicken.
Cook the filling: Heat about 3 tablespoons olive oil, cook the chicken for about 5 minutes, add the veg and cook about 5 minutes more. Take off the heat and let it cool completely before wrapping.
Make the guacamole: Mash the avocados chunky first, then stir in the garlic, red onion, tomato, chilli, coriander and lime juice. Season to taste and chill while you wrap.
Wrap: Lay a little mozzarella on a spoonful of filling, wet the wrapper edges with water (or cornflour-water glue if they won't stick), then roll up and seal.
Fry: Fry in oil until browned; the filling is already cooked. Drain on a rack rather than kitchen paper so they stay crisp.
Serve: Cut open and serve with the guacamole.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_fisP8EPZSk

recipes.title: POTATO ASH in a GIANT YORKSHIRE Pudding
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and sliced (skins left on in the video) — 1 kg (2.2 lb) or more
Tinned corned beef (or diced bacon) — 340 g tin (optional)
Beef or vegetable stock — 1 litre (4 cups), about 2 Oxo cubes
Salt and pepper — to taste (go easy on salt)
Fresh parsley, chopped — a small bunch (optional garnish)
Butter or oil — for frying (a couple of tablespoons of butter used)
Shortening, beef dripping or vegetable oil — as needed
Salt and black pepper — a pinch each (optional)
steps: Make the batter: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, water, salt and pepper together and set aside; no need to refrigerate.
Prep: Cube the onion and carrot and slice the potatoes about half a centimetre thick, skins on.
Sauté: Melt butter over a moderate flame and cook the onion, carrot and potato about 8 minutes, seasoning with pepper and a little thyme. If using bacon, cook it with the onions first.
Add stock: Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves and the stock (about a litre of hot water with the stock cubes).
Stew: Lid on, simmer about 18 minutes, turning occasionally, until the potatoes soften and start to dissolve and thicken the stew. Add the corned beef in chunks; it breaks up into the gravy.
Bake the Yorkshire: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 230–250°C with the tray and a little oil in it for a minute. Pour in the batter and bake about 18 minutes.
Serve: Remove the bay leaves, spoon the potato ash into the giant Yorkshire pudding and add gravy around the side.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iYu0QWLKNa4

recipes.title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: Soy sauce — a couple of tablespoons
Sweet and sour plum sauce — amount not stated
Red/orange food colour — a little on the end of a spoon
Cornflour (cornstarch) slurry — about 1 tablespoon cornflour to 3 tablespoons water
Pork loin, cut into bite-sized cubes — amount not stated
Baking soda — ½ to ¾ teaspoon
Water, salt, a little oil — for the batter
Onion, diced — 1 (½ onion used on screen)
Red, green and yellow bell pepper (capsicum), cubed — ½ of each
Tinned pineapple chunks — amount not stated
steps: Make the base sauce: In a pan combine ketchup, sugar, about 3 cups water, about 5 tablespoons cider vinegar, a couple of tablespoons of soy sauce, the plum sauce, a drop of red-orange food colour and a little pineapple juice. Bring to a simmer to dissolve the sugar.
Lightly thicken: Stir in about 1 tablespoon of cornflour slurry just to give a little body; turn off as soon as it starts to thicken. Cool; this base can be bottled and kept in the fridge.
Prep the veg: Mash the garlic. Cut the onion and peppers into cubes or angled wedges (no white pith), slice the carrot and chunk the pineapple.
Tenderise the pork: Toss the pork cubes with baking soda, white pepper and a little soy sauce; leave 5–7 minutes.
Blanch: Boil salted water and blanch the pork for a couple of minutes until about 60% cooked (it will foam). Remove and rinse.

Make the batter: Mix self-raising flour, about 1 tablespoon cornflour, salt, water and a little oil into a coating batter that is not watery. Season the pork with a touch of white pepper and soy, then coat it in the batter.
Double-fry: Fry the pork in hot oil, a few at a time without crowding, until lightly golden. Remove, then return them all to the oil to crisp up. Rest on a rack.
Stir-fry: In a hot pan, cook the garlic, onion, peppers, carrot and pineapple briefly, then add a couple of ladles of the base sauce and let it bubble.
Thicken to cling: Add cornflour slurry a little at a time until the sauce clings without turning to jelly; add water if it goes too thick.
Serve: The sauce will soften the batter, so for crispy pork keep some back, pile the veg and sauce on a plate and put the crispy pork on top with sauce drizzled over.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QiuGAL2kq68
Uploaded 2024-08-15.

recipes.title: Calcium Rich Sardine and Cream Cheese Pâté Simply Delicious!
ingredients: Canned sardines in tomato sauce, with bones — 1 can (125 g), partly drained
Garlic, minced — 1 small clove (or garlic powder)
Hot sauce (Tabasco used) — a few drops (optional)
Black pepper and salt — to taste
steps: Load the blender: Add the cream cheese, garlic, drained sardines (bones and all), lemon juice, pepper, parsley and hot sauce. Drain off some of the tomato sauce for a thick paste, adding a little back if needed.
Blend: Blend, stop and scrape down, repeating until smooth. Taste and add more hot sauce if you like.
Chill: Pack into a tub, cover with cling wrap and chill in the fridge for an hour so the flavours meld.
Serve: Spread on buttered toast, or serve with celery.

recipes.title: Beef and Onions STIR FRY in Oyster sauce
ingredients: Flank steak, sirloin or topside, thinly sliced — 370 g
Water, for the beef — about 2½ tablespoons
Green onions, chopped — 2 stalks, for garnish
Soy sauce — 2–3 tablespoons (½ tablespoon of it for the beef)
Shaoxing wine — 1 tablespoon (video says about ½)
Cornstarch — 1 teaspoon for the sauce, plus a little to coat the beef
Water, for the sauce — ¼ cup
steps: Prep the veg: Cut the onions into thick slices; slice the garlic and ginger.
Slice the beef: Cut on an angle into pieces about the thickness of a thick coin.
Tenderise: Toss the beef with the baking soda and white pepper, then add the water and work it in until absorbed. Leave 10–15 minutes.
Mix the sauce: Combine the oyster sauce, soy, Shaoxing wine, dark soy, sugar, water and cornstarch.
Rinse and season the beef: Rinse off the baking soda (optional) and drain. Stir in ½ tablespoon of soy sauce and leave about 5 minutes, then mix in a little cornflour.
Sear the beef: Stir-fry in hot oil, leaving it a moment before moving it, until about 80% cooked. Drain it out.
Cook the aromatics: In a little fresh oil, fry the onion until just tinged, then add the garlic and ginger until the rawness goes.
Combine: Return the beef, add the sauce and let it sizzle and boil before tossing; cook until the sauce is as thick as you like.
Finish: Off the heat add a drizzle of sesame oil and a shake of white pepper, stir, and serve topped with green onion.

recipes.title: MUSHROOM and HALLOUMI Burgers
ingredients: Halloumi, sliced — 1 block (225 g), cut into 4 pieces
steps: Prep the mushrooms: Wipe the mushrooms clean with tissue and remove the stalks.
Make the sauce: Stir together the mayonnaise, whole-grain mustard, lemon juice and honey.
Cook the mushrooms: Brush with olive oil (save some for the buns), season, and cook gill side down in a pan for about 5 minutes, turning once, until cooked.
Grill the halloumi: Heat a little oil in the pan and grill the halloumi until it has a few scorch marks, then flip and finish. Set aside on a tray.
Warm the veg: Briefly cook the onion slices to loosen them, then give the tomato slices a quick sear, keeping it raw inside.
Toast the buns: Brush the insides of the brioche buns with olive oil and toast quickly.
Build: Spread sauce on the bun base, then add mushroom, halloumi, onion, tomato and rocket, and top with the bun lid. Cut through and serve.

recipes.title: Brioche Buns Super soft and Fluffy
ingredients: Flour (bread flour and all-purpose/plain, 300 g of each) — 600 g
Large eggs, at room temperature — 3 (or 4 small)
Unsalted butter, softened and cut into small pieces — 160 g
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the sugar into the milk, add the yeast and let it bloom.

Mix the dough: Combine the flours and salt, add the eggs, yeast milk and softened butter, and knead in a stand mixer on low (no higher than setting 2) for about 6 minutes. The dough is sticky but not completely stuck to the bowl.
First rise: Oil your hands and the bowl, turn the dough over to coat, cover and leave about an hour.
Divide: Turn onto a floured surface and cut into 12 pieces (not perfectly equal).
Shape: Pull the sides in to make a ball, then roll it on the surface by pushing forward and pulling back with your fingers with a slight twist, until smooth. Place 6 on each parchment-lined tray.
Second rise: Cover and let rise about 40 minutes at most.
Glaze: Beat the egg with a little water and brush over the buns, down the sides too. Add sesame seeds if you like.
Bake: Bake at about 160°C in the air fryer for 16 minutes (oven 175°C for 20–25 minutes), until golden.
Cool: Cool on a rack. Use for burgers or toast with butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qk_XcDTCNdc
Uploaded 2024-08-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Makes 12 big Buns; Oven 175°C (350°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 160°C (320°F)  for about 16-20 minutes.

recipes.title: Doner Meat Kebab and Sauces
ingredients: Lamb mince (or lamb and beef mix) — 1 kg
Medium onion, finely grated (flesh only, squeeze out the juice) — 1
White vinegar (apple cider vinegar used) — 1 teaspoon
Plain yoghurt or sour cream — 1–2 tablespoons (optional, for creaminess)
Fresh mint (or 1 tbsp dried), or Colman's mint sauce — 2 tablespoons fresh mint, or 1 tablespoon Colman's
White vinegar (apple cider used) — ½ tablespoon
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Pita bread (see the Easy PITA Bread recipe), warmed
Red onion, red cabbage, iceberg lettuce, tomato, cucumber — any veg you like
steps: Mix the meat: Squeeze the grated onion to remove the juice and combine it with the garlic, lamb mince, all the spices, salt, breadcrumbs and the egg if using. Squash it together until tacky and sticky. It can marinate overnight in the fridge but doesn't need to.
Wrap: Shape into a sausage, roll in foil and double-wrap, as it will leak a lot of fat. Set on a baking tray.
Bake: Bake covered at 160°C in the air fryer oven (180°C in a regular oven) for about 45 minutes, turning it over halfway and draining off some of the juices.
Make the garlic mayo: Mix the mayo with the garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, pepper, salt and the yoghurt or sour cream.
Make the tomato sauce: Mix the ketchup, coriander, cumin, mint sauce, vinegar, pepper, a little salt, sugar and yoghurt.
Brown: Carefully unwrap the very hot meat, then return it to a hotter oven (about 190°C) and turn it over to form a brown crust.
Slice: Let it cool a minute, then slice as thin as you can.
Assemble: Fill warmed, split pita with salad, doner meat, garlic mayo and tomato sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y2nQfXogrWI
Uploaded 2024-08-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the Oven to 180°C (360°F); Bake, covered for 45 minutes, turning halfway.

recipes.title: Easy PITA Bread
ingredients: Bread flour and all-purpose (plain) flour — 500 g total (250 g of each)
Extra flour and a little oil — for dusting and the bowl
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the sugar into the warm water, add the yeast and wait for it to bloom.
Mix the dough: Combine both flours, salt and olive oil, add the yeast water and mix in a stand mixer on low (about setting 2) until a sticky dough forms that doesn't stick to your hands.
First rise: Oil your hands and the top of the dough, place it in a bowl, cover and let it double, about 45 minutes to an hour.
Divide: Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and divide into 8 equal pieces (he weighs them). Fold each into a ball.
Second rise: Place the balls in a box, cover and rest about 30 minutes.
Roll: Using plenty of flour so they don't stick, roll each ball out to a pita size without squashing the dough too much.
Cook: Heat a non-stick frying pan on very low, controlling the heat. Lay a round in, let it puff, then flip for a couple of seconds to colour the other side.
Keep soft: Cover the cooked pitas, then cut partway open to stuff. They freeze well; reheat about 20 seconds in the microwave.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RMbxenu-rlA

recipes.title: Blue Cheese Sauce Pasta Casserole with Ham, Peas, and Leeks
steps: Cook the pasta: Boil the penne in salted water until nearly al dente, drain and let it cool.

Soften the leeks: Slice the leeks about ½ cm thick (white and green). Cook them with the garlic in butter or oil over a gentle heat with a little pepper and salt (go easy, as the cheeses are salty) for 5–6 minutes until wilted and tender.
Add peas and ham: Add the frozen peas for 1–2 minutes, then the cooked ham; a pinch of Italian herbs is optional.

Make the sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook briefly, whisk in the milk and cream and let it thicken. Add the blue cheese, turn off the heat and stir until melted. Thin with more milk if it gets too thick.
Combine: Mix the sauce through the pasta and vegetables.
Pack the dish: Press the mixture into a casserole dish.
Top: Cover with the mozzarella, then breadcrumbs mixed with melted butter and Parmesan.
Bake: Oven 190°C (380°F), or air fryer 180°C (360°F), for 20–25 minutes until crispy and golden.
Rest: Let it cool for about 10 minutes before cutting.

recipes.title: Corned Beef and Cabbage Egg Rolls | Spring Rolls
ingredients: Onion or green onions, finely chopped — ½ cup
Rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar — 1 tablespoon
Vegetable oil — for stir-frying and brushing
steps: Defrost and prep: Thaw the wrappers. Slice the onion, grate the carrot, ginger (and garlic if using) and shred the cabbage.
Stir-fry the veg: Stir-fry gently in oil, leaving some crunch, then add the soy sauce, sesame oil and vinegar. Set aside to cool.
Add the beef: Crumble the corned beef in; no extra salt, as it is salty. Add a shake of white pepper, mix and let cool.
Make the dip: Stir together the mustard, honey, mayonnaise, garlic powder and white pepper; adjust sweetness to taste and chill.
Fill: Place filling on a wrapper at a slight angle, fold the sides in, wet the edge with water and roll up tightly. Place seam side down on a tray.
Brush: Brush the rolls with oil all round.
Bake: Oven or air fryer at 190°C (380°F) for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway, until crispy and golden (the video used the chip setting for about 12 minutes).
Serve: Cut in half and serve with the mustard dip. The creator found the dip too mustardy and suggests less Dijon.

recipes.title: Potato and Leek Soup with Parmesan Croutons
ingredients: Large leeks (white and light green parts), cleaned and sliced — 4
Garlic, minced — 2 cloves (1 clove used on screen)
Bay leaf — 1 (two small ones used on screen)
Thyme — 1 teaspoon fresh leaves (or ½ teaspoon dried)
Fresh chives or parsley, chopped — to garnish
steps: Prep: Slice the leeks (including some green), peel and cube the potatoes and keep them in water.
Soften the leeks: Melt the butter with a little oil over a gentle flame and cook the leeks and garlic low and slow to bring out their sweetness.
Simmer: Add a pinch of thyme, the bay leaves and the stock, bring to a boil, add the potatoes and simmer about 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft and breaking up.
Blend: Remove the bay leaves and use a stick blender, smooth or chunky as you like.
Add cream: Stir in about 1 cup of cream and rewarm if you like, then season.
Make croutons: Toss the cubed bread with about 3 tablespoons olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder and grated Parmesan.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (his air fryer) about 12 minutes, flip, and bake again until crisp.
Serve: Ladle the soup into bowls, top with croutons and the crispy baked Parmesan bits, finish with pepper and, if you like, a swirl of cream or parsley.

recipes.title: Crispy Corn Fritters Smokey Beans
ingredients: Kidney beans, drained and rinsed — 1 can
Sour cream and coriander — to serve
Sweet corn, drained — 1 can (half blended, half left whole)
Spring onions, finely chopped (green tops used) — 3
Butter and olive oil (or just oil) — for frying
steps: Make the beans: Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil, add the paprika, tomato purée and sugar, then the tomatoes (chopped in the can with scissors) and the beans.
Simmer: Simmer about 15 minutes until the beans are tender and the sauce is thick, adding a little water if it gets too thick. Serve warm or cold.
Blend the corn: Blend half the corn with the milk.
Whisk: Whisk the egg whites until stiff.
Mix the batter: Stir the egg yolks into the corn and milk mix, add the flour and baking powder, then the whole corn, spring onion tops, salt and pepper, and the grated cheddar.
Fold: Fold in the whisked egg whites.
Fry: Drop spoonfuls into a pan with butter and olive oil on a gentle shimmer, turning until golden. Drain on a rack.
Crisp up: For extra crispness, put the fritters on a tray with a little cheddar on top and bake about 10 minutes until melted.
Serve: Serve with the smoky beans, sour cream and coriander.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ru3tONti4PE
Uploaded 2024-08-05.

recipes.title: Mexican Chili Lasagna
ingredients: Water — 1 can (use the empty tomato can)
Black beans, drained and rinsed — 1 can (15 oz)
Ground cayenne pepper — ½ teaspoon (adjust to taste)
Parmesan, grated — ½ cup (optional; cheddar and mozzarella used in the video)
Shredded Mexican blend cheese (cheddar, Monterey Jack etc.) — 2 cups
Fresh cilantro, chopped — ¼ cup, to garnish
steps: Prep: Dice the onion, peppers and jalapeños (seeds optional) and mash the garlic.
Brown the meat: In oiled pan, cook the pork and beef with salt and pepper plus the onion and garlic, working it down until the pan is fairly dry.
Spice: Add the chili powder, coriander, cumin, oregano, cayenne and smoked paprika and cook them into the meat, then add the jalapeños and peppers.
Tomatoes: Add the tomatoes with their juice (chopped in the can with scissors), fill the empty can with water and add that, then stir in the tomato paste. Cook down to thicken and intensify.
Beans and corn: Stir in the black beans and corn and cook about 5 minutes, then add the cilantro. Set aside.

Make the béchamel: Melt equal amounts of butter and flour together, cook off the raw flour, then add the milk and stir over gentle heat until it thickens. Season with nutmeg, then melt in cheddar and mozzarella (or Parmesan) until thick and stringy.

Layer: Smear a little sauce in the dish, then layer lasagna sheets, chili and some béchamel and cheese, repeating, with a layer of cheese over the top reaching the edges. Go light on the white sauce in the lower layers.
Bake: Tent with foil and bake at 180°C (170°C in the air fryer) for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake about 8–10 minutes to brown.
Rest and serve: Let it cool before cutting, then garnish with cilantro.
recipes.notes:

recipes.title: Cherry & Apple Turnovers
ingredients: Granny Smith apples, peeled and diced small — 3
King cherries, halved and pitted — 200 g
Ready-rolled puff pastry, cut into squares — 4½ × 4½ inch
Vanilla ice cream — optional, to serve
steps: Cook the apples: Cook the diced apples with the butter, sugar, mixed spice, vanilla and a pinch of salt (and a splash of water if you like) until softened.
Add the cherries: Stir in the halved, pitted cherries and lemon juice.
Thicken: Mix the cornflour with the water into a slurry, stir it in to thicken, then turn off the heat and cool the filling.
Fill: Line a tray with parchment, lay out the pastry squares, put filling on one half, and stretch the pastry over the top.
Seal: Crimp the edges with a fork.
Glaze: Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with demerara sugar and cut a couple of small slits in the top to let steam out.
Bake: Bake at about 175°C in an oven for 20–25 minutes (air fryer 160°C for 17–20 minutes) until golden brown.
Serve: Cool briefly and serve warm with vanilla ice cream.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RsNDK_aad9M
Uploaded 2024-08-03.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 175°C (350°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 160°C (320°F)  for about 17-20 minutes.
