recipes.title: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca ITALIAN pasta dish
ingredients: Olive oil — 2 tablespoons (plus the oil from the anchovy tin)
Anchovy fillets in olive oil, chopped or mashed to a paste — 6
Red pepper flakes (Korean chilli flakes used) — 1 teaspoon, heaped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — to taste
Fresh parsley, chopped — for garnish (some cooked in the sauce)
steps: Prep: Mince the garlic, rinse and drain the capers, halve the olives, chop the parsley and mash the anchovies with a fork; they dissolve into the sauce without making it fishy.
Boil the pasta: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water per the packet instructions (no oil needed in the water).
Start the sauce: Heat the olive oil over a low flame, add the garlic and cook until you smell it, then stir in the anchovy paste so it dissolves.
Bloom the chilli: Add the chilli flakes and let them bloom in the oil without burning, then add the capers and olives.
Tomatoes: Add the canned tomatoes (cut up in the tin with scissors), the tomato paste and the oregano.
Balance: Stir in the sugar to balance the salty, sour flavours, then add pepper and some of the parsley.
Simmer: Simmer about 10 minutes at most so the flavours come together.
Finish: Toss in the cooked spaghetti and serve with fresh parsley and, if you like, Parmesan.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6DmdFhp5jHA
Uploaded 2024-08-02.

recipes.title: BELGIAN Buns POPULAR UK Treat
ingredients: Flour (bread flour, or 250 g bread flour plus 250 g all-purpose/plain) — 500 g (3½ cups)
Filling (the description lists two versions; the longer one is first):
Unsalted butter, softened — 100 g (½ cup); the shorter version lists 50 g
Mixed spice (or ground cinnamon) — 1–2 teaspoons; the shorter version lists 1 teaspoon cinnamon
Currants or raisins — 150 g (1 cup); the shorter version lists 100 g
Sugar and boiling water — amounts not stated (stirred to a sugar syrup for brushing)
Baked in a 10 × 10 inch tray lined with parchment.
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the sugar into the warm milk, add the yeast and leave to bloom.
Mix the dough: Combine the flours and salt, add the egg, the yeast milk and softened butter, and knead in a stand mixer on about setting 2 for 6–8 minutes, without speeding it up.
First rise: Cover and leave until doubled, about an hour.

Shape: Flatten the dough on a lightly floured surface by hand (no need to roll it to a perfect square). Spread with the softened butter mixed with a couple of blobs of lemon curd, then scatter over the sugar, mixed spice and dried fruit.
Roll and cut: Roll up gently and cut into pieces with a serrated knife or dental floss, halving then dividing into three as needed.
Second rise: Arrange in a parchment-lined tray, leaving small gaps, cover and rise another 40–45 minutes.
Bake: Bake at about 175–180°C (160°C in the air fryer) for around 20 minutes.
Glaze: Stir sugar into a little boiling water to make a quick syrup and pour it over the hot buns. Cool a little, then pull the buns apart.
Ice: Mix icing sugar with a little water to a thick icing (more sugar if too thin, more water if too thick), swirl over the buns and top with a glacé cherry. Let it set slightly before eating.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dk1YtAKzACA
Uploaded 2024-08-01.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 175°C (350°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 160°C (320°F)  for about 20-25 minutes.

recipes.title: Jam & Lemon Curd Tarts
ingredients: Jam of choice (raspberry used) — a good spoonful per tart, thinned with a little water
Lemon curd — as much as you like (homemade; separate recipe on the channel)
Baking beads (or rice or sugar) and parchment for blind baking
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the fats into the flour and salt with your fingers to fine breadcrumbs, stir in the sugar and lemon zest, then the egg, water and cider vinegar, and bring together. Ready-made shortcrust works too.
Cut and line: Roll out and cut rounds (fluted cutter about 4½ inches for his large muffin tins), then press them gently into the tins. Re-rolled pastry tightens, so be gentle.

Blind bake the lemon curd shells: Line with crumpled parchment and baking beads, set on a tray and bake at about 165°C in the air fryer (175–180°C in a regular oven) for 12 minutes. Take out the paper and beads carefully, and put the beads in a tub to cool.

Fill the jam tarts: Stir a little water into the jam to thin it, then spoon it into the unbaked pastry cases and bake about 12 minutes. The jam bubbles up and will set as it cools; more water makes a softer jam.
Fill the lemon tarts: Let the blind-baked shells cool, then spoon in the lemon curd.
Serve: Let the jam tarts set before eating.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4dPDZcNRz5A
Uploaded 2024-07-31.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: BRATWURST & SAUERKRAUT Cups
ingredients: Bratwurst sausages (smoky), cooked and sliced or cubed — 3
Shredded cheese (Swiss, or cheddar and mozzarella as in the video) — 1–2 cups
German sweet mustard (Händlmaier used in the video) — 1 tablespoon
Salt and pepper — to taste (none used in the video)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C), or an air fryer to 360°F (180°C).
Roll the bread: Cut the crusts off the bread and roll each slice out flat with a rolling pin.
Butter: Brush the flattened bread lightly with butter on both sides.
Shape the cups: Press each slice into a muffin tin, folding and flattening it against the sides.
Blind bake: Line each cup with scrunched-up baking paper, fill with baking beads and bake for 8–10 minutes. Remove the beads and let the cups cool completely in the tin.
Cook the bratwurst: Boil the bratwurst until cooked through (or cook them in beer or fry them), then cut into small cubes or slices, keeping any juices.
Make the filling: Drain the sauerkraut, mix in a good tablespoon of the sweet mustard, then add the bratwurst and about a cup each of grated cheddar and mozzarella, mixing evenly.
Trim and fill: Trim the rims of the cooled cups with scissors to neaten them, then fill generously with the mixture.
Bake again: Bake for 5–7 minutes, just until the cheese melts and the tops crisp.
Serve: Cool briefly, sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve, with extra German mustard if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msiyBSKQJas
Uploaded 2024-07-30.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C); Bake cups 8-10 mins; Bake with filling 5 mins.

recipes.title: EASIEST LEMON Curd (4 Ingredients)
ingredients: Lemons (zest and juice) — 3, giving about 150 ml (5.1 fl oz) juice
steps: Zest and juice: Zest the 3 lemons into a bowl, avoiding the white pith, then juice them to get about 150 ml of juice.
Melt the butter: Melt the butter in a small pan, then turn off the heat as soon as it has melted and move the pan off the heat.
Add the sugar: Stir in the sugar and dissolve as much as you can (it won't fully dissolve).
Cool slightly: Let it cool a minute so the eggs don't scramble.
Beat in the eggs: Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the lemon zest and juice.
Cook: Return to a flame high enough to bring it to the boil without burning, stirring. Once it boils, keep stirring for about 25 seconds, then turn off the heat.
Cool and jar: Let it cool, covered with plastic wrap to stop a skin forming, until completely cold, then spoon into sterilised jars. It keeps about 10 days to 2 weeks in the fridge.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZlWCagjB__c
Uploaded 2024-07-29.

recipes.title: Roasted Red Pepper Paste | Ricotta & Spinach Tortellini | Creamy Red Pepper Sauce
ingredients: Smoked paprika — ½ teaspoon, or a pinch of chilli flakes (optional)
Creamy red pepper sauce and pasta:
Fresh basil or parsley, chopped — for garnish
steps: Prep the peppers: Remove the seeds and pith from the peppers and lay them cut side down, skin side up, on a lined tray.
Char: Roast at the oven's highest setting (230°C in the video) for about half an hour, until the skins are blackened.
Infuse the oil: Gently cook the garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil until just coloured, then turn off the heat.
Steam and peel: Put the hot peppers in a bag (or covered bowl) to steam for 5–6 minutes, then peel off the skins.
Blend the purée: Blend the peppers with the garlic oil, salt, black pepper, smoked paprika if using, and balsamic vinegar until smooth. Jar and refrigerate any you don't use.
Cook the tortellini: Boil the tortellini in salted water for about 2 minutes, according to the packet, and drain.
Start the sauce: Gently cook the garlic in 2 tablespoons of olive oil to take the rawness off, then stir in the red pepper purée and cook briefly.
Make it creamy: Season with salt and pepper, stir in the cream, then the Parmesan until melted.
Combine and serve: Toss the tortellini through the sauce and serve garnished with fresh basil or parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-nrg1uqbjuA
Uploaded 2024-07-28.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Ultimate MELTY BEEF & Pickle Crunch
ingredients: Cooked roast beef, thinly sliced — as needed
Beef stock cube, dissolved in boiling water — 1
Silverskin pickled onions, halved or sliced — as many as you like
Bread (thick slices of deli bread: rye, sourdough or crusty baguette) — 2 slices per sandwich
Butter — a thin coating for the bread
Shredded cheese (cheddar, Swiss, or American slices) — 1½ cups
steps: Warm the beef: Thinly slice the roast beef. Dissolve the stock cube in boiling water and add the beef to loosen and flavour it (it's already cooked, so it only needs warming).
Prep the onions: Cut the pickled onions in half into a bowl.
Start the cheese sauce: In a cold pan, whisk the cornflour into the evaporated milk and season with a little pepper and salt.
Thicken: Cook over a low flame, stirring, until it starts to thicken.
Add the cheese: Stir in the cheese until it comes together into a thick sauce, then take it off the heat (it thickens more as it cools).
Mark the bread: Butter the outside of the bread thinly and press briefly in a toastie maker just to get toasted lines.
Assemble: Spread horseradish on the bottom slice, then add the beef, pickled onions and cheese sauce. Put the top on, press down, slice and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ywYmEb9_DHs
Uploaded 2024-07-27.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Dutch BABY GERMAN pancake EASY recipe
ingredients: To serve (optional) — powdered sugar, lemon wedges, fresh berries or jam
steps: Make the batter: Mix the flour with a pinch of salt, then add the eggs, milk and vanilla and mix until smooth. Leave it to rest (10 minutes is suggested, though a couple of minutes is used in the video).
Preheat: Heat the oven or air fryer to 460°F (230°C).
Melt the butter: Rub butter around the tray, leave the rest in it and put it in the oven just until the butter melts.
Bake: Pour the batter into the buttered tray and bake for about 25 minutes in the oven, or 12–15 minutes in the air fryer, until puffed and golden.
Serve: Let it sit a minute, lift it out and serve with powdered sugar and lemon, jam, berries, or as is.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HwK0KRqIIes
Uploaded 2024-07-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 460°F (230°C). Bake for 25 minutes; Bake for 12- 15 minutes.

recipes.title: CHEESY Shredded BEEF Cannelloni
ingredients: Cooked shredded beef — 2 cups (about 250–300 g in the video)
Ricotta cheese (cottage cheese used in the video) — 1 cup
Dried oregano — ½ teaspoon, and dried basil — ½ teaspoon (or 1 tsp Italian herbs, as in the video)
Parmesan — a little, for the top (used in the video)
steps: Soften the aromatics: Sauté the onion and garlic gently in the olive oil just to take off the rawness. Season with a little salt and pepper, stir in the herbs and turn off the heat.
Make the sauce: Mix the condensed tomato soup with about ½ cup of water, using it to rinse out the can.
Make the filling: In a bowl, mix the shredded beef with the ricotta or cottage cheese, the onion mixture and about a cup of grated mozzarella.
Fill the tubes: Fill the cannelloni tubes with a spoon or a piping bag with a wide-cut tip.
Layer: Spread a little soup sauce in the dish, lay in the filled tubes, add more sauce and a little mozzarella, repeat, then finish with sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan and a sprinkle of herbs.
Bake covered: Cover loosely with lightly oiled foil and bake at 375°F (190°C), or 360°F (180°C) in an air fryer, for 25 minutes.
Brown: Remove the foil and bake another 10–15 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Leave 6–7 minutes to cool slightly, then serve garnished with fresh basil, with a crisp salad.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7FEPWf8Q_zY
Uploaded 2024-07-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C); Bake - covered for 25 minutes.

recipes.title: BUFFALO Chicken So SAUCY in the OVEN
ingredients: Chicken wings or middle wings — 2 pounds (1 kilo)
Cayenne pepper — ½ teaspoon (optional, for heat)
Cooking spray or oil — for the baking rack
Hot sauce (Frank's RedHot is traditional) — ½ cup
White vinegar — 1 tablespoon (optional; not used in the video)
Cayenne pepper — ¼ teaspoon (optional, for extra heat)
Salt — to taste (none used in the video)
steps: Marinate overnight: Put the wings in a zip-lock bag with the white pepper, sugar, fish sauce and water, seal, mix and refrigerate overnight.
Mix the coating: Combine the salt, cayenne, garlic powder, paprika, onion powder and baking powder (not baking soda).
Dry the chicken: Drain the wings and pat them as dry as possible with kitchen towel; leave to air-dry for half an hour if needed.
Coat: Toss the wings in a bowl with the seasoning until evenly coated.
Set up the tray: Line a tray with foil, set an oiled rack on top and arrange the wings on the rack.
Bake: Bake at 200°C (400°F), or 190°C (380°F) in an air fryer, for 12 minutes, then turn the wings over and cook about another 15 minutes, keeping one temperature throughout.

Make the sauce: While they cook, gently heat the butter, hot sauce, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, paprika, cayenne and sugar until the butter and sugar melt (or simply stir it together without heating). Add more sugar if it tastes too sour.
Toss and serve: Toss the hot wings in a bowl with some of the sauce, plate them and drizzle over more sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rTHHQBj-4UA
Uploaded 2024-07-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cooked in the oven 12 mins - turned cooked another 15 mins; Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: EASY TUNA  & Broccoli CASSEROLE
ingredients: Tuna in water, drained — 2 cans (5 oz each)
Large potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks — 4
Fresh parsley, chopped — a little (used in the video)
Garlic powder or other seasoning — ¼ teaspoon (optional)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Boil the peeled, cubed potatoes in salted water until tender for mash.
Cook the broccoli: Microwave (or steam or blanch) the broccoli florets for about 3 minutes in a 700–800 W microwave, less in a more powerful one.

Butter the breadcrumbs: Melt the butter in a small pan over a gentle flame, stir in the breadcrumbs, season with black pepper, salt and garlic powder, and stir until the butter is absorbed and the crumbs dry a little. Let them cool (mix in Parmesan only once cold).

Make the cheese sauce: Melt 2 tablespoons of butter, whisk in the flour, then pour in the milk all at once and whisk. Add the English mustard and a little salt and pepper and stir until thickened, then melt in most of the cheddar, keeping some for the top.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with butter, a splash of milk, salt, pepper, the sour cream and chopped parsley.
Assemble: Preheat the oven to 180°C (360°F). In a baking dish set on a tray, mix the broccoli with a little sauce, add the flaked tuna, spread over more sauce and sprinkle with a little cheese.
Top two ways: Spread mashed potato over one half, working it to the edges with a fork, and scatter the breadcrumbs over the other half. Sprinkle a little cheese and Parmesan over both.
Bake: Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden, then leave to cool for about 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CKrUQYgABkY
Uploaded 2024-07-23.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (360°F); bake 20 - 25 mins.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Sausage & Mash Pie | Bangers & Mash Pie
ingredients: Sausages (pork, beef or your choice) — 1 lb (450 g)
Butter — a little (used in the video for the onions)
Large onion, sliced or finely chopped — 1
Beef or chicken stock (cube, powder or gravy granules) — 1–2 cups (240–460 ml)
Frozen peas or mixed veg, defrosted — 1 cup (150 g)
Potatoes, peeled and chopped — 2 lbs (900 g)
Milk or cream — ½ cup (120 ml)
Grated cheddar cheese — ½ cup (60 g) (optional)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Boil the peeled, cubed potatoes in salted water until tender.
Cook the sausages: Put the sausages in a pan with the oil and a little water, cook while turning so the water evaporates and they plump up, then fry for colour. Remove to rest.
Caramelise the onions: Add a little butter to the sausage fat and cook the onions and garlic low and slow until coloured and sweet.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with butter, milk, a little salt and pepper, the sour cream and parsley.
Make the gravy: Stir the flour into the onions, then the Worcestershire sauce and tomato paste, then the stock/gravy. Bring to a bubble and cook to the thickness you like.
Add the veg: Stir in the frozen veg for a minute or two at most, then take off the heat.
Assemble: Preheat the oven to 180°C (360°F). Slice the sausages, lay them in a baking dish set on a tray and pour over the onion gravy so it surrounds them.
Top: Spread the mash over the top and rough it up with a fork into peaks, then scatter with cheddar.
Bake: Bake for 20–25 minutes until golden, then cool 6–7 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0C-i2HVjAFI
Uploaded 2024-07-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (360°F); bake 20 - 25 mins.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Spinach Mushroom LASAGNA EASY Creamy Recipe
ingredients: Spinach, chopped (fresh, or frozen and squeezed dry as in the video) — 2 cups
Condensed cream of mushroom soup (Campbell's) — 1 can (10.5 oz)
Ricotta cheese (homemade/cottage cheese in the video) — 1 cup
Cheddar — some, for layering and topping (used in the video)
steps: Prep the veg: Dice the onion, crush the garlic and slice the mushrooms. If using frozen spinach, squeeze out all the liquid and chop it.
Sauté: Gently cook the onion and garlic in the olive oil with pepper and only a tiny pinch of salt until the rawness is gone, without browning.
Cook the mushrooms: Add the mushrooms and sauté to drive off some of their moisture. Add more pepper but no more salt, as the soup is very salty.
Add spinach and herbs: Stir in the spinach, oregano and basil or Italian herbs, cook briefly, then set aside to cool.
Make the sauce: Mix the condensed soup with about a cup of milk and a pinch of nutmeg if using. No cooking needed.
Layer: Spread a little sauce in the dish, add lasagna sheets, then some of the vegetable filling, more sauce, ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan and a little cheddar. Repeat the layers.
Top: Finish with sheets, the remaining sauce, cheddar and clumps of mozzarella.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (360°F), or 170°C (340°F) in an air fryer, covered for 25 minutes, then uncovered for 8–10 minutes until golden. Garnish with parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mNLx0-nym8E
Uploaded 2024-07-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (360°F); bake 25 mins – covered - 8-10 mins uncovered.

recipes.title: Ultimate Sausage Bean Cheese Melt FULLY Loaded
ingredients: Puff pastry (or shortcrust) — 1 sheet, cut into 4 squares about 4 × 4½ inches
Oil — a splash (for cooking the sausages)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat the oven to 190°C (380°F), or an air fryer to 180°C (360°F).
Score the pastry: Cut a frame about 1 cm in from the edge of each square, without cutting all the way through, and prick the centre all over with a fork.
Pre-bake: Bake the pastry for 10 minutes, then leave to cool.
Cook the sausages: Put the sausages in a pan with water and a splash of oil, boil while turning so they plump up, then let the water evaporate and brown them all over in the oil. Slice them.
Shape the cases: Press the centre of each pastry square down flat to make a case inside the risen frame.
Fill: Arrange the sausage slices in each case, spoon beans in between, then top with cheddar and mozzarella.
Bake again: Bake for 8–12 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling, then serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tdf9d2YNJKY
Uploaded 2024-07-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (380°F); bake the base for 10 mins – allow to cool; bake again for 8 – 12 mins.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: CHELSEA Buns: The ORIGINAL Cinnamon Roll
ingredients: Bread flour or all-purpose/plain flour — 500 g (3½ cups)
Olive oil — a little, for the bowl
Ground cinnamon — 2 teaspoons (or mixed spice, as in the video)
Currants or raisins — 150 g (1 cup) (soaked in rum and hot water in the video)
Lemon and orange zest — some (used in the video)
Icing sugar with a tiny drop of water — for drizzling (used in the video)
steps: Activate the yeast: Stir the yeast into the warm milk with the sugar and leave about 5 minutes until it blooms.
Mix the dough: Put the flour and salt in a stand mixer bowl, add the butter, the beaten egg and the yeast mixture.
Knead: With the dough hook, mix on speed 1 briefly, then on speed 2 for 6–8 minutes until you have a soft, sticky dough.
First rise: With oiled hands, shape the dough into an oiled bowl, cover (a plastic bag works) and leave 45 minutes to 1½ hours until doubled.
Prepare the tray: Line a 10 × 10-inch tray with parchment and rub it with butter.
Shape: Press the dough out on a lightly floured surface into a rough, even rectangle.
Fill: Spread with the softened butter, sprinkle over the sugar mixed with the spice, then the citrus zest and the dried fruit.
Roll and cut: Roll up to enclose the filling, dampening the end with water to seal, then cut into 12 pieces.
Second rise: Place in the tray, cover and leave about 30 minutes until risen.
Bake: Bake at 175°C (350°F) in the oven, or 160°C (320°F) in an air fryer, for about 20–25 minutes.
Glaze and ice: Brush the hot buns with apricot jam thinned with a little boiling water. Lift them out, then drizzle over a thick icing of icing sugar and a drop of water. Tear and share.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bT6dsKblqvs
Uploaded 2024-07-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 175°C (350°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 160°C (320°F)  for about 20-25 minutes.

recipes.title: EASIEST Cinnamon Rolls Recipe
ingredients: Unsalted butter, melted — ½ cup (115 g)
Bread flour or all-purpose/plain flour — 4½ cups (540 g)
Oil — a little, for the bowl
Unsalted butter, softened — ½ cup (115 g)
Brown sugar, packed — ½ cup (100 g)
Unsalted butter, softened — ¼ cup (57 g)
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the sugar and yeast into the warm milk and leave a few minutes until frothy.
Mix the dough: In a stand mixer bowl, combine the flour and salt, then add the lightly beaten eggs, melted butter and yeast mixture.
Knead: Knead with the dough hook on a low speed (setting 2) for about 6–8 minutes until slightly sticky but not sticking to your hands.
First rise: Shape into a ball in an oiled bowl, cover with a bag and leave about 1 hour, until doubled.
Fill: Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon. Press the dough out on a lightly floured surface, brush with butter and spread over the sugar and cinnamon mixture.
Roll and cut: Roll up the dough and cut into 12 rolls.
Second rise: Place in a buttered, parchment-lined tray (10 × 10 or 12 × 12 inches), cover and leave about 30 minutes.
Make the icing: Beat the cream cheese with the butter and vanilla, beat in the powdered sugar, then loosen with about a tablespoon of milk, adding more if needed.
Bake: Bake at 175°C (350°F) in the oven, or 160°C (320°F) in an air fryer, for about 20–25 minutes.
Ice and serve: Spread the icing over the warm rolls and tear and share.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hrBFHteUr7U
Uploaded 2024-07-18.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: 1 cup (240 ml) warm milk (110°F/45°C); Oven 175°C (350°F)  for about 20-25 minutes; Airfryer 160°C (320°F)  for about 20-25 minutes.

recipes.title: Party PORK PIES Mini Size
ingredients: Butter — 110 g (plus a little for greasing the tin)
Egg, beaten, for egg wash — 1 (with a splash of milk in the video)
Pork shoulder, cut into small cubes — 400 g
Gelatin — 1–2 tsp, depending on how set you like it
steps: Make the pastry: Gently heat the water, butter and shortening until the fats melt (no need to boil hard). Pour into the flour and salt, mix, then bring together by hand.
Rest: Split the pastry into ⅔ for bases and ⅓ for lids, wrap in cling film and leave somewhere cool for about 30 minutes, so it is cool but still pliable.
Make the filling: Mix the cubed pork shoulder with the mince, then the breadcrumbs and all the herbs and spices until fully combined.
Line the tins: Butter a muffin tray or small tins. Roll the pastry out about 3 mm thick on a floured surface, cut rounds and press them into the tins.
Fill and lid: Pack the meat mixture into the cases. Cut lids, brush the pastry edges with egg wash, press the lids on and crimp to seal, making an air hole in the top.
Egg wash: Stand the tins on a tray and brush the tops with egg wash.
Bake: Bake at 170–180°C (340–360°F) for about 25 minutes until golden, then let cool.
Add jelly (optional): Dissolve the stock cube and gelatin in the boiling water. Make a hole near the edge of each pie and carefully pour in the jelly until it fills.
Set: Leave the pies to go completely cold so the jelly sets, then serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2WBOMVPdSxM
Uploaded 2024-07-17.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (360°F).

recipes.title: Blue Cheese Sauce
ingredients: Crumbled blue cheese — ½ cup (plus a little extra to crumble over, optional)
Minced shallots or onion — 1 tablespoon (2 tablespoons onion used in the video)
steps: Soften the onion: Melt the butter and gently cook the shallot or onion until translucent, without colour, about 3 minutes.
Simmer the cream: Add about a cup of cream and bring it up to a simmer.
Melt the cheese: Add the blue cheese and stir until completely melted.
Season: Add about a teaspoon of Worcestershire sauce, pepper and only a little salt, as the cheese is salty.
Thicken: Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring so it doesn't burn, until it is as thick as you like.
Serve: Pour over a cooked steak, crumbling a little extra blue cheese on top if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sH4VEwNSsgM
Uploaded 2024-07-16.

recipes.title: LONDON Cheesecake CLASSIC BRITISH pastry
ingredients: Puff pastry (or shortcrust) — 1 sheet, cut into 4 squares about 4 × 4½ inches
Salt — a pinch (used in the video)
Raspberry jam (or your preferred flavour) — 4 tablespoons
Desiccated coconut (fresh coconut used in the video) — 100 g
steps: Score the pastry: Score a border about 1 cm in from the edge of each square without cutting through, then prick the centre closely all over with a fork.
Pre-bake: Bake at 190°C (380°F), or 180°C (360°F) in an air fryer, for about 10 minutes so the border rises.
Make the cases: While warm, gently press the centres down with your fingers to make a hollow.
Make the frangipane: Cream the butter, sugar, almond extract and a pinch of salt until light. Beat in the eggs with the flour (which stops curdling), then the ground almonds.
Fill: Put a blob of jam in the centre of each case, then spoon frangipane over to cover and seal in the jam.
Bake again: Bake for about 12 minutes at 180°C, then let cool.
Ice: Mix the icing sugar with a little water and vanilla, adding water gradually, to a thick icing. Spread it over the tops up to the pastry edge.
Finish: Sprinkle with coconut, top with a cherry if you like, and let the icing set before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qWLdIiOckh4
Uploaded 2024-07-15.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (380°F); Air fryer 180°C (360°F).

recipes.title: How to make  shape super soft KAISER Rolls
ingredients: Olive oil — less than 1 tablespoon (for the bowl)
Poppy seeds or sesame seeds — optional (white sesame used in the video)
steps: Activate the yeast: Stir the sugar and yeast into the lukewarm milk and leave about 5 minutes until it blooms.
Mix: In a stand mixer bowl, combine both flours and the salt, then add the beaten egg, softened butter and yeast mixture.
Knead: Knead with the dough hook on low for about 8 minutes until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
First rise: Loosen with floured hands, place in a lightly oiled bowl, turn to coat, cover and leave about an hour (45 minutes if warm) until risen.
Divide: Tip out and divide into 8 roughly equal pieces. Tuck each under into a smooth ball.
Shape: Roll each ball into a long rope, gently lifting and stretching as you roll, then tie it into a knot and tuck the ends back through to form the Kaiser pattern.
Second rise: Cover with plastic wrap and leave to rise for about 30 minutes.
Top: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F / Gas Mark 6, or an air fryer to 160°C / 320°F. Brush the rolls with milk and sprinkle with seeds.
Bake: Bake for about 20 minutes until golden, then cool and slice for sandwiches.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yEpi5Gs6U94
Uploaded 2024-07-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F / Gas Mark 6; Bake 20 mins.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: ROCK cakes / Buns TRADITIONAL BRITISH treat
ingredients: Cold unsalted butter, diced — 100 g (1 stick)
Mixed spice or cinnamon — ½ tsp (optional)
Mixed dried fruit (e.g., sultanas and raisins; a few dried cranberries in the video) — 150 g (1 cup)
Buttermilk — 50 ml (¼ cup) (or milk with a splash of apple cider vinegar)
steps: Make buttermilk: If you have no buttermilk, add a splash of apple cider vinegar to milk (1 tbsp per cup) to curdle it.
Rub in: Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then rub in the cubed butter with your fingers until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Add sugar and spice: Stir in the caster sugar and mixed spice.
Mix the wet: Beat the egg into the buttermilk with the vanilla.
Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F / Gas Mark 6, or an air fryer to 170°C / 340°F.
Combine: Stir the dried fruit into the dry mix, then add the wet mix and stir together with a fork.
Shape: Spoon rough heaps onto a parchment-lined tray without compressing or flattening, keeping them about the same size.
Bake: Sprinkle with demerara sugar and bake for about 15 minutes.
Cool: Leave on the tray a couple of minutes, then cool on a wire rack. Serve warm with butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iqrHkjmwvD4
Uploaded 2024-07-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F / Gas Mark 6.

recipes.title: EASY Sandwich Bread Homemade Pain De Mie
ingredients: Unsalted butter, softened or melted — 45 g (3 tbsp)
Olive or other oil — a little, for the bowl
Covered loaf tin — 8 × 4 × 4½ inches in the video
steps: Grease the tin: Butter the inside of the lidded loaf tin and its lid.
Activate the yeast: Stir the sugar and yeast into the warm milk and leave until it froths up.
Mix: Combine both flours and the salt in a stand mixer bowl, add the yeast mixture and start mixing with the dough hook, then drizzle in the butter.
Knead: Knead for about 6 minutes until smooth.
First rise: Tuck the dough into a ball, place in an oiled bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for 45 minutes to an hour.
Shape: Tip out and push down to expel some air, then roll or fold it up to fit the tin, tucking in the sides and ends.
Second rise: Press it into the tin, put the lid on, cover and leave about 30 minutes until the dough reaches the top.
Bake: Bake with the lid on at 180°C (360°F), or 160°C (320°F) in an air fryer, for 25–35 minutes, until it sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool and slice: Rest in the tin about 5 minutes, turn out, and cool at least 10 minutes before slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XRpJE2MDu6k
Uploaded 2024-07-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (360°F); Air fryer 160°C (320°F); Bake the bread in the preheated oven with the lid on for 25-35 minutes, or until the bread sounds hollow when tapped.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: ITALIAN Sausage and POLENTA Casserole
ingredients: Water or chicken broth (stock from a cube in the video) — 4 cups
Salt — 1 teaspoon (optional; none used with salty stock)
Potatoes, peeled and diced into small cubes — 500 g
Dried Italian herbs (oregano, basil, thyme) — 1 teaspoon, plus a little for the top
Tomato passata or crushed tomatoes (a can in the video) — 250 ml
Fresh basil leaves, chopped — for garnish (optional)
Grated Parmesan cheese — 50 g (or mozzarella or cheddar)
steps: Make the polenta: Bring the stock to the boil, whisk in the polenta straight away to avoid lumps, and stir for a few minutes. Turn off the heat and stir in the butter, Parmesan and a little black pepper. Set aside.
Cook the sausages: Put the sausages in a pan with water and a little oil, turning them as they boil so they plump up. When the water evaporates, fry them for colour, then set aside.
Fry the potatoes: Add a little olive oil and the cubed potatoes to the same pan with a tiny pinch of salt and fry, turning, until coloured. Remove and wipe the pan.
Make the sauce base: Sauté the red pepper, garlic and onion in olive oil until soft, then add pepper and the Italian herbs. Return the potatoes.
Add tomatoes: Add the tomatoes and their juice, chopping whole tomatoes with scissors in the can, plus the tomato purée if you like. Simmer about 5 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Assemble: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C), or an air fryer to 360°F (180°C). Slice the sausages thickly. Spread some potato sauce in a baking dish, add the sausages, then the rest of the sauce.
Top: Spread the polenta over to the edges, sprinkle with Italian herbs and cover with grated Parmesan.
Bake: Bake for 20–25 minutes until crisp on top. Rest 5–7 minutes, garnish and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0kWXdZJJwbY
Uploaded 2024-07-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C); Bake - for 20 - 25 minutes.

recipes.title: Mandarin Orange TIRAMISU PERFECT for any SPECIAL occasion NO Egg
ingredients: Canned mandarin orange segments, drained — 1 cup (plus a little of the can juice)
Freshly squeezed mandarin orange juice — 1 cup
Water — ¼ cup (juice from the can used in the video)
Orange liqueur — ¼ cup (optional; leave out for a non-alcohol version)
Fresh mint leaves and extra mandarin segments — for garnish
Quick homemade orange liqueur (optional, made a day ahead):
Sugar — ½ cup, and water — ½ cup (for syrup)
steps: Liqueur (optional, a day ahead): Dissolve ½ cup sugar in ½ cup water over heat and let it cool. Put orange zest in a jar with the brandy, vodka and vanilla, add the syrup, mix, and leave in a dark place for 24 hours, shaking occasionally.
Make the soaking syrup: Dissolve the ½ cup sugar with the mandarin juice, zest and a little juice from the can over a low flame, then turn off and let it cool completely.
Mascarpone base: Gently blend the mascarpone with the powdered sugar and about a teaspoon of vanilla.
Whip the cream: Beat the cream to stiff peaks and fold it into the mascarpone.
Add liqueur: Stir about ¼ cup of orange liqueur into the cooled syrup, if using.
First layer: Dip each ladyfinger in the syrup for about 2 seconds a side and lay them in the dish. Add a little of the zest, without making the base soggy.
Layer up: Spread over a layer of cream, add mandarin segments, then another layer of dipped ladyfingers and zest, and finish with cream to the edges.
Chill: Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Serve: Dust lightly with cocoa and garnish with mandarin segments and mint.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TFnHqiWAM8A
Uploaded 2024-07-10.

recipes.title: German Bratwurst and Beer Braised Golden Potatoes Pie
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and diced into small cubes — 500 g
Beer (light or amber; German beer in the video) — 550 ml
Beef or chicken broth (chicken stock from a cube in the video) — 125 ml
Freshly ground black or white pepper — to taste
Fresh parsley or chives, chopped — for garnish
steps: Boil the mash potatoes: Boil the quartered potatoes in salted water until tender.
Prep: Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and cut the other potatoes into small cubes, patting them dry with kitchen towel.
Brown the bratwurst: Heat the olive oil and butter and colour the bratwurst on a fairly low flame, turning, then remove.
Fry the potatoes: Fry the cubed potatoes in the same fat with a little salt, turning, until golden like roast potatoes.
Add aromatics: Add the onion, garlic and caraway seeds and stir-fry just to take the rawness off.
Make the sauce: Stir in the flour and cook it out, then add the stock and all the beer.
Braise: Return the bratwurst and simmer for 10–12 minutes until thickened.
Make the Kartoffelpüree: Drain the potatoes and mash with the milk, butter, a little salt, black pepper and a pinch of nutmeg until creamy, then mix in about 2 tablespoons of sour cream.

Assemble: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C), or an air fryer to 360°F (180°C). Put some sauce in a baking dish, add the bratwurst, then the rest of the potato mixture, and spread the mash over, roughing up peaks.
Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes until golden and bubbling, then rest 7–8 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mN-x5DJuWiY
Uploaded 2024-07-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C); Bake - covered for 25 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Chicken Leek and Mushroom Filo Pie
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs (breast in the video), bite-sized pieces — 1 pound (450 g)
Butter — a little, for the vegetables (used in the video)
Mushrooms (cremini or button), sliced or chopped — 2 cups
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 teaspoon (or ½ teaspoon dried)
Chicken broth — ½ cup (about a cup in the video)
Filo pastry — 10 sheets (5 for the bottom and 5 for the top)
steps: Prep: Slice the leeks, crush the garlic and chop the mushrooms into chunks.
Brown the chicken: Heat the oil, add the chicken, season with salt and black pepper and stir-fry for colour. Remove from the pan.
Cook the leeks: Add butter, then the leeks, garlic, thyme, a little salt and pepper and stir-fry about 2 minutes.
Cook the mushrooms: Add a little more butter and the mushrooms with a pinch of salt and cook about 4–5 minutes to draw out their moisture. Return the chicken.
Make the sauce: Stir in the English mustard and the flour and cook about 30 seconds, then add the chicken stock and the cream. Simmer 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened and check the seasoning.
Cool: Let the filling cool before it goes into the pastry.
Line the tin: Brush the tin with melted butter and line it with overlapping, buttered filo sheets, letting them hang over the sides and patching any tears.
Fill and top: Spoon in the filling, lay more buttered filo on top, then fold the overhanging pastry back over the top.
Butter and vent: Preheat the oven to 190°C (180°C in an air fryer). Drizzle the top with butter and cut a few vent holes.
Bake: Bake on a tray for about 25 minutes until golden, then let it cool until just warm before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIlsUwdA4Rc
Uploaded 2024-07-08.

recipes.title: Bacon and Leek Cannelloni
ingredients: Bacon (smoked in the video), diced — 8 slices
Large leeks, cleaned and thinly sliced — 2
Olive oil or butter — for sautéing
Ricotta cheese (homemade/cottage cheese in the video) — 1 cup
Grated mozzarella cheese — 1 cup (divided between filling and topping)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
steps: Crisp the bacon: Cook the bacon in the oven until crisp, then chop or blend it into small bits.
Cook the leeks: Thinly slice the leeks and crush the garlic. Sauté them in a little butter with a pinch of salt, black pepper and thyme for a couple of minutes without browning, then let cool.

Make the sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook about 20 seconds, then stir in the milk on a low flame, followed by the cream. Season with black pepper, a pinch of salt and the English mustard, and keep it pourable, not too thick.
Mix the filling: Combine the leeks with the ricotta or cottage cheese, some of the mozzarella, the bacon bits, a little Parmesan and black pepper.
Fill the tubes: Stand the tubes upright (a cake ring helps) and fill them with a wide-cut piping bag or a spoon.

Assemble: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C), or an air fryer to 360°F (180°C). Lay the tubes in the dish, scatter a little mozzarella between them, pour over the sauce, then top with mozzarella, Parmesan and black pepper.
Bake covered: Set the dish on a tray, cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Brown: Remove the foil and bake another 10–15 minutes until golden and bubbly.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Vdsdg3IMFP0
Uploaded 2024-07-07.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C); Bake - covered for 25 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: EASY SHEET Pan CHICKEN Fajitas
ingredients: Chicken breasts or thighs, sliced into thin strips — 3
Green pepper and jalapeño, sliced — some (used in the video)
Olive oil — 2 tablespoons (plus a little for the chicken and tray)
Homemade fajita seasoning mix (below) — 3–4 tablespoons, or 1 packet (1 ounce)
Cheese of choice (mozzarella, cheddar or Jack) — optional
Garlic, minced — 1 small clove (optional; not used in the video)
Ground cumin — ½ teaspoon (ground coriander used in the video)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
steps: Make the seasoning: Mix all the seasoning ingredients well and store in an airtight bag or tub; it keeps about 6 months.
Make the dip: Mix the sour cream with the lime zest and juice, spices, salt, pepper and chopped cilantro. Chill at least 30 minutes.
Prep the veg: Slice the onion, peppers and deseeded jalapeño, not too thin, into a bowl.
Season: Toss the veg with about 2 tablespoons of olive oil and 2 tablespoons of seasoning. Toss the chicken strips with 1 tablespoon of seasoning and a little olive oil.
Heat the tray: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 180°C (365°F) and warm the tray in it for a couple of minutes.
Roast: Oil the hot tray, spread the vegetables on it, top with the chicken and roast for about 25–35 minutes (24 minutes in the video's air fryer).
Warm tortillas and add cheese: In the last few minutes, warm the tortillas briefly, then wrap them in foil. Sprinkle cheese over the fajitas if using and return them until melted.
Serve: Fill the tortillas with the chicken and veg, a little sour cream dip, a sprinkle of cilantro and a squeeze of lime, then roll up.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ptw1GVJYoEs
Uploaded 2024-07-06.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (365°F).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: LA Mexican Bacon Wrapped Hot Dog
ingredients: Hot dog buns — 4 (homemade in the video)
Large onion, sliced — 1 (red onion in the video; any onion works)
Ketchup, American (yellow) mustard and mayonnaise — for topping
steps: Prep the veg: Slice the onion as thick or thin as you like. Deseed the jalapeño and slice it thinly, then slice the red and green peppers into strips. Put them all in a bowl.
Wrap the dogs: Wrap each hot dog in a slice of bacon.
Fry the veg: Heat the oil in a frying pan, add the veg with salt and pepper and fry until soft, caramelized and lightly browned. Set aside.
Cook the hot dogs: Add the bacon-wrapped hot dogs to the pan and cook, turning, until the bacon is crisp; cover loosely if you like.
Warm everything together: Return the veg to the pan with the hot dogs to warm through in the bacon fat, then briefly rub the buns in the pan fat to warm them.
Assemble: Split each bun, spread mayo down the inside, add a hot dog and pack in the veg. Top with pico de gallo if using, then ketchup and mustard. Add avocado or pickled jalapeños if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fj-cbYhqPpE
Uploaded 2024-07-05.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Hot Dog Buns - Air fryer
ingredients: Active dry yeast — 2¼ teaspoons (1 packet, 7 g)
All-purpose flour — 3 cups (360 g) (the video uses 1 cup bread flour and 2 cups all-purpose)
Vegetable oil — ¼ cup (60 ml), plus a little for the bowl
steps: Bloom the yeast: Mix the warm water and sugar, stir in the yeast and leave about 5 minutes until frothy.
Mix the dough: Pour into a stand mixer bowl and add the flour, salt, oil and beaten egg. Knead with the dough hook on slow for about 7 minutes.
Bring it together: Turn the sticky dough out with a little flour and work it for a minute or so, without overworking, until it holds together.
First rise: Rub the dough with oil in a bowl, cover and leave about 45 minutes to an hour until risen.
Divide and shape: Knock back the dough and divide into 9–10 pieces of about 85–90 g. Fold each piece in on itself into a log and place on a parchment-lined tray.
Second rise: Cover and rest about 40 minutes until swollen.
Bake: Preheat the air fryer on the bake setting to 140°C (285°F) and bake about 15–17 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Glaze (optional): Beat the egg with the milk, brush over the buns, raise the heat to 170°C and bake 7 more minutes only.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JKAComl0nVQ
Uploaded 2024-07-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: 1 cup warm water (110°F/45°C) (240ml / 8 fl oz); Preheat your air fryer on the bake setting to 140°C (285°F); Bake at 140°C (285°F) for about 10-15 minutes, or until the buns are golden brown on top and cooked through.

recipes.title: Pico De Gallo | Salsa Fresca | Salsa Cruda | ROOSTER's beak a classic Mexican condiment
ingredients: Jalapeño peppers, finely chopped (seeds removed for less heat) — 1–2
steps: Dice the tomatoes: Cut the tomatoes into small cubes and put them in a bowl. Scoop out the seeds first if you prefer.
Add onion and jalapeño: Dice the red onion. Halve the jalapeños, scrape out the seeds with a small knife if you want less heat, dice finely and add both to the bowl.
Add cilantro and season: Add the chopped cilantro, salt and black pepper.
Add lime and taste: Squeeze in the lime juice a little at a time, stir and taste so it doesn't get too sour. Serve with chips or on tacos, burritos and grilled meats.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rqIUfik94Co
Uploaded 2024-07-05.

recipes.title: Crusty Farmhouse Loaf Air Fryer
ingredients: Active dry yeast — 1 packet (2¼ teaspoons, 7 g)
Olive oil — 1 tablespoon (15 ml), plus a little for the bowl
Egg and a little milk, beaten — for brushing
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the sugar into the warm water (about 36–43°C), whisk in the yeast and leave 5–8 minutes until frothy.
Knead: Tip into the stand mixer bowl with the bread flour, plain flour, salt and olive oil and knead with the dough hook for 8–10 minutes.
First rise: Oil a bowl, bring the dough together with a light dusting of flour, put it in the bowl, cover and leave 40 minutes to 1 hour until doubled.
Shape: Knock the dough back on a lightly floured surface and fold it into a loaf shape. Grease the tin with butter, line with baking paper, put the dough in and press it down gently to fill the tin.
Second rise: Cover and leave about 30 minutes. Dust the top lightly with flour.

Bake: Preheat the air fryer on the bake setting to 140°C (280°F). Set the tin on a trivet and bake 25–35 minutes. In a conventional oven, bake at 180°C for about 25–30 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding.
Glaze: Brush the top with egg and milk and bake about 8 minutes more, watching that it doesn't burn.
Crisp the sides: Take the loaf out of the tin, put it straight on the tray and bake at 170°C (340°F) for 5 minutes. Dust with a little flour and cool before slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U1CaS8SmocI
Uploaded 2024-07-04.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: 1 cup warm water (240ml / 8 fl oz, 110°F / 45°C); Preheat your oven to 180°C (365°F); Airfryer 140°C (280°F)  for about 25-35 minutes – egg/milk wash – cook 8 mins. Take out of tin and cook on tray 170°C  (340°F) – 5 mins; NOTE this loaf could probably be cooked at 160°C (320°F)  for about 35 minutes.

recipes.title: Macaroni Salad classic, refreshing dish perfect for picnics, barbecues, and potlucks.
ingredients: Green bell pepper, seeded and chopped — 1
Large cucumbers, small to medium diced — 2
Pimento peppers, drained — 2 small jars or 1 large jar (red bell pepper used in the video)
Apple cider vinegar or lemon juice — 1 tablespoon
Fresh chives, chopped — 2 tablespoons (green onion tops used in the video)
steps: Cook the macaroni: Boil the macaroni in salted water for about 8 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water and leave to drain fully, stirring now and then so no water stays in it.
Prep the veg: Grate the carrot and dice the onion, celery and peppers. Quarter the cucumber, scoop out some of the seeds and dice it. Mix all the veg in a large bowl.
Combine: Add the drained macaroni to the veg and toss in a big bowl.
Make the dressing: Mix the mayonnaise, Greek yogurt, white vinegar, apple cider vinegar, sugar, Dijon, pepper and a little salt until combined.
Dress and chill: Toss the dressing through the pasta, cover and chill for about 4 hours.

Finish: Stir in most of the sliced green onion tops or chives and parsley, keeping a little back for garnish. Add the cheddar and crumbled bacon, top with quartered boiled eggs and garnish with the reserved herbs.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QlJ3HLbuH8s
Uploaded 2024-07-03.

recipes.title: Guinness Shepherd's Pie An IRISH Delight!
ingredients: Lamb shoulder (boneless leg in the video), cut into 1-inch chunks — 2 lb
Butter — 1 tablespoon (plus extra for the mash)
Mashed potatoes — 4 cups (with butter, pepper, a little salt and optional milk)
Cheddar cheese — optional, for the top
steps: Boil the potatoes: Put the potatoes on to boil in salted water.
Brown the lamb: Heat the olive oil, add the lamb, season with salt and pepper and brown it. Transfer it to the pressure cooker pot (or a slow cooker or large pan).

Make the base: In the same pan, melt the butter, then sauté the garlic, onion and a pinch of thyme. Add the carrots, stir in the flour and cook out the rawness. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for about a minute.
Add the liquids: Add the Worcestershire sauce, pepper and a little salt, then the whole can of Guinness and the beef broth. Stir and pour over the lamb.

Cook the filling: Pressure cook on high for 28 minutes, natural release 10 minutes, then release manually. Alternatively, slow cook on low 6–8 hours or high 3–4 hours, or simmer on the stovetop 1½–2 hours until the lamb is tender.
Make the mash: Mash the potatoes with butter, pepper and a little salt, adding a little milk if you want it creamier.
Add the peas: Stir the frozen peas into the hot filling; they cook in the residual heat.

Assemble: Put the filling in a baking dish with about half the gravy, saving the rest for serving. Cover with the mash, leaving the top rough, and sprinkle with a little cheddar. Set the dish on a tray in case it bubbles over.
Bake: Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 20–30 minutes (or 25–30 minutes in a 350°F / 175°C air fryer) until golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with the reserved gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xelkhEvg6No
Uploaded 2024-07-02.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Simmer: Cook for 1.5 to 2 hours or until the lamb is tender; Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C); Preheat your air fryer to 350°F (175°C); Cook 25-30 mins.

recipes.title: Golden Potato and Bacon Cheese Casserole Bake
ingredients: Large potatoes, cut into 1–1.5 cm cubes — 4–5
Smoked bacon rashers, chopped — 4–5 (8 used in the video)
Dried thyme and parsley — a pinch each
Sour cream or Greek yogurt — ½ cup (120 ml) (optional, not used in the video)
Mozzarella, Parmesan and cheddar — for sprinkling
steps: Prep the potatoes: Cut the potatoes into 1–1.5 cm cubes, rinse off the starch and drain well.
Fry the bacon: Fry the chopped bacon until crisp, then remove it and keep the fat in the pan.
Fry the onion and garlic: Add a little butter, quickly soften the onion and garlic with a pinch of thyme and parsley, then remove.
Fry the potatoes: Fry the potato cubes in the remaining fat with a pinch of salt until golden, then remove.

Make the cheese sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook briefly. Gradually whisk in the milk with some pepper until smooth and thickened, adding more milk if it gets too thick. Stir in the English mustard, then take it off the heat and stir in the cheddar and Parmesan.

Layer: Mix the onions and some crumbled bacon with the potatoes. In a baking dish set on a tray, layer a little sauce, then the potato mix, extra Parmesan and more sauce. Repeat, scatter the remaining bacon and finish with the rest of the sauce.
Top and bake: Top with mozzarella, Parmesan, cheddar and black pepper. Bake at 140°C (280°F) in an air fryer, or 160°C (320°F) in an oven, for about 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest: Leave about 10 minutes to settle before cutting through the top and serving.

recipes.title: Coney Dog Hot dog topped with a savoury meat sauce
ingredients: Tomato sauce — 1 cup (or 2 tablespoons tomato paste mixed with water)
Paprika — ½ teaspoon (smoked in the video)
Water — ½ cup, plus more as needed
Oil or butter — a little, for frying
Water — about 1 cup, enough to boil the onions
steps: Soften the onions: Gently sauté the chopped onions in butter over a low flame without browning. Add water, turn up the heat and boil about 5 minutes until soft but still textured. Set aside.
Start the sauce: In another pan, heat a little oil or butter and soften the garlic and onion with pepper and a little salt.
Brown the beef: Add the ground beef and break it up as it cooks.
Add the spices: Stir in the chili powder, cumin and paprika, then the Worcestershire sauce and yellow mustard.
Add the tomato: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for a minute, then add the ketchup.
Simmer: Add the water and simmer about 20 minutes, adding a little more water as needed, until soft and saucy. Blend with a hand blender if you want it smoother. Cover to keep it from drying out.
Cook the dogs and buns: Boil the hot dogs and steam the buns.
Assemble: Put each hot dog in a steamed bun and top with Coney sauce, soft onions and a line of yellow mustard.

recipes.title: Creamy Chicken Corn Chowder
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces — 1 lb (450 g)
Corn kernels (fresh, frozen or canned) — 2 cups
Cooked bacon, crumbled — 2–3 strips (optional, for garnish)
Fresh parsley, chopped — optional, for garnish
steps: Sear the chicken: Melt a little butter with a splash of oil in a pan, add the chicken, season with salt and pepper and lightly colour it without cooking it through. Transfer to the Instant Pot liner.
Soften the aromatics: In the same pan, stir-fry the garlic and onion, then add the carrots and celery with only a little seasoning, since the stock adds salt.
Make the roux: Add the remaining butter, the thyme and parsley, then stir in the flour and cook it with the vegetables to remove the raw taste.
Deglaze: Add a little stock to loosen everything, then tip it into the pot with the chicken.
Fill the pot: Add the rest of the stock, the corn and the potatoes and stir.
Pressure cook: Cook on high pressure for 10 minutes, let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then release the rest manually.
Add cream: Stir in the cream and simmer on sauté for a couple of minutes to thicken slightly. It should stay a creamy soup.
Serve: Top with crisp bacon, chopped parsley and a little pepper.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RCruwmAGgDQ
Uploaded 2024-06-29.

recipes.title: Quick ROAST BEEF Dinner 1 Hour 20 mins and could be LESS!
ingredients: Butter and oil — a little, for searing (rice bran oil in the video)
Beef broth (made with gravy granules) — about 1½ cups
Flour — 1 tablespoon (for the gravy, per the description)
Potatoes, peeled and cut to roasting size — 1.5 kg
Shortening, beef dripping or vegetable oil — a little for the tin
Carrots — with a little water, microwaved
steps: Parboil the potatoes: Cover the potatoes with water, add the baking soda and a little salt, bring to the boil and boil 5 minutes only. Drain, return to the hot pan to dry, then shake to rough up the edges.
Sear the beef: Season the chuck with salt and pepper and sear all over in a little butter and oil.

Pressure cook the beef: Put the beef in the Instant Pot with the beef broth and pressure cook 22 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally about 10 minutes, then release the rest manually. Cover the beef to rest and keep the cooking liquid for gravy.
Make the batter: Whisk the flour with salt and pepper. Beat the eggs, add the milk and water, then mix into the flour. No need to chill it.

Bake the Yorkshires: Preheat the air fryer oven with its tray to 230°C for 4 minutes, then heat the muffin tray for 1 minute. Add a little oil to each cup, pour in the batter and bake 17 minutes per tray.
Microwave the veg: Microwave the cauliflower florets 5–7 minutes (800 W) and the carrots with a little water 4–6 minutes. Stand the peas, covered, in boiling water for 6 minutes.
Roast the potatoes: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Toss the potatoes in oil with salt and thyme and roast about 25 minutes.

Make the cauliflower cheese: Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk with pepper and the English mustard until thickened. Stir in cheese off the heat. Arrange the cauliflower in a dish, pour the sauce over, top with more cheese and pepper and bake 15 minutes above the potatoes.
Roast the beef: Put the cooked beef in with the potatoes to brown the outside (about 15 minutes).
Make the gravy: Melt the butter, soften the onions with black pepper, add the flour, then pour in the Instant Pot liquid and heat through.
Serve: Slice the beef and plate it with the roast potatoes, cauliflower cheese, carrots, peas and reheated Yorkshire puddings, then pour over the gravy.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z9REB_eowkw

recipes.title: Frickles POPULAR  appetiser or snack
ingredients: Dill pickles, sliced (spears in the video), drained and patted dry — 2 cups
Buttermilk — 1 cup (or 1 cup milk soured with a little apple cider vinegar)
Garlic cloves, minced — 2 (or 1 teaspoon garlic powder)
Dijon mustard — 1 teaspoon (a good heaped teaspoon in the video)
Salt and pepper — to taste (go easy on the salt)
steps: Make the aioli: Mix the mayo, garlic, Dijon, lemon juice, pepper and a little salt. Cover and chill at least 15 minutes.
Make the buttermilk: If you don't have buttermilk, stir a little vinegar into the milk and rest 10 minutes until it splits, then beat in the egg.
Prep the pickles: Drain the pickles, pat dry, slice them (spears are best for dipping) and pat dry again.
Season the flour: Mix the flour and cornmeal with the garlic powder, paprika, cayenne, salt and black pepper.
Bread: Dip each pickle in the flour mix, then the egg mixture, then the flour mix again (repeat for a thicker crust) and lay on a tray.
Fry: Heat the oil to about 175°C (350°F) and shallow-fry the pickles a couple of minutes per side until the batter is crisp.
Drain and serve: Drain on a wire rack, not straight on paper, so they stay crunchy. Serve with the aioli.

recipes.title: DISCO FRIES  New Jersey ICONIC late-night snack
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and cut into fries — 2 lb (1 kg)
Baking soda — 1 teaspoon (for the soaking water)
Onion, chopped — some (used in the video)
Beef broth (from stock, cubes or granules) — 2 cups
steps: Cut the fries: Square off the peeled potatoes and cut them into roughly even chips.
Soak: Soak the chips for 5–6 minutes in water with the baking soda, then drain and pat as dry as possible.
Coat: Shake the chips in a bag with the cornflour in batches, then season with salt and pepper and toss with the oil.
Cook: Spread on a parchment-lined tray and air fry at 190°C (380°F), or bake in a 200°C (400°F) oven, for about 28 minutes, turning at 10 minutes and again partway through, until crisp.

Make the gravy: Melt the butter and soften the onion with black pepper and a little salt. Stir in the flour and thyme and cook out the rawness, then whisk in the beef broth (and Worcestershire). Add water if it gets too thick.
Melt the cheese: Pile the fries up, top with the mozzarella and cheddar and return to the oven for about 5 minutes until melted.
Serve: Pour gravy over the cheesy fries and season to taste.

recipes.title: Strawberry Cheesecake EASY NO BAKE
ingredients: Digestive biscuits — 250 g (or 1½ cups graham cracker crumbs, about 10–12 crackers)
Heavy whipping cream, cold — 1 cup (240 g)
Fresh strawberries — 1 cup (halved and stood around the tin in the video)
Strawberry jelly powder or cubes — 1 packet
Water — ¼ cup, plus boiling and cold water per the packet
steps: Make the base: Crush the biscuits in a bag (or blender), then mix with the sugar and melted butter.
Line and press: Line an 8-inch springform tin with parchment. Press the crumbs in firmly and evenly, leaving a rim of about ½ cm around the edge. Chill.
Bloom the gelatin: Stir 2 teaspoons of gelatin into the water and leave 6–7 minutes, then microwave 10–15 seconds until just lukewarm.
Halve the strawberries: Hull and halve enough strawberries to go around the tin.
Make the filling: Beat the cream cheese with the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth. Whip the cream to fairly stiff peaks. Blend the gelatin into the cream cheese mixture.

Assemble: Stand the strawberry halves, cut side out, around the edge of the base. Fold the whipped cream into the cheese mixture and pour it into the middle so it holds the strawberries against the sides. Level and chill at least 4–5 hours or overnight.

Make the jelly topping: Bloom and lightly warm the second lot of gelatin. Dissolve the jelly in the packet's boiling water, add a little under the packet's cold water, then stir in the gelatin for a firmer set. Let it cool.
Top and set: Pour the cool jelly gently over the back of a spoon onto the cheesecake to make a thin pink layer. Chill until firm.
Unmould: Release the tin, peel away the parchment and decorate with strawberries.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3E3rNQ3pZwU

recipes.title: Ireland’s OWN Barmbrack also known as Brack cake
ingredients: Strong tea (3 tea bags), for soaking — 300 ml
Strong tea, for the batter — 100 ml
Mixed spice — 5 g (about 1 teaspoon; pumpkin spice works too)
A coin wrapped in parchment — optional, for tradition
steps: Soak the fruit: Pour 300 ml of strong, hot tea over the sultanas and raisins, cover and leave overnight. Drain, keeping any leftover tea.
Line the tin: Line a 9 × 4 × 3-inch loaf tin with a cake liner or parchment.
Mix the dry ingredients: Combine the self-raising flour, baking powder, salt, mixed spice and sugar.
Mix the wet ingredients: Beat the egg with the 100 ml of tea (and the whiskey if using).
Make the batter: Stir the egg mixture and any leftover soaking tea into the dry ingredients until combined, then stir in the fruit.
Fill the tin: Spoon the batter into the tin and push a parchment-wrapped coin into the middle if you like.

Bake: In a fan oven, bake at 160°C (320°F) for about 1 hour 30 minutes. In an air fryer oven, bake at 140°C (280°F) for 40 minutes, then cover with foil and bake about 25 minutes more. Keep checking until a skewer comes out clean, covering the top if it browns too fast.
Finish and cool: Uncover for the last 5 minutes to colour. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then cool fully on a wire rack. Slice and serve with butter.

recipes.title: One Pot Beef and Barley Soup
ingredients: Beef stew meat (chuck roll), trimmed and cut into about 1-inch cubes — 1 lb (750 g per the description)
Canned tomatoes with juice — 1 can (14.5 oz) (whole tomatoes snipped in the can in the video)
Beef broth (granules or stock cube) — 6 cups (4 cups broth plus 2 cups water in the video)
Olive oil — 1 tablespoon (plus a little butter in the video)
Rosemary — 1 teaspoon dried (fresh in the video)
steps: Prep: Dice the onion, celery and carrots and mince the garlic. Trim the silver skin off the beef and cut it into roughly 1-inch cubes, since it shrinks under pressure.
Sear the beef: Heat the oil (and butter) in a pan, add the beef, season with salt and pepper and brown it briefly. Transfer to the Instant Pot liner.
Soften the veg: In the same pan, sauté the onion and garlic for a couple of minutes, then add the carrot and celery for a minute or two. Leave some crunch, as they finish in the pot. Add to the beef.

Fill the pot: Add the tomatoes with their juice (snip whole ones in the can), the Worcestershire if using, thyme, pepper, a little salt, the tomato paste, rosemary, broth, water and rinsed barley. Stir.
Pressure cook: Cook on high pressure for 25 minutes, let the pressure release naturally about 15 minutes, then release the rest manually.
Serve: Garnish with parsley and serve with crusty bread and butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VilDvNgn1mA

recipes.title: Classic British Fish Pie
ingredients: Milk, taken from the fish-poaching milk — 100 ml
Mixed fish fillets (e.g. salmon, smoked haddock, white fish such as cod, sea bream or barramundi), cut into chunks — 600 g
Raw prawns, peeled and deveined — 200 g
Onion — 1, quartered and studded with cloves
Cheddar cheese, grated — to taste, plus extra for the top
Hard-boiled eggs, quartered — optional (used in the video)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Peel and dice the potatoes and boil until tender for mashing.
Infuse the milk: Stud the quartered onion with cloves, add it to the milk, bring to the boil and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Strain out the onion and cloves.
Cube the fish: Cut the white fish, smoked haddock and salmon into chunks.
Poach: Poach the fish and prawns in the infused milk for about 5 minutes at most. Lift them out and keep the milk.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with butter, pepper, a little salt and some of the fishy milk.

Make the sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the reserved milk a little at a time until smooth and thick, adding more milk if needed. Stir in the English mustard and cheddar and season with pepper.

Assemble: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) or the air fryer to 170°C (340°F). Spread the fish and prawns in a dish with the peas, sweetcorn if using, and the egg quarters. Pour over the sauce and sprinkle with chopped tarragon.
Top and bake: Spread the mash over the top, leaving it rough for a crisp crust, and sprinkle with cheddar. Bake about 25 minutes until golden, then rest 5–10 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Ultimate Cheese and Onion Pasties Two Ways: Shortcrust vs. Puff Pastry
ingredients: Shortcrust pastry (or use ready-rolled shortcrust or puff pastry):
Potatoes, peeled and chopped — 2 cups (450 g)
Cheddar cheese, grated — 2 cups (200 g) (about 300 g in the video, plus extra for topping)
Large egg, beaten — 1, for egg wash
steps: Make the shortcrust: Rub the shortening and butter into the flour and salt until crumbly. Beat the egg with the water and vinegar, stir it in with a fork, then bring the dough together by hand. Cover and set aside.
Boil the potatoes: Dice the potatoes evenly and boil in salted water until tender.
Poach the onion: Simmer the diced onion in the milk for about 5 minutes to soften it and take off the harshness. Lift out the onion and keep the milk.

Make the filling: Drain the potatoes and roughly mash, keeping some texture. Add a little of the onion milk, keeping the mix fairly dry, then stir in the onion, salt, pepper and mustard powder. Cool 5–10 minutes, then mix in the cheddar and mozzarella.

Puff pastry pasties: Cut puff pastry into 4½ × 5-inch pieces on a lined tray. Pile filling on one half and dot with cheese. Cut three slits in the lid, brush the edges lightly with egg, fold over, press and crimp with a fork. Egg wash and bake at 180°C for about 20 minutes.

Shortcrust pasties: Roll out the shortcrust and cut 7-inch circles. Add filling and a little extra cheddar, lightly egg the edge, fold over, press and crimp. Egg wash, poke a couple of vent holes and bake at 180°C for about 25 minutes until golden.
Cool: Cool on a rack before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken Schnitzel with Curry Ketchup Burger
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts — 2 (each cut into 4 thin pieces)
Salt and black pepper — a little
steps: Start the curry ketchup: Melt the butter in a small pan, sweat the onion, then add the apple with a little salt and pepper and cook about 2 minutes to soften. Keep it chunky.

Finish the sauce: Stir in the curry powder and other spices, then the sugar or honey, Worcestershire, soy sauce and ketchup. Simmer on a very low flame about 5 minutes, stirring so it doesn't catch. Set aside.
Prep the chicken: Butterfly and cut each chicken breast into four thin pieces and tap them gently flat with a meat hammer.
Season: Season the chicken directly with salt (or chicken powder), pepper, garlic powder and paprika.
Bread: Coat each piece in flour, then egg, then panko.
Fry: Heat the oil until a wooden skewer bubbles, then fry the chicken, flipping a couple of times, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack to keep it crisp.
Stack with cheese: While hot, layer the schnitzels with a slice of cheese between each piece.
Assemble: Fill buns with lettuce, the chicken and cheese stack, tomato and plenty of curry ketchup.

recipes.title: Jägerschnitzel   German Schnitzel with Brown Jäger Sauce Red Cabbage Rotkohl
ingredients: Medium red cabbage, cored and finely shredded — 1
Red wine — ¼ cup (2 tablespoons red wine vinegar used in the video; add a little more sugar)
Beef broth (stock or gravy granules) — 1 cup
Pork cutlets (from pork tenderloin), about 150–200 g each — 4
Vegetable oil or clarified butter — for frying
steps: Start the cabbage: Thinly slice the cabbage and apples. Melt the butter in a pan and gently sauté the onion, then add the cabbage and apple and season with salt and pepper.
Braise the cabbage: Stir in the vinegars (or wine), sugar and spices. Cover, turn the heat down and cook about 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft. Taste for seasoning.
Start the sauce: Melt the butter and gently sauté the onion, then add the mushrooms with pepper and stir-fry until softened.

Thicken the sauce: Stir in the flour and cook about a minute, then add the beef broth, Worcestershire, soy sauce and hot mustard. Simmer about 2 minutes, then stir in the cream and warm through. It can be made ahead and reheated gently.
Prep the pork: Cut cutlets from the tenderloin and flatten them gently with the flat side of a meat mallet. Season the meat, not the flour, with salt and pepper.
Bread: Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, patting the crumbs on.
Fry: Fry in hot oil, turning when a brown ring shows around the edge and turning once more for an even colour. Drain on a rack, not kitchen paper, to keep crisp.
Serve: Serve the schnitzel with Jäger sauce, red cabbage and mashed potatoes, garnished with parsley.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqc3y9zSJ2U

recipes.title: Gala Pie Traditional British Oblong Pie
ingredients: Pork belly, finely chopped — 200 g (pork mince used in the video)
steps: Make the pastry: Gently heat the water with the butter and lard until melted and just bubbling, then turn it off. Pour it into the flour and salt, stir with a spoon, then bring together by hand once cool enough.
Divide and cool: Split the pastry roughly two-thirds (base) and one-third (lid). Flatten slightly, wrap loosely in cling film and let cool.
Boil the eggs: Boil about 8 minutes, cool under the tap and peel.
Make the filling: Mix the chopped bacon and minced pork with the small cubes of pork shoulder. Add salt, pepper, thyme, sage and onion and mix well by hand. Let it rest while you prepare the tin.
Line the tin: Put a strip of parchment in a 9 × 5-inch (2 lb) loaf tin. Roll out the larger piece of pastry and press it into the tin with an overhang.
Fill: Press some filling into the base and make a well down the middle. Trim the ends of the eggs so they butt together in a row in the well, then pack the rest of the meat around and over them.
Lid: Roll out the lid, egg the edges, press it on, trim and crimp. Egg wash, cut a couple of vent holes and decorate with pastry leaves, egg-washing them too.

Bake: Set the tin on a tray. Bake in a conventional oven at 180°C (360°F) for 30 minutes, then at 160°C (320°F) for about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes. In an air fryer oven, bake 30 minutes at 160°C, then about 1 hour at 140°C covered. The centre should reach at least 75°C (165°F). Uncover at the end if needed to drain off juices and finish the top.
Cool: Let the pie go completely cold.

Add the jelly: Bring the stock to the boil, cool slightly and whisk in the gelatin (never boil gelatin). Let it cool, then pour it slowly through one vent hole until the pie is full, letting air escape through the other.
Set and serve: Chill 2–3 hours, then turn out of the tin and slice.

recipes.title: Sausage and Baked Bean Melt
ingredients: Ready-rolled puff pastry, cut into 4.5 × 5-inch pieces — 1 sheet
Baked beans in tomato sauce — 1 can (400 g)
Oil — a little, for the sausages
Fresh herbs (e.g. parsley) — optional, for garnish
steps: Cook the sausages: Put the sausages in a pan with water and a little oil and boil, turning, until the water evaporates. Then fry them in the remaining oil until browned.
Drain the beans: Drain off most of the sauce from the beans so the pastry doesn't go soggy.
Slice the sausages: Cut the sausages into slices.
Preheat: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a tray with parchment.
Fill: Lay half the pastry pieces on the tray and top each with a layer of beans and some sausage slices. Brush the edges very lightly with egg wash and let it go tacky.
Top: Cut a slit in each lid. Add a little cheddar over the filling, then stretch the lids over, press down and crimp with a fork. Brush lightly with egg wash.
Bake: Bake about 20 minutes until golden, then cool 5 minutes before cutting.

recipes.title: Custard Slice with a Party Top
ingredients: Ready-rolled puff pastry — enough for two 10 × 10-inch squares
Milk — 2 tablespoons (plus a little more if needed)
Chocolate and sprinkles — optional, for decoration
steps: Cut and dock the pastry: Cut two squares of puff pastry to fit a 10 × 10-inch tray and prick them all over with a fork so they rise only a little.

Bake flat: Put each square on parchment, cover with another sheet of parchment and weigh it down with a tray (and baking beads) so it stays flat. Bake one at a time, at 190°C (380°F) in an oven or 180°C (360°F) in an air fryer, for about 18 minutes. Cool.
Heat the milk: Warm the milk and cream, stirring, until steaming and just starting to boil, then take off the heat.
Temper the yolks: Mix the egg yolks with the sugar, cornstarch and a pinch of salt. Beat in the hot milk a little at a time to dissolve the sugar, adding colouring if you like.
Thicken: Return everything to the pan and cook, stirring, until it thickens quickly. Stir in the vanilla, then the butter.
Set the custard: Pour into the lined 10 × 10-inch tin, cool completely, then chill until fully set.
Assemble: Lay one pastry sheet over the custard, flip it out onto a board and neaten the edges, then lay the second sheet on top. Cut through gently into slices but keep them together.

Ice and decorate: Mix the powdered sugar and vanilla with just enough milk for a thick, spreadable icing and spread it over the top. Pipe lines of melted chocolate, drag through them, add sprinkles and chill until set.
