recipes.title: Classic English Custard Tart
ingredients: Beaten egg — a little, to seal the case
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the shortening and butter into the flour, salt and sugar until crumbly, then mix in the lemon zest. Beat the egg with the water and vinegar, stir in with a fork handle, then bring together by hand. No need to rest it.
Line the tin: Preheat to 180°C (360°F). Roll the pastry fairly thick and press it into a 7-inch springform tin, leaving an overhang. Prick the base all over with a fork.
Blind bake: Line with parchment and baking beads and bake 12–15 minutes (14 in the video's air fryer).
Seal: Remove the beads, brush the inside with egg wash and bake about 5 minutes more. Cool completely, then trim the overhang.
Heat the milk: Heat the milk and cream until steaming but not boiling, stirring occasionally.
Temper: Beat the yolks and sugar until the sugar dissolves and the mixture lightens. Slowly whisk in the hot milk so the eggs don't scramble.
Strain and flavour: Strain into a jug and stir in the vanilla and salt.

Fill and bake: Pour into the case and grate nutmeg over the top. Bake at 160°C (320°F) in an oven, or 140°C (280°F) in an air fryer on low fan, for 35–45 minutes, until set with a slight wobble in the middle.
Cool and chill: Cool completely, then chill and serve cold.

recipes.title: Corned BEEF Bierocks
ingredients: All-purpose flour, plus more for kneading — 5 cups
Small head of cabbage, finely shredded — 1
steps: Make the dough: In a mixer with a dough hook, combine the flour, salt, sugar, yeast, milk, water, butter and egg. Knead 8–10 minutes; it will be sticky, so knead briefly on a floured surface, adding a little flour as needed.
First rise: Place in an oiled bowl, cover and rest for an hour.
Cook the filling: Soften the onion and garlic in butter or oil, add the shredded cabbage with salt and pepper and stir-fry until cooked down. Stir in the caraway (optional) and paprika. Cool.
Divide: Knock back the dough and divide into about 12 pieces; roll or press each into a flat round.
Fill: Put cooled cabbage mix and corned beef in the middle, bring the edges up over the top and squash to seal. Place seam side down on parchment-lined trays.
Second rest: Cover and rest about 20 minutes while the oven preheats.
Bake: Oven 190°C (380°F), or air fryer 170°C (340°F), for 20–25 minutes (the video baked at 170°C for about 25 minutes).
Finish: Brush with melted butter, rest a few minutes on a rack and serve warm.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mWRd6twqqnU

recipes.title: Aubergine Parmo Oven cooked NO Breading
ingredients: Tomato paste/purée — a couple of tablespoons
Tinned chopped tomatoes — amount not stated
Sugar, to offset acidity — amount not stated
Grated Parmesan — ½ cup (some also goes into the béchamel)
Fresh basil — for garnish and stirred in (optional)
steps: Slice and salt: Cut the aubergines into slices about 1 cm thick. Salt both sides and stand them in a basket over a bowl for about 30 minutes to draw out the liquid.
Rinse and dry: Rinse off the salt and pat dry.
Bake: Lay on two oiled trays and cook at 180°C. Turn and swap trays after 15 minutes, then cook until coloured on the other side.
Start the tomato sauce: Fry the onion and garlic in olive oil with salt until the raw edge goes, add pepper, then the tomato paste, a little sugar, oregano and allspice.
Simmer: Add the tinned tomatoes (chopped in the tin with scissors) and cook about 15 minutes until thick. Stir through fresh basil off the heat.
Make the béchamel: Cook the butter and flour briefly, add the milk gradually, then the nutmeg and some Parmesan; keep it not too thick.
Assemble: Stack aubergine slices with tomato sauce, béchamel and mozzarella between and on top, with basil leaves.
Bake: Cook at about 180°C for about 10 minutes until the cheese melts. Oven setting 190°C (380°F) / air fryer 170°C (340°F) per the description.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t-_xn4LmhGw
Uploaded 2024-06-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (380°F).

recipes.title: Moussaka | How to make Moussaka
ingredients: Red wine — ½ cup (optional; not used in the video)
Bay leaf — 1 (the video used two small)
Large potatoes, skins on, sliced 1 cm — 4
Large eggplants, sliced into 1 cm rounds — 2
Ground nutmeg — ¼ teaspoon (optional; not used in the video)
steps: Salt the eggplant: Slice into 1 cm rounds, salt both sides and stand in a basket over a bowl for 25–30 minutes to draw out moisture; rinse and pat dry.
Fry the potatoes: Fry the 1 cm slices in 180°C oil, browning both sides to about 60–70% cooked; they finish in the oven. (Baking them is an alternative.)
Start the meat sauce: Soften the onion and garlic in olive oil, add the meat and brown it, breaking it up. Season with salt, pepper, oregano, cinnamon and allspice.
Add tomato: Stir in the tomato paste and cook off the sourness, then add the tinned tomatoes and bay leaves.
Simmer: Simmer gently, uncovered, 15–20 minutes until thick. Remove the bay leaves.
Bake the eggplant: Spread on oiled trays, brush with oil and bake at 180°C for about 12 minutes, turn and bake another 12 until coloured.
Make the béchamel: Melt the butter slowly, cook in the flour briefly, gradually add the milk and stir until thick. Stir in the Parmesan; off the heat.
Layer: Potato on the bottom, then eggplant, then half the meat sauce; repeat with potato, a little Parmesan and the remaining meat. Press down towards the edges.

Top and bake: Pour the béchamel over. Oven 190°C (380°F) or air fryer 180°C (360°F) for 25–40 minutes (shorter in the air fryer in the video, about 25); everything is already cooked, so this crisps and sets the top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u-lUdyupfsE
Uploaded 2024-06-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 190°C (380°F); Cook 25 - 40 mins. Big difference in time - air fryer and oven -.

recipes.title: Creamy Bacon Ham and Pea Pasta Salad Plus What Extras You Like!
ingredients: Pasta (fusilli, penne or your favourite) — 300 g
Apple cider vinegar — 1 tbsp (plus a splash for the onion)
Extras you like (cucumber, red chilli, tomato)
steps: Tame the onion: Soak the chopped onion in cold water with a splash of apple cider vinegar for 10 minutes, then drain (lemon juice or a 10–15 second blanch into ice water also works).
Cook the bacon: Fry the bacon until crisp and cool it. Ham needs no cooking, just dice it.
Boil the pasta: Cook in salted water for the packet time (5–7 or 10–11 minutes). Cool under cold water and drain.
Cook the peas: Give the frozen peas a minute in the pasta water, then cool in cold water and drain.
Make the dressing: Mix the mayonnaise, sour cream, Dijon, honey, vinegar, pepper, a little salt and the Parmesan; add more sour cream for creaminess.
Combine: Toss the pasta, onion, bell pepper, bacon, ham, peas and parsley with the dressing, plus any extras.
Chill: Refrigerate about an hour before serving; it keeps a couple of days.

recipes.title: Joey Grey Traditional Romany Stew | Gypsy Stew
ingredients: Large potatoes, peeled and sliced about ½ cm — 4
Beef Oxo cubes (or other beef bouillon) — 2 (the video used 3)
Water — 2 cups, or enough to cover
Optional: sliced carrots 1 cup, sliced bell peppers 1 cup, or other vegetables
steps: Prep: Chop the onion (and carrots if using), slice the bacon and slice the potatoes about ½ cm thick.
Brown the sausages: Cut into chunks and brown in oil for colour only; they finish in the stew. Remove to a bowl.
Cook the bacon: Fry the bacon in the same pot until it takes colour.
Add the veg: Add the onion (and carrots, garlic) and cook for a minute or so to soften, with pepper, a little salt and the paprika.
Add stock and tomatoes: Crumble in the Oxo cubes, then add the tinned tomatoes (chopped in the can with scissors).
Add potatoes and sausage: Return the sausage, add the potatoes and enough water to cover.
Simmer: Put the lid on and simmer about 45 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender (the video was ready at about 30–35 minutes in a small pan).
Serve: Ladle into bowls with crusty bread and butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J5MY7TSkvnQ

recipes.title: Fish Fingers Recipe | How to Make Fish Fingers | Fish Sticks | Homemade Fish Fingers
ingredients: White fish fillets (cod, haddock, pollock or whiting), cut into finger-sized strips — 500 g
Tempura flour (plain flour in the video) — 1 cup
Salt and pepper (white pepper in the video) — to taste
Cooking oil (vegetable or canola) — for frying
To serve: vinegar, salt, ketchup, bread (for a fish finger butty)
steps: Rinse the fish: To take off any fishy smell, swish the fish briefly in a bowl of water with a little vinegar, then dry thoroughly with kitchen towel.
Cut the fingers: Cut the fillets along the natural line and across, into proper finger-sized strips (halve any pieces that are too thick).
Season: Salt and white pepper the fish directly (seasoning the fish rather than the flour).
Coat: Dust in flour, dip in beaten egg, then press into breadcrumbs, coating all round.
Heat the oil: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat; it is ready when bubbles form around a wooden skewer.
Fry: Fry the fingers without overcrowding, turning once, until golden brown (a couple of minutes a side). Turn the heat down if it builds up, and skim burnt crumbs.
Drain: Rest on a rack over kitchen towel so they stay crisp.
Serve: Eat with vinegar, salt and ketchup, or in bread as a fish finger butty.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rS_GVeairMg

recipes.title: Prawn Cocktail | Shrimp Cocktail
ingredients: Cooked, peeled prawns (fresh or thawed frozen) — 300 g
Brandy — a dash (used in the video)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — to taste
Small iceberg lettuce (or curly lettuce), shredded — 1
steps: Cook the prawns: If raw, drop into boiling water briefly, then cool in cold water to stop the cooking.
Make the Marie Rose sauce: Mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, Worcestershire, Tabasco, a dash of brandy, pepper, salt and a squeeze of lemon; taste and adjust.
Prep the salad: Shred the lettuce and dice the cucumber (slice or cube the avocado if using).
Layer: Put the lettuce in serving glasses or bowls, then cucumber (and avocado), with a squeeze of lemon.
Dress the prawns: Stir the prawns through the sauce and pile on top; keep a couple whole for garnish.
Finish: Dust with cayenne or paprika and scatter with chives.

recipes.title: How to Make Spam at Home + Delicious Spam & Pineapple Cheeseburger
ingredients: Pork mince (ideally pork shoulder and belly) — 2 kg
Pink curing salt (Prague Powder #1) — 1 tsp (about 5 g; 2.5 g per kg of meat)
Milk powder as binder — 10 g per kg (optional)
Burger buns, mayonnaise, pineapple slices, American cheese, lettuce, tomato, ketchup or sauce of choice
steps: Blitz the pork: Process the mince to a fine paste (the video does this in a food processor), keeping some fat for the gelatine.
Mix: Combine the cornflour, cure, salt, sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, white pepper, ice water and milk powder, then work thoroughly through the pork by hand.
Fill the tubes: Oil the inside of the tubes, split the mixture between them and press down firmly to avoid air pockets; fit the spring-loaded lids.
Cook: Stand the tubes on a trivet in a pan of water, with thermometers in, and keep simmering until the internal temperature reaches 70°C (160°F).
Chill: Cool completely (a couple of hours), then refrigerate, ideally overnight.
Unmould: Run a knife around the edge to break the seal and tip out the Spam; the jelly around it is real gelatine. Slice.
Burger: Spread mayonnaise on the buns and toast them in a pan with the pineapple slices. Fry the Spam slice, top with American cheese to melt, then assemble with lettuce, tomato and ketchup or sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bhja8DQfluk
Uploaded 2024-06-06.

recipes.title: ROCKER Sprouts a dish with a BOLD , EDGY TWIST
ingredients: Pork belly, skin on, sliced — 1 kg
Brussels sprouts, cleaned and halved — 480 g
Salt (sea salt) — 2 tbsp, for the boiling water and rubbing the skin
Small green chillies, smashed — 10, or to taste
steps: Boil the pork: Simmer the pork belly, skin side down, in salted water for about 10–15 minutes to soften the skin. Lift it occasionally so the skin doesn't stick.
Stab and score: Stab the skin all over, then score it through the top skin only in strips about an inch wide. Rub with salt.
Level it: Pack foil under the thinner side so the skin sits level.
Roast: Cook at 230°C (460°F) for about 35–40 minutes until the skin is crispy.
Cut: Cut the cooked pork into cubes.
Stir-fry the aromatics: Stir-fry the garlic and chillies in oil over low–medium heat until tinged.
Add the sprouts: Add the halved sprouts and a splash of water to soften, then fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar. Cook briefly.
Finish: Off the heat, stir through the pork (already cooked, just warming), add white pepper and serve, ideally with rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gXTcGcum5BQ
Uploaded 2024-06-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven cook 230c - 460f about 35 - 40 mins until skin crispy.

recipes.title: Potatoes Au Gratin  DELICIOUS COMFORT food CLASSIC with a twist
ingredients: Large potatoes, peeled (skins left on in the video) and thinly sliced — 2
Large parsnips, peeled and thinly sliced — 2
Green onions/scallions, finely chopped — 2 (save a little for the top)
Grated Gruyère (or cheddar or another melting cheese) — 1 cup
steps: Slice: Slice the potatoes and parsnips to roughly the same thin thickness.
Infuse: In a pan warm the milk and cream with the garlic, green onions, thyme leaves, salt and pepper to a simmer. Take off the heat and let it infuse as it cools slightly.

Layer: Dot butter in the dish, then layer potato and parsnip slices with the cheese (and Parmesan) between layers, pouring over the infused milk and cream so it soaks through. Finish with cheese on top.
Bake covered: Cover with foil on a tray (it may bubble over) and bake 40 minutes at 190°C (380°F) in the oven, or air fryer 180°C (360°F) (the video used 160°C for 40 minutes).
Brown: Remove the foil and bake about 15 minutes more (video: 180°C) until browned and crispy; check with a skewer that the vegetables are soft.
Rest and serve: Rest about 5 minutes, scatter with the reserved green onion and cut into portions (about six).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vhd4A4vgYxA

recipes.title: Mackerel and Tomato Quiche A Nutritious and delicious choice
ingredients: Tins of mackerel in tomato sauce (about 200 g each) — 2
Olive oil — 1 tablespoon (butter in the video)
steps: Soften the onion: Cook the onion and garlic in the oil or butter until translucent, then cool and spread over the pastry base.
Prep the mackerel: Drain off the tomato sauce (keep it), and flake the mackerel gently into chunks; the fine bones are soft.
Make the custard: Whisk the eggs with salt, pepper, milk and cream; stir in half the cheese and the parsley.
Assemble: Scatter the mackerel over the onion in the crust, drizzle over some of the tomato sauce, then pour in the custard and top with more pepper.
Bake: Oven 190°C (380°F) or air fryer 180°C (360°F) for about 30 minutes.
Finish: Grate the remaining cheese over it, add fresh parsley, and cool about 10 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Pulled Chicken With Creamy Honey Mustard BBQ Sauce
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs — 4
BBQ sauce — 1 cup (or your preferred sauce)
steps: Make the sauce: Mix all the sauce ingredients, taste, and refrigerate at least half an hour so the flavours meld.
Season the chicken: Mix the garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, salt and pepper and rub over the chicken.
Load the pot: Pour the broth into the Instant Pot, add the chicken (more seasoning on top than underneath) and cover with the BBQ sauce.
Pressure cook: Lid on, high pressure for 10 minutes, then natural release for 10 minutes and vent the rest. (A slow cooker takes about 4 hours.)
Shred: Pull the chicken apart and moisten with the cooking juices and extra sauce until nicely wet.
Serve: Pile into buns and top with the creamy honey mustard BBQ sauce.

recipes.title: British Cheddar Cheese Scones: A Savoury Everyday Treat
ingredients: Unsalted butter, cold and cubed — 100 g (7 tbsp)
Grated mature cheddar — 300 g (2½ cups), plus extra for topping
steps: Mix the dry: Stir together the flour, baking powder, salt and mustard powder.
Rub in the butter: Rub the cold butter into the flour to loose breadcrumbs (a food processor works too).
Add cheese: Toss the cheese through the flour mix, lifting to coat it.
Add milk: Pour in the milk and bring together into a dough, adding a little more milk or flour if needed. Don't overwork it.
Shape: Pat or roll out to about 3 cm thick and cut with a 3-inch cutter; scones may touch slightly on the parchment-lined tray.
Glaze: Brush with egg wash (milk also works) and add extra cheese on top.
Bake: Oven 220°C (425°F) or air fryer 180°C (360°F) for 12–15 minutes (14 in the video) until well risen and golden.
Cool briefly: Rest on a rack about 5 minutes; split and butter while warm.

recipes.title: EASIEST Creamy POLENTA & Cake
ingredients: Polenta/cornmeal (medium or coarse; quick-cook in the video) — 1 cup
Olive oil — a drizzle on the water
Parmesan or Pecorino, freshly grated — ½ cup
To serve: vine tomatoes, thick-sliced bacon, scrambled egg, olive oil, parsley, black pepper, balsamic vinegar (optional)
steps: Start cold: Put the polenta, cold water (or broth) and a drizzle of olive oil in a pan and stir.
Heat: Bring to the boil slowly, stirring until it turns creamy and soft; quick-cook polenta is ready within about 5 minutes.
Finish: Stir in the butter, then the Parmesan, and season with salt (less if the butter is salted) and pepper. It is ready when it pulls away from the pan.
Set for polenta cake: Pour into an oiled tray and let it cool and set.
Fry or grill: Cut into shapes and fry or grill in oil until coloured on both sides.
Roast the tomatoes: Roast vine tomatoes in olive oil and salt at 200°C for about 5–6 minutes.
Serve: Plate the polenta cake with the tomatoes, bacon and scrambled egg, with olive oil, parsley, black pepper and balsamic vinegar.

recipes.title: The Burger With The Lot Australia's own
ingredients: Small can sliced beetroot, drained (or fresh homemade) — 1
Large red onion, sliced into rings (fry if you like) — 1
Tomato sauce (ketchup), barbecue sauce and mayonnaise
steps: Shape and freeze: Press 100 g balls of mince flat between two sheets of plastic (trim round), stack with plastic between them in a tub and freeze. The video cooks the patties straight from frozen so they char outside and stay pink inside.
Toast the buns: Spread mayonnaise on the cut sides and toast in a pan; do the same with the pineapple rings.

Cook the patties: Season and cook the frozen patties in a dry pan, flipping to colour both sides and seasoning again.
Melt the cheese: Add a cheese slice and cover with a lid until melted.
Assemble: Build with lettuce, patty and cheese, bacon, beetroot, pineapple, tomato, onion and fried egg, with tomato sauce and the lid of the bun.

recipes.title: EASY  Sicilian Grandma Pizza Sfincione & My Grandma Isn't Sicilian
ingredients: Olive oil — 30 ml, plus oil for the tray
steps: Mix: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, water and olive oil in a stand mixer until it comes together.
Rest: Cover and leave 15–20 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Knead: Knead about 5 minutes in the mixer (8–10 minutes by hand) until slightly sticky but smooth.
First rise: Shape into a ball in an oiled bowl, cover and rest for about 1–1½ hours until doubled.
Shape: Oil the tray lightly (blot excess so the base doesn't fry), stretch the dough into the corners, bring up an edge and cover for another 30–40 minutes.
Preheat: Preheat the oven to 220°C (440°F), or the air fryer to 200°C (400°F), with the tray in.
Top: Spread on the sauce, add mozzarella, basil and garlic oil.
Bake: Oven 220°C for 16–24 minutes or air fryer 200°C for 14–20 minutes (about 14 in the video; the base was only lightly browned, so up to 5 more minutes would crisp it).
Finish: Cool about 5 minutes, drizzle with olive oil and add basil.

recipes.title: Lamb Chops Creamy Polenta Ratatouille Black Olive Red Wine Sauce Just a bit of fun in the kitchen
ingredients: Lamb chops (fat left on) — as many as you need
Vine tomatoes and sea salt, to roast alongside
Salt — 1 teaspoon (skip if using salty stock)
Heavy cream or whole milk — ½ cup (optional)
Freshly ground black pepper — to taste
Red wine (Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot) — 1 cup
Kalamata olives, pitted, finely chopped — ½ cup
Shallot (onion in the video), finely chopped — 1
Medium zucchini, thinly sliced — 2 (not used in the video)
steps: Cook the polenta: Bring the stock to the boil, stir in the polenta so it doesn't clump and keep stirring about 20 minutes until thick. Stir in butter and Parmesan, season, and pour into an oiled tray to set.
Start the sauce: Soften the onion in olive oil, add the garlic, then the red wine and cook a couple of minutes. Add the tomato paste, beef stock, olives and thyme.
Reduce: Simmer gently about 20 minutes until reduced by half. Season, add the balsamic and finish with the butter for sheen; add a touch of brown sugar if too sour. Set aside and rewarm to serve.

Quick ratatouille base: Sweat the onion and garlic with the carrot, squash and other veg in olive oil with salt, pepper, thyme, oregano, tomato purée, a pinch of sugar and the chopped tomatoes; cook 10–15 minutes until thick.
Layer: Put the base in an oiled tin, then line the sides with slices of eggplant, carrot, red pepper and squash, finish with the thin tomato slices and oregano.
Bake the ratatouille: In the oven for about 10 minutes.

Sear the chops: Season the chops with salt and pepper, render them fat-side down in olive oil, then sear all sides; prick the fat so it doesn't burst. Move them to a tray in the oven with the vine tomatoes (sea salt on top).
Rest: Take the lamb out to rest.
Griddle the polenta: Cut and sear the set polenta in olive oil, flipping once.
Plate: Slice the lamb and serve with the polenta, tomatoes, ratatouille and olive sauce.

recipes.title: CHIKO Roll Iconic AUSTRALIAN savoury snack
ingredients: Green beans, finely chopped — ¼ cup
Minced beef — ½ lb (225 g) (already-cooked beef in the video)
Cooked barley or rice — ½ cup (optional)
Cornflour (cornstarch) — 2 tablespoons mixed with 4 tablespoons water
steps: Soften the veg: Heat the oil, then cook the onion, garlic, carrot, celery and green beans; add the cabbage with salt and pepper to draw out moisture.
Add the beef: Stir in the minced beef (cook it first if raw) with the barley or rice.
Season and thicken: Add the Worcestershire and soy sauce and a splash of beef broth, then the cornflour slurry for a thick filling.
Cool: Cool the filling completely before rolling.
Double the wrappers: Layer two spring roll wrappers together for a thicker crust.
Fill and seal: Egg-wash three edges, spoon in the filling, fold over and roll up, sealing with egg wash.
Fry: Fry seam side down in oil at about 175°C until crisp and golden; drain on a rack.
Serve: Serve with tomato sauce if you like.

recipes.title: STEAK PERFECTION You Got This In The Bag
ingredients: Sirloin steaks, 1 to 1.5 inches thick — as many as needed
Garlic, crushed — 2 cloves (optional, for the pan)
Fresh herbs such as thyme or rosemary — for the pan
Equipment: sous vide precision cooker, large pot or container, vacuum sealer and bags or resealable freezer bags.:
steps: Set the temperature: Clip the circulator to a container of water (above the minimum mark) and set it: medium-rare 54°C (129°F), medium 57°C (135°F), medium-well 63°C (145°F). The video used 57°C.
Season: Salt and pepper both sides of the steaks. Only salt and pepper go in the bag; butter and herbs are saved for the pan.
Bag: Seal each steak in a vacuum bag (or resealable bag with the air pushed out).
Cook: Submerge in the water bath and cook for 2½ hours.
Store or sear: Take them out (they can go into an ice bath, then be frozen in the bag, and reheated about an hour at the same temperature).
Dry: Open the bag and pat the steak very dry, or it won't sear.
Sear: In a warm (not screaming hot) pan with butter and rosemary, sear the fat cap first, then about a minute each side, basting with the butter.
Rest and serve: Rest about 5 minutes, then slice.

recipes.title: ITALIAN  BEEF & Giardiniera Chicago QUICK Style
ingredients: Boneless beef chuck roast or top round — 3–4 lbs (1.5 kg)
Dried oregano, basil, thyme, rosemary — 1 tablespoon each
Giardiniera (2 cups) or sautéed sweet bell peppers
White vinegar (or part apple cider vinegar) — 2 cups
steps: Make the brine: Dissolve the salt in the water and vinegar, add the oregano and pepper, and let it cool.
Cut the veg: Dice or slice the cauliflower, celery, chillies, bell pepper, carrots and olives small and evenly.
Blanch: Boil the vegetables (not the olives) for 2 minutes, then plunge into cold water.

Pickle: Submerge the vegetables in the cooled brine for about 2 hours, then refrigerate. Drain, keeping just enough brine, mix with the olive oil and jar. It is ready to eat after a couple of cold hours (the video gives about 4 hours total).
Sear the beef: Season the chuck with salt and pepper and sear in oil on all sides. Add the garlic off the heat.

Pressure cook: Put the beef in the Instant Pot with the broth, water, wine, herbs, onion powder, garlic powder, pepper flakes and bay leaves. Cook on high for 65 minutes, then release naturally for 15 minutes.
Cool and slice: Remove the beef and cool it, then slice (or pull apart with a fork).
Gravy: Warm and slightly thicken the cooking juices, then heat the sliced meat in it.
Build: Toast the split rolls, pile in the beef, top with giardiniera and cheese if using, and dip in the gravy.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fYX0dDY-BSY

recipes.title: CREAM CHEESE In under 30 mins CANT BUY - CAN MAKE
ingredients: Vinegar or lemon juice (apple cider vinegar in the video) — 3 tbsp
Cream from a carton — a couple of tablespoons
steps: Heat the milk: Bring the milk to the boil, stirring now and then (more often as it starts to rise) so it doesn't catch on the bottom.
Curdle: When boiling, add the vinegar or lemon juice, stir gently, and turn off the heat. If it doesn't split, add more vinegar.
Rest: Leave a minute or two for the curds to form fully.
Drain: Pour through a wet 100% cotton cloth set in a sieve over a bowl; don't squash or weigh it down or it turns solid like paneer. The whey can be used in baking.
Blend: Blend the curds with a little whey, the salt and the butter, scraping down, until smooth, then add the cream.
Store and flavour: Pack into a container. Stir in herbs or garlic powder (it rehydrates and keeps better than fresh garlic) for a herby version.
